title: Puppet tools: pin editing, rigging to nulls, follow-through; expression runtime fix
author: bflatastic
body:
Puppet tool depth for the character-animation workflow (rigging, follow-through, pin editing), checked against the public Puppet tools help page, plus a fix in the expression runtime found along the way. One task id per commit.

## Changes

**M8.1: expressions keep working on long-lived threads**
- boa leaves values on its VM stack whenever an exception unwinds through call frames. Every pending host request does that.
- So after tens to hundreds of evaluations that read layers or effects, every expression on that thread failed with "maximum stack size": slider-driven expressions, pick-whips, pin rigs.
- A run that hits the limit now gets a fresh context and is retried once.
- Regression test: 6000 host-reading evaluations on one thread.

**M13.14: puppet pin editing**
- Click / Shift-click selects pins (`puppet.selectPins`). A drag from empty canvas, or Alt-drag, marquee-selects them.
- Select All with a pin selected takes every pin of that kind.
- **Bug fix:** Delete with a pin selected used to delete the whole layer. It now removes the selected pins (`puppet.removePin {pins?}`).
- Advanced and Bend pins rotate by their ring and scale by its square. Shift snaps to 15° / 5 % steps. One undo step per drag.
- ⌘/Ctrl-dragging one of several selected pins records them all (`puppet.recordPin {pins}`).
- Pins use their kind's colour and grow under the pointer.
- The five pin tools get original code-drawn pushpin icons, replacing one shared stick-figure icon.

**M13.15: rig puppet pins to nulls**
- Window ▸ Create Nulls From Paths now works with puppet pins (`paths.pointsFollowNulls` / `paths.nullsFollowPoints {pins?}`). It uses the selected pins, the named pins, or every pin of a layer with no path.
- **Points Follow Nulls:** each Position / Advanced pin is driven by a null (`fromComp` of the null's anchor), so parented nulls rig limbs.
- **Nulls Follow Points:** nulls ride on pins, to carry other layers.

**M13.16: Follow-Through**
- `puppet.follow`, plus Puppet tool ba…

title: Viewer pan no longer snaps back; drag to reorder layers in the Timeline
author: bflatastic
body:
Two everyday fixes, one task id per commit.

## Changes

**M13.17: the viewer keeps its pan after a middle-button or Hand drag**
- egui reports no total drag on the frame the button is released.
- The pan was recomputed as `start + 0` on that frame, so the view snapped back to where the drag began.
- It now keeps the pan already reached.

**M13.18: drag layer rows in the Timeline to reorder them**
- This was never implemented; the row code said "drag → reorder (later)".
- Dragging a layer row shows an insertion line and moves the layers there on release.
- The selected layers move together; an unselected row moves alone.
- One undo step, and nothing is recorded for a drop in place.
- New `layer.arrange {above: layer}` (put the layers right above that layer), so agents and MCP can do the same.

## Testing
- New headless tests (egui_kittest):
  - a middle-button drag and a Hand-tool drag keep their pan after release (this failed before the fix: pan back to `[0, 0]`)
  - dragging a real Timeline row below / above another reorders the layers in one undo step, and a drop in place does nothing
- New engine test: `layer.arrange {above}` ordering, multi-layer moves, undo, errors.
- Clippy (`-D warnings`), `cargo xtask layers` and `wasm` pass.
- The whole `effectcraft-engine` and `effectcraft-ui-egui` suites pass except tests that also fail on `main` on this Windows machine:
  - render-queue / settings path tests (they expect `/tmp/...`)
  - the GPU viewer and ScriptUI image tests (DX12 shader compile)
  - `ui_and_menu_shortcuts_do_not_collide`

title: Expressions: keep the runtime usable after errors and property reads
author: storybored379
body:
boa leaves the value stack of inner call frames behind when an exception
leaves a script (or a function called from Rust) from a nested call. Every
property read throws the pending-host-request abort from inside a prelude
helper, and so does any helper error (`thisComp.layer("Ghost")`), so the
thread's runtime filled up after ~100 evaluations of a pick-whip
expression: from then on every expression on that thread failed with
"RuntimeLimitError: reached the maximum stack size" and silently fell back
to its keyframed value (e.g. a follower layer stops following after ~90
render_frame calls).

Wrap the script and `__finish` in try/catch and rethrow from their own
frame, which unwinds the stack; backtraces (error line numbers) survive.

The underlying leak is in boa 0.22's exception unwinding (`handle_throw` takes an early-exit path without truncating the value stack); this works around it from our side. Happy to file it with boa separately.

### How it was found and tested
- Reproduced end-to-end through the headless MCP server (`effectcraft-cli mcp`), then fixed.
- Regression test added; verified it **fails without the change and passes with it**. `cargo test -p effectcraft-expr` passes on current `main`; `cargo fmt --check` clean on the touched crate.
- Files: `crates/expr/src/prelude.js`, `crates/expr/src/runtime.rs`, `crates/expr/src/tests.rs`
- Clean-room: no third-party source consulted; only public specs and black-box tools (poppler/ffprobe etc.) as oracles.

Found and fixed with Claude Code (AI-assisted).

title: Compositions: reject zero and negative frame rates instead of panicking
author: storybored379
body:
comp.new / comp.settings passed `frameRate` straight to
FrameRate::from_f64, so 0 (or anything below 0.0005) became a 0/1 rate
and the next frame-duration computation divided by zero, killing the
process (and an MCP session with its unsaved project); a negative rate
was accepted as-is. Scripts hit it via addComp(..., 0) or
comp.frameRate = 0. Return a parameter error like renderQueue.add's
frameRate check does.

title: Shortcuts: don't bind macOS-only Ctrl+Cmd shortcuts off macOS
author: storybored379
body:
Off macOS `Cmd` maps to Ctrl, so View ▸ Enter Full Screen's Ctrl+Cmd+F parsed to the same keys as
Edit ▸ Find's Cmd+F, and both commands were bound to Ctrl+F on Linux and Windows. The existing test
`ui_and_menu_shortcuts_do_not_collide` fails there because of it.

### What changed
`menus::bindings` skips shortcuts that use both Ctrl and Cmd when it builds the key bindings off
macOS, since they can't be typed distinctly there. Enter Full Screen keeps its menu item (and its
shortcut on macOS); off macOS it has no shortcut, and Ctrl+F is Find again. F11 is already taken,
so I didn't pick a replacement — happy to bind one if you have a preference.

### How it was found and tested
- Found by running the workspace tests on Linux: `ui_and_menu_shortcuts_do_not_collide` fails on
  current `main` (Ctrl+F bound to both `app.find` and `view.fullScreen`) and passes with this change.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui` (129 passed; `ui_scriptui::on_draw_concave_fills_and_images_render`

title: Keyframes: a Hold key no longer eases the motion into it
author: storybored379
body:
`segment_value` treated any in-side of the next key that wasn't Linear as Bezier. A key set to Hold
(`KeyframeInterpolationType.HOLD` from a script, `"interpolation": "hold"` on add_keyframe, or the
Keyframe Interpolation dialog — all set both sides) therefore turned the linear segment *into* it
into an ease-in with the default ease: 0 → 100 over 2 s read 27.0 instead of 25 at 0.5 s.

Hold only affects what follows the key, which the out side of that key already handles. The Graph
Editor and the Lottie exporter already treat a Hold in-side as linear, so Lottie exports didn't
match the preview either.

### What changed
The in-side counts as eased only when it is Bezier; a Hold in-side shapes the incoming segment like a
linear one (scalar and spatial paths).

### How it was found and tested
- Found by comparing preview values against the Lottie export of the same keys through the headless
  MCP server (`effectcraft-cli mcp`).
- Regression test `hold_key_keeps_its_incoming_segment_linear` (scalar + spatial) **fails on current
  `main` without the fix and passes with it**.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-keyframe`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-keyframe --all-targets` (no new
  warnings), `cargo fmt --check` on the touched file, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask wasm`.
- Files: `crates/keyframe/src/lib.rs`
- Clean-room: behaviour from After Effects' public documentation; no third-party source consulted.

Found and fixed with Claude Code (AI-assisted).

title: Never crash: steering rules, clippy.toml, forbid unsafe
author: echelon
body:
First PR of the never-crash rollout ([craftrules `standards/never-crash.md`](https://github.com/storytold/craftrules/blob/main/standards/never-crash.md)).

- **AGENTS.md**: a prominent "Never crash" section before the asset rules: the rule and why, that it outranks feature work, the bans (`unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/`unreachable!`/`todo!`/`unimplemented!`/`unsafe`), `Result`/`?` patterns, checked indexing and arithmetic on input-derived values, allocation caps, bounded recursion, lock-poison handling, the last-resort guard, and a regression test per crash fix.
- **CLAUDE.md** (non-negotiables) and **CONTRIBUTING.md** (ground rules): short pointers to it.
- **clippy.toml**: `allow-{unwrap,expect,panic,indexing-slicing}-in-tests = true`, so crates can carry `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, …)]` while tests keep unwrapping. (The crate-by-crate fix PRs carry an identical copy of this file so each can merge on its own; identical adds merge cleanly.)
- **`unsafe_code = "forbid"`** (was `"deny"`). I checked first: there is no `unsafe` and no `allow(unsafe_code)` anywhere in `crates/`, `apps/` or `xtask/`.

title: Unsaved changes: ask before closing a modified project; the modified mark follows undo
author: bflatastic
body:
First task of the M3 (project operations) completion pass, one task id per commit.

## Changes

**M3.9: closing a modified project asks to save it first; the modified mark follows undo**
- Before this change, Quit, the window's close button, File ▸ New Project, Open Project, Open Recent, Close Project, Revert, the demo project and Home templates all dropped unsaved work without asking. The window title was always "EffectCraft".
- These now show **Save / Don't Save / Cancel** when the project has unsaved changes.
  - Save asks for a path when the project is untitled; cancelling that dialog keeps the project open.
  - Revert asks only whether to discard the changes.
  - Opening from Home keeps Home open until the prompt is answered.
- The window title shows the project's path, with `*` while it has unsaved changes.
- **The modified mark follows undo.** The session keeps the snapshot it last opened or saved (`Session::saved_project`). `bump()` marks the project saved again whenever the current snapshot *is* that snapshot. So undoing, jumping in the History panel, or rolling back an atomic batch to the saved state clears the mark. Before, revision numbers only went up, so the project stayed modified.
- **Edits that change nothing record nothing.** Setting a value to what it already is no longer adds an undo step or marks the project modified (`Project::same_content`). The check compares the comps the edit left shared by pointer, so it only walks the comp(s) the edit actually copied.
- **Agents and MCP:** `engine.execute` / MCP calls are never prompted. `ui.menu.invoke` behaves like a click and shows the prompt, with automation ids `dialog.unsaved.save`, `dialog.unsaved.dontSave`, `dialog.unsaved.revert` and `dialog.unsaved.cancel`. The control channel's `app.quit {force: true}` skips the prompt.
- Docs: architecture (§7), agents, control protocol and parity.

title: Never crash: interchange import/export (bad precomp refs, deep XML) without panics
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (see #12). Covers `crates/interchange` (Premiere / FCP XML / FCPXML / OTIO / EDL import and export).

- **A real crash, now fixed:** a precomp layer whose `LayerSource::Comp` points at something that isn't a composition (a footage item, or an item that's been deleted) made `export` panic (`expect("comp")` in `Exporter::sequence`). That layer is now left out of the export. Exporting a non-comp item gives `Error::NoComp`. Regression test: `export_survives_a_precomp_layer_pointing_at_a_non_comp`, which panics on `main`.
- **Another real crash, now fixed: deeply nested XML.** The XML parser behind FCP 7 XML/FCPXML import recurses per element: about 1 000 nested elements overflowed an 8 MiB stack, which **aborts the app** (it can't be caught). `import` now scans XML (skipping comments, CDATA, PIs and quoted attributes) and OTIO JSON nesting first, and returns `Error::TooDeep` beyond `MAX_DEPTH` = 256 levels. - `track_item` returns `Option` instead of `expect("item exists")`. The Motion/Opacity/Volume effect templates come from a small `effect_or_new` helper instead of `find_effect(..).expect(..)`. On import, `motion()` skips a layer that has no transform group instead of panicking.
- Adds `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, clippy::unimplemented, clippy::todo, clippy::unreachable)]` to the crate.

title: Never crash: SVG path data loop and deep nesting
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (see #12). Covers `crates/svg` (SVG import, also used for PDF/AI/EPS artwork).

- **A real crash, now fixed (found by mutation fuzzing):** path data with a number right after `Z`/`z` (e.g. `…Z9 C…`, or a single byte dropped from a valid file) sent `parse_path_data` into an endless loop. `Z` was treated as an implicit repeat but consumes no numbers, so the loop never advanced and kept appending `ClosePath` until the process was OOM-killed. A one-byte mutation of our own `favicon.svg` grew to 24 GB RSS. A number after `Z` is a syntax error, so parsing now stops there and keeps the prefix, as the spec asks. Regression test: `pathdata::tests::number_after_close_stops_instead_of_looping` (on `main` it never finishes and exhausts memory).
- **Another real crash, now fixed: deeply nested elements.** roxmltree recurses per element and overflows a 2 MiB stack at a few thousand nested `<g>`s, which **aborts the app**. `parse` now checks the element depth with a quick scan (skipping comments, CDATA, PIs, declarations and quoted attribute values) and returns `Error::Xml("elements nested more than 256 levels deep")`. Regression test: `tests::deep_nesting_errors_instead_of_overflowing_the_stack` (100 000 levels).
- Adds `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, …)]` to the crate. It had no production panic sites.

Not fixed here (third-party, debug builds only): with extreme coordinates, tiny-skia 0.12's scan converter can trip its own `debug_assert!(edges[..].last_y >= curr_y)`. Release builds are unaffected.

title: Never crash: media crate without expect()
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (see #12). Covers `crates/media` (footage import and decode).

title: Never crash: PSD reader bounds overflow and input-sized allocations
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (see #12). Covers `crates/psd` (the Photoshop PSD/PSB reader behind PSD import and PSD footage).

**Real crashes, now fixed.** Each has a regression test, and both tests panic on `main`:
- `extreme_layer_bounds_error_instead_of_overflowing`: a layer record whose bounds span the whole i32 range made `Rect::width()`/`height()` overflow the i32 subtraction (a panic in debug builds, and nonsense sizes in release). Widths and heights are now computed in `i64` and clamped to `u32`.
- `huge_layer_bounds_error_instead_of_allocating`: a ~100-byte file claiming a 2³¹ × 2³¹ layer made `layer_pixels` allocate `w × h` pixels before reading any data, which panicked with "capacity overflow" (smaller claims abort on out-of-memory instead). Every decoded image (the composite, a layer, a mask) is now capped at **2²⁸ pixels** (e.g. 16 384 × 16 384, 4 GiB as float RGBA) and returns `Error::Unsupported("… too large to decode")` beyond that.

- `descriptor::tests::deeply_nested_descriptors_error_instead_of_overflowing_the_stack`: a descriptor's nesting limit (64) restarted at 0 inside every nested `Objc`/`GlbO`/`ObAr`, so 100 000 nested descriptors (a 2.4 MB layer-effects or text block) recursed until the **stack overflowed and aborted the app**. The depth now carries through nested descriptors. On `main` this test aborts the test process.

**Hardening against other input-sized allocations:**
- ZIP-compressed channels inflate with `decompress_to_vec_zlib_with_limit` (the expected size) instead of without a limit.
- RLE byte-count tables and UTF-16 descriptor strings reserve at most what the remaining bytes could hold.
- The per-pixel copy in `layer_pixels` iterates only the rows and columns that land in the output, in 64-bit arithmetic, rather than the whole (file-sized) source rect.

Adds `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, …)]` to the crate. It had no production panic sites. I also mutation-fuzzed the reader (30k mutations of written 8/16/32-bit RGB/CMYK/Gray/…

title: Never crash: reject deeply nested expressions instead of overflowing the stack
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (see #12). Covers `crates/expr` (the expression engine).

**A real crash, now fixed: stack overflow on deeply nested expressions.** Boa's parser recurses once per nesting level. Probing `check_syntax` with `((((…1+2…))))`:

| thread stack | debug | release |
|---|---|---|
| 2 MiB | ok at 60, **aborts** by 100 | ok at 60, **aborts** by 80 |
| 8 MiB | ok at 200, **aborts** by 300 | ok at 200, **aborts** by 400 |

A stack overflow can't be caught, so the whole app dies along with the user's unsaved work. The array-maths rewrite turns each `+ - * /` into a nested helper call (`a+b+c+…` → `__add(__add(…))`), so a long sum hits the same limit. With 100 000 brackets, the rewriter's own recursion overflows too.

- `rewrite()` measures nesting (brackets, plus runs of prefix operators like `!!!!x`) on the source and again on the rewritten output. Anything deeper than `MAX_NESTING` (32) becomes `throw new RangeError("expression is nested too deeply …")`, so it shows up as a normal expression error and the property falls back to its value. `check_syntax` reports the same error without touching the parser.
- 32 leaves about 2× headroom on a 2 MiB thread. Real expressions rarely go past 10.
- Regression test: `rewrite::tests::deep_nesting_is_an_error_not_a_stack_overflow`, covering 33, 100 and 100 000 levels of parens, unclosed brackets, long sums and `!` chains. On `main`, `check_syntax` aborts the test process.

**Also:** the `unwrap_or_else(|| unreachable!())` in the bracket-tree builder is now a let-chain, and the crate gets `#![deny(clippy::unwrap_used, …)]`. Production panic sites in the crate: 1 → 0.

`crates/expr/src/runtime.rs`, `prelude.js` and `tests.rs` are untouched because #6 is changing them. The guard sits in `rewrite.rs` (which `runtime.rs` already calls for every expression) and `lib.rs`.

author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (see #12). Covers `crates/av1enc` (the AV1 encoder used for MP4/WebM export).

title: Never crash: last-resort guard around command execution, and a logging panic hook
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (see #12). This is the **last-resort guard** from the standard. It's a safety net, not a substitute for returning errors.

Before this PR, nothing caught a panic. A bug in any command (and every UI action, CLI call, control-channel/MCP request, script call, import, export and save is a command) took the whole app down, along with the user's unsaved work.

- **`crates/engine/src/guard.rs`**: `guarded(what, f)` runs `f` under `std::panic::catch_unwind`. A panic becomes `EngineError::Other("command `x` failed with an internal error (<message>); it was stopped and your project is still open")` and is logged.
- **`Session::execute`** wraps `(spec.run)(self, &params)` in it, so every frontend gets the error through its existing error path: the UI's status line, the control channel's error reply, the CLI's error message.
- `Session::edit` already works on a copy of the project and only swaps it in at the end, so an edit that panics halfway leaves the project (and the undo history) untouched. `guard::tests::the_session_survives_a_panicking_edit` checks this, and that later edits still work.
- **Panic hook:** `logging::install_panic_hook()` logs every panic (message and location) through the app logger (Help ▸ Enable Logging), then runs the previous hook. The desktop app installs it at startup.
- `panic = "unwind"` stays (it's the default; no profile overrides it).

Not covered (kept small on purpose): panics on background threads outside commands. Engine analysis jobs run on `std::thread`s whose join results are already ignored, so they don't abort the app. Frame rendering runs on a rayon pool, whose `spawn` aborts on panic by default; the ui-egui PR adds a `panic_handler` there. On wasm32 the target aborts on panic, so the guard compiles but can't unwind there.

title: Never crash: engine without expect() (job polling, commands, menus)
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (see #12). Covers `crates/engine` (the session, the command registry and every command behind the UI, CLI, control channel and MCP).

- **Job polling** (`camera_track.rs`, `mask_track.rs`, `roto.rs`, `tracking.rs`, `warp.rs`, `render_queue.rs`): `self.X_job.take().expect("job")` after an `is_some`/`is_finished` check is now `let … else { return false }` or `if finished && let Some(..)`. `stop_render` no longer `expect`s the job and its remote.

title: Never crash: Tick and timecode arithmetic can't overflow or divide by zero
author: echelon
body:
Part of the never-crash rollout (see #12). Covers `crates/time` (`Tick`, `FrameRate`, timecode). Every frontend and every file format goes through this crate.

**Real crashes, now fixed.** Each panics in debug/dev builds and silently wraps in release:
- **Control channel / MCP:** I fuzzed every engine command with extreme parameters, and `layer.timing {"delta": -1e308}` panicked. `Tick::from_seconds_f64(-1e308)` saturated to `i64::MIN`, and `FrameRate::snap_nearest` then overflowed.
- **UI timecode fields:** `parse_timecode("99999999999999:00:00:00")` overflowed `h * 3600`. `parse_feet_frames` had the same problem.
- **Damaged files:** a zero frame rate or timebase divides by zero in `frame_duration`/`frame_at`/`tick_of`/`from_units`/`from_rational`/`mul_ratio`. #7 rejects zero rates in the comp commands; this PR covers every other path, such as a project or media file that carries one.

**Changes:**
- `Tick::from_seconds_f64` clamps to `Tick::MIN..=Tick::MAX` (the existing ±i64::MAX/4 range), and NaN becomes 0.
- `Tick` `+`, `-`, unary `-`, `+=`, `-=` and `abs` saturate. Behaviour only changes where it used to overflow.
- The i128 intermediates saturate when narrowed to i64, and a zero divisor counts as 1 (a nonsense result instead of a crash).
- Timecode and feet+frames parsing returns `ParseError("timecode too large")` / `"number too large"`. Formatting uses saturating/unsigned absolute values, and drop-frame math saturates.
- Regression test: `tests::hostile_numbers_never_overflow`.

title: Fix the periodic freeze on Windows; keyframe drag, copy/paste and Graph Editor behave like After Effects
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes the two reported problems: the app froze every few seconds, and keyframes could not be dragged or copied and pasted. It also brings keyframe handling in line with After Effects. One task id per commit.

## Changes

**M12.8: the app no longer freezes every 10 s on Windows**
- Every 10 seconds the UI thread re-read the system's memory for the cache budgets. On Windows that starts PowerShell (`Get-CimInstance`) and waits for it: about a second, during which the app froze.
- The reading now runs on a background thread (`sysinfo::MemoryWatch`). `memory_tick` takes the last reading and never waits.
- The interval is now 30 s, and console programs start with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`.
- Measured with a control-channel probe on the running app: idle UI frames are about 10 ms; before, there was a stall every 10 s.

**M3.15: Ctrl+C / Ctrl+X / Ctrl+V work in the app**
- egui-winit delivers these as `Copy` / `Cut` / `Paste` events, not key presses, and the shortcut dispatcher only read key presses. Copying and pasting with the keyboard did nothing. Tests passed because they inject key presses.
- The events now map back to their keys with the modifiers held, so Ctrl+Alt+C and the other variants work too. On-canvas text editing is excluded.
- Copying also puts a line on the system clipboard ("EffectCraft: 3 keyframes"), because Ctrl+V with an empty clipboard sends no event.

**M5.9: keyframe drags follow the pointer to the end**
- Each key's widget id included its time. After the first frame of movement it became a new widget, and egui ended the drag.
- The Timeline now follows the whole gesture itself (`KeyDrag`), starting from where the button went down.

**M5.10: keyframes behave like After Effects**
- **Drags never destroy keys:** the steps of one drag apply their total offset to the keys as they were before it. A key passed over survives, and only the drop position replaces a key.
- **Stretched layers:** keys move with the pointer, in comp time (drags and Alt+Arrow nudges).

author: bflatastic

title: M4.14: content-keyed RAM preview frames (M4 done); proxies in the disk cache key
author: bflatastic
body:
## Summary
- **RAM preview frames are keyed by content, not by project revision.** Editing one comp keeps the cached frames (green bar) of every other comp. Undo finds the frames of the state it returns to, as in After Effects. This was the last open item in roadmap **M4**, which is now **Done**.
- **Cheap identity.** It hashes the addresses of the comps a comp draws, plus footage, solids, proxies and settings by value. It takes about **0.1 ms** on the 1500-layer test project; the full content hash took about 117 ms there, too slow to run on every edit.
- **Why addresses are safe:** the RAM cache keeps a project snapshot for every identity that has frames cached or rendering. That forces `Arc::make_mut` to copy an edited comp, so it always gets a new address, and old addresses can't be reused while frames depend on them. At most 64 identities are kept: a long drag drops its oldest states together with their frames.
- **Bug fix.** The disk cache's content key ignored proxies and Use Proxy, so it could serve stale frames. It now covers both.
- **Test fix.** It corrects a wrong expectation in the M13.31 Home size test (12.5 KB rounds to "12 KB"), which went red after #51.

## Test plan
- [x] Frames unit tests: content keys; edits elsewhere and undo; bounded long drags; an in-place edit still changes the identity.
- [x] `ui_ram_preview` end to end: switching comps, an edit in another comp, undo.
- [x] Disk cache proxy key test.
- [x] Suites: ui-egui and render (twice, clean) and engine. The only failures are the known Windows `/tmp` baseline tests, which also fail on main.

title: M13.35: Roto Brush trained model — swappable segment module, MobileSAM in pure Rust
author: bflatastic
body:
## Summary
Roto Brush can now use a **trained segmentation model**, in a module that is **composable and swappable** (as requested). Impact on the system is low: installers don't grow, nothing is downloaded unless asked for, and there's no ML framework.

- **`effectcraft-segment` (new layer-1 crate)**
  - **`MaskModel` trait:** prompts (points, box, prior mask) in, foreground probability out. Roto Brush only talks to this trait.
  - **Registry:** every model must be open source under a licence compatible with ours, and declare its source URL, size and SHA-256.
  - **MobileSAM (Apache-2.0)** in plain Rust (rayon plus ndarray's safe matrix multiply), loading the official `mobile_sam.pt` exactly as published (our own checkpoint reader).
  - **Verified against an independent implementation** (Hugging Face candle): embeddings within 0.3% RMS, 99.9% of mask pixels equal. Our encoder is about 7× faster than candle's: 0.7 s/frame at 32 threads, 1.3 s at 4 threads. The embedding is cached per frame, so new strokes on the same frame rerun only the decoder (about 0.1 s).
- **Roto Brush integration**
  - **Base frame:** points along the strokes prompt the model.
  - **Propagation:** the flow-warped matte prompts the model.
  - **Fusion:** the model's mask becomes a strong prior for the existing graph cut, so strokes stay hard constraints and edges still snap to colour.
  - **Safety:** a model that fails, or disagrees with the flow, is ignored for that frame.
  - **Versions:** Version 2.0/3.0 use the chosen model; 1.0 and "no model installed" use the classic engine. The model id is part of the cache keys, so switching models recomputes the mattes.
- **Settings ▸ Roto Brush**
  - Choose the model, then **Download** (official file, SHA-256 verified, via the system `curl`), **Install from File…** or **Remove**.
  - Licence, size and links are shown for each model.
  - Weights live in `<config>/models`, shared by the desktop app, CLI and MCP.

title: M13.36: face tracking trained model (MediaPipe Face Landmarker, pure Rust)
author: bflatastic
body:
Face tracking can now use a trained model, in the same swappable model module as Roto Brush.

## What
- **Model:** MediaPipe Face Landmarker (Google LLC, **Apache-2.0**): the BlazeFace detector and the 478-point Face Mesh V2. It's an optional **3.8 MB** download (Settings ▸ Face Tracking, or `face.model.download`), pinned by SHA-256 and never bundled.
- **Runtime:** a pure-Rust TensorFlow Lite reader and interpreter (`segment::tflite`). It needs no ML framework and no `unsafe`, and builds on every platform, including wasm (the browser keeps the classic tracker for now).
- **Interface:** `segment::face::FaceModel`. Each model maps its own points to the tracker's landmarks and outline, so models can be swapped without touching the tracker.
- **Tracker:** `FaceTracker::new_with` uses the model and falls back to the classical fitter when the model finds no face. Chin and jaw come from the outline either way, so Extract Face Measurements means the same with either engine.
- **Engine:** `roto_models` becomes `models`, covering both tasks.
  - New commands: `face.models` and `face.model.{select,install,download,remove}`.
  - `wait: true` on select, install and download, so scripts and MCP agents can block until the model is in use.
  - `track.mask` reports `faceModel`.
- **Credits:**
  - `ATTRIBUTION.md` lists the optional models (MobileSAM was missing too) and the Apache-2.0 specs the code follows.
  - Settings shows each model's authors, licence and links.
  - Installed weights get a `<file>.NOTICE.txt`.

- **Interpreter vs TensorFlow Lite** (`ai-edge-litert` 2.2.0): both models match to about one part in a million. The recorded sums are pinned in a test.

title: GPU on wgpu's OpenGL backend (FreeBSD / Linux without Vulkan)
author: echelon
body:
The FreeBSD CI job (#60, run 37309226076) runs the GPU tests on Mesa llvmpipe over wgpu's GL backend, and 22 `effectcraft-gpu` tests failed. Each one is explained and fixed below.

### Root causes and fixes

| Failures | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 11 (`tests_adv3d::*`, `tests_deferred_jobs::advanced_3d_resolves_in_passes`) | Advanced 3D's camera-depth target was `R32Float`, which GLES can't render to without `EXT_color_buffer_float`, so `create_render_pipeline` failed validation. Release builds only log that error and then draw nothing, so the output was silently wrong. | The depth target is now `R32Uint` and holds the f32's bits (`bitcast`). That is lossless and renders on every backend. `GpuContext::new` also checks `adapter.get_texture_format_features` (render attachment for all three targets, blendable colour) and `INDEPENDENT_BLEND` (`adv3d::raster_unsupported`). If any of them is missing, the render pipelines are never built, and Advanced 3D falls back to the existing CPU path. |
| 2 (`tests_fx_lut::ocio_custom_config`, `tests_fx_noise::edge_preserving_blurs`) | `Could not lock adapter context`: wgpu's GL backend has one context lock per adapter with a 6 s timeout. When tests drive devices concurrently, a waiting thread panics. | One process-wide lock serialises the GPU tests. `tests::hold_gpu_lock()` is taken by every helper that hands out a device (`gpu()`, the adv3d tests' own devices, `deferred_gpu()`). The calling test thread holds it until it exits, and the lock is reentrant per thread. In other test binaries, `ui_web_job_gpu.rs` is the only one with more than one device test, so its two tests now share a lock. The other ui-egui binaries that create devices have a single non-ignored device test each. |
| 6 (`tests_fx_generate::generators` (Cell Pattern tiling), `tests_fx_vr::*`) | Signed `%` with negative operands. naga emits GLSL `%`, which is undefined for negative operands, and Mesa gets it wrong. This broke the VR effects' horizontal wrap and Cell…

title: Fix #63: scaling a layer by its handles follows the pointer
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #63.

**Causes**
1. The handle drag rescaled *incrementally*: every frame it multiplied the current scale by a ratio and re-based. Rounding built up, edge handles changed both axes, and once a factor came near 0 the next ratios had nothing to scale, so the layer stayed at 0. That's the "scales to 0 and can't be fixed" in the video.
2. The gesture tested for a handle at the point where egui decided a drag had started, which is past the drag threshold. On a quick grab the pointer had already left the 9-px handle, so the layer was moved instead of scaled.

**Fix** (After Effects behaviour)
- Scaling is computed from the layer **as the drag began**, about its **anchor point**, so the grabbed point stays under the pointer.
- **Corners** scale both axes; **edges** scale one.
- **Shift** on a corner keeps the proportions, following the pointer along the handle's diagonal.
- Dragging past the anchor **flips** the layer. Dragging back out recovers.
- Selection-tool gestures (handle, layer pick, marquee) start at the **press point**.
- The whole drag is still one undo step.

**Test:** `handle_drags_scale_about_the_anchor_and_follow_the_pointer` drags the real handles in the headless app. It covers a corner to 2×, a drag through the anchor and back out to 1.5× (the old code stuck at 0), a flip, an edge (x only), and Shift (proportional). All UI tests and clippy pass.

title: Fix #65: the viewer keeps up while a layer is dragged
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #65.

**Measured:** I timed the real app headlessly with the GPU on the demo project, dragging the EFFECTCRAFT text layer 20 steps.

| | per drag step until the viewer shows it | frame render |
|---|---|---|
| before | **102 ms** on average (worst 413 ms) | 20 ms |
| after | **16 ms** (worst 17 ms) | 11 ms |

**Cause:** while paused, as soon as the viewer's frame finished the app started pre-rendering the frames around it for the RAM preview. During a drag every step changes the project, so those frames were already stale at the next step. Worse, they held the CPU and GPU the next viewer frame needed, so the frame you were waiting for queued behind them. Playback was fast because it plays cached frames.

**Fix:** paused prefetch waits until the project has stopped changing for 0.3 s, then resumes as before. Playback, scrubbing (no edits) and Cache Frames When Idle are unchanged.

**Test:** `prefetch_waits_while_edits_keep_coming` makes 8 edits and checks that only the viewer's frame is queued or cached for each, and that prefetch resumes once the edits pause. On the old code it fails on the first edit, which had already pre-rendered 13 frames. Clippy is clean; the only UI test failures are the 2 known DX12-on-this-machine ones.

title: Fix #43: the AppImage's window shows the EffectCraft icon on Wayland
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #43.

**Cause:** on Wayland the compositor (GNOME, KDE…) takes a window's icon from the desktop entry named by the window's app ID, `ai.storyteller.effectcraft.desktop`. The app sets that ID, and the .deb, .rpm and Flatpak install the entry, but an AppImage installs nothing, so its window got the generic Wayland icon. winit can't set a window icon on Wayland directly (it only does that on X11 and Windows).

**Fix:** `apps/effectcraft/src/appimage.rs`. When started from an AppImage (`$APPIMAGE` is set), before the window opens, the app writes:
- a **hidden** desktop entry (`NoDisplay=true`: no menu item) whose `Exec` points at the AppImage, quoted per the Desktop Entry spec;
- the 256 px icon in the hicolor theme;

both under `$XDG_DATA_HOME` (else `~/.local/share`). Safeguards:
- **Nothing is written** when an installed package or the user's own entry already provides the ID. It only ever rewrites entries it wrote itself (they carry a marker key).
- The entry **follows the AppImage** when it moves.
- Writes are atomic, and failures are only logged.

**Tests** (they run on every OS):
- `Exec` quoting and escaping per the spec.
- First write, no-op when up to date, follows a moved AppImage, leaves the user's own entry alone, writes nothing when a package's entry exists.

title: text: script-aware system font fallback; accept PostScript / full font names
author: fortesnow
body:
## Problem

On Windows (11, ARM64 native build; the same code path on every platform), Japanese text renders as missing-glyph boxes unless the text layer explicitly names a Japanese *family*:

- The default family Inter has no CJK glyphs, and `fonts::fallback_for` only searches the bundled faces and the faces some other layer already loaded. So `洗濯機の水抜き` in Inter shows `NO GLYPH` boxes — unless another layer below it happened to use Meiryo first, in which case it renders. The result depends on render order.
- `textDocument.font = "YuGothic-Bold"` (the PostScript name, which is how After Effects scripts set fonts) is not a family name, so `resolve` falls back to Inter, and then the same thing happens.

Repro (headless):

```
effectcraft-cli script jp.jsx
# jp.jsx: comp + one text layer "水抜き", no font set (Inter)   -> NO GLYPH boxes
# jp.jsx: same with td.font = "YuGothic-Bold"                      -> NO GLYPH boxes
# jp.jsx: same with td.font = "Yu Gothic"; td.fontStyle = "Bold"   -> renders
```

## Change

`crates/text/src/fonts.rs`:

- `fallback_for`: after the existing cheap candidates (bundled, already-loaded), it classifies the character (kana → Japanese, hangul → Korean, Han ideographs / CJK punctuation / full-width forms → shared) and tries the families the platforms' own fallback tables use for that language (Windows, macOS, then the Noto / Linux names), in the preferred face's style so bold text gets the bold cut. If none of those is installed or covers the character, it searches every installed face once, reading each file without keeping its bytes. Results are cached per 256-character block and preferred face; a negative result is cached too, so the exhaustive search runs once per block, not per character.
- Han ideographs are shared by Japanese, Chinese and Korean; the order comes from `LC_ALL` / `LC_CTYPE` / `LANG` (`EFFECTCRAFT_CJK_LOCALE` overrides), Japanese first when nothing says otherwise. Kana and hangul in the same text pick their language regard…

title: Preview: Audio, Lock and Shy keep the cache; playback with audio waits for frames (#103)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #103, both parts.

### 1. Audio, Lock and Shy switches wiped the cache
Toggling a layer's Audio, Lock or Shy switch (or the comp's Hide Shy Layers) threw away every cached frame, so everything re-rendered. None of these change pixels.

**Cause:** the RAM preview identity of a comp hashes the comp's address, and every edit replaces it. The layer cache and disk cache keys hashed every switch.

**Now:**
- `effectcraft-project`: `Switches::pixels` (Audio, Lock and Shy at their defaults), `Layer::same_pixels` and `Comp::same_pixels` (exhaustive field lists, so a field added later can't be skipped by accident), and `Comp::pixel_form` for keys that hash the whole comp.
- Layer cache keys hash `Switches::pixels`. The disk cache's comp content key hashes `Comp::pixel_form`.
- `Frames::identity`: when the comps in a new revision draw the same pixels as the comps behind the comp's last new identity, that identity is kept, together with the project that holds those comps' addresses. The cached frames stay, including when the switch is toggled back.
- Expressions can't read these switches (only scripting can), so pixels never depend on them.

### 2. Playback with audio skipped frames
With audio on, the audio clock drove playback and dropped frames that weren't rendered yet.

**Now:** the sound waits for the frames. Until the frames ahead are cached (to the end of the preview, or as many as fit in the RAM preview), every frame shows as it renders, silently, the same as a preview without audio. Then the sound starts in sync. If playback reaches a frame that isn't cached, the sound stops instead of frames being skipped, and it comes back once the frames ahead are cached again. Slowing the audio down to match slow frames, as the issue suggests, would need time-stretching; this change doesn't do that.

**Docs:** architecture.md (audio and caches).

**Tests:**
- `audio_lock_and_shy_switches_keep_the_frames` (frames.rs): Audio, Lock and Shy on the outer and nested comps, Hide Shy…

title: GPU: running out of video memory falls back to the CPU instead of crashing (#106)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #106: when video memory ran out during preview, every frame thread panicked, and the frames that crashed never rendered again.

**Cause (as the report says):**
- The desktop app composites on egui-wgpu's device, which had no uncaptured-error handler, so wgpu's default handler turned an out-of-memory error into a panic on whichever frame thread hit it.
- A frame whose render panicked stayed in the "in progress" set forever, so it was never asked for again.
- The GPU frame budget was a fixed 1 GiB, whatever the GPU has.

**Now:**
- `GpuContext::new` logs uncaptured device errors once its pipelines are built. Errors while building them still panic on the shared device, which the app already catches to fall back to CPU compositing.
- `Gpu::within_memory` runs GPU work inside an out-of-memory error scope (wgpu error scopes are per thread). On an error the result is discarded and the uploaded layers and pooled textures are freed.
- Frame workers render each frame inside it, both for GPU display frames and for GPU-composited frames that are read back. If the GPU runs out of memory, that frame renders on the CPU and the RAM preview keeps half as many GPU frames from then on, down to 64 MiB. wgpu can't report how much video memory a GPU has, so the budget adapts to what the GPU actually managed.
- A frame whose render panics is rendered again on the CPU, or released, so it is never left in progress.
- Docs: architecture.md.

**Tests:**
- `a_frame_whose_render_panics_is_released` (frames.rs): a footage decoder that panics; the frame is released. It failed before the fix.
- `running_out_of_video_memory_halves_the_gpu_frame_budget` (frames.rs).
- `within_memory_returns_the_work_when_there_is_room` (gpu). Forcing a real out-of-memory error isn't safe on CI machines.

**Gate:** fmt, workspace clippy `-D warnings` (release, all targets), `xtask wasm`, and the ui-egui and gpu tests (gpu on Vulkan). Everything passes except the known Windows baselines (`ui_gpu`'s DX12 shader c…

title: Control: ui.click / ui.drag hold their modifiers for the whole gesture
author: echelon
body:
Control-channel clicks and drags with modifiers arrived as plain ones. For example, a `ui.click` with `modifiers: {shift: true}` on a Timeline effect replaced the selection instead of adding to it. That breaks multi-select for agents driving the app.

**Cause:** egui takes `i.modifiers` from `Event::ModifiersChanged`, not from the modifiers attached to a pointer event. The synthetic events also arrive one per frame, so the press and release never saw Shift.

**Fix:**
- `ui.click` and `ui.drag` now queue `ModifiersChanged(m)` before the gesture and `ModifiersChanged(NONE)` after it, the same way egui_kittest does.
- The synthetic-input feeding moves from `raw_input_hook` into `EffectcraftApp::feed_synthetic` (no behaviour change), so it can be tested.

**Tests:** `ui_control_modifiers.rs` checks that a Shift-click holds Shift from press to release (and that a plain click after it has none), and that a Shift-drag holds it through the moves. Both tests fail without the fix and pass with it.

**Verified on the branch base** (`588d269`):
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui`: all 31 test binaries pass.

title: Fonts: use craft-fonts as an optional build input
author: echelon
body:
Makes [storytold/craft-fonts](https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts) an **optional build input** for EffectCraft ([craftrules `standards/fonts.md`](https://github.com/storytold/craftrules/blob/main/standards/fonts.md)). craft-fonts is never added to a `Cargo.toml`. If `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR` is unset, the app builds, tests and runs exactly as before.

## How it works

- **`crates/text/build.rs`** (the recipe from craft-fonts' `docs/integration.md`; it reads a local directory and never touches the network). With `CRAFT_FONTS_DIR=<absolute path to a checkout>`, it embeds every font in `fonts/manifest.txt` as `effectcraft_text::fonts::CRAFT_FONTS`. If the variable is unset, the slice is empty. A bad path produces a warning, or a build error when `CRAFT_FONTS_REQUIRED=1`. `effectcraft-text` is the lowest crate that both the UI and the text engine depend on, so `ui-egui` uses it from there.
- **wasm32 embeds only BIZ UDPGothic Regular** (4.7 MB raw, about 3.0 MB zipped) to keep the web download small. Native builds embed all four faces.
- **Text engine** (`fonts.rs`): the `Jpan` faces are registered after the bundled faces, with origin `"craft-fonts"`. `fallback_for` tries them for Japanese before any system font (#84's script-aware search still follows). Serif text gets a Mincho (Shippori Mincho, then BIZ UDMincho); everything else gets BIZ UDPGothic, in the cut nearest the requested weight. Han ideographs use them only when the locale puts Japanese first, so zh/ko locales keep their own system families. The families also appear in the font menus.
- **UI** (`theme.rs`): `add_craft_fonts` appends the `Jpan` faces to every egui family after Inter/JetBrains Mono and egui's defaults. BIZ UDPGothic comes first, and its Bold comes first in the `semibold` family. #71's system-font fallback still runs after it, but only when craft-fonts didn't supply the face, so a Japanese font is never embedded twice. The web build has no system fonts, so craft-fonts is the only way it gets Japa…

title: GPU: land #139 (contain GPU initialization errors) with a readback latency fix
author: bflatastic
body:
Lands @dexterlabs1's #139 (*Contain GPU initialization errors and retire failed compositor work*) with its commits unchanged, plus one follow-up fix. When this merges, GitHub marks #139 as merged too.

## What #139 does (reviewed)
- **Initialization:** builds every pipeline, layout and buffer inside OOM / internal / validation error scopes (`init_resource`), so a shader that fails to compile returns `Err` and the app falls back to CPU compositing instead of panicking.
- **Device handlers:** the desktop executable and the web page install the shared device's error and device-lost handlers. They forward failures through a weak, latched bridge (`gpu_failure`) that retires GPU preview without touching the project, undo history or preferences. Owned devices (CLI, workers) install their own handlers.
- **Readbacks:** a registry (`readback.rs`) settles every readback exactly once, with a 10 s deadline and isolated callbacks. Late results are discarded.
- **Frames:** a retired context can't publish GPU frames to the RAM preview. CPU frames survive, and CPU retries don't reuse layer-cache entries from a failed GPU attempt.
- **Security review:** no new third-party crates (`web-time`, `wasm-bindgen` and `js-sys` were already in the lockfile). No `unsafe`, network, process or file access. Non-test code doesn't panic, and lock poisoning is handled.

## The follow-up fix (`80dff0f`)
#139's bounded `read_buffer` polled without waiting and slept up to 10 ms between polls. That added up to 10 ms to every readback, and the desktop viewer reads every GPU frame back. The gpu crate's test suite took **227 s against 119 s** on main. It now waits with `PollType::Wait` and the remaining deadline as its timeout (a timeout still retires the context), so the suite takes **71–79 s**.

## Checked (Windows, RTX 4090)
- Workspace clippy `-D warnings` (release, all targets), `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm`.
- The gpu tests on Vulkan, and the ui-egui and automation tests. Everything passes except the…

title: Control: close the connection on input that isn't a request
author: Luskish
body:
Same bug as storytold/filmcraft#119. The control server answers a non-JSON line with an error and keeps reading. So while `--control` is open, a web page's cross-origin POST to `127.0.0.1:<port>` gets its JSON body run as a command.

Ports LightCraft's fix (storytold/lightcraft#129):

- A line that isn't a JSON object with a string `method` gets one error reply, then the connection closes.
- Lines over 4 MiB are refused, and at most 16 connections are served at once.
- `docs/control-protocol.md` documents the rules.

`effectcraft-cli mcp --bridge` sends valid requests, so it's unaffected.

**Testing:** new tests in `control_server.rs` cover the browser POST and other junk input. They failed before the fix and pass now. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p effectcraft`, `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets` all pass.

title: CLI: --format hevc / av1 write HEVC / AV1; an unknown comp is named (#154, #155)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #154. Fixes #155.

**#154: `effectcraft-cli render --format hevc|av1` wrote H.264.** `renderQueue.add` (and `render.addOutputModule`) applied `format`, then dropped it before applying the output path, so the `.mp4` extension switched the module back to H.264 (and `.mov` / `.webm` to ProRes / VP9).
- An explicit format now wins. A mismatched extension follows it: `--format av1 --out x.webm` writes `x.mp4`, as choosing a format in the Output Module renames Output To.
- An extension that agrees with the format keeps the name as given. That matters because the CLI passes the extension as the format: `--out still.png` stays a PNG sequence named as before.
- The format error now lists `hevc` and `av1` in all three places (one `FORMATS` string).

**#155: an unknown `--comp` was reported as "no active composition".** `comp_id` now returns `no composition "Nope"` (new `EngineError::NoSuchComp`) for a name or id that matches no comp, and `comp_for_queue` passes that error on instead of collapsing it to `None`. `render`, `props`, `get` and `exec` all report it now, like `render-frame`.

**Tests:** `an_explicit_format_wins_over_the_output_extension` (both commands, every mismatch case, extensions that agree with the format, and no format at all) and `an_unknown_comp_is_named_in_the_error` (by name and by id, across three commands). With the CLI itself, the files are `hevc,hvc1` and `av1,av01` and decode with ffmpeg without errors. `render --comp Nope` and `props Nope BG` print `no composition "Nope"`.

**Gate:** fmt, clippy `-D warnings` (release, all targets) for effectcraft-engine, effectcraft-cli and effectcraft-automation, all 399 engine tests, and the CLI's tests.

title: Timeline: per-layer reveals, Time Remap reveal, full zoom-out, navigator handles (#157–#160)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #157. Fixes #158. Fixes #159. Fixes #160.

- **#160: U closed other layers.** The reveal shortcuts (U, P, S, R, T, A, E, M, F, L) kept one filter for the whole Timeline and replaced the open layers with the selected ones. Each layer now has its own filter (`TimelineState::layer_reveal`). A shortcut applies to the selected layers (all layers with none selected) through `apply_reveal`, and other layers keep their twirl state and their own reveal. U's results replace only the target layers' earlier picks, so U after UU shows keyframed properties again. `anim.reveal` now reports which layers it looked at. Twirling a layer by hand, Ctrl+` and Collapse All clear the filters they cover.
- **#157: Enable Time Remapping showed nothing.** When the command turns remapping on, the layers that have it now twirl open on Time Remap with its two keys (same per-layer reveal as RR).
- **#158: Alt+wheel stopped short of the whole comp.** Its lower limit came from the current zoom and the ruler's start stayed where the pointer put it, so a 10-minute comp stopped on 0:05:02–0:10:27. Alt+wheel and `=`/`-` now go through `set_zoom`, whose limit is the comp's fit (`fit_pps`, the formula the ruler and slider use). Reaching it fits the whole comp from 0.

author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #147. Fixes #156. Fixes #162.

- **#147: Pan Behind didn't snap the anchor to its own layer.** The gesture excluded all of the dragged layer's snap targets, not just its anchor. `engine::viewer::layer_targets(ctx, layer, anchor)` now holds the per-layer target code that `targets()` already used. Pan Behind captures its layer's own targets without the anchor (box points, edges while unrotated, path vertices) when the drag begins, and passes them to `viewer_tools::snap_with`. The active viewer now doesn't record the active comp while an `OpenComp` event is pending, so the routing sees the comp the locked viewer really shows and sends the new comp to an unlocked or new viewer.

title: VP9: frames never end in a byte that reads as a superframe marker (#161)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #161: VP9 WebM exports reported success but some frames couldn't be decoded.

**Cause:** a frame whose last byte happened to match the superframe marker pattern (`0b110xxxxx`, Annex B) was taken by decoders for a superframe with an index at its end. ffmpeg rejected it ("Invalid le value at frame_sizes[i]"), libvpx reported a corrupt frame, and later frames lost their reference. In the reporter's file, exactly the 3 frames that failed (10, 22, 24) ended in `0xc8`, `0xc0` and `0xca`.

**Fix:** such frames get a zero byte after the last tile. The last tile's bool-coded data may end in zero padding (§9.2.3), so the frame decodes the same.

**Tests:** `frames_never_end_in_a_superframe_marker` (effectcraft-export, `vp9_roundtrip.rs`) encodes sequences until a frame needs the padding. It checks that no frame ends in a marker byte, and that the padded frames decode exactly with FilmCraft's VP9 decoder and with ffmpeg, with ffmpeg's error log empty. Before the fix it failed with "96x64 q40 frame 22 ends in 0xde". The ffmpeg IVF oracle is now a helper shared with the existing inter-frame test.

**Checked with the reporter's exact steps:** ffprobe reads 60/60 frames, and ffmpeg's `vp9` and `libvpx-vp9` decoders report no errors, for both RGB and RGB + Alpha (before: 57 frames and 11 / 6 error lines).

**Gate:** fmt, clippy `-D warnings` (release, all targets) for effectcraft-vp9enc and effectcraft-export, and their tests.

title: Media: conformed audio keeps its sound past 12:36 (#172)

body:
Fixes #172: preview audio went silent about 12:36 into long audio/video files.

**Cause:** conforming a footage file's audio (the cache preview playback reads, under Settings ▸ Disk ▸ Conformed Audio Folder) timed each 65,536-frame chunk as `frame index × ticks per second / rate` in `i64`. That overflows past 36,310,516 frames: 12:36.47 at 48 kHz, or 25:13 at 24 kHz, which is why the reporter's workaround helped. Chunks after the overflow decoded at a wrapped, negative time and came out silent. Sound therefore stopped at 12:37.76, the end of the last chunk that started in time, exactly where the reporter's cached file goes quiet.

**Fix:**
- Chunk times come from `Tick::from_units` (exact, 128-bit), through a small `sample_time` helper.
- The conformed files' names now include a format version, so caches written by earlier builds are ignored and conformed again. As the reporter pointed out, the broken files would otherwise stick around.

**Tests:** `conform_chunks_keep_their_times_on_long_files` checks every chunk start of a 2-hour file at 24, 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz. It failed before with a multiply overflow.

**Checked end to end:** a 13-minute file conformed at 48 kHz through `MediaPool` has sound at 760 s and 790 s.

**Gate:** fmt, clippy `-D warnings` (release, all targets) and the tests of effectcraft-media.

title: Window: saved workspaces are listed in Window ▸ Workspace (#191)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #191: a workspace saved with Save as New Workspace didn't appear in Window ▸ Workspace, so it couldn't be chosen.

**Cause (two parts):**
- The Workspace submenu was a fixed list of the built-in workspaces. Saving stored the layout, and `window.workspace {"name": …}` could switch to it, but no menu entry was ever made for it.
- The in-window submenu was too short anyway. egui lays out a new submenu in its default 400 pt area, and the scroll area inside took that height and kept it, so Window ▸ Workspace (514 pt tall) opened with its last rows (Undocked Panels, Reset to Saved Layout, Save Changes…, Save as New…, Edit Workspaces…) scrolled out of view. A saved workspace listed there would have been hidden too.

**Fix:**
- A `savedWorkspaces` dynamic node after the built-in workspaces (`DynCtx` carries the saved names). It is in both the in-window and the native (macOS) menus, and the current workspace gets a check mark like the built-ins (dynamic entries now go through `entry_checked`).
- Submenus open at their full height (`min_scrolled_height` = window height − 40) and scroll only when they are taller than the window, as Blending Mode and the effect categories already did.

**Tests:**
- `saved_workspace_is_listed_in_the_workspace_menu`: saves "My Layout", switches to Default, opens Window ▸ Workspace from the menu bar, clicks "My Layout", and gets its layout back. It failed before both parts of the fix: first with no entry, then with the entry unclickable below the 388 pt fold.
- `saved_workspaces_are_in_the_native_workspace_menu`: the native menu lists it, checked only while it is current.

**Not in this PR:** saved workspaces live in memory only, so they are gone after a restart (the current layout isn't saved on exit either). That is a separate feature: persisting them through the settings store.

**Gate:** `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-engine -p effectcraft-ui-egui -p effectcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`; `cargo xtask layers`; test…

title: Render Queue: clicking the Output To file name opens a save dialog (#192)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #192: clicking the Render Queue's Output To path didn't let you choose where to save. It showed the file-name template instead.

**Test:** `clicking_the_output_file_name_opens_the_save_dialog` (egui_kittest) installs a recording save hook, clicks the file name, and checks the dialog was asked for the resolved output path with the `mp4` extension and that the chosen path became the output. title: Fix NVIDIA Dust & Scratches threshold rounding
author: jonassneu
body:
Dust & Scratches can keep a pixel on NVIDIA Vulkan that the CPU replaces. On the RTX 4070 Ti, the median alpha `154 / 511` rounded to `0x3e9a4d26` instead of the CPU's `0x3e9a4d27`, even with the shader's residual correction. That one-ulp error changes the candidate colour enough to flip the strict threshold decision. It reproduces in `dust_threshold_on_quantized_input` and `medians` on upstream `3af4649`.

Upload the 512 CPU-rounded median levels as a 2 KiB lookup buffer and read them in both the bisection and sliding-histogram kernels. This preserves CPU behavior and the strict `>` threshold, with no additional rendering pass. Add regression coverage for every median level in both kernels, the NVIDIA failing pixel, and exact/adjacent threshold boundaries.

This is a separate GPU rendering fix from right-click PR #210.

Validation:

- All 193 GPU tests pass on **NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Ti / Vulkan**, with the adapter explicitly logged and no skipped GPU comparisons.
- All 15 noise-family tests also pass with the default release profile.
- Full `cargo xtask ci` passes formatting, strict workspace Clippy, workspace release tests, layering, asset attribution, and all 32 WASM crate checks with:

```sh
CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG=0 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false \
CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16 WGPU_BACKEND=vulkan cargo xtask ci
```

Before/after: actual GPU readbacks of the procedural seed-7 regression frame, with the affected pixel boxed and magnified. The fixed 70×44 frame equals the CPU reference bit-for-bit in all 3,080 pixels. The image is original project content with an attribution sidecar.

title: Puppet: dragging pins keeps the layer under the Puppet cached (#212)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #212: dragging Puppet pins lagged.

**Cause:** on every pointer move the mesh overlay asks for the Puppet's input: the layer's source, masks and the effects before the Puppet. It does that on the UI thread, at full size, and deep-copies the result. That input should come from the layer cache, but the input's cache key hashed *all* of the layer's effects, the Puppet's pins included. So each pin move changed the key of the Puppet's own input and re-rendered it.

**Fix:**
- `cache::input_key` covers only the effects that run before the given one, so the input stays cached while pins move. This also helps the Time effects that read a layer's input.
- `puppet_eval` returns the cached buffer (`Arc`) instead of a deep copy.

Measured with a throwaway test (not committed) on a 1000 × 800 layer: the mesh comes from its cache in about 2–3 ms; the ARAP solve takes 17–36 ms and the rasteriser about 12 ms. Those two remain. Loosening the CG tolerance barely changed the solve time, so I left the numerics alone. A cached factorisation of the solve would be the next step if dragging still feels slow.

**Test:** `input_keys_ignore_later_effects`. Editing a later effect keeps the input key; editing an earlier one changes it.

**Not checked:** I didn't drag pins in the live app.

**Gate:** `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -D warnings` on the touched crates (all targets); tests: render lib (181), engine lib (406), effects lib (413).

author: bflatastic
body:
Three browser-build reports from @Jagalite, one commit per issue. Each report pointed at the right code.

| Issue | Fix |
|---|---|
| #218 | Every write of a stored file gets a version. Job workers remember the version they were sent instead of the byte length, so footage replaced by different bytes of the same length at the same path is sent to a reused worker again. Frame workers had the same gap in a stronger form: they remembered paths only, so they never got a replaced file at all. They now track versions too. |
| #216 | `worker.js` re-raises a rejected start (its async init) outside the promise, as it already does for other worker failures, so the page's `onerror` sees it. Before, nothing reached the page and the job waited for "ready" forever. The job now fails with the error and `host.js` terminates the worker. |
| #215 | A failed browser-storage write stays pending and is retried after 2 s, with the delay doubling up to a minute while it keeps failing. A newer change of the same key goes along with the retry. `effectcraft.flush()` rejects with the error instead of resolving. Before, the write was dropped, flush resolved, and a reload restored the project from before the change. docs/web.md says so. |

**Tests**
- Store (native): `versions_change_with_every_write` (#218) and `failed_writes_retry` (#215).
- `apps/effectcraft-web/tests/workers.mjs`: new, Node only, no build needed, documented in docs/web.md. With a fake `Worker` it loads the real `host.js`, and checks that an equal-length replacement is sent to a reused worker once and an unchanged file is not resent (#218), and that a worker whose start fails fails its job and is terminated (#216). It also loads the real `worker.js` with a stub module whose init rejects, and checks that the failure is raised where a Worker `error` event sees it, not left as an unhandled rejection. title: Fix variable-font animator test axis selection and endpoint delta
author: ulanch
body:
The variable_font_axes_animator test can fail on an installed variable font even when axis animation works. It finds a nonconstant axis but creates the animator using the first listed axis, which may be constant. It also always applies a positive full-range delta, so a font whose default is already the maximum cannot move.

On macOS with SF Compact Black Italic, the selected face reports opsz=[19,19,19] and wght=[1,1000,1000] (minimum, default, maximum). The test identifies wght but animates opsz, leaving the outline unchanged. Selecting wght alone would still leave the positive delta clamped at its default maximum.

Use the identified axis tag, animate from its default toward the more distant endpoint, and clamp the expected advance calculation at both bounds. This changes only the test; the outline, advance and undo assertions remain in place.

Validation:
- Before the patch, variable_font_axes_animator fails on this machine with unchanged outline area 2191.5321350097656.
- After the patch, the same test passes:

  Result: 1 passed, 0 failed, 407 filtered out.
- cargo fmt --all --check passes.
- git diff --check passes.

Tested against 172b7cfcc0f15eabb4908a6033e43aca7b1e918d on aarch64 macOS 27.2 (26B5091g), rustc 1.98.0 (88d9e12ae), LLVM 22.1.8. The targeted passing run is from the investigation; the patch has not changed since that run. cargo xtask ci was attempted: formatting and strict release-mode Clippy passed, but the full release workspace test build was stopped after approximately 20 minutes of compilation, before tests ran. title: Effects: Turbulent Displace displaces the whole layer, not one quadrant (#227)
author: bflatastic
body:
Part of #227: on a shape layer, Turbulent Displace at default settings only moved the bottom-right quadrant of the shape. Wave Warp (Pinning) and Bulge (Pin All Edges) had the same problem.

**Cause:** Edge pinning holds the layer bounds still. For shape and text layers the bounds are comp-sized, but they started at the layer's origin, and a shape layer's content sits around its origin (anchor 0,0). Anything left of or above the origin counted as outside the layer and was pinned, so with Turbulent Displace's default Pin All only the bottom-right quadrant moved. Measured on a 180×80 rectangle centred in a 200×100 comp (alpha change per comp quadrant TL/TR/BL/BR): Turbulent Displace `[0, 0, 0, 824]`, Wave Warp with All Edges `[0, 0, 0, 251]`.

**Fix:** The renderer now passes the bounds' top-left in layer coordinates, `EffectEnv::bounds_origin`: (−w/2, −h/2) for layers without a source rectangle (shape, text) and (0, 0) otherwise. The new `util::pin_rect` places the bounds there. Turbulent Displace, Wave Warp and Bulge use it on the CPU and in their GPU kernels' parameters, and it is part of the GPU chain cache key. After the fix: Turbulent Displace `[1889, 1261, 760, 838]`, Wave Warp `[106, 113, 106, 114]`. I also checked a headless snapshot of the app: an ellipse shape layer with default Turbulent Displace now wobbles on all sides.

**Test:** `effectcraft-render` `edge_pinning_displaces_all_of_a_centred_shape_layer` (fails before the fix with three quadrants unchanged) and `effectcraft-gpu` `edge_pinning_on_a_shape_layer` (GPU vs CPU on a shape layer for all three effects; it fails if the GPU path ignores the new bounds).

**Not checked:**
- Effect point parameters on shape and text layers are unchanged. They are still measured from the layer origin, so defaults at "layer centre" (Twirl, Bulge, CC Lens and Ripple centres, Turbulent's Offset handle) land at the comp's bottom-right corner for a default shape layer. author: bflatastic
body:
Three reports from @Jagalite, one commit per issue.

| Issue | Fix |
|---|---|
| #231 | The Project panel's vertical scroll bar clamped its thumb between 16 points and the track's height. A track shorter than 16 points (an empty project at 1280 × 800 with device pixel ratio 2, i.e. 640 × 400 points) made that clamp panic on the first frame: the canvas went blank and the command channel stopped. The thumb is now at most the track's length, and both Project scroll bars use the same calculation. It affected every platform, not only the browser. |
| #226 | Add Files… / Upload Folder… read the picked files in one go and rejected on the first unreadable one. The Media Browser dropped the rejection, so nothing was added and nothing said why. Cancelling the picker reports nothing. |

The page now covers the canvas with a notice that offers **Save Project** (a download) and **Reload**. Reload first writes pending changes to browser storage (`effectcraft.flush()`), so the session snapshot brings the project and its unsaved changes back. If that write fails, the notice says so and offers **Reload Anyway**. Without a kept session (`?empty`, memory storage) it says to save first. |

title: Viewer: a press on a selected layer behind others acts on it (#230)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #230: a press in the Composition panel always acted on the topmost layer under the pointer, even when a selected layer was under it too.

**Before:** select a layer that another layer covers, then press on it in the viewer. The press selected the layer in front, so the selected one couldn't be dragged there.

**Now:** as in After Effects, a selected layer under the pointer comes before the layers in front of it. It stays selected and a drag moves it. With no selected layer under the pointer, the topmost layer is picked as before. Shift still toggles the topmost layer. The same rule applies to Rotate, Pan Behind and the right-click menu's selection, which all go through `pick`.

`layers_at` (selectable layers under a point, front to back) now backs `layer_at`, `pick` and the context menu's list of layers under the pointer. Before, that list repeated the hit test inline. `pick` computes each layer's quad once per press.

**Test:** `ui_viewer` `viewer_press_prefers_a_selected_layer_under_the_pointer`. With the back layer selected, a click keeps it selected, and a drag moves it while the front layer stays put. After Deselect All, a click picks the front layer. It fails on main: the click selects the front layer.

**Not checked:** not compared against a running After Effects.

**Gate:** `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`; `ui_viewer` (31 tests).

author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #229: the interface language didn't follow the system language.

**Change:** Settings ▸ General ▸ Language has a new **Match System** choice (`general.language` = `system`), and it is now the default. It uses the operating system's interface language where EffectCraft has a translation, and English otherwise. title: Logging: RUST_LOG prints to stderr, and start-up logs its milestones (#234)
author: bflatastic
body:
For #234 (macOS 27 on Apple Silicon: the app exits after about 10 s without ever showing a window). This doesn't fix it. It makes start-up diagnosable, because the reporter ran with `RUST_LOG=debug RUST_BACKTRACE=1` and got no output at all. I can't reproduce the bug here (Windows).

**Cause of the silence:** the engine's logger (`effectcraft_engine::logging`) kept warnings in memory and wrote to a file only after Help ▸ Enable Logging. It ignored `RUST_LOG`, so eframe, winit and wgpu messages and our own were never printed.

**Change**
- `RUST_LOG` is read the way env_logger reads it: a level, `target=level`, or a bare target. What it lets through also goes to stderr. The maximum log level is raised only when `RUST_LOG` asks for more than `info`. Without it nothing changes.
- The desktop app logs its start-up milestones at `info`: opening the window, the graphics adapter (`AdapterInfo`), the app created, the first frame drawn, the window being asked to close (from any source), and the window closed. The last two show whether the 10 s exit is a close request or something else.

Example run here with `RUST_LOG=info,wgpu_core=warn,wgpu_hal=warn,naga=warn`:
```text
INFO  effectcraft: effectcraft 0.4.0: opening the window
INFO  egui_wgpu: There are 7 available wgpu adapters: …
INFO  effectcraft: graphics: AdapterInfo { name: "NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090", … }
INFO  effectcraft: app created; the window shows after its first frame
INFO  effectcraft_ui_egui: GPU compositor: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (Vulkan)
INFO  effectcraft: first frame drawn
INFO  effectcraft: the window closed
```

**Test:** `logging` `rust_log_filters_by_level_and_target` (levels, per-target levels with the longest prefix winning, bare targets, unknown levels skipped). I also ran the app as above and quit it over the control channel.

**Not checked:** macOS. Windows release builds have no console, so stderr shows nothing there, as before.

author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #232: `sim_effects_golden_hashes` fails on macOS 27.2 (rustc 1.98) for 1 of its 404 cases, `ec.sim.ccmrmercury/1/32bpc/t2.2`. The hash there is `0x3823bd73a3cdab0d`, pinned `0x2fc62cc580704437`.

- All other cases stay exact, and a variant passes only for its own case.
- The comparison moved into `mismatches`, so it can be tested on every platform.
- The module docs and docs/testing.md describe how to tell a libm difference from a code change: compare `SIM_GOLDEN_OUT` frames with the pinning commit.

I didn't re-pin the case to the new hash, because that would break the gate on macOS 26.

title: App: a launch whose window never drew makes the next use OpenGL (#243)
author: bflatastic
body:
Fixes #243 (Intel UHD 600, Windows 10: the process appears for a second and disappears, with no message). The same thing was reported on #198 after its fix: an Intel UHD with 2020 drivers exited with code 0xC0000005, and only `WGPU_BACKEND=gl` helped.

**Cause:** an access violation inside the graphics driver as the window's DirectX 12 or Vulkan device is created. A crash in a driver can't be caught, so no error handling of ours could show a message. #198's fix (adapter limits, after 0.4.0) only covers a device that fails cleanly.

**Fix**

| | |
|---|---|
| Launch guard (`apps/effectcraft/src/launch_guard.rs`) | Each launch leaves a `launch-pending` marker in the settings folder until its window has drawn a frame. A launch that finds the previous one's marker switches **Settings ▸ Startup & Repair ▸ Window Graphics** to OpenGL, saves it and says so in the status bar. A window that fails to open cleanly says the next launch will try OpenGL. `WGPU_BACKEND` still wins. macOS has no OpenGL backend, so it never switches there. |
| Window Graphics | A new Startup & Repair setting: Automatic / OpenGL (compatibility), `startup.windowGraphics` = `auto` / `gl`. It applies from the next launch and is documented in docs/preferences.md. Validating it shares one choice check with Language. |
| GPU compositor | It now declines OpenGL adapters at once, as it already declines adapters without compute shaders. On OpenGL it used to translate its kernels for **22 s** (on an RTX 4090) before one failed validation, all before the first frame, and a Celeron would take far longer. |

**Tests**
- `a_launch_that_never_drew_switches_the_next_to_opengl` (app): a launch that draws changes nothing, one that never draws makes the next use OpenGL with the notice, it stays without repeating the notice, and `WGPU_BACKEND` wins.

title: feat(aep): Initial native After Effects (.aep / .aepx) project decoder and import (Early Stage) (#190)
author: PlayzAe
body:
### Summary
Adds an early-stage, native Rust decoder and importer for Adobe After Effects binary (`.aep`, RIFX `Egg!`) and XML (`.aepx`) project files, addressing #190, #248, and `docs/gaps.md` (G4). 

> ⚠️ **Status: Early Stage / Foundational**  
> This implementation provides an initial in-engine parsing and comp reconstruction foundation. It is **in early stages and not yet perfect**: complex nested shape hierarchies, custom effect plugins, certain keyframe interpolation styles, and advanced expressions will still have render/layer fidelity differences or omissions compared to native After Effects.

---

### Motivation & Context (Native In-App Workaround vs External Tools)
In #248 and `docs/gaps.md` (G4), external Python tools like `py-aep` were discussed. As noted by maintainers, running Python as an external converter breaks the pure Rust, single-binary distribution model of EffectCraft.

We found a viable workaround: **building the parser directly inside EffectCraft in pure Rust**. This keeps everything inside the app without requiring users to install Python, run external converter CLI scripts, or depend on non-Rust runtimes.

---

### What Works Today
- **Pure Rust In-App Binary RIFX Chunk Parsing (`crates/engine/src/aep.rs`)**:
  - Traverses the `Egg!` chunk tree (`LIST`, `head`, `btdk`, `utf8`, `pins`, etc.) entirely in memory inside EffectCraft.
  - Extracts project hierarchies, compositions, and footage references without any external CLI or sub-processes.
- **XML `.aepx` Support**:
  - Basic XML parsing for text-based After Effects project files.
- **Composition & Layer Reconstruction**:
  - Builds compositions, solid layers, text/camera layers, markers, and basic transform properties (position, scale, rotation, opacity, anchor point).
  - Handles basic precomp nesting and timeline durations.
- **Missing Asset Detection & Relinking**:

title: Timeline: a selected key selects its property and layer (#252)
author: bflatastic
body:
Part of #252: "When highlighting keyframes their parent property isn't selected on the layer… nothing shows in the graph editor until you select the property separately."

**Cause:** the Timeline's key click and marquee called `keys.select` with the keys only. The Graph Editor shows the selected properties (Show Selected Properties) or else the animated properties of the selected layers. With neither selected, it showed nothing.

**Fix:** `keys.select` takes `selectProperties`. The selected keys' properties and layers are then selected too: they replace the current selection, or with Shift (add/toggle) are added to it. The Timeline's click, Shift-click and marquee pass it, as After Effects highlights a clicked key's property and layer. The Graph Editor's own key clicks don't, so selecting keys there doesn't narrow what it shows. Delete, Copy and the other key commands still act on the keys first.

**Test:** `ui_keyframes` `a_key_clicked_in_the_timeline_shows_in_the_graph_editor`. With nothing selected, it clicks a key in the Timeline, checks that its property and layer are selected, opens the Graph Editor and finds the key there. It fails on main: `left: ([], [])`.

**Not checked:** not compared against a running After Effects.

**Gate:** `cargo fmt --check`; `cargo clippy -D warnings` for effectcraft-engine and effectcraft-ui-egui (all targets). Tests: engine lib (413), `ui_keyframes` (7), `ui_viewer` (35), `ui_timeline_shapes`, `ui_workflow_selection`, `ui_timeline_zoom` and `ui_timeline_switches`.
