title: #882: pixel-exact Composition viewer at 100 % and above
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #882.

## Problem (reported on Discord)
Arashi (Windows 10, anime footage with aliased lines): the Composition viewer looks antialiased/blurred even at Full resolution, so the viewer doesn't match the render.

## Root cause
1. The frame's screen rect was centred in the panel without snapping to physical pixels, so at 100 % each screen pixel sampled between two frame pixels and the bilinear sampler blended them. This happens at any display scaling and is worst at 125 %/150 %.
2. Viewer Zoom Quality "More Accurate" also used bilinear filtering for magnification (`zoom_texture_options` / `zoom_sampler`), so 200 %+ and lower resolutions were smoothed instead of shown as pixel blocks.
3. View ▸ Zoom In / Zoom Out (`.` / `,`) stepped through magnifications in points, so at 125 % display scaling they jumped over 100 %.

## Fix
- The frame origin snaps to the physical pixel grid. `ViewerMap` carries the snapped origin, so overlays and hit-testing stay aligned with the frame.
- Magnification is nearest-neighbour in both Zoom Quality modes, for CPU texture options and the GPU frame sampler. More Accurate keeps the averaged (mipmapped/box) minification below 100 % from #417. The snapshot texture uses the same options.
- Zoom In / Zoom Out step through magnifications measured in screen pixels (…, 66 %, 100 %, 150 %, …), as the magnification menu already did.
- `docs/preferences.md` updated.

title: Plug-ins: external effect helpers (safe, out-of-process native effects) + plug-in API 2
author: glumbis
body:
## Why

This answers the review of #508. Native plug-in code (OpenFX and the like) should not run inside
EffectCraft: it needs `unsafe`, and one crash in a third-party plug-in loses the user's work.
This PR adds no OpenFX code and no `unsafe`, and loads nothing native. Instead it gives
EffectCraft a small, generic, versioned way to use effects served by **separate helper
programs**. If a helper crashes, it takes only itself down.

Decision record: `docs/adr/0001-external-effect-helpers.md`. Protocol and usage:
`docs/external-helpers.md`.

## Why this is safe to merge into `main`

The concern in #508 was that native plug-ins compromise EffectCraft's safety. This PR addresses that by design, not just by testing:

- **No native code ever runs inside EffectCraft.** `crates/helper-host` is `unsafe_code = "forbid"`, links no plug-in libraries and calls no FFI. EffectCraft's process stays 100% safe Rust. Memory bugs in third-party code cannot corrupt EffectCraft's memory, because that code lives in a different process.
- **A crashing plug-in cannot lose the user's work.** A helper that crashes, hangs or sends garbage is stopped. The render fails with a visible message, the frame is left as it was and the project keeps running. The helper restarts on the next render. Plug-ins that keep failing are turned off automatically by the block list and the restart limit.
- **The protocol is small and validated.** It uses JSON lines plus a frame exchange file. Everything a helper sends back is parsed and checked like any other untrusted input, and anything that doesn't fit the protocol is a protocol error rather than undefined behaviour. Stray plug-in output on stdout is ignored.
- **Users stay in control.** No helper runs unless the user asks: Effect ▸ Scan for Effect Helpers starts them, and starting them at launch is an explicit opt-in (`EFFECTCRAFT_HELPERS=1`, an environment variable rather than a setting, so writing to the settings folder can't turn it on). Agents confined with …

title: Text: stop capturing keyboard input after clicking away (#831)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Closes #831.

After typing into a text layer, clicking somewhere else, such as a solid in the Timeline, didn't stop the editing. Typed characters still went into the text, and **Space added a space instead of starting playback**.

## Cause
Two things kept the keyboard in the text:
- The edit only ended on clicks inside the Composition viewer. A click in another panel left it open.
- egui does drop the editor's focus when you click elsewhere. But the viewer took it back on the next frame "whenever nothing else holds it", which is right after any click that doesn't focus a widget (a Timeline row, say).

## Fix
- **Clicking another panel ends the edit.** Every click in a panel already sends `DockAction::Focus`. When it's for a panel other than the viewers and the panels that format the selected characters (Character, Paragraph, Properties), it now:
  - runs `text.endEdit`, so the text is kept and an empty layer the Type tool started is removed
  - surrenders the viewer's text focus, so typing and shortcuts go back to the app
- **A press on another tab waits for that tab's click** (second commit). A press anywhere in a panel group used to focus the group's *shown* panel, even when the press was on another of its tabs. So opening Properties or Character behind Effects & Presets (as in Undocked Panels) ended the edit on the press. After that, formatting went to the whole layer instead of the selected characters, and an empty Type-tool layer was removed.
- **Keys after a click away in the same frame aren't typed** (second commit). The click away is only resolved after the frame's panels. The text keyboard handler now takes that frame's keys in order and stops at a press outside the viewer:
  - keys before the click are typed into the text
  - keys after it in that frame are neither typed nor run as shortcuts
  - from the next frame, keys are the app's again

title: #878: context menus act on the whole selection
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #878.

## Problem
Reported on Discord by Arashi (Windows 10): with two layers selected, picking **Pre-compose…** or **Delete** from the right-click menu acted on only one layer, because the menu deselected the other. The keyboard shortcuts worked.

## Root cause
`timeline::layer_context_menu` always called `layer_menu` with `&[layer.id]`, the right-clicked layer only. Every menu item first sends `layer.select` with that list, so the rest of the selection was dropped before the command ran. This affected both the layer name rows and the layer bars. Right-clicking an unselected layer also left the old selection in place until a menu item was chosen.

In the Project panel, **Move to Project Root** moved only `[id]`, while Delete and Label already used the selection. The Composition viewer was already correct.

## Fix
- Timeline rows and bars: if the right-clicked layer is part of the selection, the menu targets every selected layer (in comp order). Right-clicking an unselected, unlocked layer selects only that layer. This matches After Effects.
- Project panel: Move to Project Root uses the same `targets()` as Delete and Label.

## Tests
New tests in `crates/ui-egui/tests/ui_workflow_selection.rs`. Both fail without the fix:
- `timeline_context_menu_acts_on_the_whole_selection`: Delete from a selected row removes both layers, and Duplicate from a selected bar duplicates both. Right-clicking an unselected row selects only that row.
- `project_context_move_to_root_acts_on_the_whole_selection`

## Gates
- `cargo fmt --check`: ok
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`: ok

- `cargo xtask layers`: ok

title: Scripting: text range selectors resolve by match name and limit the animator (#837)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #837.

The issue reports two problems. This PR fixes both.

**1. `ADBE Text Percent Start/End/Offset` returned null.** `matchnames::node` had no entries below `ADBE Text Selectors`, so the selector's match name was its internal id (`rangeSelector`) and its properties had no After Effects names. I added two tables next to `TEXT_ANIMATOR`:
- selectors: `ADBE Text Selector` (range), `ADBE Text Wiggly Selector`, `ADBE Text Expressible Selector`. These are the same names `resolve_add` already accepts for `addProperty`.
- Range Selector properties: `ADBE Text Percent Start`, `ADBE Text Percent End`, `ADBE Text Percent Offset`.

**2. The scripted selector did not limit the animator.** The renderer is fine. `addProperty("ADBE Text Animator")` calls `layer.addTextAnimator` with `properties: []`, and `build::text_animator` always adds a default "Range Selector 1" (0-100%). The script's `addProperty("ADBE Text Selector")` then added a second selector, "Range Selector 2". The script set Start on that one, but the default selector still selected every character, so the animator hit all of them. In After Effects, a scripted animator has no selectors until the script adds one. The empty-animator path (`properties: []`, used only by scripting) now clears the default selector. Animators added from the UI or with named properties keep "Range Selector 1" as before.

**Tests**
- `matchnames::tests::text_range_selector_names`: the selector and Start/End/Offset map to their AE match names.
- `tests::scripted_text_range_selector_resolves_and_is_the_only_selector`: runs the issue's script end to end. It checks that the animator has exactly one selector, that Start is set to 50 through `ADBE Text Percent Start`, and that End and Offset resolve by match name. Without the fix, the script fails on the null property, and `numProperties` would be 2.

title: Export: stream frames through a shared CPU/GPU work queue, convert to YUV 4:2:0 on the GPU, and tune to the hardware
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Closes #897. This branch merges cleanly onto current main and does not depend on #688. It works with or without #688; with #688 (GPU-resident effect stacks, texture reuse) it gets most of the 4K gain measured below. `GpuContext::set_upload_budget` (default unchanged) is also added by #688. Its code here (the `upload_budget` field and initialiser, `set_upload_budget`/`upload_budget`, and the budget check and one-time "upload cache full" warning in `upload_buf`) is written line for line as in #688, so git applies it once in either merge order. Merging #688 into this branch, or this branch into #688, both on top of main, gives the same tree with no conflicts and no duplicate field.

On the test PC (RTX 3090), a 3 s 4K comp exports with `--gpu` in 49.7 s instead of 201.9 s on main (median of 3 runs each).

## What this PR does

- **Streaming scheduler** (`crates/export/src/stream.rs`, `pipeline.rs`). Main sends a batch of up to 16 frames to the GPU at once. This PR has `gpu-frames` GPU workers and adaptive CPU workers claim frames from a shared queue, and a bounded reorder buffer feeds the in-order encoder. A CPU worker is added only while measured throughput improves and never when a CPU frame is slow enough to stall the encoder. Every GPU decline is logged with its reason.
- **GPU YUV 4:2:0 and async readback** (`crates/gpu/src/yuv.rs`, `shaders/yuv.wgsl`). A compute kernel does the export's `to_rgba8_over` and `rgba_to_yuv420`, so a 4K frame reads back 12 MB instead of 133 MB of RGBA f32. The copy goes through the context's bounded readbacks and an 8-buffer staging ring, and the GPU worker records the next frame while it runs. H.264 only; other formats take RGBA as before.
- **Hardware-adaptive tuning** (`crates/export/src/tuning.rs`, `hw.rs`, `TUNING.md`). Each option resolves independently: CLI, then `EFFECTCRAFT_EXPORT_<OPTION>`, then a `--tuning-config` file, then auto. Auto reads VRAM, vendor, unified memory, core kinds and RAM, and `render --print-tuning` print…

title: #903: downmix 5.1 and other multichannel audio to stereo
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #903.

## Problem (reported on Discord)
Reported by Risll while investigating a clipping report (no clipping reproduced). Footage audio kept only its first two channels, so the centre (dialogue), LFE and surrounds of 5.1 files were dropped and the level came out far below a proper downmix. AAC 5.1 was worse: FilmCraft's AAC-LC decoder delivers AAC's native order (C L R Ls Rs LFE), so left was the centre and front-right was lost.

## Root cause
`read_stereo` in `crates/media/src/pool.rs` used `channels[0]`/`channels[1]` regardless of layout. Preview, waveform and export mixdown all read through `MediaPool::audio_samples`, so there is one place to fix.

## Fix
New `crates/media/src/downmix.rs`: ITU-R BS.775 matrix (L = FL + 0.707 FC + 0.707 Ls, R likewise; back-centre at 0.5 on both sides), LFE excluded (ffmpeg/swresample default; Adobe docs not found stating it), scaled by one fixed gain, the reciprocal of the largest row sum (5.1: 1/2.414, 7.1: 1/3.12), as swresample does for integer output, so full scale cannot clip. Orders by channel count: WAVE/SMPTE (what FilmCraft's AC-3/PCM/FLAC/Opus deliver) and AAC's native order. More than 8 channels: front pair only, 0 channels: silence. Mono (duplicated at unity) and stereo unchanged; I did not change mono because I could not confirm Adobe's mono behaviour.

## Tests
- `crates/media/tests/downmix.rs`: ffmpeg-made 5.1 (AAC, AC-3, WAV, FLAC), 7.1 (WAV, FLAC), 5.0 and quad, one sine per channel; each channel asserted at its expected gain per side; overall RMS within 1 dB and peak within 1.5 dB of `ffmpeg -ac 2` (16-bit output, where swresample normalises); loud 5.1 does not clip; mono/stereo unchanged; 3, 4, 7, 9, 12, 16 channel files do not panic.
- Unit tests in `downmix.rs` for the matrix, orders, 0..40 channel counts, ragged input.
- `flac_audio_of_any_shape_reads_in_device_blocks` expected the old front-pair-only level for its 6 and 8 channel files; it now expects the downmix level.

title: Shape layers: always rasterise at the on-screen scale (#751)
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
Fixes #751

A shape layer scaled up rendered soft unless Collapse Transformations / Continuously Rasterize was on: `Renderer::raster_scale` only used the layer's on-screen scale for shape layers with that switch, so otherwise the contents were drawn at 100% and the bitmap was enlarged. In After Effects shape layers are always continuously rasterised, and text layers here already are (#390, #194).

The fix makes shape layers take the same path as text: `raster_scale` returns the output scale times the layer's effective 2D scale (own transform and parent chain, quarter-octave steps, capped at 64x and about 16 Mpx of buffer) whether or not the switch is on. Effects, masks and layer styles already work on the scaled buffer through `Buf::scale`, so they behave as before, just at the higher resolution. The renderer no longer looks at the switch for shape layers; it's still stored and shown, it just doesn't change the output.

Tests in `crates/render/src/tests_collapse.rs`:
- `shape_scaled_up_stays_sharp_without_the_switch` replaces the old test that asserted the soft result with the switch off. It scales a 10 px square 800% by its own Scale and by a parent null, switch on and off, and checks the edge is at most 1 px wide. Before the fix it failed with an 8 px edge.
- `effects_on_a_scaled_shape_follow_its_scale` checks a 10 px square at 800% with a 2 px Gaussian blur matches an 80 px square at 100% with a 16 px blur (max difference 0.11 before the fix, under 0.05 after).

Text layers don't have this problem on main; they were fixed by #390.

With the issue's CLI steps (native 60 px rect at 470%, switch off) the left edge now reads `48, 210`, the same as the issue's "collapse on" numbers.

Not covered: the raster scale is measured from the 2D layer-to-comp matrix, so a 3D shape layer pushed towards the camera isn't scaled up for the camera's projection (same as text today). I didn't look at the app by hand. `cargo xtask ci` can't build the whole workspace here (alsa-sys nee…

title: UI: draw concave icons as convex pieces (fixes Selection arrow, Speaker, Sparkle glyphs)
author: pravdomil
body:
## Problem
The Selection tool's arrow glyph in the toolbar rendered broken. Its outline is concave (a notch each side of the tail), but `Pen16::fill` sends every icon through egui's `convex_polygon`, which only tessellates convex outlines and fans slivers across the notches. The Speaker and Sparkle glyphs are concave too.

## Fix
In `crates/ui-egui/src/icons.rs` the three concave glyphs are drawn as hand-split convex pieces (`SELECTION_ARROW`, `SPEAKER`, `SPARKLE`):
- pieces overlap rather than abut, so the antialiased edges leave no seam;
- only one wide piece reaches the arrow's tip, so it does not antialias into a spike.

`Pen16::fill` itself is unchanged, and now documents that it takes convex outlines only.

## Testing
- New regression test `concave_glyphs_are_filled_as_convex_pieces` (every piece is convex).
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --lib icons` passes; checked all three glyphs in a headless `snapshot` render.

title: Desktop: write log records to standard error and a rotating log file
author: itrycodinganditsbad
body:
EffectCraft already had a logger, but by default it only kept warnings in memory for the System Compatibility Report. Standard error got records only when `RUST_LOG` was set, and a file only after Help > Enable Logging. A launch from the Dock, the Start menu or a launcher has no terminal, so the start-up milestones, GPU fallbacks and the panic report were gone by the time someone wanted to file an issue.

This ports the fix from the sibling apps (storytold/pdfcraft#239, storytold/photocraft#1143, storytold/wordcraft#17) into the existing `effectcraft_engine::logging` rather than adding a second logger:

- Records go to standard error and to `Logs/effectcraft.log` in the settings folder (`EFFECTCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` or the platform config directory). Each launch moves the previous log to `effectcraft.1.log` and that one to `.2`, so the log of a run that crashed survives the next start. The file stops at 16 MiB with one note.
- Default levels are `info` for `effectcraft*` targets and `warn` for everything else. `RUST_LOG` still replaces that, with the same parser as before.
- Records logged before the file is opened are buffered (up to 512) and written first. The file is opened after argument parsing, so `--version` leaves nothing behind.
- Lines now carry a UTC timestamp with milliseconds and the thread name, like the siblings, instead of Unix seconds. This applies to Enable Logging's file as well.
- Help > Reveal Logging File shows this run's log unless Enable Logging is on. Enable Logging still appends to `EffectCraft Log.txt` across launches.
- The remaining `eprintln!`s in the desktop app (control server, audio output, files from the command line, the start-up failure) now go through the logger.
- `docs/preferences.md` gets a short Logs section.

No new dependencies. Nothing panics: a directory that can't be used, or a failed write, leaves standard error as the only sink.

Tests: new unit tests in `logging.rs` cover the default filter, UTC timestamps (leap days, end …

title: Resume an open mask path when the Pen clicks its last vertex (#912)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #912.

Once a Pen path in progress ends (Esc / Enter, or switching to another tool and back, as in the issue's steps), the Pen forgot which path it was drawing. Clicking the path's endpoint then fell through to the "new path / add vertex on segment" branch and placed a new vertex on top of the endpoint instead of continuing.

Now, when no path is in progress, a Pen press within 8 px of an open path's last vertex makes that path the Pen's current path again, so the following clicks append vertices to it (and pressing its first vertex still closes it). The 8 px tolerance is the same one already used for closing on the first vertex. This works for masks and shape paths alike, since both already go through `mask.addVertex` once a path is current.

- `viewer_overlays.rs`: new `open_end_at(paths, map, pos, tol)` returns the open path whose last vertex is under the pointer (closed paths are ignored).
- `viewer.rs`: `pen_press` checks it before the motion-path / segment / new-path branches; the Pen comments are updated.

Resuming from the first vertex (continuing the path backwards) is not included: it would need the Pen to remember the drawing direction, which is a separate design choice.

Test: `pen_resumes_an_open_path_at_its_last_vertex` covers the last vertex (hit), the first vertex, a far point and a closed path (no hit).

title: Interpret Footage: apply the Loop (times) value sent as a float (#909)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #909.

The Interpret Footage dialog builds "Loop (times)" with `Field::num`, and `Form::params` sends every number field as an `f64` (`3.0`). `Interpretation::parse` read `loop` with `Value::as_u64`, which returns `None` for a float. The value was dropped, so the loop count stayed at 1.

`loop` is now read with `f_p` (`as_f64`), as `frameRate` and `pixelAspect` already are in the same function. The value is rounded and clamped to 1..9999 as before, and non-finite values are ignored. Interpret Proxy goes through the same parser, so it is fixed too. Integer JSON (`"loop": 3`) from scripts still works.

Test: `interpret_footage_loop_from_form_float` sends `{"loop": 3.0}` to `file.interpretFootage` and checks `loop_count == 3`. It fails on main, where the count stays at 1.

title: Cap text animator range selector Start, End and Offset (#908)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #908.

The Range Selector's Start and End were used as typed, so values like End 300% or Start -200% stretched the selection past the text. Offset was not limited either.

`range_params` in `crates/render/src/text.rs` now limits them when the selector is evaluated:

- Start and End: 0..100% (0..n characters/words/lines when Advanced ▸ Units is Index).
- Offset: -100..100% (-n..n in Index units).

The limit is applied where the selector is evaluated, so it covers every way a value gets there: typed values, keyframes, expressions, scripts and Lottie import. The stored value is not changed.

Test: `range_start_end_and_offset_are_capped` in `crates/render/src/text/tests.rs`. It sets End 300% with Offset -150%, then Start -200% with Offset 100%. With the limit nothing is selected. Without it every character is selected. (Once Start and End are within 0..100%, an Offset beyond ±100% already moves the range past every character, so limiting Offset makes no visible difference and the test cannot show it on its own.)

title: Release workflow: pass the Azure signing secrets
author: echelon
body:
Since this repo's `release.yml` moved to `storytold/craft-common-actions`, it has passed the Apple and `WINDOWS_CERTIFICATE*` secrets to the shared workflow, but not the six `AZURE_*` secrets that Azure Trusted Signing uses.

The shared workflow's signing jobs run in this repo's `release` environment and read the values from there, but only for names the caller lists. So the next release would have built **unsigned** Windows MSIs and portable zips, with only a warning. craft-launcher 0.3.1 did exactly this, and storytold/craft-launcher#174 fixed it with this same change.

This adds the six names. All twelve secrets are already set in this repo's `release` environment. storytold/craft-common-actions#3 makes release builds fail outright if signing secrets are missing, and fixes the riscv64 `--formats` call. This PR should land first.

`actionlint` passes.

title: Project panel: Replace with Precomposition (used N times)
author: Themolx
body:
> **Discord:** themolx (ArtCraft Discord) · long-time After Effects power user

Two Project panel features from After Effects that belong together: **Replace with Precomposition**, and the **"used N times"** count in the panel's header, which shows how many layers a precomposed item replaced.

## 1. Replace with Precomposition

Right-click a footage item or solid in the Project panel and choose **Replace with Precomposition (used N times)**, directly in the context menu, not in a submenu. The label shows how many layers will be switched. Agents and scripts can run it as `file.replaceWithPrecomp {item?}`.

For the selected footage or solid item it:
- creates a composition with the item's size, pixel aspect and frame rate, in the same Project folder, named `<item> Comp`;
- places the item in it as a single layer;
- switches **every layer in every composition** that used the item to the new composition, so the item is precomposed globally in one action.

Layers keep their timing, transforms, effects and masks. The original item stays in the project because the new comp uses it. Video and sequence footage set the comp's duration. Stills and solids get a comp as long as the longest layer that showed them. Adjustment layers keep their solid, since they only borrow it for size. The whole operation is one undo step.

How:
- `crates/engine/src/commands/app_more.rs`: `replace_with_precomp`, built like the existing `replace_with_layered_comp` and wrapped in `grouped(...)` so it's a single undo step. Uses `layer.addItem` for the inner layer.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/project.rs`: a top-level context-menu entry, labelled with the use count.
- `docs/footage.md`: documented.

author: Themolx

## Problem
With a layer soloed, moving the playhead outside that layer's in–out range made the viewer (and renders) show every other layer again, as if nothing were soloed.

## Why this is the right behaviour
- **After Effects:** solo is not time-dependent. While any layer is soloed, non-soloed layers are excluded at every time; outside the soloed layer's range you see only the background.

`any_solo` drops `l.is_active_at(t)` everywhere the rule appeared. The visibility filter still requires each drawn layer to be active, and hidden or locked soloed layers still activate solo as before.

title: Pen tool: hold S/L/D/I while closing a mask to set its mode
author: Themolx
body:
> **Discord:** themolx (ArtCraft Discord) · long-time After Effects power user

## What

When the Pen tool draws a **mask** in the viewer, holding a key while clicking the first vertex to close the path sets the mask's mode directly, so there's no trip to the Timeline to change it:

| Held key | Mode |
|---|---|
| S | Subtract |
| I | Intersect |
| L | Lighten |
| D | Darken |
| none | Add (default, unchanged) |

Shape-layer paths are unaffected; the key is ignored for them.

## How

- `mask.setClosed` takes an optional `mode` (any `MaskMode` label; masks only, ignored for shape paths). Closing and setting the mode happen in **one undo step**: a new `edit_path_group` helper edits the path and then the group inside the same `Session::edit`. An unknown mode is an error and changes nothing. The `cmd!` params doc is updated.
- `viewer.rs`: a small `MASK_MODE_KEYS` table (key to mode label). `held_mask_mode` reads `key_down` from egui input, and `pen_press` passes the mode when it closes on the first vertex.

## Shortcuts

S, I and L are also plain-key shortcuts (Reveal Scale, Go to Layer In Point, Reveal Audio Levels; D has none). They keep working while you draw, exactly as in After Effects: pressing I to close a mask also moves the time to the layer's In point, just like in AE. That only matters for a mask path that already has keyframes.

## Manual testing

I'm a long-time After Effects power user. I tested this by hand in the desktop app: holding S, I, L or D while clicking the first vertex closes the mask as Subtract, Intersect, Lighten or Darken, and with no key it stays Add.

## Environment

- macOS 13.7.8 (Ventura), Apple M1 (arm64)
- Rust 1.97.1 (Homebrew)
- Written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), then tested by hand by me
- Rebased on current `main`

title: Timeline: trim all selected layers together
author: Themolx
body:
Fixes #965.

## What
In the Timeline, dragging the in- or out-point edge of a layer bar while several layers are selected now trims **all** selected layers by the same amount, each from its own in/out point (After Effects behaviour). Before this change, only the dragged layer was trimmed. Moving a bar already acted on the whole selection.

## How
- `layer.timing` gains relative `inDelta` / `outDelta` params (seconds, snapped to frames), applied per layer:
  - in-point stops at the comp start (0) and at out − 1 frame;
  - out-point stops at the comp end and at in + 1 frame;
  - a point that is already outside the comp trims from where it is and does not jump onto the edge.
- The timeline bar drag (`panels/timeline.rs`) sends `inDelta`/`outDelta` for the selection (or for just the dragged layer if it isn't selected). It keeps the existing `merge` key, so a whole drag is one undo step.

title: Effects: Fractal and Turbulent Noise stay inside the layer's alpha (#939)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #939.

## What and why

Masks are applied before effects, so Fractal Noise receives a solid that is transparent outside its mask. `noise3::composite` then built the noise as `[v·op, v·op, v·op, op]` and returned it, or blended it over the layer, without looking at the layer's alpha. Every pixel came out with alpha `op`, so the noise covered the whole layer and the mask had no visible effect. Turbulent Noise goes through the same function.

The composited noise is now multiplied by the original pixel's alpha (premultiplied RGBA) before Blend With Original mixes it with the original. The noise stays inside the mask, and a feathered edge keeps its softness. Inside an opaque layer nothing changes. The GPU has two paths, and both get the same change so CPU and GPU still match: the default-settings branch in `kernels.wgsl` and the other modes in `fx_noise.wgsl`.

This follows the issue's description of After Effects, and the usual AE workflow of masking a Fractal Noise solid to confine fog to part of the frame. I haven't checked it in After Effects myself.

## Before / after

A gradient background with a grey solid above it, an ellipse mask on the solid, and Fractal Noise with default settings (`effectcraft-cli render-frame`, release build):

| `main` | this PR |
|---|---|
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HEOJUNFO/effectcraft/pr-assets/939/before.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HEOJUNFO/effectcraft/pr-assets/939/after.png) |

## How it was tested

- New test `noise3::tests::noise_stays_inside_the_layer_alpha`. It runs Fractal Noise on a layer with alpha 0, 0.5 and 1 in three bands, with Blending Mode None, Normal and Multiply. It checks that the output alpha equals the input alpha, that colour stays at or below alpha, and that noise is drawn where the layer is opaque. On `main` it fails with `mode 0: alpha 0 became 1`.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-gpu`: all 203 tests pass. `tests::gpu_effects_match_cpu` renders Fractal Noise on a layer…

title: engine: build well-formed file:// URLs for Edit Original, Reveal and File.execute
author: SteamSmith
body:
## Summary

Three places in `crates/engine/src/commands` build `file://` URLs by string concatenation:

| Where | Before | Example on Windows |
|---|---|---|
| `edit.rs` Edit Original | `format!("file://{path}")` | `file://C:\Footage\take #1.mov` |
| `layer_menu.rs` `folder_url` (Reveal in Explorer/Finder, Reveal Log File) | `format!("file://{dir}")` | `file://C:\Footage` |
| `app_more.rs` `File.execute()` | `file://` + spaces → `%20` only | `#`, `%`, `?` unescaped |

On Windows these aren't valid file URLs, and on any platform a path containing `#`, `%`, `?` or non-ASCII characters points at the wrong file (everything after `#` becomes a fragment, for instance).

This adds `layer_menu::file_url(path)`:
- backslashes → `/`

- bytes outside the plain path characters (`A-Za-z0-9 / - . _ ~ : @ ! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; =`) are percent-encoded, with non-ASCII as UTF-8

…and uses it in `folder_url`, Edit Original and `File.execute()`. No other behaviour changes.

title: SVG: percentages inside a nested <svg> resolve against its own viewport
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Nested `<svg>` elements without a `viewBox` resolved their children's percentage lengths against the outer viewport. A `width="50%"` rectangle inside a 40x20 nested `<svg>` in a 100x80 document imported as 50x40 instead of 20x10.

SVG 1.1 (Coordinate Systems, sections 7.9 and 7.10) says a nested `<svg>` establishes a new viewport. Percentages inside it refer to that viewport's size in its own user space: the `viewBox` size when there is one, otherwise the element's own width and height. The fix uses the nested element's width and height when it has no `viewBox`. The `viewBox` case is unchanged. The element's own `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` still resolve against the parent, and the parent viewport is restored for later siblings.

Not covered here: a root `<svg>` without a `viewBox` still resolves percentages against 300x150 rather than its own width and height, and `<use>` of a `<symbol>` without a `viewBox` has the same kind of issue. Happy to send those separately.

The first commit adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`; the fix is the second commit.

How it was tested
- New test `nested_svg_percentages_use_the_nearest_viewport` checks imported geometry and raster pixels for a nested viewport, a viewport nested two levels deep, a sibling after the nested element, and a nested viewport with a `viewBox`. It fails on main with the rectangle at 50x40 and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-svg`: 12 passed.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: all pass. Nine GPU tests need a GPU and fail the same way on current main on this machine, so they were skipped.
- `cargo xtask layers` and `cargo xtask assets`: ok.

title: Scale the timeline waveform by the layer's Audio Levels (#974)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #974.

The Waveform row in the timeline (LL) drew the footage's raw peak summary, so changing the layer's Audio Levels changed what you hear but not what you see. The mixer (`effectcraft_render::audio::mix_into`) multiplies each channel by `db_to_gain` of the layer's `audio > levels` value, evaluated at comp time.

`panels/waveform.rs::draw` now does the same: for each column it reads the Audio Levels at the column's comp time (keyframes included) and scales the left and right peaks by their gains before clamping and drawing. It uses the mixer's own `db_to_gain`, made `pub` in `crates/render/src/audio.rs` with no change to its behaviour, so -96 dB and below draws a flat line exactly where the mix is silent. Layers without the property draw at unity, as before. The cached peak summary is unchanged; only drawing applies the gain, so changing the level needs no re-analysis.

Expressions on Audio Levels are not applied to the drawing (the timeline has no expression host there); keyframed and static values are.

Test: `waveform_follows_audio_levels` checks that -6.02 dB gives half gain, -96 dB gives zero, and a layer without Audio Levels gets unity on both channels.

title: Show the Continuously Rasterize switch on vector footage layers (#957)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #957.

The timeline only drew the Collapse Transformations / Continuously Rasterize switch for precomp, shape and text layers, so imported vector footage (SVG, PDF, AI, EPS) never got it. The renderer already re-rasterizes vector footage at the layer's scale when `switches.collapse` is set (`crates/render/src/lib.rs`, gated by `is_vector_footage`), and `docs/file-format-parity.md` lists Continuously Rasterize for these formats; only the UI gate was missing.

The gate now lives in a small `collapse_applies` helper in `panels/timeline.rs`. It keeps the existing precomp/shape/text cases and adds footage whose item is vector, using the same `effectcraft_render::is_vector_footage` check the renderer uses, so the switch shows exactly when it has an effect. Raster footage and other layer kinds are unchanged.

Test: `collapse_switch_shows_for_vector_footage_only` builds an SVG footage layer and a PNG footage layer and checks that only the SVG one gets the switch.

Fixes #997. The desktop app took any argument it didn't recognise as a file to import, and it wrote that argument to Recent Footage. title: Portable mode: a portable.txt beside the exe keeps settings in EffectCraftData (#993)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Closes #993.

EffectCraft always kept its settings folder in the per-user location (`%APPDATA%\EffectCraft` on Windows), so the portable zip still wrote there. This adds portable mode the way PhotoCraft does it (#228 there): if a `portable.txt` (or `EffectCraft.portable`) file sits next to the executable, `config_dir()` returns `EffectCraftData` beside it, so preferences, shortcuts, recovery files, logs, models and plug-ins all move with the folder. `EFFECTCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` still wins, and if `EffectCraftData` can't be written (read-only drive, Program Files) a warning is logged and the normal folder is used. Without a marker nothing changes.

The logic is in a new `crates/host/src/app_dirs.rs`, with the resolution split into `resolve(env, exe_dir)` so it can be tested without touching the real environment; it's resolved once per process because the writability check probes the disk. The Windows portable zip now ships `packaging/windows/portable.txt`; the MSI doesn't.

Not covered: the disk cache, media cache and conformed audio still default to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\EffectCraft` (`disk_cache::default_folder`); they can be pointed elsewhere in Preferences ▸ Disk, and `portable.txt` says so.

Validation:

title: Rotation tool: keep counting past a full turn, as in After Effects
author: Themolx
body:
> **Discord:** themolx (ArtCraft Discord) · long-time After Effects power user

## What

Dragging with the **Rotation tool** past a full turn wrapped the Rotation value: after 359° it jumped back to 0x +0° instead of continuing to 1x +0°, 1x +10°…, and the same happened counter-clockwise. In After Effects the Rotation tool keeps counting across revolutions in both directions. It does now too.

## Cause

The `Gesture::Rotate` drag in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/viewer.rs` computed `start_rotation + (atan2(now) − atan2(at press))`. `atan2` wraps at ±180° (when the pointer passes to the left of the anchor), so every time the pointer went round, the value jumped back by 360° and could never get much beyond ±180° from where the drag started.

## How

- The gesture now keeps the last pointer angle and the total turned so far. Each frame it adds the change since the previous frame, wrapped to (−180°, 180°], so the total accumulates across revolutions without jumps.
- Two small helpers: `turn_delta` (wrapped change between two angles; NaN/∞ counts as no turn) and `rotate_value` (start rotation + turn, falls back to the start value if not finite, applies Shift snapping).
- **Shift** (45° snapping) snaps the accumulated value, so 400° snaps to 405° (1x +45°), not 45°.
- Other selected layers turn by the same amount from their own start values; one drag is still one undo step.
- On 3D layers the tool edits `transform/rotation` (Z Rotation), which shouldn't wrap either. The Timeline already shows revolutions (from the #93 work), so 360° displays as 1x +0.0°.

## Manual testing

I'm a long-time After Effects power user. I tested it by hand in the desktop app: rotating a layer more than once around with the Rotation tool now counts 1x, 2x… in both directions, as in AE.

- macOS 13.7.8 (Ventura), Apple M1 (arm64)
- Rust 1.97.1 (Homebrew)

- Based on current `main`

title: Shortcuts: Numpad * marks the selected layers (#976)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
# Layer markers from the layer context menu and Numpad * (#976)

Closes #976.

There was no way to put a marker on a layer from the Timeline: right-clicking a layer had no marker entry, and Numpad * always added a composition marker, even with a layer selected.

**Context menu.** The layer context menu (Timeline rows and bars, and the Composition panel, which shares it) gets After Effects' **Markers ▸ Add Marker**, between Time and Blending Mode as in AE. The shortcut handler now does that: when `*` is bound to `comp.addMarker` (the default) and layers are selected, it runs `layer.addMarker` instead. A custom binding is left alone. The two changes are separate commits, so the second one is easy to drop if you'd rather keep `*` comp-only.

title: Timeline: UU reveals an effect's changed parameters only
author: pravdomil
body:
Follow-up to #857 and #867 (both merged).

## Problem
UU (Reveal All Modified Properties) showed every effect on the layer as a whole group, whether or not anything in it had been changed.

## Change
`anim.reveal` with `kind: modified` compares each effect with a new instance of the same effect.
- **Revealed:** parameters whose value differs from the new instance's, and keyframed or expression-driven parameters as before. They show under their effect, twirled open.
- **Revealed in full:** groups a new instance does not have, such as puppet meshes and pins or paint strokes.
- **Unchanged:** an effect whose plug-in is missing still shows in full, since its defaults are unknown. Masks still show in full.

## Seeing the rest of an effect
A group twirled open by hand on a revealed layer shows all its properties: collapse and expand an effect that shows only its changed parameters to see every parameter. The next U / UU on the layer filters it again, and twirling the layer itself resets it. This applies to any reveal that lists properties under their effect (U, UU, EE), not only UU.

## Behaviour change to review
An effect that was applied and left at its defaults no longer appears under UU at all. This is my reading of After Effects' behaviour and was not checked against After Effects.

## Tests
- `tests_timeline::modified_reveal_shows_changed_effect_parameters_only` (new): a just-applied Gaussian Blur reveals nothing; a changed Blurriness is revealed; set back to the default it goes again; keyframed at the default it shows.
- Two UI timeline tests that relied on the whole effect showing now change Blurriness first and assert that only that row appears under the effect.

title: theme: the symbol test asks the definitions, not epaint's replacement-face check
author: FeiLiuEM
body:
`interface_symbols_have_a_glyph_in_every_family` (from 01400f0) has been red since that commit: the FreeBSD job fails on the `release` push ([run 38234073233](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/actions/runs/38234073233)) with `• has no glyph in FontId { family: Name("medium") }`, and it reproduces on Linux.

The assertion asks `Fonts::has_glyph` per symbol, and that answers "does this family resolve `c` to a face other than the family's *replacement* face" (epaint 0.36, `text/font.rs`):

```rust
pub fn has_glyph(&mut self, c: char) -> bool {
    self.resolve_face(c) != self.cached_family.replacement_face_key
}
```

The replacement face is the first one in the chain that carries epaint's `PRIMARY_REPLACEMENT_CHAR` (`'◻'`). The bundled Inter faces carry neither a replacement glyph nor triangles, so in `medium` and `semibold` the replacement face is the weight face itself — and every symbol that face owns reads as "no glyph":

```
family Proportional      missing = ""
family Monospace         missing = ""
family Name("medium")    missing = "•›·▶◀●○⚠…×"
family Name("semibold")  missing = "•›·▶◀●○⚠…×"
```

Only `▸` answers true there, which is the tell: Inter leaves triangles to JetBrains Mono. The fonts are fine — Inter-Regular/Medium/SemiBold carry ten of the eleven symbols (all but `▸`), JetBrains Mono carries all eleven — and rendering is unaffected, because the atlas resolves through the same chain, finds the weight face and draws the glyph. The assertion was asking a question the API cannot answer for these families.

It now asks what the wiring promises, from the definitions that were installed:

```rust
let defs = ctx.fonts(|f| f.definitions().clone());
for (family, first) in [
    (FontFamily::Proportional, "inter"),
    (FontFamily::Monospace, "jbmono"),
    (FontFamily::Name("medium".into()), "inter-medium"),
    (FontFamily::Name("semibold".into()), "inter-semibold"),
] {
    let chain = defs.families.get(&family).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{family:?} is…

title: Viewer trackpad gestures: two-finger scroll pans, pinch zooms
author: pravdomil
body:
## What

The Composition and Layer viewers treated every scroll as a zoom, so a trackpad could not pan them.

- **Two-finger scroll pans** (scroll events in points: trackpads, Magic Mouse, other pixel-precise devices).
- **Pinch zooms around the pointer**, as do Ctrl/Cmd + scroll, Alt + a trackpad scroll, and a mouse wheel (scroll events in lines), so mouse users keep today's behaviour.
- `ui.scroll` on the control channel gains `unit?: point|line` and `pinch?`, so agents can drive both gestures.

The device split lives in one helper, `panels::viewer_scroll`, used by both viewers.

## Behaviour change to note

- `ui.scroll` over a viewer with the default unit (`point`) now pans instead of zooming; pass `unit: "line"` or `pinch` to zoom.
- On the web, browsers report a mouse wheel in pixels, so there the wheel pans and Ctrl + wheel zooms.

## Tests

- New `ui_viewer_trackpad.rs` (Composition viewer: scroll pans; pinch, wheel and Alt + scroll zoom around the pointer) and a Layer panel case in `ui_layer_panel_zoom.rs`.
- Existing wheel-zoom tests now send line-unit wheel events.

title: Keep closed comps' layer selections across scripts (#1001)
author: vbasky
body:
## What
`Session::sanitize_state` no longer drops selected layers (and props/keys/vertices) that live in a comp other than the active one; only ids gone from every comp are dropped.

## Why
#1001: `layer.selected = true` in a comp that is not open in the viewer was visible for the rest of that script but gone by the next script call (the way panels talk over the control channel), because every script run ends in `settle()` → `sanitize_state()`, which retained only active-comp ids. After Effects keeps a selection per comp. I audited UI/engine selection lookups: they resolve per comp (`first().and_then(|id| comp.layer(*id))`, `filter_map`, `contains`) and tolerate foreign ids, so retaining them is safe.

## Verification
- New script test `layer_selection_in_a_closed_comp_survives_to_the_next_script` replays the issue repro across two `run_code` calls. Fails without the fix, passes with it.
- Suites green: effectcraft-script (81), engine lib (546), ui-egui lib (227). fmt + clippy clean.

title: Compensate cameras and lights when parenting, preserving the world frame (#1010, #1020)
author: vbasky
body:
## What
`layer.setParent` (compensated, the default) now re-expresses Position — and Point of Interest for two-node rigs — in the new parent's space for cameras and lights, exactly like 3D layers: values, keys, spatial tangents (as vectors) and ease speeds. They have no Scale, so Orientation stays as authored.

## Why
#1010 / #1020: parenting a camera to a default null moved its eye by the null's world transform (a default null sits at the comp centre, not the origin) and the framing jumped, because cameras/lights were explicitly excluded from parent compensation. The fix is exact by construction (the parent-space map comes from the actual world matrices).

Known follow-up (out of scope): under a *rotated* parent a two-node rig's basis also turns with the parent; counter-rotating authored Orientation needs euler decomposition and is left for later.

## Verification
- New test `parenting_camera_to_default_null_preserves_framing`: eye/forward/down unchanged (< 1e-9), authored Position/POI re-expressed, one undo step, unparenting restores values. Fails without the fix, passes with it.
- Full engine package green (571 passed, 5 suites). fmt + clippy clean.

title: Fix #989: paste animated effects at the playhead
author: onlymoein
body:
Copying an animated effect currently pastes its keyframes at their original times. This change aligns the earliest copied key with the destination composition's playhead and preserves the relative timing across all copied effects and nested parameters. For example, keys at 1s and 3s now paste at 5s and 7s when the playhead is at 5s.

The clipboard stores composition-time offsets from a shared anchor. Paste converts those offsets to each target layer's clock, including start offsets, time stretch and reverse stretch, while preserving easing and spatial tangents. Invalid or overflowing timing returns an error without changing the clipboard or leaving a partial paste. Existing UID assignment, naming, insertion and undo behavior are retained.

Adds nine regressions covering the reported Edit-menu path, nested parameters, stretched/reversed easing, spatial paths, cross-composition CTI, clipboard snapshots, repeated paste, exact NTSC offsets and atomic error handling. Updates the command documentation and G2 regression evidence, and adds the contributor's chosen names.

Closes #989.

## Validation

- `cargo xtask ci`: passed (formatting, workspace Clippy with `-D warnings`, workspace tests, dependency layering, asset attribution, and WASM checks for 32 crates).
- 3,124 tests passed, including 555 engine tests and all nine new regressions; 26 existing tests remain ignored.
- Offscreen UI smoke through `ui.menu.invoke` for Edit → Copy/Paste: all commands succeeded; property readback and the timeline show keys at 5s and 7s with values 10 and 30.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

Local validation used Rust 1.99.0 on macOS ARM64 with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16` to reduce linking time. Repository build profiles are unchanged.

author: vbasky
body:

The script evaluator's `EvalCtx` now carries the session's footage source, so `sampleImage` on a footage layer (directly, or through a Layer Control) returns the image's colour instead of transparent black.

## Why
#1000: a script reading an expression that calls `sampleImage` on an imported image got `[0,0,0,0]` while solids/shapes/precomps worked. `crates/script/src/model.rs` built its `EvalCtx` with `EvalCtx::new` (no footage source), so the renderer substituted transparent frames; procedural sources were unaffected. title: Cmd/Alt-click a twirl arrow opens its whole tree
author: pravdomil
body:
## What

Cmd-click (or Alt-click) a twirl arrow now twirls the whole tree under it open, and closed again on the next Cmd-click. The Timeline's layer arrow already did this; everything else only toggled itself.

- **Timeline Audio ▸ Waveform**: the Waveform row (not in the property tree) now twirls with Audio and with the layer.
- **Effect Controls**: an effect's header arrow and its nested group arrows.
- **Project panel**: a folder's arrow opens or closes every folder inside it.

A plain click, and a double-click on a group or folder name, still toggle just that one row.

## How

- `UiAct::ToggleGroup` carries the layer and an "all" flag; `walk_groups` also yields Audio's Waveform row (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`).
- `toggle_closed` in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/effect_controls.rs` for both Effect Controls arrows.
- The folder arrow in `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/project.rs` walks its subfolders.

## Testing

New tests, all passing:
- `command_clicking_a_group_twirl_opens_its_whole_tree` (`ui_viewer`)
- `command_clicking_an_effect_twirl_closes_and_opens_its_groups` (`ui_effect_controls`)
- `command_clicking_a_folder_twirl_opens_the_folders_inside_it` (`ui_project_rows`)

title: Cover keyframe interpolation and ease on effect parameters (#994)
author: vbasky
body:
## What
Adds a script regression test that `setInterpolationTypeAtKey` and `setTemporalEaseAtKey` (the `keys.interpolation` / `keys.velocity` commands) set bezier interpolation and speeds/influences on effect parameters — a Slider Control's slider and a 3D Point Control's point — not just transform properties.

## Why
#994 reported both calls silently no-op'ing on effect parameters. On current main they work (the script's per-key path in `crates/script/src/runtime.rs` resolves effect params via the recursive `Props::find`), but nothing covered effect params, so this locks the behaviour in against regression.

title: Interpret Footage: looped footage lasts its loops on new and re-timed layers
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1045.

The loop count itself is stored fine (since #925), and the media pool already wraps the frame index by `loop_count` for movies as it does for sequences. The problem is the layer length: `layer.addItem` sized a footage layer by `f.duration`, which is one pass, so a 2 s clip looped 3 times still gave a 2 s layer and the loops were never reached. Changing the loop count on footage already in a comp didn't re-time anything either, because `file.interpretFootage` compares one-pass durations, which don't change. I added `Footage::looped_duration()` (duration × loops) and used it for new layers, for the re-time in Interpret Footage, for `Item::duration()` (Project panel duration, New Comp from Selection, Time Remap end, the timeline's source ghost), and in `layer.slip`, which already did the same multiplication inline. Using the looped length in `Item::duration()` is how After Effects reports looped footage, but happy to switch to touching only the layer paths if you'd rather keep that one as is.

The issue doesn't say which container/codec the Discord user had. If it turns out to be specific to one format, I'm glad to look at a sample.

Validation:
- `tests_menu_cmds::interpret_footage_loop_extends_video_layers`: fails on main (a new layer on a 2 s clip looped 3× ends at 2.0 s, expected 6.0), passes here. It also checks that a layer added before the change is re-timed and that the item reports 6 s
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine --lib` filtered on slip / relink / remap / new_comp / interpret / loop / add_item
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-project -p effectcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Layer sampling toggle, Show Channel grayscale and colorized, Timeline zoom back in
author: pravdomil
body:
Makes three of EffectCraft's shortcuts toggle. These were the "Known limits" of #1050.

> **Stacked on #1050.** This branch starts from that PR's branch, so until it merges the diff here also shows its three commits. The new work is the last three commits.

## 1. Layer sampling toggle

`Alt+B` (Bilinear) and `Alt+Shift+B` (Bicubic) only set the sampling. Now, when every selected layer already has it, the key switches them to the other one, so one key goes back and forth.

- `layer.sampling` takes `toggle`. Without it the command only sets, as before.

After a colorized channel (`Alt+Shift+1`), `Alt+1` on the same channel went back to RGB. It now shows that channel in grayscale, and `Alt+Shift+1` after `Alt+1` shows it colorized. Pressing the same key twice still returns to RGB.

`view.channel {toggle}` now counts a channel as "the active one again" only when `colorized` is not given or matches the current state.

## 3. Timeline zoom back in

`Shift+;` (Zoom to Fit Comp) zoomed out to the whole comp and a second press did nothing. It now remembers the span it left and goes back to it when pressed again. With nothing to go back to, the whole comp stays.

The remembered span is not saved with the workspace.

title: Add a Nix flake (NixOS, GNOME and Hyprland)
author: untypequicode
body:
## What

Adds `flake.nix` and `nix/package.nix` so that `nix build`, `nix run` and an overlay give a source-built effectcraft and effectcraft-cli on NixOS, modelled on the existing LightCraft flake.

- `Cargo.lock` drives the dependencies (git sources through `cargoLock.allowBuiltinFetchGit`), so there is no `vendorHash` to maintain. The version comes from `[workspace.package]`.
- Installs the desktop file, hicolor icons, MIME types and AppStream metadata from `packaging/linux/`, validated at build time (`desktop-file-validate`, `appstreamcli`).
- Wayland and X11: the binaries are wrapped so the libraries winit/wgpu/rfd `dlopen` are found on NixOS — `libwayland-client`, `libxkbcommon` (incl. x11), the X11 libs, the Vulkan loader, `libEGL` and `libdbus` (xdg-desktop-portal file chooser). It runs natively on Wayland under GNOME and Hyprland, with X11/XWayland as fallback. Hyprland needs a portal backend for the file dialogs (`xdg.portal.extraPortals = [ pkgs.xdg-desktop-portal-gtk ]`); this is noted in `nix/package.nix`.
- The fonts from `storytold/craft-fonts`, where the app embeds them, are a pinned non-flake input at the revision the release workflow uses.
- Also: `overlays.default`, `apps.default`, a dev shell, `nix fmt` and a formatting check.
- `doCheck` is off: the suite needs corpora and a GPU the sandbox cannot provide (`cargo xtask ci` stays the gate); it can be turned on with `overrideAttrs`.

No Rust, packaging or CI file is touched.

## Testing

`nix build .#effectcraft` builds both binaries and passes the desktop-file and AppStream validation, on NixOS.

title: Graph Editor: a handle drag moves handles of its own curve only (#1053)
author: vangel76
body: Refs #1053  ## Cause Key selection is per property and time (`KeyRef`), not per dimension, so selecting a key on one curve of a multi-dimension property (or keys on several properties) shows handles on every curve. A handle drag then collected the same-side handles of every selected key on every curve (`panels/graph.rs`, drag start), so dragging one curve's handle also moved the handle of other curves (another dimension or property), as in the report.  ## Fix The drag now moves the same-side handles of the selected keys of the dragged curve only (`grabs_on_curve` / `curve_grabs`). Moving several selected keys of the same curve together (#284) is kept. Mirroring for continuous keys is unchanged and stays inside the engine (`keys.setEase`).  ## Assumptions - The reporter's project was not available; the issue does not say which curves were involved. I took "another keyframe curve" to mean a different curve (dimension/property) of the selection. If the report was about several selected keys on a single curve, that is the intended #284 behaviour and is not changed here. - Expected behaviour: a handle drag affects only the dragged curve's selected keys.  ## Tests - New unit test `handle_drag_moves_only_own_curve_same_side` (side filter, curve/dimension mapping). The call site could not be exercised headlessly, so the selection logic was extracted into a pure function; the test did not exist before the refactor. - `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --no-fail-fast`: all pass except the known main failure `theme::tests::interface_symbols_have_a_glyph_in_every_family`. - fmt, `clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers`, wasm32 check of the engine: clean.  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: SVG: percentages in the root <svg> resolve against its own width and height
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
Follow-up to #969, which listed this as a known gap.

A root `<svg>` without a `viewBox` resolved percentage lengths against 300x150 even when it set its own width and height. A `width="50%"` rectangle in a 100x80 document imported as 150x75 instead of 50x40.

SVG 1.1 (Coordinate Systems, section 7.10) says percentages refer to the viewport's size in its user space: the `viewBox` size when there is one, otherwise the viewport's width and height. The fix uses the document width and height the importer already computes for the root. The `viewBox` case is unchanged. A root with percentage or missing width and height keeps the same document size as before, and its percentages now match that size. A size that is not a finite positive number falls back to 300x150, so it cannot produce NaN geometry.

`<use>` of a `<symbol>` without a `viewBox` is still open.

How it was tested
- New test `root_svg_percentages_use_the_document_viewport` covers explicit sizes, percentage sizes, no sizes, a `viewBox`, and an unusable size. It fails on main with the rectangle at 150x75 and passes with the fix.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-svg`: 13 passed. `cargo test -p effectcraft-media -p effectcraft-pdf`: pass.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: all pass. Nine GPU tests need a GPU and fail the same way on current main, so they were skipped.

title: SVG: non-finite viewBox and nested sizes no longer panic the importer
author: webdevtodayjason
body:
A viewBox or nested `<svg>` size that overflows to infinity made the SVG importer panic: percentages resolved against it became NaN, and the rectangle corner-radius clamp (`clamp(0.0, NaN)`) panics on NaN.

What changes:

- `viewbox()` now ignores a viewBox with any non-finite number, the same as one with a zero or negative size. That also covers an infinite min-x or min-y, which produced a NaN transform.
- A nested `<svg>` with a non-finite width or height uses the parent viewport, the same as when the attribute is missing or cannot be parsed. Zero and finite negative sizes are unchanged and still draw nothing, as on main. A width of -1e400 now also uses the parent viewport, which matches SVG 2's handling of negative sizes as auto.
- The rectangle size check is NaN-safe, so a zero-percent or zero-em size against an infinite base is dropped instead of reaching the clamp.

The nested viewport path came in with #969. This complements #1082, which handles the root `<svg>` size, and does not change that code.

How it was tested:

- Red/green: the two new non-finite tests panic on unchanged main at `clamp(0.0, NaN)` and pass with the fix. They cover overflowing viewBox sizes and min-x, overflowing nested sizes, zero-percent rectangles and circles, and check that the resulting geometry and transforms are finite. A third test checks that zero-size nested viewports still draw nothing, as on main.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-svg`: 15 passed.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-media -p effectcraft-pdf`: pass.
- `cargo fmt --all --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- Trial merge with #1082: no conflicts.

title: #1070: a fresh import or opened project reads overwritten footage again
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1070

**Cause:** `MediaPool` keys decoded frames by path only. Nothing dropped them when a new project (or a new import) named a file that another app had overwritten since, so a same-size overwrite showed the old pixels. The disk cache keys already hash size and modification time; the in-memory pool did not. (The EXR case in the issue differed only because its size changed, which the EXR channel cache notices.)

**Fix:** importing footage and `Session::replace_project` (new/open) now make the media layer `forget` the files involved (path and sequence frames) and clear the layer cache. No per-frame stat; reload and change-watcher paths are unchanged.

**Tests:** `a_new_project_importing_an_overwritten_file_shows_the_new_pixels` in `crates/host/tests/footage_reload.rs` failed before the fix (red pixels) and passes now. `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine -p effectcraft-host` pass, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo xtask layers` and wasm32 check of the engine are clean.

title: Refresh layered composition sources on import
author: onlymoein
body:
After #1086, importing an overwritten PSD as Composition or Composition – Retain Layer Sizes can still show pixels from an earlier import. Composition sources are created in `prepare_import`, so they bypass the decoded-footage refresh for probed files.

Refresh the footage items created by composition imports through the existing `Session::forget_decoded` helper, before any background probe job starts. This refreshes decoded sources and processed layer buffers without emitting `PurgeCaches`, preserving the RAM preview.

Related to #1070; builds on #1086.

## Validation

- Three generated-fixture regressions fail on current `main` and pass with the fix: fresh PSD composition imports in both sizing modes, re-import preserving unrelated decoded media and one-step undo, and layered sources refreshed before a mixed background import finishes. All three assert that importing emits no `PurgeCaches` event.
- Host footage-reload suite: 10 tests passed.
- Full `cargo xtask ci`: passed (3,401 tests passed, 26 existing tests ignored; formatting, release workspace Clippy with `-D warnings`, dependency layering, asset attribution and all 32 WASM crates).
- `git diff --check`: clean.

Validated on macOS ARM64, Rust 1.99.0, using `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16`.

title: Path vertices win over the bounding-box handles (#1042)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1042

**Cause.** In the Composition viewer a path/mask vertex marker had a grab reach of 6 points while a layer bounding-box handle reaches 9 (HANDLE + 2), so a vertex lying under or next to a handle lost the press to the handle and scaled the layer. The box handles were also painted after (over) the vertex markers, and the resize cursor showed over the vertex.

**Fix.** `vertex_grab_radius`: wherever a box handle is in range of the pointer, the vertex reaches as far as the handle, so vertices and tangent handles win there (all of press, click, double-click). The hover cursor over a vertex is a pointer instead of a resize cursor. Vertex markers are collected by `draw_paths` and drawn after the bounding boxes (`draw_vertex_marks`). Box handles stay usable away from path points. Not addressed: hiding the box while editing vertices (#1033).

**Tests.** New `vertex_reaches_as_far_as_a_box_handle_over_it` (fails without the fix, passes with it). ui-egui: 227 pass, 1 pre-existing failure on main (`theme::tests::interface_symbols_have_a_glyph_in_every_family`), all integration tests pass; fmt, clippy -D warnings, `xtask layers` and the wasm32 check are clean.

title: Orient Along Path keeps its heading at the end of the path (#1081)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1081

**Cause.** Auto-Orient > Orient Along Path measures the direction of travel with a central difference of the position around the current time. At and after the last position keyframe (and before the first), the position is clamped, so the difference is zero, there is no tangent, and the extra rotation fell back to 0 degrees. A layer heading e.g. left (180 degrees) therefore snapped to 0 degrees on the last frames of the path and looked flipped, while the numeric values did not change.

**Fix.** `path_tangent` (crates/render/src/three_d/camera.rs) keeps the last valid direction of travel when there is no motion at the current time: it takes a backward difference at the latest earlier position key that has motion, and only before the first key looks forward. Applies to 2D and 3D layers. Non-finite or zero-length differences return no tangent, so no NaN. Assumption: AE keeps the last heading past the end of the path.

**Tests.** New `orient_along_path_keeps_the_last_heading_at_and_after_the_end` (2D and 3D, at the final key and after it). It fails without the fix (heading snaps to +x at t=1.2) and passes with it. effectcraft-render: 211 pass; clippy -D warnings, fmt, `xtask layers`, `xtask wasm` clean.

Not covered: a path whose keys repeat the same point can overshoot through the spatial auto-Bezier, which is a separate matter.

title: EPS: arc and arcn with huge angles no longer hang the import
author: dotCooCoo
body:
`arc` and `arcn` in EPS files computed the sweep with a loop that added or subtracted 2π until the sweep had the right sign. For an angle of 10^18 degrees the loop took about 3e15 passes, and from 2^56 radians (about 4.1e18 degrees) up, adding 2π left the sweep unchanged and the loop never ended. A sweep that needed no loop, as in `0 10^18 arc`, was passed unchanged to kurbo, which divides it into more than 10^16 curves (about four per turn at a radius of 10), and `arc` appended each curve to the path. Importing an EPS file probes it with `effectcraft_pdf::parse` (in `layered::probe`, `crates/media/src/layered.rs`), which has no time limit, so importing such a file did not finish. With `main`'s `arc`, parsing a file with `newpath 50 50 10 1000000000000000000 0 arc` did not finish within 20 seconds.

## What changes (`crates/pdf/src/ps.rs`)

- As in https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/pull/1062, every arc starts at the first angle's remainder after whole turns, and when the second angle is below the first (`arc`) or above it (`arcn`), the sweep is worked out from the two angles' remainders (`ccw_turn`).
- A sweep of up to 1,024 turns is drawn whole. For a longer one, the import records a skip note (`arc (too many turns)`) and leaves out whole pairs of turns, so that between 1,022 and 1,024 turns remain. The arc still ends at its second angle, and an even-odd fill covers the same area as the full sweep.
- Arcs of up to 1,024 turns whose angles are within about 10^6 degrees are unchanged apart from rounding, except some whose angles are a whole number of turns apart or within rounding of that (next item). For larger angles, the old conversion to radians lost precision: at 10^15 degrees, a quarter-turn arc swept 1.5723 radians instead of 1.5708.
- When raising (`arc`) or lowering (`arcn`) the second angle by whole turns makes it equal to the first, as in `7 -353 arc` or `2 362 arcn`, rounding sometimes made the old loop add a turn and draw a full circle. Those arcs…

title: Markers: adding one during playback no longer stops the audio (#1083, #1085)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1083, fixes #1085

#1168 landed in the same batch and keeps the RAM frames when a plain marker changes (`Comp::same_pixels_ignoring_markers`). This PR is now what is still needed on top of main: the same rule for the **disk-cache key**, and one shared predicate for both caches.

**Cause.** `comp_content_key` hashed `Comp::pixel_form()`, which includes comp and layer markers. Adding a marker with Num* during a preview changed the disk key, so frames cached on disk no longer matched and the playing preview stopped its sound until they were rendered again.

**Fix.**
- `Comp::pixel_form_with(with_markers)` is used by `comp_content_key`. Without marker-reading expressions it drops layer markers and the comp's plain markers.
- It KEEPS the markers that can change pixels: protected markers with a duration, which `render::eval::protected_regions` / `responsive_source_time` read to retime stretched precomp layers (only their time and duration matter there). The predicate is `is_timing_marker`, one function used for both the RAM identity and the disk key.
- With any expression in the project (`Project::reads_markers`, the same test #1168 used) all markers count, as before.
- `Comp::same_pixels_with` / `Layer::same_pixels_with` replace `same_pixels_ignoring_markers` and `project_has_expressions` from #1168 with this shared predicate (no behaviour change for the RAM side: `frames::tests::markers_keep_the_frames_unless_an_expression_reads_them` and `timing_markers_and_expressions_still_change_the_frames`).
- `pixel_form_with` used to borrow the comp unchanged when it had only comp markers and no layer markers, so a lone plain comp marker still reached the key. Fixed.

**Tests.**
- `tests_disk_cache::protected_markers_with_a_duration_change_the_content_key`: a plain marker on a precomp's source keeps the key of the comp nesting it (stretched layer); adding a protected marker with a duration, and changing its duration, changes it. Fails when `pixel_form_with` drops all mark…

title: Fix #1063 item 8: render carriage-return text as paragraphs
author: onlymoein
body:
After Effects scripts commonly use carriage returns in Source Text. EffectCraft previously split paragraphs only on LF, so `addText("Line 1\rLine 2")` rendered as one line and `sourceRectAtTime()` returned single-line bounds, breaking scripts that fit text to a box.

Rendering and TextDocument paragraph metadata now share CR/LF/CRLF paragraph boundaries. A CRLF pair is one break, with empty and trailing paragraphs retained. The original Source Text is preserved, including Unicode byte/character offsets. Paragraph edits map formatting back to the original text so joining or splitting CRLF at an edit boundary preserves following paragraph styles.

Adds seven regressions for CR rendering, mixed-break ranges and serialization, paragraph formatting through edits, CRLF boundary edits, point/box/vertical geometry, Unicode character styles, and multiline `sourceRectAtTime()` through the scripting API.

Addresses **item 8 only** of #1063. The other compatibility gaps in that issue remain open.

## Validation

- CR regression: red before the fix (1 line instead of 2), green afterward, with bounds matching LF.
- Keyframe, text and scripting suites: 172 tests passed, including all seven new regressions.
- Full `cargo xtask ci`: passed; 3,122 tests passed / 26 existing tests ignored, workspace release Clippy with `-D warnings`, layering, asset attribution and all 32 WASM crates passed.
- Offscreen UI smoke: original `First line\rSecond line` retained, both lines visibly rendered, scripted bounds 117.85 px high at 60 px text.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

Validated on macOS ARM64 with Rust 1.99.0 and `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16`. Serial tests avoid the existing system-font ordering failures observed during #1039; repository build profiles and existing assertions are unchanged. No live After Effects comparison or native Linux/Windows run was performed.

title: Project files: compact .ecproj JSON, with a setting for indented files
author: pravdomil
body:
## What

`.ecproj` files are now written as compact JSON by default, and a new setting turns indentation back on.

- **Compact by default:** `Project::to_file_json_with_view` uses `serde_json::to_string`. The `project.ecproj` inside exported template packages (`templates.rs`, `commands/essential.rs`) uses `to_json_compact()`.
- **New setting:** Settings ▸ Project ▸ Project Files ▸ **Format Project Files for Reading** (`project.formatProjectFiles`, off by default). When it's on, File ▸ Save / Save As write indented JSON, one value per line, so projects diff cleanly in version control. `to_file_json_with_view` takes a `pretty` flag for this. Auto-saves, XML copies and template packages stay compact.
- **Docs:** README and `docs/preferences.md` describe the setting.

Reading is unchanged, so files of either kind, including those from earlier versions, open the same. Prefs, shortcuts, workspaces and package `manifest.json` keep their indentation.

## Tests

- New `project_files_are_compact_unless_formatting_is_on`: saves with the setting off and then on, checks the layout of each file, and checks both read back as the same project.
- Three assertions that matched the indented text (`"schema": 2`, `"activeComp": …`, `{\n  "savedBy"`) now match the compact layout.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-project`: 32 passed. `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine --lib -- project_files tests_settings tests_effects`: 44 passed.
- `cargo xtask ci` was **not** run, and the commits carry `[skip ci]`, as requested.

title: Gap 21: percentage guides and effect colour labels (#1095)

title: Fix #978: keep form choices and buttons inside the dialog
author: pravdomil
body:
Refs #978. Replaces the approach of #980.

#980 gave Project Settings its own 800 px width. This puts the dialog back at the shared 480 px form width and fixes the overflow itself, for every form:

title: feat(design): native Figma transfer and FigCraft copy/paste
author: eliasx45
body:
## What

Transfer designs into native, editable EffectCraft layers from Figma or FigCraft. This extends the existing Figma transfer contribution (the Figma part of #858) with one-time FigCraft Copy/Paste and shared rendering fixes.

- **Figma:** `file.importFigma` accepts node JSON from the transfer plug-in/MCP, or a Figma link through the REST API. The plug-in in `integrations/figma/plugin` uses the local `effectcraft-cli figma-bridge` HTTP endpoint to forward into the app's control channel. Supported shapes/text become editable layers; unsupported Figma nodes use PNG renders.
- **FigCraft:** ordinary Copy/Cmd+C produces SVG with bounded native metadata. EffectCraft Paste/Cmd+V routes it to `edit.pasteFigCraft`; explicit JSON is accepted too. Each paste is independent and one undo step, with no live link. Text editing and ordinary SVG paste retain their own routes. Frames create compositions; other selections use the active composition and its timing.
- **Fidelity:** original PNG/JPEG fills become footage plus native crop mattes, preserving editable text/vector children. Shared mapping/rendering fixes retain overflow bounds, multiple shadows, affine radial/linear gradients, angular/diamond gradients, and source text baseline/line-height. Redo restores the newly created composition when the viewer has no active composition.

Companion FigCraft Copy/export support: https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/pull/535.

## Validation and security

- Version 2 embeds validated original PNG/JPEG bytes; version 1 remains accepted. Carrier/JSON sizes, node count/depth and bitmap bytes/dimensions/pixels are bounded before project mutation. Bitmaps are decoded and importer-probed before one project edit. Malformed marked payloads fail without falling back to stale clipboard contents or flattened SVG.
- Clipboard payloads cannot name local files or URLs. Figma payload images retain the existing inline-only rule. Automation sessions with file-access confinement reject `edit.pasteFi…

title: feat(shortcuts): AZERTY physical-key bindings, Go to Work Area keys, Graph Editor zoom and fit

- **Go to Work Area Start / End** (`time.workAreaStart` / `time.workAreaEnd`), bound to Shift+Home /

- **Graph Editor zoom**: the layer bars and the Graph Editor share one time zoom; the footer's

  Editor fits the selection (or all graphs), and the fit goes through the timeline zoom; AZERTY zoom
  keys work in the graph.
- **View stops at the comp end**; a ruler scrub past the edge scrolls with the CTI.

On AZERTY keyboards several of After Effects' default shortcuts couldn't be reached or collided;
the Graph Editor had its own zoom. Split out of #858 as asked.

title: feat(xtask): cargo xtask bench render benchmark with --compare and --fail-over
author: eliasx45

`cargo xtask bench`: a render benchmark over generated scenarios that records peak memory, CPU
time, wall time (and max RSS / instructions retired where the OS reports them) to
`results.jsonl`. `--compare` sets two runs side by side; `--fail-over PCT` exits 1 when a matched

#858 as asked.
