title: fix(effects): CC Particle World / Systems II replace their layer; Time effects see earlier effects
author: eliasx45
body:
## What
Two effect fixes found comparing against After Effects 2026 renders:

- **CC Particle World / CC Particle Systems II replace their layer with the particles.** They were
  composited over the original layer by the Transfer Mode, so the solid they're applied to stayed
  visible (a red rectangle around a flame, black blocks over light). The Transfer Mode now only
  sets how particles meet each other. Their 112 pinned CPU golden hashes change on purpose (re-pinned
  in its own commit); no other effect changed.
- **Time effects see the effects applied before them.** Echo, Posterize Time and the other Time
  effects read the layer at other times without its earlier effects; After Effects renders them
  with those effects (e.g. Echo after CC Particle Systems II, Posterize Time after Turbulent
  Displace). The host already bounds the count to the effects before the one rendering.

## Why
Mean absolute error vs After Effects on test projects: 0.0191 → 0.0130, 0.1177 → 0.0937, and
0.1855 → 0.0071 for one using both; 15 other projects with a Time effect after another effect are
pixel-identical. Split out of #858 as asked.

## How tested
- `crates/render/src/tests_time.rs` (new case) and `crates/effects/tests/particle_golden.rs`
  (re-pinned); written with the changes, not re-run on this branch.
- `rustfmt --check` and `cargo check --all-targets` on the affected crates on current upstream
  `main`.

title: Tracker: a track point can be grabbed when zoomed out
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1067.

I couldn't see the recording, so I went after the zoom angle: screen-to-comp conversion is fine at every zoom (a drag moves the point by exactly delta/zoom), but the hit areas aren't. The attach point's grab area is a fixed 12 px square at the centre of the point, and it's tested before the feature region. Zoomed out, a default track point's feature region is smaller than that on screen (43 px on a 1080p layer is 10.8 px at 25%), so every press inside it grabbed the attach point: the crosshair moved, the point never did. At 1080p that kicks in below ~50%, i.e. at the usual fit-to-viewer zoom. Now, when the attach point sits inside the feature region, its grab area is capped to the region's inner half, so the rest of the region still grabs the point; at normal sizes nothing changes, and an attach point dragged outside the region keeps its full 12 px. Happy to switch to a different rule (e.g. the point wins over the attach point when the region is tiny) if you prefer.

Validation:
- `ui_tracker::zoomed_out_track_point_can_be_grabbed` (1080p comp, default track point, real drags at 25/50/100%): fails on main (at 25% the point moves by (0, 0) and the attach offset by (160, 80)), passes here
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --test ui_tracker`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- (macOS, Apple silicon)

title: Keyboard Shortcuts: OK button in view, Enter is OK, visible scroll bar handles
author: pravdomil
body:
Three fixes that came out of using Edit ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts, one commit each.

## OK button in view
The editor's content was slightly taller than the dialog, so the dialog's outer scroll area cut the OK button in half and its scrollbar covered the right edge.

The editor no longer sits in an outer scroll area (`modal_fit` instead of `modal`). The command list and the selected-command editor take whatever height is left under the keyboard, so the OK row always fits, also in a small window. The dialog is 40 px taller when the window has room.

## Enter is OK
Enter closes the editor like its OK button, also while the search field has focus. It stays with the shortcut recorder (Enter can be recorded), the preset rename field and an open preset menu.

## Visible scroll bar handles (app-wide)
The scroll bar handle was filled with the colour of its own track (both the field background), so it only showed while hovered or dragged. It now takes the text colour (`ScrollStyle::foreground_color`). This is a theme change, so it applies to every scroll area, not only the command list.

title: Floating panels: no widget ID clash when dragged past the window edge [skip ci]
author: pravdomil
body:
## Problem
Undocking a panel (e.g. Preview) and dragging it past an edge of the window painted egui's red "Double use of widget ID" warning over it.

## Cause
- The floating group's title strip was registered as `id.with("move")`, which is also the id egui's `Area` gives its own background widget.
- The `Area` was constrained to the window, so once the group's rect hung past an edge it was drawn shifted back in while its stored rect kept moving. The strip then no longer sat inside the area's rect, and egui reported the shared id as a clash. The panel also stopped following the pointer there.

## Fix
- The strip has its own id (`id.with("strip")`).
- The `Area` is not constrained: the group is drawn where its rect says (the existing clamp still keeps its strip reachable).

## Tests
`floating_panel_dragged_past_the_window_edge_is_drawn_at_its_rect` in `crates/ui-egui/tests/shared_docking_ui.rs` (fails without the fix: drawn at y=700 while its rect is at y=805). Ran the `shared_docking_ui`, `ui_panel_windows` and `ui_workspace_focus` suites and `cargo fmt --check`; the full `cargo xtask ci` was not run (CI skipped as requested).

title: Effects: CC Particle World replaces the layer instead of compositing over it (#839)
author: redonion23
body:
Fixes #839

**Cause**
`particle_world_plan` (crates/effects/src/sim.rs) shared `particle_sprites` with CC Particle Systems II, which maps Transfer Mode to `Post::Combine`: Composite drew the particles *over* the layer's own pixels. On a solid (the usual set-up) the layer stayed opaque and hid everything below. Before the first particle was born the plan was `None`, so the solid showed unchanged.

**Fix**
CC Particle World's plan now always uses `Post::Replace`: the particles replace the layer in every Transfer Mode (Add still accumulates particles with `Acc::Add`), and the unborn case is an empty plan, i.e. a transparent layer. The GPU compositor reads the same `SpritePlan`, so both paths change together. CC Particle Systems II is left as it was.

**Tests**
- New `sim::tests::particle_world_replaces_the_layer`: an opaque black solid in each of the four Transfer Modes leaves transparent pixels between the particles, and the unborn layer is fully transparent. It fails on `e2f314f7` (`mode 0: transparent between particles`) and passes with the fix.
- Reproduced the report with `effectcraft-cli` on Windows 11 (aarch64): red solid below, black solid + CC Particle World (defaults) above, `render-frame --time 1 --transparent`. Before, 0 red pixels were visible. After, the red layer shows around the particles. Without the lower layer, the output is transparent (min alpha 0).
- `cargo xtask ci` on Windows 11 aarch64: fmt, clippy, layers, assets and wasm pass. `cargo test --workspace --release --no-fail-fast` has six failures, and all six fail the same way on unmodified `e2f314f7`. title: Scripting: Google Earth Studio camera scripts key the camera
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1077.

The Earth Studio export stopped halfway through, for two reasons. It keys the camera through layer-level shortcuts (`cameraLayer.position`, `.xRotation`, `.zoom`), which only existed on AVLayer, so `cameraLayer.xRotation` was undefined and the script threw right after keying the two helper nulls. Then it fills camera Position with an expression and runs Convert Expression to Keyframes through `app.executeCommand` on the selected property, but `prop.convertExpressionToKeyframes` needed an explicit `path`. CameraLayer now has the transform and camera-options shortcuts (Point of Interest, Position, Orientation, X/Y/Z Rotation, Zoom, Depth of Field, Focus Distance, Aperture, Blur Level), and the convert command, called with no layer/path, converts the selected properties that have an expression, like the menu item does.

With the attached eiffel-tower-orbit.jsx the camera goes from 0 keys (script error) to 1500 Position keys and 1501 keys each on X/Y/Z Rotation and Zoom; the helper nulls are removed as in AE. Converting several selected properties gives one undo step per property outside a script; happy to fold them into one if you prefer.

title: #595: RAM preview no longer stalls on a gap right after the playhead
author: pravdomil
body:
## What you see

Press play on a stretch that still has to render: the playhead stands still for seconds. The cache bar shows a gap of a few frames right after the playhead while frames further ahead turn green, and playback starts only once the whole prefetch window is cached.

The earlier #595 change (prefetch order and eviction, #793) is in the build that shows this. It starts the right frames first; they still finish last. Cache Frames When Idle has the same cause and leaves the same late-filling gaps.

## Cause

Prefetch frames render side by side on one rayon pool, and each frame's own parallel loops run on that pool too.

1. An idle thread steals a piece of a frame that is rendering.
2. That piece waits on a nested parallel loop, and the thread picks up a queued frame job instead.
3. The thread renders queued frames until the queue is empty, and only then returns to the piece it stole.

The frame that piece belongs to cannot finish while frames keep being queued. The frames started first are the ones just ahead of the playhead, so those are the ones left as a gap.

## Why #793 did not cover this

#793 fixed which frames are started first and which are evicted last. This stall comes from the order frames finish in, which it did not touch.

- #793 takes the frame the playhead reaches first from the queue first, keeps the frames just ahead of the playhead when the cache is full, and stops prefetch at what the cache holds. All of that works as intended.
- Here the cache had just been cleared, so nothing was evicted, and the frames right after the playhead were started first. They did not finish until prefetch stopped feeding the queue, which is when the whole window was cached. Starting them first makes them the ones that get stuck.
- #793's case was a preview longer than the cache, where the next frames kept being evicted and queued again at the back. Its tests check the pick order and the eviction choice on the queue and cache directly, without rendering frames…

title: Text: fallback tries a script's usual families before faces loaded earlier
author: dotCooCoo
body:
`fallback_for` tried every face that was already loaded before the usual families of the character's script (`crates/text/src/fonts.rs:789` on `main`). Which faces are loaded depends on every earlier lookup. On macOS, `/Library/Fonts/Arial Unicode.ttf` is a link to `/System/Library/Fonts/Supplemental/Arial Unicode.ttf`, so Arial Unicode MS is the first face in the scan, and it covers every script that has usual families except Sinhala. `variable::find_variable_face()` loads it, because it reads faces in scan order until one has a variation axis. The fallback for a character that Arial Unicode MS covers and the bundled faces and the usual families lack, such as the Simplified Chinese 们, loads it too, because the search over every installed font starts with it. On `main` at e2f314f, த in Inter falls back to Tamil Sangam MN, but after a lookup of 们, த and あ fall back to Arial Unicode MS. With this change, த still falls back to Tamil Sangam MN after 们, and あ falls back to Hiragino Sans.

In the `effectcraft-text` unit tests, `other_scripts_fall_back_to_a_plain_system_family` and `cjk_falls_back_to_a_system_family` depend on which faces the other tests have loaded, and the two variable font tests load Arial Unicode MS. On a Mac, `cargo test --release -p effectcraft-text --lib` failed in 7 of 100 runs on `main` at e2f314f: "த → Arial Unicode MS" 4 times, "ก → Arial Unicode MS" once, and twice the check that a second lookup of 水 returns the same face. It failed in 24 of 100 runs while other builds were running. #802 and #1039 report the same two tests failing on their Macs, and #285 left this order out of scope.

## What changes (`crates/text/src/fonts.rs`)

- For a character of a script with usual families (CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, Indic, Thai), `fallback_for` tries those families right after the bundled faces. `family_faces` lists the installed faces of the script's families in the order `system_fallback` tried them, each in the preferred face's style. The list is cached per…

title: Viewer eyedropper: stay armed until there is a frame to sample
author: pravdomil
body:
## Problem

`timeline_colour_eyedropper_samples_the_comp` (`crates/ui-egui/tests/ui_timeline_shapes.rs`) was flaky: 8 failures in 30 runs on 470ea7a3 (Apple M1 Max), with the fill still red instead of the comp's green.

The cause is a real bug, which the test's timing exposed. Viewer frames render on background threads. A colour pick clicked in the Composition panel before the viewer had a frame to sample found no pixels, set nothing, and was still used up, so the eyedropper silently did nothing.

## Fix

- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/effect_controls.rs`: a click on a colour pick with no frame to sample leaves the eyedropper armed (the text colour eyedropper already behaves this way). Point picks and keyer picks do not read the shown frame and are unchanged. A click outside the frame still cancels the pick as before.
- `ui_timeline_shapes.rs`: the test waits for the viewer frame before clicking (same `settle` as `ui_ram_preview.rs`). It tests sampling, so it needs a frame.
- `ui_effect_controls.rs`: regression test `the_eyedropper_stays_armed_until_the_viewer_has_a_frame`, which clicks while a large blurred frame is still rendering.

## Verification

- `timeline_colour_eyedropper_samples_the_comp`: 0 failures in 60 runs (was 8 in 30).
- New regression test: 0 failures in 15 runs with the fix; 4 of 5 runs fail without it (a race, so not every run reaches the no-frame click).

title: PSD import: bound group nesting at 64 (#1128)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1128

## Cause
`Psd::tree()` built an unbounded nested `Node::Group` tree from the `lsct` dividers/folders, and the importer recursed over it (`build_comp` -> `build_layer` -> `build_comp`). The tree's own `Drop`/`Clone`/`PartialEq` recurse too. A file with a few thousand nested groups aborted the process with a stack overflow (not catchable by the panic guard).

## Fix
- `crates/psd`: new `MAX_GROUP_DEPTH = 64` and `Psd::tree_report()` (`tree()` calls it). Groups nested deeper are flattened into their depth-64 parent: their children stay in order and the deeper group record becomes a plain `Node::Layer`, so no layer is lost. The tree is now at most 64 deep, which also bounds `rev`, `Drop`, `Clone`, `PartialEq` and the importer recursion.
- `crates/engine/src/psd_import.rs`: the import result gets a warning ("N group(s) nested deeper than 64 levels were flattened into their parent") through the existing `warnings` channel (reported in `errors` of `file.import`).

## Tests
- `effectcraft-psd`: `deeply_nested_groups_are_flattened_at_the_depth_limit` (70 nested: exactly depth 64, 6 flattened, every layer/group record present once; 64 nested: nothing flattened), `thousands_of_nested_groups_do_not_overflow_a_small_stack` (5000 nested, parse + tree + clone + eq + drop on a 2 MiB thread).
- `effectcraft-engine`: `psd_with_thousands_of_nested_groups_imports_on_a_small_stack` (5000 nested groups through `file.import` on a 2 MiB thread, 65 comps, one flatten warning). Without the fix (limit raised temporarily) this test aborts with SIGABRT stack overflow; the depth test fails with a limit of 1000.

title: PSD: drop non-finite values, no panic in Warp::apply / Rect::new (#1130)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1130

## Cause
- EngineData numbers use `str::parse::<f64>()`, which accepts `nan`/`inf`/`-inf`; descriptor doubles, the `TySh` transform, the `PlLd` quad, `expA` f32 values and 32-bit samples were taken as read. The importer forwarded them to font size, tracking, leading, position and scale.
- `Warp::apply` indexed `mesh` directly (public `cols`/`rows`/`mesh`, invariant only checked in `Warp::read`), and `Rect::new` added without overflow handling.

## Changes
- EngineData: non-finite or overflowing literals are not numbers (so the style value is `None`); font size must be > 0 and is capped at 10 000, tracking and leading are clamped to +-100 000.
- Descriptor `doub`/`UntF`/`UnFl` and `PlLd` read non-finite as 0 (`Reader::f64_finite`); a `TySh` transform with a non-finite entry becomes the identity; `expA` falls back to exposure 0, offset 0, gamma 1.
- `samples()` (32-bit): NaN -> 0, +inf -> 1.0 (white, like the maximum of the integer depths), -inf -> 0.
- Importer (`psd_import.rs`): `set_vec2`/`set_scalar` ignore non-finite values, `text_doc` guards scale, size, leading and box.
- `Warp::mesh_point` returns `Option` using `get()` and saturating/checked math, `apply` leaves the point unchanged for a missing or short mesh or zero/huge `cols`/`rows`; `Warp::read` computes `(3c+1)(3r+1)` with checked math. `Rect::new` saturates.

## Tests (each fails without its fix, verified by temporarily reverting)
- `engine_data::tests::non_finite_and_out_of_range_numbers_are_not_numbers`
- `tests::non_finite_transform_and_exposure_values_are_dropped`, `tests::non_finite_32_bit_samples_become_finite`, `tests::rect_new_near_i32_max_saturates`
- `placed::tests::custom_warp_with_a_missing_or_short_mesh_does_not_panic`

title: PSD: share the duplicated decode, placed-transform and writer helpers (#1133)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1133

## What changed (crates/psd, no behaviour change)
- S1: `SoLd` reading uses `placed::floats` (via a new `placed::eight`) instead of its own `nums` closure; the corner quad is built by one `placed::quad_from` (was spelled twice, `SoLd` and `PlLd`).
- S2: raw / RLE / ZIP plane decoding lives in `open_planes` (RLE row counts, inflate) and `decode_plane`; `decode_channel` and `composite` both use them. Error order and errors are unchanged (counts first, then planes; `Truncated` for a short ZIP buffer in composite; `decode_channel` still zero-pads a short inflate result).
- S3: write.rs uses `descriptor::put_u16` / `put_u32` instead of its own `u16b` / `u32b`; `unicode_plain` and `put_unicode` share one `put_utf16(out, s, terminated)` (they differ in the trailing NUL: `luni` names are not terminated, descriptor strings are, so they are not merged into one function). Removed the dead `let _ = h;`.

## Left alone on purpose
`write::encode_samples` still silently writes 8 bit for any depth other than 16 (including 32). That is a behaviour question, not a simplification; not touched here.

## Tests
Existing tests are unchanged and pass. Added, because the ZIP and RLE-composite paths had no coverage: `zip_channels_decode_like_raw_ones` (8 and 16 bit, compression 2 and 3, composite and layer channels incl. a layer mask, compared with the raw document) and `rle_composite_matches_the_raw_one`. 32 bit is not covered by the new tests (the writer cannot produce it).
Note: decode_channel's ZIP path now copies the inflated plane once more than before (decode_plane borrows the inflated buffer); that copy is removed again in the follow-up optimisation PR.

title: #1132: a damaged PSD layer section keeps the merged image
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1132

## Cause
`Psd::parse` propagated any error from the layer section (`layer_info(...)?`), so a bad layer record signature, an implausible channel count or a channel length running past the layer info discarded a document whose header and merged image were fine. AGENTS.md asks lenient readers to fall back and record the repair.

## Change
- `crates/psd`: when the layer section fails, `parse` clears the layers, keeps the header and merged image and records a message in the new `Psd::warnings`. If the file has no merged image data after the layer section there is nothing to fall back to, so the original error is returned. A 16/32-bit layer block that still recovers layers clears the warning.
- `crates/engine/src/psd_import.rs`: a document with no layers and a parse warning is imported as a composition with one layer (the merged image as footage, `layer: None`), and the warning is carried into `PsdImport::warnings`. It reaches the user through the existing import report (`errors` of `file.import`, shown as a toast), the same channel as the adjustment-layer warnings. Valid files are unchanged.

## Tests
- psd: `damaged_layer_section_keeps_the_merged_image` (broken second-record signature and an oversized channel length: `Ok`, no layers, one warning, `composite()` equal to the undamaged file's), `header_damage_and_missing_merged_image_still_fail`.
- engine: `psd_with_damaged_layer_section_imports_the_flattened_image` (exactly one layer, the warning, footage is the merged image).
- Both new fix tests fail with the fallback disabled (checked by temporarily forcing the error return, then restored).

## Commands run
`cargo test -p effectcraft-psd`, `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine` (547 passed), `cargo test -p effectcraft-media layered`, `cargo test -p effectcraft-host --test vector_import`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -p effectcraft-psd -p ef…

title: PSD: avoid redundant plane copies, per-pixel mask tests and repeated quad solves (#1136)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1136

## What changed (crates/psd; output is bit-identical)
- O3: raw channel data is borrowed from the file (`Cow`), not copied; the merged image's ZIP planes are un-predicted in place in the inflated buffer (no per-plane `to_vec`); the 32-bit un-predictor reuses one scratch row instead of copying every row.
- O5: the layer-mask loop evaluates the "inside the mask rect" test once per row (the column range is computed once), applies the constant factor to the outside parts as a slice, and skips it when it is exactly 1.0 (e.g. no mask data and default colour 255). No mask data: one bulk pass, no per-row test. Mask reads use `get` with the default colour as fallback instead of indexing.
- O6: `SmartObject::map`, `placed_bounds` and `placed_size` keep their signatures; internally the quad's projective matrix is solved once per call and shared (`render_placed` solves it once for the bounds, the size and the 49x49 grid; `placed_size` no longer recomputes bounds separately inside a bake). In the triangle loop the source corners and the barycentric coefficients are hoisted out of the pixel loop (same operations, same order, so results do not change; the per-pixel division by the denominator is kept on purpose, a reciprocal would change rounding).

## Tests (crates/psd/src/tests_opt.rs)
The replaced implementations are kept in the test module as references (`ref_unpredict`, `ref_decode_channel`, `ref_composite`, `ref_layer_pixels`, `ref_map`, `ref_placed_bounds`, `ref_render_placed`).
- Equality, compared bit for bit: composite and layer pixels for depths 8 / 16 / 32 x raw / RLE / ZIP / ZIP with prediction (channels and merged image re-encoded from synthetic planes); the same on truncated files (errors compared too); layer masks moved to overlap the layer/canvas partly, wholly or not at all, default colour 0 / 255 / 90, inverted, disabled, with and without mask data, canvas and layer-sized output; placed bakes for perspective, affine, degenerate quads and warp styles…

title: PSD: a memory budget for one decode and a capped smart-object bake (#1138)
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1138

## Cause

`MAX_DECODE_PIXELS` (2^28) bounded one decoded image only. `composite()` kept the ZIP output (`want * rowbytes * h`), one `Vec<f32>` per channel and the result `Vec<[f32; 4]>` alive together, `layer_pixels()` the channel planes, alpha, mask and output. A 16384 x 16384 header with a small ZIP stream of zeros therefore asked for roughly 10-14 GiB (an uncatchable abort), and on wasm32 `vec![[0f32; 4]; n]` panics with a capacity overflow for n >= 2^27. The smart-object bake size came from the file: a quad corner of 1e6 gave `needs_bake` and a 16384 x 16384 (4 GiB) bake.

## Change

- `crates/psd/src/lib.rs`: a `Budget` (4 GiB; 1 GiB under `target_pointer_width = "32"`) that every buffer of one decode is charged against. `composite()` and `layer_pixels()` first check their whole expected peak (result at 16 bytes a pixel, CMYK black plate, the channel or ZIP buffer, the mask) and return `Error::Unsupported("... over the N MiB memory budget")` before allocating anything. Allocation goes through `try_reserve_exact`, not `vec![..; n]`. The ZIP limit is the size the channels need.
- Channels are written straight into the result (no `Vec<f32>` per channel, no second result; audit item O4). The CMYK black plate is the only extra float plane.
- `crates/psd/src/placed.rs`: `SmartObject::bake_scale(w, h, k, doc)` lowers `k` so a bake is at most 4x the document across either way and at most `MAX_BAKE_PIXELS` (2^24); `render_placed` returns `None` for an output over the cap and reserves with `try_reserve_exact`. `crates/engine/src/psd_import.rs` uses `bake_scale`. Interpretation of "4x the document": 4x per side, not 4x area.
- Over-budget decodes reach the user through the existing `MediaError::Decode` mapping in `media/layered.rs`, an ordinary decode error.

## Tests (`crates/psd/src/memory_tests.rs`, `placed.rs`)

- Equality against the previous decoder, kept in the test module as a reference: composite and every layer (canvas and own bounds, partly off-can…

title: UI: a Simplified Chinese interface picks a face with the simplified hanzi
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1141.

The interface picks its Chinese fallback face by asking the text engine for a face that covers 文. Japanese faces cover 文 too, and `fallback_for` returns a face that is already loaded before it looks at the Chinese families. An English (or Japanese) interface loads a Japanese face for kana first, so after switching to Simplified Chinese that Japanese face became the Chinese fallback as well, and the simplified-only hanzi (选, 删, 层, 设, 页 …) were drawn as boxes. Traditional Chinese mostly survives because Japanese faces carry most of the traditional forms. A Simplified Chinese interface now probes 页 instead, which only a face with the simplified set covers, so the lookup skips the Japanese face and lands on Microsoft YaHei / PingFang SC / Noto Sans CJK SC. wordcraft probes with the same character for its Chinese interface font (storytold/wordcraft#248). No font is added to the repo. I left the Traditional probe at 文, since that is not what the issue reports; happy to give it a traditional-only probe too.

Validation:
- `simplified_chinese_interface_draws_simplified_hanzi_after_another_language` (installs the English fonts, then the zh-hans ones, and checks the hanzi are not drawn with the replacement glyph): fails on main (`an installed face covers 选删层设导页, but the Simplified Chinese interface draws boxes`), passes here; probing 文 again for zh-hans makes it fail the same way
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --lib theme::` (8 passed)

title: Timeline: Quick Offset layers and keyframes in selection order (#1012)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Closes #1012.

After Effects 25.4 added **Quick Offset**: Ctrl+Alt (Windows) / Cmd+Opt (macOS) dragging selected layers or keyframes in the Timeline staggers them in the order they were selected. The first selected stays, the last moves by the drag, and the ones between move by equal steps, landing on subframes ([Adobe's feature post](https://community.adobe.com/announcements-532/feature-focus-quick-offset-stagger-your-layers-just-by-dragging-them-314472)). EffectCraft had Alt-drag time-scaling and Sequence Layers, but nothing that staggers interactively by selection order.

## What it does
- **Timeline gesture.** Ctrl/Cmd+Alt dragging a selected layer bar, or a selected key, runs a Quick Offset as one undo step.
  - The mode is chosen when the drag starts and needs at least two unlocked layers.
  - Like the key drag, the layer bars' Quick Offset follows the pointer outside the rows' code. It ends when the button is released, even with the bar's row scrolled out of view; before, it stayed active and took over the next drag of that bar.
  - The last selected layer moves by whole frames with the pointer.
  - A readout by the pointer shows **Total Offset** and **Per Layer** (e.g. `Total Offset: +52 f   Per Layer: +17.33 f`), translated in every catalog.
- **Layers** (`layer.quickOffset {delta, layers?, merge?, fromStart?}`). Each layer's start, in and out point move by `delta × i / (n − 1)`, in the selection order or the `layers` order. Duration and the keys (in layer time) come along.
- **Keys** (`keys.quickOffset {delta, merge?, fromStart?}`).
  - The layers are taken in the order their first key was selected.
  - All of a layer's selected keys, across its properties, move together by that layer's offset in comp time. The offset goes through the layer's start and stretch, reversed layers included.
  - Values, interpolation, easing and labels are kept.
- **Exact timing.** The offsets are worked out once in ticks with integer arithmetic: one frame over four layers give…

title: Fix Intel Mac crash: probe Metal shader language version support
author: mjohnson7cd
body:
## Summary

Fixes crashes on Intel Macs where all ArtCraft apps fail to launch with `Metal: error: invalid value 'metal3.2' in '-std=metal3.2'`.

The wgpu Metal backend was choosing MSL version purely from OS version, but legacy Intel GPUs have older Metal compilers that reject newer MSL versions.

## Solution

Vendors wgpu-hal 30.0.1 with the patch from gfx-rs/wgpu#10592:
- Probes the Metal compiler at adapter creation by compiling a test kernel
- Steps down from OS-selected version until compiler accepts it
- Modern Macs: tries Metal 3.2 → succeeds immediately
- Legacy Intel Macs: tries 3.2 → 3.1 → ... → 2.4/2.3 until one works

## Issues Fixed

Fixes storytold/photocraft#1859
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2126  
Fixes storytold/artcraft#2190

## Testing

- ✅ Compiles on macOS
- ✅ Passes clippy
- ⚠️ Untested on real Intel Mac hardware (awaiting community testing)

## Notes

The vendored wgpu-hal will be removed once upstream releases the fix and ArtCraft can bump to that version.

---
— sent on behalf of @mjohnson7cd by Claude Code

title: macOS: open the window on Intel Metal by skipping indirect-call validation
author: fabian-co
body:
## What this changes

On a Mac whose integrated GPU is an Intel Iris Pro (MacBookPro11,3, macOS 12.7.6), EffectCraft can't open its window when it draws on that GPU (`EffectCraft couldn't start its window: WGPU error: Parent device is lost`). On this dual-GPU machine the default picks the NVIDIA GPU, so it shows with `WGPU_POWER_PREF=low`; a Mac with only that Intel GPU has no other Metal adapter to fall to.

The cause is wgpu's indirect-call validation: when the device is created, wgpu compiles a compute shader to validate indirect draw/dispatch arguments, and Metal's Intel compiler aborts on it. The log shows:

```
ERROR [main] wgpu_core::indirect_validation: indirect-validation error: ComputePipeline(Internal("new_compute_pipeline_state: NSError { code: 2, localizedDescription: \"Compiler encountered an internal error\", domain: \"CompilerError\", .. }"))
ERROR [main] eframe::native::run: Exiting because of error: WGPU error: Parent device is lost
```

and each attempt leaves `MTLCompilerService` crash reports ending in `IGILErrorMessageHandlers::reportUnsupportedMaxWorkGroupSizeMetadataError` (libIGIL-Metal).

EffectCraft draws and dispatches nothing indirectly (no `draw_indirect`, `draw_indexed_indirect`, `multi_draw_*` or `dispatch_workgroups_indirect` in `apps/` or `crates/`), so this removes `VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL` from the window instance's flags. `WGPU_VALIDATION_INDIRECT_CALL=1` turns it back on. This is the same fix VectorCraft already has (storytold/vectorcraft#651); PhotoCraft and LightCraft skip the check too.

Only the window's instance is changed; the headless `GpuContext::request` in `crates/gpu` keeps wgpu's default flags. No docs, asset or dependency change.

## How you verified it

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean
- `cargo clippy --locked -p effectcraft --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

title: Scripting: key calls fetch only the key they need, so removeKey stays fast (#814)
author: redonion23
body:
Fixes #814

**Cause**
Every per-key script call (`removeKey`, `keyTime`, `keyValue`, `setValueAtKey`, `setInterpolationTypeAtKey`, ...) goes through `Property.__key(i)` in `crates/script/src/prelude.js`. That function called `__keys()`, which serialised the property's whole key list (values, eases, spatial tangents) in `model.rs` and parsed it in the script engine, for one key. Going through a long property key by key was therefore quadratic. As @raisulsohan measured, the time is almost entirely the read; the `keys.delete` edit itself is cheap.

**Fix**
- `keys` query (`crates/script/src/model.rs`): optional zero-based `index` returns `{count, key}` with just that key (`key: null` when out of range). Without `index` it returns the full array as before; the per-key JSON is the same closure for both.
- `__key(i)` uses it, and keeps the same `keyIndex N is out of range 1..M` error.

**Tests**
- New `tests::script_key_lookup_fetches_only_that_key`: 2,000 keys; the `index` query returns one key and the count, and `null` past the end; `removeKey`, `keyTime`, `keyValue` and the out-of-range error still behave as before. It fails on `470ea7a3` and passes with the fix.
- The script from the issue, `effectcraft-cli script repro.jsx --empty`, release build, Windows 11 aarch64:

| keys | before (`470ea7a3`) | after |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 | 3.5 ms | 0.2 ms |
| 1,000 | 48.1 ms | 0.3 ms |
| 2,000 | 103.7 ms | 0.4 ms |

- On Windows 11 aarch64, `cargo fmt --check`, `clippy --workspace --all-targets --release -D warnings`, `xtask layers`, `xtask assets` and `xtask wasm` pass. `cargo test --workspace --release --no-fail-fast` passes except six tests unrelated to this change. title: Parented cameras and lights keep their static and keyed Orientation (refs #1010) [draft]
author: nanox333
body:
**Draft, waiting on #1038 and #1159.** This branch includes their commits: #1038 (Position and Point of Interest for cameras and lights) and #1159 (the Y-angle precision fix). Those two commits sit underneath this PR's own changes, which are the last four.

**What:** a rotated parent now re-expresses a camera's or light's Orientation, so one-node lights and cameras keep their direction and two-node cameras keep their roll. Keyed Orientation is re-expressed too. Under a Z-only parent the keys are shifted exactly. Under a tilted parent, Euler angles are blended between keys, so converting the keys alone changes the motion between them; keys are added wherever the blend drifts more than 0.05 degrees from the exact rotation (each segment is halved up to 10 times, at most 4096 keys). title: Scripting: a stroke's Dashes use After Effects' match names (#815)
author: redonion23
body:
Fixes #815 (the Dashes part; the Path Options names were already fixed on main by 0467e110).

**Cause**
`matchnames::node` had no entry for the children of a stroke's Dashes group, so they reported EffectCraft's ids (`dash`, `gap`, `offset`). `property("ADBE Vector Stroke Dash 1")` therefore found nothing. `resolveAdd` had no case for Dashes, so `addProperty` threw `Can not add a property to "Dashes"`.

**Fix**
- `matchnames.rs`: Dashes children report `ADBE Vector Stroke Dash 1/2/3`, `Gap 1/2/3` and `ADBE Vector Stroke Offset`. `stroke_dash()` maps a match name back to the id.
- `resolveAdd` (model.rs) on Dashes: a name that names an existing child returns it (`kind: existing`). EffectCraft's Dashes always holds Dash 1, Gap 1 and Offset, and Dash 0 draws no dashes. Dash/Gap 2 or 3 that don't exist yet return `kind: dash`. Unknown names keep an error.
- `addProperty` (prelude.js): `existing` returns that property; `dash` runs `shape.dashes.add` on the stroke until the asked-for one exists (at most three times, since the first add only turns Dash 1 on when it is 0).
- Lookups by the old ids (`property("dash")`) still work through the existing fallbacks.

**Tests**
- New `tests::script_stroke_dashes_use_after_effects_match_names`: the children's match names, `addProperty` of Dash 1 returning the existing property (and setting it), `property()` by Offset's match name, `addProperty` of Gap 2 adding the Dash 2 / Gap 2 pair, and the error for an unknown name. title: Workspaces: report failed saves instead of returning success (#696)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Refs #696. This doesn't claim to fix the report: the reporter's version and the actual storage failure are still unknown. It closes the gap that made a workspace look saved when it never reached disk.

## What was wrong
- **Save as New Workspace, Save Workspace and Edit Workspaces (rename, delete) always returned success.** Write errors only went to the log and the status bar. A file rejected at load blocks writes for the session, and an explicit save then did nothing and still reported success. Without a settings folder it also reported success. The workspace stayed usable until the app closed, then disappeared.
- **Errors from frontend-only commands never reached the caller.** These commands go through the engine, which queues an `Event::Frontend` and returns `Ok({"frontend": id})`. `run_engine` put any frontend error in the status bar only, so `menus::invoke` (menus, dialogs, `ui.menu.invoke`) always returned `Ok`.
- **Deleting the current custom workspace failed validation.** It saved before switching to Default, so validation rejected the save ("current workspace has no saved definition"). It was only written later by the background retry.

## Changes
- `WorkspaceStore::save_now`: the explicit save. It returns `Err` when there's no settings folder, when the file was preserved after a failed load (the message gives the file's path), or when the write fails.
- `store_saved_workspaces` returns that error, prefixed with "Workspace changes couldn't be saved and may be lost after a restart: …". After a restart the file on disk is what comes back: a new workspace is missing, a rename keeps its old name, and a deleted workspace returns. It puts the message in the status bar and logs it. The four commands propagate it with `?`. The in-memory layout stays usable, and the existing retry, existing-file preservation and atomic writes are unchanged.

title: Preview: preserve opening audio while preparing video playback (#947)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Closes #947.

A preview with sound and **Video** on, without **Cache Before Playback**, lost its opening, about the first third of a second. Those frames played silently, and the sound only started from a later frame. With Video off, or with Cache Before Playback on, the opening was heard.

## Cause
`play_with` held the sound (`Playback::audio_held`) while the playhead advanced through frames as they rendered. Once the frames ahead were cached, or rendering had kept up for at least a quarter second (#219), it called `start_audio()` at the **current, already advanced** frame. So the samples before it never reached the output: they weren't delayed, they were skipped. Lowering the 0.25 s would only shorten the loss.

## Fix
Starting an audible video preview now has its own state, `Playback::starting`:
- The **playhead holds the first frame** while the frames ahead render, never the whole work area. How many it waits for is `startup_frames(ahead, window, budget, frame_bytes)`: the prefetch's `ahead`, capped by the frames the prefetch window actually requests from the playhead, and capped by how many fit in 90 % of the RAM preview budget **at the size the first frame really rendered at** (Extended Viewer frames are larger than the comp). It's never below 1, the current frame. So the wait always ends: it only waits for frames that are requested and can stay cached together. (An earlier revision waited for `ahead.min(fit)`, which could hold the first frame for ever. Thanks to the review that caught both cases.)
- Then **sound and picture start together from that frame**, and the sound's clock drives the picture as before.
- **No output device** (or it fails to open): the picture plays from that frame on its own clock, without waiting any longer.
- **It never waits for ever.** When the RAM preview can't hold even one frame (a zero budget, or one frame larger than the budget), startup doesn't wait at all. Otherwise the wait for the frames ahead gives up `STARTUP_WAIT` (2 s) …

title: Graph editor: speed graph handles keep dragging once their key leaves the plot
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1171.

In the speed graph an end key sits at the speed of its only side, so it climbs together with the handle you're dragging. As soon as the key went above the plot, the loop that draws keys and handles skipped it (`!plot.expand(6.0).contains(kp)`), and its handles with it. The handle's widget disappeared mid-drag, so the drag stopped at the top edge. On release the graph auto-zoomed and the handle landed back at the same height, so it looked like it couldn't be dragged up. Keys with a handle being dragged are no longer skipped (the painter is still clipped to the plot), so the speed follows the pointer for as long as the drag lasts.

While testing I noticed something unrelated: on a property that goes down (Opacity 100→0, Rotation 0→−90) with Easy Ease (speed 0), dragging a handle up gives a positive speed, so the layer starts off moving the wrong way. The sign comes from `negative: h2.speed < 0.0`, which doesn't take the segment's direction into account. I left it out of this PR; happy to open a separate one.

Validation:
- `ui_keyframes::speed_graph_handle_drags_upward_past_the_top`: fails on main (40 px up gives 28.1, 400 px up only 175.8 because the drag stops at the top edge), passes here

title: #473: Cryptomatte: resolve the rank planes once and reduce them on all cores (GPU path ~9.5 s → ~0.2 s per 1440p frame)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Part of #473 (point 4, the GPU path's speed). Picking in the viewer, the Layer popup and quoted names are not touched.

## Cause

`gpu::fx_depth::cryptomatte` built its aux image in a single-threaded loop over every aux pixel, and for every pixel `AuxChannels::crypto_ranks` formatted the channel names (`format!("{layer}{k:02}.R")`, …) and searched the channel list for them. The CPU effect called the same function per pixel, in parallel.

## Change (1 commit)

* **raster:** `AuxChannels::crypto_rank_planes(layer)` resolves a layer's (ID, coverage) planes once, in rank order (`00.R/G`, `00.B/A`, `01.R/G`, …, same rules as before: case-insensitive, stops at the first missing rank). `crypto_ranks` keeps its signature and is now built on it.
* **effects:** the matte and the ID-colour preview are two small per-pixel functions over the resolved planes, used by the CPU effect and by the new `crypto_aux_image` (rayon, all cores), so the CPU and GPU paths share one reduction.
* **gpu:** `fx_depth::cryptomatte` uploads `crypto_aux_image` instead of its own serial loop.

The arithmetic and its order are unchanged, so the output is bit-identical. The reduction stays on the CPU: after this change it costs ~0.2 s at 2560×1440 on the test PC, so moving it to a shader is not worth the extra code.

## Measured

title: #879: cap GPU frames in flight during export
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Fixes #879

## Problem

During export, `Cx::frames` (crates/export/src/pipeline.rs) rendered every frame of a batch at once (`ks.into_par_iter()`). With a GPU accelerator, each frame in flight holds its own working textures. On the #879 project (142 shape and text layers, 1080p), a 30-frame `--gpu` export used about 20 GB above idle on an RTX 3090 (23.9 GB total). On an 8 GB card it filled the card, and main quietly rendered every frame on the CPU: its PNGs are byte-identical to a CPU render. On shared-memory GPUs (the Intel and AMD reports in #879) the same burst can take the process down instead.

## Change

- **Only the GPU render is capped, only for GPU-accelerated projects.** The cap applies only when an accelerator is attached *and* the project's GPU acceleration is on (the same condition #898 uses). Software Only projects and accelerator-less exports keep the one parallel batch they had.
- **One frame by default, on every vendor.** This is what #898's single GPU worker does for image sequences: its async readback, and so more than one frame in flight, only applies with GPU YUV conversion. On an 8 GB card, three frames at once still filled the card; one stayed on the GPU at about 6.0 GB.
  - The default isn't sized from free VRAM, because the GPU backend reports no free or total device memory portably.
  - It is decided once per batch.
- **Encoding stays parallel.** Frames go in windows of `max(cap, threads)`. Each window renders in chunks of the cap, then encodes in parallel, so at most one window of images is held in RAM.
- **Override:** `EFFECTCRAFT_GPU_INFLIGHT=N`. An invalid value (0, negative, not a number, too large) logs a warning and uses the default.
- **Safety:** the chunks hold no lock or slot. A failing or panicking frame can't leak one, and nested parallelism inside a frame or a single Rayon thread can't deadlock.
- **Scope:** no new dependencies, and no unwrap, expect, panic or unsafe outside tests.

title: i18n: an effect's name draws in the interface language, the generated Effect menu included (#821)
author: cjcwwww
body:
## What

An effect's name draws in the interface language — the generated Effect menu included (#821, option A).

The interface below the menu bar is localized (618 fixed menu entries, ~490 panel rows) but an
effect's name still rendered in English everywhere it appeared: the generated Effect menu, Effect
Controls, the Timeline and Effects & Presets.

The registry's English name is the effect's **identity**: `effect.list`, `effect.apply {"effect": …}`,
scripts, expressions and the property tree's group name all match on it, and the written project file
must not change with the interface language. So only the *drawing* goes through a catalog.

## Where the catalog lives

title: Track matte on an adjustment layer limits where its effects show
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1201.

`Renderer::draw_adjustment` mixed the adjusted comp back in by the layer's footprint and opacity only, so the track matte that `composite_iso` applies to every other layer was never looked at, and the GPU twin in `gpu/src/walk.rs` did the same. The matte step is now its own helper (`apply_track_matte` on the CPU, `track_matte` in the GPU walk), shared by `composite_iso_with` and both `draw_adjustment`s: the footprint is multiplied by the matte factor before the mix, so all four kinds (alpha, alpha inverted, luma, luma inverted) behave as on a normal layer.

Validation:
- `render` `track_matte_limits_an_adjustment_layer` (Invert adjustment over a 0.25 grey, white matte on the left, each matte kind): fails on main (`Alpha: 0.75 inside, 0.75 outside`), passes here
- `gpu` `tests_adjust::track_mattes_limit_gpu_adjustments_like_the_cpu` (8 and 32 bpc, each kind, GPU vs CPU): passes; with the GPU matte line removed it fails (`3537 of 5917 pixels over tolerance`)
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-render --lib track_matte`, `cargo test -p effectcraft-gpu --lib tests_adjust`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-render -p effectcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: UI: Quick Apply keeps an IME composition while pinyin is typed
author: cjcwwww
body:
Chinese (and Japanese/Korean) could not be typed into Quick Apply at all: with Windows' Microsoft Pinyin every letter of the pinyin vanished as it was typed, so nothing could ever be committed. Latin typing was unaffected.

## Cause

`palette()` took the keyboard on every frame it was drawn:

```rust
let r = ui.add(egui::TextEdit::singleline(&mut q) …);
r.request_focus();
```

egui's `Memory::request_focus` interrupts the IME composition (its doc comment says so), and `Context::end_pass` turns that into `PlatformOutput.ime.should_interrupt_composition`, which `egui-winit` acts on with `window.set_ime_allowed(false); window.set_ime_allowed(true);` — on Windows that is `ImmAssociateContextEx(hwnd, 0, IACE_CHILDREN/IACE_DEFAULT)`, which drops the composition in progress. Asking once per frame cancelled the pre-edit text over and over: the pinyin never accumulated and no candidate could be committed.

It is the only per-frame focus request left in the UI: the inline editors guard theirs in `widgets::keep_focus`, and the rename fields use a one-shot flag.

## Fix

Ask for the focus only when the field hasn't got it — the same guard the inline editors use. The palette still takes the keyboard when it opens, and still takes it back when something else takes it away.

## Tests

`panels::dialogs::tests::the_palette_leaves_a_pinyin_composition_alone` opens the palette, feeds `ImeEvent::Preedit("n" … "nihao")` frame by frame and asserts that the frame never asks the platform to cancel the composition, that the whole pre-edit text is in the query the next frame filters with, and that the field claims the keyboard back when another widget takes it. Before the fix it failed on the first letter: "typing `n` cancelled the composition".

Verified on 470ea7a3: the test above, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, and `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` (all clean).

Found by typing Chinese into Quick Apply on Windows 11 with Microsoft Pinyin.

title: fix(export): prevent OOM crashes via memory-budget batching and encoder optimizations
author: thanhcong2k7
body:
### Summary
Fixes an issue where video and sequence exports caused excessive memory consumption, leading to system out-of-memory (OOM) crashes on 16GB RAM systems within seconds of starting a render.

Previously, `batch_size()` determined frame concurrency solely based on logical CPU threads (`rayon::current_num_threads().clamp(2, 16)`). On multi-threaded CPUs (e.g. 6-core / 12-thread), this spawned up to 12 concurrent frame renders regardless of composition complexity or resolution. Because each frame evaluates 32-bit float (`f32`) RGBA rasters along with intermediate effect/layer buffers, concurrent allocations easily exceeded physical memory limits. Additionally, batch frames were retained in a `Vec` throughout the batch lifecycle, and per-row heap allocations during YUV conversion caused severe allocator churn.

### Changes
- **`crates/render-export/src/lib.rs`**:
  - Replaced thread-only `batch_size()` with `dynamic_batch_size(w, h)`. Concurrency is now dynamically calculated based on a safe memory budget (~2.5 GB) and physical core limits rather than raw logical thread counts.
  - Updated `sequence` and `gif_export` to pass dimensions to `dynamic_batch_size(w, h)`.
  - Added unit tests verifying batch size scaling across resolutions (tiny, 720p, 1080p, 4K) and edge cases.
- **`crates/render-export/src/encode.rs`**:
  - Updated movie export to use `dynamic_batch_size(w, h)`.
  - Eagerly freed frame buffers using `.drain(..)` during the encode loop, immediately dropping each frame's memory after consumption rather than holding the entire batch.
  - Optimized `rgba_to_yuv420` by removing per-row heap allocations (`vec![(0f32, 0f32, 0f32); cw]`) inside parallel chunks, eliminating allocator contention and fragmentation across Rayon threads.
  - Added a unit test validating YUV conversion accuracy across multi-row dimensions.

### Testing
- **Unit Tests**: Ran `cargo test` to verify all existing and newly added regression tests pass (`dynamic_batch_size_scales_with…

title: EPS: idiv and mod of -2^63 by -1 no longer panic
author: dotCooCoo
body:
The EPS interpreter's `idiv` and `mod` checked only for a zero divisor before computing `(a as i64) / (b as i64)` and `(a as i64) % (b as i64)`. `i64::MIN / -1` and `i64::MIN % -1` overflow, and `/` and `%` panic on them in debug and release builds. The cast turns any operand at or below -2^63 into `i64::MIN`. On `main`, `effectcraft_pdf::parse` panicked with "attempt to divide with overflow" on an EPS file with `-9223372036854775808 -1 idiv`. With `mod` in place of `idiv`, it panicked with "attempt to calculate the remainder with overflow".

## What changes (`crates/pdf/src/ps.rs`)

The `idiv` and `mod` arms use `checked_div` and `checked_rem` with `unwrap_or(0)`, as the PDF calculator in `crates/pdf/src/color.rs` has done since #575. For `i64::MIN` by -1, `idiv` and `mod` give 0, which is also their result for a zero divisor. Other results are unchanged. VectorCraft's EPS interpreter also uses `checked_div` and `checked_rem` for these operators: https://github.com/storytold/vectorcraft/blob/0d0ea352df99044589a7ce0efc7004f7a5b6b7c0/crates/eps/src/import/interp.rs#L581-L585

## Tests (`crates/pdf/src/tests_import.rs`)

The programs in `postscript_idiv_and_mod_of_i64_min_by_minus_one_give_zero` fill a rectangle only when `idiv` or `mod` returns the expected value. They cover dividends at or below -2^63 with divisors that truncate to -1 (`-9223372036854775808 -1`, `-99999999999999999999 -1.5` and `2 63 exp neg -1`, result 0), divisors that truncate to 0 (`7 0` and `7 0.5`, result 0), and `-7 2` (-3 and -1). With `main`'s `ps.rs`, the test fails with "attempt to divide with overflow". With only `idiv` changed, it fails with "attempt to calculate the remainder with overflow".

`cargo test -p effectcraft-pdf --lib` (81 pass) and `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-pdf --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass. On top of `main` at 470ea7a, `cargo xtask ci` passed fmt and clippy and stopped in its test step. On the test machine, Homebrew's ffmpeg 6.0 (`ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`) does not st…

title: #1221: two path-format test failures on Windows

body:

title: Keyframes: two identical Position keys hold instead of detouring (#1196, #1197)
author: vbasky
body:
## Problem
A pair of Position (or any spatial) keyframes with the same value, sitting between moving neighbours, evaluates through the auto-Bezier cubic whose control handles point at the neighbouring keys. The object loops away from the point and back — jitter on linear keys, and a visible detour after Easy Ease (F9). Equal-value pairs are exactly the case where no motion is wanted (#1196: 'ideally as the keyframes are same there should be no motion', #1197: 'duplicate equal-value keyframes still produce incorrect behaviour').

## Fix
In `crates/keyframe`:
- `segment_value`: a spatial segment whose endpoints coincide returns the key value — no arc-length walk along the tangent loop.
- `spatial_segment_length`: a zero-chord segment counts as length 0, so Rove Across Time splits such runs by value distance instead of loop length.

The viewer motion-path overlay samples `value_at`, so the drawn path now matches the held position.

## Tests
- New regression test `tests::equal_value_spatial_keys_do_not_detour` (linear and easy-eased chains) — fails without the guard, passes with it.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-keyframe`: 38 passed. `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-keyframe -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` clean. Full `cargo xtask ci` left to this PR's CI run.

Closes #1196
Closes #1197

title: Shortcuts: panel and context scopes, one chord per scope [skip ci]
author: pravdomil
body:
First of a series that closes the gaps in EffectCraft's default keyboard shortcuts. This one adds no keys: it is the groundwork the next ones need.

## Problem
Every menu and engine command was application-wide; only frontend commands had a scope, guessed from their id. So one chord could not run one command in a panel and another elsewhere (Split Layer and Duplicate Render Item on `Cmd+Shift+D`, Copy with Property Links and Remember Interpretation on `Cmd+Alt+C`, the text-formatting chords while editing text…).

## Change
- A shortcut belongs to the application, a **panel** (Project, Timeline, Render Queue…) or a **context** (editing text, a paint or camera tool active, a mask selected).
- The narrowest active scope runs a chord: active context → focused panel → the panel sharing its shortcuts (Timeline ↔ Composition) → application.
- A context's shortcuts never run outside it. A panel's shortcut that nothing nearer claims still runs from the other panels, as before, so no key that works today stops working.
- Conflicts: the same chord in two scopes is an *override* (both keep working; `shortcuts.set` reports it with `overrides: true`). `shortcuts.conflicts` now lists only two commands of one scope on one chord.
- Scoped now, keys unchanged: Remember / Apply Interpretation and Delete Project Items Without Confirmation (Project), Duplicate Render Item (Render Queue).

title: Shapes: Merge Paths no longer erases paint belonging to a group above it
author: vbasky
body:
Refs #1174 (the Merge Paths items; midpoint snapping and child rotation are not covered here)

## Bug
Adding Merge Paths to a shape layer's Contents — the natural UI position, below the group holding the shape and its fill — removed the whole render. collect() flattened every nested draw into one list, and the merge branch did draws.clear() to implement AE's 'paint above the merge in the same group does not render'. That also dropped paint belonging to groups *above* the merge, which in AE keeps rendering inside its own group.

## Fix (crates/render/src/shapes.rs)
- Draw gains a local flag: true for fill/stroke/gradient items at the current contents level, cleared when draws bubble up from a nested group.
- Merge Paths retains !local draws instead of clearing everything; same-level paint above it is still dropped, so the existing merge_add_feeds_fill_below_and_drops_paint_above behaviour is unchanged.
- The merged path itself was already fed whole to operators and paint below the merge (the second #1174 symptom had the same root cause: everything, including the paint below, appeared erased).

## Tests
- New regression merge_paths_below_a_group_keeps_the_group_paint (Merge and Add modes); it fails on main with alpha 0 everywhere (the exact report) and passes with the fix.
- cargo test -p effectcraft-render --lib: 217 passed. fmt and clippy -D warnings clean.

Closes #1174

title: #1267: three relink path-format test failures on Windows
author: vangel76
body:
Fixes #1267.

## What this does

Three relink tests (from #1106) fail on Windows on `main`. The app is fine; the tests compare path strings. On Windows the relink code writes the paths it derives with `/`, while the tests build their expected paths with `PathBuf::join`, which mixes `\` and `/`. - **`effectcraft-host` `replacing_a_missing_file_relinks_the_others_that_moved_with_it`:** uses `Path::starts_with` instead of a string prefix check.

`Path` comparison is by components, so the tests behave the same on macOS and Linux.

## Finding
Shortcuts on the numeric keypad can't be told apart from the main row. `egui-winit` 0.36 maps `Numpad0`–`Numpad9` to `Key::Num0`–`Num9`, `NumpadAdd` to `Plus`, `NumpadSubtract` to `Minus`, `NumpadDivide` to `Slash` and `NumpadEnter` to `Enter`, for both the logical and the physical key, and eframe gives the app no access to the winit event. - Add Marker: also `Ctrl+8`.
- Preview (Alt+Numpad 0): also `Ctrl+Alt+0`.
- Defaults that use Control alone apply on macOS only; elsewhere Control is `Cmd`, so they would be a different chord and are left out rather than shown as keys that never fire.
- A frontend command can list several default keys (`"Alt+Num0, Ctrl+Alt+0"`).

title: Render: remove the blanket layer cover; per-effect padding already covers what needs it
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #1205

## Problem
Every text or shape layer with an enabled video effect paid a blanket `target.cover(layer_size)` before its stack ran, growing the effect buffer to the comp-sized layer rectangle. A glow or blur never uses that room: each of the 8 layers of the reported comp (and every frame in flight) allocated a 1920x1080 RGBA32F texture (~33 MB) on GPU via `GpuFx::cover`, and the same size again through the CPU readback/upload path — the measured ~5 GB VRAM gap.

## Fix
- Remove the blanket cover call in `Renderer::run_effects_on`, the `FxTarget::cover` trait method (and its CPU default), and the GPU `GpuTarget::cover` allocation.
- Effects that place pixels outside the painted content already pad exactly what they need — CC Tiler and CC Smear via `layer_cover_pad` (CPU `Buf::pad`, GPU `GBuf::pad`), CC Mosaic sharp likewise — so #659 semantics are preserved where they matter. Displacement-family effects keep their existing `resizeLayer`/`expandOutput` grow options and sample transparent outside the buffer exactly as they sampled the blanket's transparent margin before, so their output is pixel-identical while their buffers stay content-sized.

## Tests
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-render -p effectcraft-effects -p effectcraft-gpu --lib`: 212 + 449 + 216 passed — including the #659 tiling-across-layer-region and centred-shape edge-pinning regressions and the full GPU parity suites.
- fmt + clippy -D warnings clean. GPU parity comparisons skip on this adapterless box; CI covers them.

Closes #1205.

title: Viewer: mouse-wheel scrubbing over the Composition monitor (#1218)
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #1218

## Behaviour
A physical mouse wheel hovered over the Composition monitor now steps the playhead frame by frame, as After Effects 2023+ does: one notch per frame (line-unit scroll), clamped to 30 frames per frame of UI input, and a running preview is stopped first so the scrub is visible. Trackpad scroll (point-unit), pinch, and Ctrl/Cmd+wheel keep zooming around the pointer; the wheel's share of `smooth_scroll_delta` is subtracted from the zoom delta using egui's own `line_scroll_speed`, so a scrubbing wheel does not also zoom.

Heads-up: open PR #1036 (trackpad gestures: two-finger pan, pinch zoom) is untouched by the point-unit path here; if both merge, wheel-over-monitor scrubs while trackpad two-finger pans, which matches how AE separates the inputs.

## Tests
- New harness test `mouse_wheel_over_the_monitor_scrubs_frames` (scrub up/down with a line wheel; Ctrl+wheel zooms and does not move time).
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --test ui_viewer`: 61 passed; lib: 257 passed; ui_layer_panel_zoom, ui_panels, ui_camera_tracker green. fmt + clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean.

title: Colour picker: eyedropper that samples the Composition monitor (#1211)
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #1211

Stacked note: this branch contains #1218's wheel-scrub commit because the picker code sits where that edit lands; when #1218 merges, rebase this (or the maintainer can land this second; the two hunks don't conflict).

## What it does
The AE-style colour popup (the one that opens from any colour swatch: Effect Controls, Properties, Character/Paragraph fills, gradient stops, Solid Settings…) grows an **Eyedropper** button beside OK/Cancel. Arming it turns the Composition monitor into a sample target: the next click there reads the colour *shown* at that pixel — the rendered frame composited over the comp background, full resolution — and the popup instantly follows with the new HSB/RGB/hex. Crosshair cursor while armed; one sample per arm (AE behaves the same); closing the popup clears the arm.

## Implementation

title: CC Particle World: motion blur (#1195)
author: vbasky
body:
Closes #1195

## What it does
When both the composition's and the layer's motion-blur switches are on, the renderer already passes every effect the comp shutter (angle, phase, samples) through `EffectEnv::shutter`. CC Particle World now honours it: the stepped simulation is sampled at 2..64 instants across the shutter (the comp's Samples Per Frame, clamped as Transform does), each instant's sprite field is splatted, the fields are averaged, and the averaged image meets the layer through the sprite plan's existing Transfer Mode post (Composite/Screen/Add/Black Background). Fast particles draw motion trails instead of a frozen sharp field.

The GPU particle pass defers to the CPU for the shutter case (`catalog::gpu_supported`, mirroring how Turbulent Displace's locked pinning and Cell Pattern's HQ variants already fall back), so CPU and GPU previews agree; all other settings keep the GPU path.

Also factored `Post::apply` out of `SpritePlan::finish` so the blurred average can reuse the exact same post logic.

## Tests
- `sim::tests::particle_world_motion_blur_trails`: with a 360-degree shutter the output differs from the sharp frame, lights more pixels, and keeps alpha energy within tolerance.
- `catalog` test: `gpu_supported("ec.sim.ccparticleworld")` is false while the shutter is open, true otherwise.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-effects --lib`: 450 passed; `-p effectcraft-gpu --lib`: 212 passed; fmt + clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean.

Closes #1195.

title: Menus: switch open top-level menus on hover (#1290)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Fixes #1290. Also covers the hover-switching part of #1072.

## What was wrong
The in-window menu bar is egui's `MenuBar` with `ui.menu_button`, which opens a menu only on a click. Once one menu was open, moving to another title did nothing, so every menu took its own click. After Effects, Windows and macOS menu bars all switch on hover, and so does PhotoCraft.

## Change
`menu_bar` now collects the top-level title responses and calls a new `switch_on_hover` before the keyboard handler (`menu_keys::handle`). This is adapted from PhotoCraft's helper. It only acts when all of these hold:
- one of the bar's menus is already open (hovering a closed bar does nothing);
- the pointer is somewhere other than where the bar last saw it, so a pointer resting on File can't undo Left / Right. The last position is kept every frame, in egui's temp data, as `None` while the pointer is outside the window. That makes a pointer coming back into the window count as moving. egui's `pointer.delta()` is zero for that first position, so it can't be used here.
- the pointer is over another title's `interact_rect`, that title's layer is topmost there, and the title is enabled. A submenu or dialog over the bar keeps the pointer, and under a dialog the app is disabled.

It then opens that title's existing popup with `Popup::open_id` (which closes the other one) and requests a repaint. `Response::hovered()` isn't used because it's false while a menu's popup is open.

Unchanged: menu ids, command dispatch, translations, styling, the keyboard navigation and the close behaviour. There's no new dependency. Opening a menu on mouse-down and press-drag-release selection, also requested in #1072, are left for a separate change.

## Tests (`tests/ui_menus.rs`)
- Hovering the titles with every menu closed opens nothing.
- Click File, then hover Edit: Edit opens and File closes, then back to File. Space still doesn't start the preview behind the menu, Escape closes it, and hovering afterwards opens nothin…

title: Scripting: add the missing app.preferences.saveToDisk() so imported scripts like Duik get past startup (#1263)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1263.

Duik Angela calls `app.preferences.saveToDisk()` at startup (line 85). The scripting prelude's `app.preferences` stub had `reload()` and the `getPref*`/`savePref*` family, but no `saveToDisk`, so the call threw `TypeError: not a callable function`.

title: UI: colour expression-driven numeric values consistently (refs #1072)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Closes #1306. Refs #1072 (one item of its checklist).

A property driven by an expression showed its value in the ordinary blue. After Effects shows it **red**: its docs describe blue as the pre-expression value colour and red as the expression-driven one ([Expression basics](https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/work-with-expressions/expression-basics/expression-basics.html)). The values now turn red in the **Timeline**, **Effect Controls** and the **Properties** panel.

## How
- **`Tokens::for_value(expression)`** returns the theme tokens with `hot_text` **and** `accent_hover` set to `expr_text`, the existing expression colour, which differs between dark and light themes. The number widget paints in `accent_hover` while hovered or dragged, so changing `hot_text` alone would turn a hovered value blue again.
- **The three panels** derive these value-only tokens from `Property::has_expression()` (an enabled, non-empty expression) every frame. So disabling or removing an expression turns the value blue again, with no extra state:
  - the Timeline's `value_editor`
  - Effect Controls' parameter rows
  - the Properties panel's `transform_row`
- **Only the values change:** the number and angle fields, plus the Timeline's vector `,` separator and plain enum number. A vector or angle is never half red and half blue. Names, stopwatches, keyframe buttons, link icons, dropdowns and colour swatches keep the ordinary tokens.
- **Red means an expression drives the value, not that it evaluated.** Broken expressions keep their existing error reporting.

No dependency, project-format, translation or version change.

## Checks (Windows 10, Rust 1.95, release)
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo +1.95 clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --no-deps --all-targets --release -- -D warnings`: pass.
- `ui_expression_values` (5/5) reads the **colour the value text is actually painted in** (the frame's text shapes inside each value's area):
  - Each property names the panels that must show it.…

title: Effects & Presets: drag animation presets onto a layer
author: LloydNicholson
body:
## Problem
Animation presets in **Effects & Presets** (text presets, built-in Transitions and user `.ecpreset` files) can only be applied by double-click. Dragging one onto a layer does nothing: no drag ghost, no drop highlight, no undo entry. Effects already drag and drop fine, and After Effects lets you drag presets onto a layer.

The cause: `preset_row` used `Sense::click()` only and never set a `DragPayload`.

## Fix
- New `DragPayload::Preset { preset: PresetRef, name }`. `PresetRef` (Text / Builtin / File) maps a preset to its command (`layer.applyTextPreset`, `anim.applyBuiltinPreset`, `anim.applyPreset`), and `apply_to(layer)` adds the target (`layer` for text presets, `layers` for the others).
- Preset rows are now `click_and_drag` and start that drag. The existing drag ghost shows the preset's name.
- The **Timeline** (name column and time graph), **Composition viewer** (layer under the pointer, outlined) and **Effect Controls** apply a dropped preset to that layer, the same way they already handle effects.
- Double-click still applies to the selected layers, now through the same `PresetRef::command()`.

## Testing
- New unit test: `preset_drops_target_the_layer_with_each_commands_param`.
- Headless `snapshot` runs with `ui.drag` on the demo project:
  - Typewriter onto a Timeline layer row: applied ("Undo Apply Text Preset Typewriter").
  - Typewriter onto a layer's time bar: applied.
  - Fade In (Transitions) onto a Timeline layer: applied.
  - Fade In onto a layer in the Composition viewer: applied.
  - Blur In onto Effect Controls: applied.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings` are clean, and the ui-egui tests pass. I did not run the full `cargo xtask ci`.

title: Masks: addVertex and setVertex fill in missing tangents of a loaded path (#1250)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1250.

## What was wrong
A path's `vertices`, `in_tangents` and `out_tangents` deserialize independently, and nothing on load makes them agree. `mask.new` pads the tangents, but a path read from a project file can carry fewer tangents than vertices. `mask.addVertex` bounded its index by the vertices only and then inserted into both tangent arrays, and `mask.setVertex` indexed the tangent arrays after the same check, so either command panicked on such a path (`Vec` insert/index out of bounds, `mask.rs:209` for setVertex).

## Fix
- `ShapePath::fit_tangents` (crates/keyframe): gives both tangent arrays one entry per vertex. Missing tangents become zero (a corner), extras are dropped, and it reports whether anything changed.
- `edit_path_counted` (crates/engine/src/commands/mask.rs) calls it on the value it is about to edit, so every vertex command routed through `edit_path`/`edit_path_counted` works on a consistent path, not just these two. `convertVertex`, segment splitting and RotoBezier smoothing already padded locally; other keyframes of an animated path are padded by `apply_count_op` when the vertex count changes.

The fix is at the point of use rather than at load, matching how the rest of the mask code treats paths. Rendering and interpolation already tolerate the mismatch (`lerp` zips the arrays). A load-time repair note for paths would need a walk over every layer's property tree, which I left out to keep this small. Happy to add it if you'd prefer it there.

## Tests
- `tests_timeline::vertex_commands_fill_in_missing_tangents_of_a_loaded_path` and `…_of_a_loaded_animated_path`: save the project, cut every mask path's tangent arrays to one entry (static value and keyframes), reopen through `Project::from_json` + `replace_project`, then run `mask.setVertex` (with tangents) and `mask.addVertex`. They check that the arrays end up the same length, that the set tangents land, that a missing tangent becomes a corner, and (animated) that the other key gains t…

title: Export: a cancelled or failed overwrite keeps the previous output (#1230)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1230.

## What was wrong
`out::create` opened the destination with `File::create`, which truncates an existing file immediately, and `Cx::create` recorded every path for the cancel cleanup whether or not it existed before. So cancelling a render over an earlier one deleted the earlier render, and a failure part-way left a truncated file.

## Fix (crates/export)
- **out.rs:** on disk, an `Out` now writes to a hidden temporary sibling (`.<name>.<pid>-<n>.part`, opened with `create_new` so it never reuses or follows an existing file). `Out::finish` flushes, closes and renames it over the destination; the rename stays on one volume because the temp file is in the same folder. A `FileOut` dropped unfinished (any error, or a cancel) removes its temporary file and leaves the destination untouched. If the rename itself fails (e.g. the old file is locked by a player on Windows), the temp file is removed and the error names the destination. The in-memory `Sink` (web) is unchanged.
- **pipeline.rs:** `Cx::create` only records a path for the cancel cleanup when the file didn't exist before the job. A sequence frame that was already there keeps its old contents, or holds the new frame if that frame finished before the cancel; it is never deleted.

All writers (MP4/MOV, WebM VP9/AV1, GIF, image sequences, audio, logs) already go through `Cx::create` and call `finish()` on success, so they all get this.

## Tests (crates/export/tests/render_settings.rs)
- `cancelling_an_export_over_an_existing_file_keeps_the_previous_render`: H.264 over an existing `clip.mp4`, cancelled after the movie file is open, leaves it byte for byte (**on main it's deleted**). A PNG sequence over 50 existing frames removes none of them (**on main frame 0 is deleted**). No temporary files are left behind.
- `a_finished_export_replaces_the_existing_file`: the new movie replaces the old one and the reported size matches.
- The existing `cancelled_export_removes_only_files_it_opened` still passes (new fi…

title: Project: refuse a file whose id counter is exhausted (#1251)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1251.

## What was wrong
`Project::alloc` (and the builder's `Ids::alloc`) increment `next_id` with an unchecked `+= 1`. Loading kept whatever counter a file carried: `fix_next_id` saturates stored ids to `u64::MAX` and raises the counter to match, but nothing refused the result. After opening such a file, the first new layer, key or effect panicked on overflow (debug) or wrapped to ids already in use (release).

## Fix
- `limits::MAX_NEXT_ID` (`u64::MAX − 2³²`) bounds the id counter. `Project::from_json_repaired`, which every way of loading a project goes through (File ▸ Open, Import Project, templates, web restore, remote, offload), now refuses a file whose counter or ids reach past it: `project ids reach …, past the largest this version can allocate safely (…)`.
- A project at the limit still leaves room for four billion more allocations, far more than any session makes, so the unchecked increment can't be reached. That avoids threading a `Result` through every allocation site.
- `file.importProject` checks the combined offset (`sub.next_id + base`) against the same bound instead of only checking for overflow.

The template-offset collision (#1229) is a separate path and isn't changed here.

## Tests
- `project` (limits.rs): `a_file_whose_ids_reach_the_limit_is_refused` covers the counter at `u64::MAX`, the counter just past the bound, a layer id at the top and a property uid at the top. **On main the first case opens.** `a_file_just_below_the_limit_opens_and_allocates_fresh_ids` checks the boundary still opens and that new ids come after every id in the file.
- `engine` (tests_limits.rs): `a_project_whose_id_counter_is_exhausted_is_refused_and_the_session_carries_on`: `file.open` and `file.importProject` on an exhausted file both fail with the error, the open project is untouched, and `layer.newSolid` keeps allocating from its own counter. **On main `file.open` opens the file.**
