title: #1274: OBJ textures load when map_Kd names an absolute path
author: LloydNicholson
body:
An MTL written on another machine names its textures by absolute paths (C:\Users\…\checker.png). The media pool joins names onto the model's folder, so such a path replaced the folder and the texture was silently dropped: the model rendered flat in its Kd colour.

- Texture and mtllib names are tried as written, then with `\` read as a separator, then as the bare file name next to the model.
- map_* options are skipped by their argument counts, so file names may contain spaces (`-o 0.5 0.5 my checker.png`).
- A missing or undecodable texture, or a missing mtllib, logs a warning.

Kd still tints map_Kd (left for the maintainers, as asked in the issue).

title: Masks: repair short tangent arrays in vertex commands instead of panicking (#1250)
author: saadkhantareen
body:
Fixes #1250

## Summary

`ShapePath` vertices and the two tangent arrays deserialize independently, and a loaded project can hold fewer tangents than vertices. `mask.setVertex` validated only against `vertices.len()` before indexing the tangent arrays, `mask.addVertex` inserted into them at a vertex-bounded index, and `mask.deleteVertices` removed from them unguarded — all three panicked on such a path (the session's panic guard turned it into an opaque command error).

## Changes

- `effectcraft-keyframe`: new `ShapePath::normalize_tangents()` restoring the one-tangent-pair-per-vertex invariant — missing tangents become `[0.0; 2]` (corner, the same default `ShapePath::polygon` and `mask.new` use), surplus tangents are dropped, existing ones untouched. This is the same resize the neighbouring `mask.convertVertex`, `split_segment` and `roto_smooth` already do inline, factored into one helper.
- `effectcraft-engine`: `mask.addVertex`, `mask.setVertex` and `mask.deleteVertices` call it before mutating the tangent arrays.

Well-formed paths are unaffected (normalizing a matching path is a no-op).

Scope note: this repairs the three commands the issue names. Normalizing at load time (in `Project::from_json_repaired`) would cover every other reader too, but changes what a loaded file looks like before any edit; happy to add that instead/as well if maintainers prefer it.

## Tests

- keyframe: `normalize_tangents_pads_short_arrays_with_corners`, `normalize_tangents_truncates_long_arrays_and_keeps_matching_ones` — `cargo test -p effectcraft-keyframe`: 112 unit + 17 doc/integration tests passed.
- engine: `vertex_commands_repair_short_tangent_arrays_from_loaded_paths` — truncates a mask path's tangents in the project (the loaded-file state) and runs setVertex / addVertex / deleteVertices through the command API, asserting success and equal lengths (passed; neighbouring viewer suite 21/21 and mask-filtered tests 21/21 also pass).

title: GPU: contain frame-local validation failures (refs #1319)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Refs #1319. This is "refs", not "fixes": the reporter's first failure is still unknown. This PR stops that kind of failure from turning off the GPU compositor for the rest of the session, and makes the next report say which texture failed.

## What was wrong
- **`Gpu::within_memory` (the guard around each viewer frame) only had OutOfMemory and Internal error scopes.** A Validation error, like the reported `Texture::create_view: Texture with '' label is invalid`, escaped as an uncaptured error. The desktop app's handler then retires the GPU compositor, and preview stays on the CPU until restart. One way this happens: a texture allocation fails, the code goes on with the invalid texture, and its `create_view` is then a validation error that the allocation scopes don't catch.
- **A failed frame's textures could go back into the reuse pool.** Its result was dropped only after the pool was emptied, so pooled textures in it went back in. Even in the right order, emptying the pool cleared only its free list. A texture released while another frame's encoder was still open waited in `released`, and became free (and reusable) when that encoder closed.
- **Working textures had no label**, so the error couldn't say which texture failed. The empty label in the report fits these working textures (`GpuContext::texture`). The viewer's display texture is labelled `viewer frame`.

## Changes
- `within_memory` also pushes a Validation scope. On any scoped error it reports every error, allocation errors first (`…; then: …`). It drops the failed result, then frees everything kept for reuse with a new `GpuContext::discard_kept`: uploads, staging buffers, the shared zero textures, the particle checkpoints and the texture pool. For the pool, `Pool::discard` drops the free textures, those waiting for an open encoder, and those kept by a live encoder, and raises a pool generation. A texture taken before the failure is then never handed back to the pool. The encoders' bookkeeping (`open`, ids…

title: Fix autosave retries after failed background writes
author: onlymoein
body:
A failed background autosave previously marked its revision as saved and advanced the recovery path and rotation slot before the write finished. Later ticks could then skip the unchanged dirty revision indefinitely.

Commit autosave bookkeeping only after a successful write for the originating project. Pending writes retain the snapshot's revision, slot, project path and project-instance counter. Completion cannot mark newer edits as saved or publish A's snapshot as B's recovery copy after Open or Save As; reopening the same path is also a new project instance. Failed writes keep the previous recovery snapshot and slot, and ticks retry the unchanged revision without blocking on an in-flight write.

Closes #1231.

## Validation

- All 43 settings tests pass, including the original failed-write retry and edits-during-save regressions.
- Three permanent transition regressions hold A's writer until after the path/project switch, then fail the final recovery-record reset: Open B, reopen the same path, and Save As. They verify the retained record, recovery offered on the next launch, and unchanged destination file bytes for Open. All three pass against upstream `main`, fail with the prior PR implementation, and pass with the fix.
- Full `cargo xtask ci`: passed (3,413 tests passed, 26 existing tests ignored; formatting, release Clippy with warnings denied, dependency layering, asset attribution and all 32 WASM crates).
- `git diff --check`: clean.

Rebased on `main` at `2c08f675`. Validated on macOS ARM64 / Rust 1.99.0 with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16`.

title: Reject corrupt benchmark results and incomplete regression evidence

Select the latest run for each key before checking success, and require matching successful runs with at least one comparable resource metric per key when gating. Exploratory comparisons remain available without `--fail-over`, and latest failures remain visible in the table. Blank lines, unavailable platform metrics, and zero-frame project-open runs stay supported.

Closes #1303.
Closes #1245.

All four fail before the fix and pass afterward; all 18 xtask tests pass. title: Prevent duplicate automation edits after lost replies
author: onlymoein
body:
The automation bridge could apply an engine command twice when the app executed it but closed the connection before its reply arrived. The client treated EOF and transport errors as safe to reconnect and resend.

Retry only explicitly read-only control queries. Engine commands, UI edits and unknown methods now return an actionable unknown-outcome error after ambiguous transmission/reply failures, then reconnect on the next call. Playback status remains retryable; play/stop/toggle and its default toggle do not. Timeouts and malformed replies remain unresent, with unknown-outcome context for mutations. Request-ID exhaustion returns an error instead of overflowing.

Closes #1247.

Validation: a synthetic loopback server executes `comp.new` and drops the reply, reproducing duplicate application before the fix. Seven new bridge tests cover lost/malformed mutation replies, unknown methods, read-only retries, playback status versus edits, and connection failure before the app starts. All 46 automation unit tests and 8 QA integration tests pass. Full `cargo xtask ci` passes formatting, release Clippy with warnings denied, workspace tests, layering, assets and all 32 WASM crates. `git diff --check` is clean.

Validated on macOS ARM64 / Rust 1.99.0 with `RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6 CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_CODEGEN_UNITS=16`.

title: Ease Presets: apply incoming and outgoing easing to selected keyframes (#1329)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Closes #1329.

The Ease Presets panel only eased **pairs of neighbouring selected keyframes**. A single selected key, keys that aren't neighbours, or one key on each of several properties changed nothing. `selectedPairs()` found no pairs, so `applyCurve()` had nothing to do.

## What changes
- **An Ease selector: In, Out, In-Out** (In-Out by default, ScriptUI name `mode` so agents can set it). It applies to both preset clicks and **Apply**.
  - **In** eases each selected key's incoming side with the curve's in side (In % and Speed).
  - **Out** eases its outgoing side with the curve's out side.
  - **In-Out** eases both sides.
- **A side is eased when it has a neighbouring key**, selected or not. The neighbour isn't changed. The first key only has an out side to ease, and the last key only an in side.
- **Each side scales to its own segment.** For example, `0 → 100` over 1 s then `100 → 20` over 2 s average **+100/s** and **−40/s**, so the in and out speeds differ. It reuses `slopes()`: per dimension, and along the motion path for spatial properties.
- **The side not eased keeps playing as it did** (the existing `easeSide()`): a Hold stays a Hold, and an auto-Bezier side keeps its shape.
- **One undo step**, "Apply Ease Preset". All sides are measured before any key changes. When no selected key has a segment on the chosen side, no undo step opens and the status says which neighbour is missing.
- **Roving keyframes are skipped**, and the status says how many ("…; skipped 1 roving keyframe(s); turn off Roving to ease them"). A roving key passes speed straight through: the engine keeps both its sides linear on every key edit (`retime_roving`), so an ease set on one would never play. Before, the panel reported such a key as eased. The old pair-only panel did the same for a pair containing a roving key. If only roving keys are selected, nothing changes and no undo step opens. Fixed keys next to a roving key still ease.
- **From Keys** still reads the curve between a sel…

title: Templates: refuse ids that would collide instead of merging items (#1229)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1229.

## What was wrong
- `essential::offset_ids` shifted every id with `saturating_add` and reinserted items by their new id. Two distinct ids near `u64::MAX` both became `u64::MAX`, and the later item replaced the earlier one, silently dropping it.
- `essential.importTemplate` skipped the range check that `file.importProject` does and computed the manifest comp as an unchecked `tcomp.0 + base`.
- It also extracted the template's media to disk before any of this was checked.

## Fix
- **crates/project/src/essential.rs:** `offset_ids` now returns `Result<(), OffsetError>`. Every shifted id (items, layers, property uids, Essential Graphics controls and the references to them) uses `checked_add`. An item whose shifted id is already taken (a damaged file whose map key and `id` disagree) is refused too, so distinct objects stay distinct. On error the throwaway project is left part-way shifted and the callers discard it.
- **essential.importTemplate:** remaps the ids and checks the manifest comp first. The comp id must shift without overflow and be a composition of the template. Only then does it write media or edit the project, so a refused template changes nothing: no items, no counter change, no instance, no `<name> Media` folder.

title: Composition Mini-Flowchart: Tab from the Timeline and viewer, focus navigation with every branch, as in After Effects
author: Themolx
body:
> **Discord:** themolx (ArtCraft Discord) · long-time After Effects power user

## What

The **Composition Mini-Flowchart** existed (Composition menu, navigator button, Tab binding) but in practice:
- **Tab never opened it** from the Timeline or viewer: egui's own Tab focus traversal took the press first (it moved keyboard focus to the toolbar);
- it showed only one level on each side of the active comp, so you couldn't move through a chain of precomps or see where a comp branches.

Now it works like After Effects:
- **Tab** toggles it while the Composition, Layer or Timeline panel is active. Tab in a text field, a dialog or during keyboard traversal keeps its widget meaning.
- It opens at the pointer with the **focused comp** (the active one at first) in the centre, the comps that nest it on the left and the comps it nests on the right.
- **Left / Right** move the focus to a neighbour (back the way they came first). The comp the focus arrives on shows **all its branches at once**, so a comp that nests several precomps shows them all without reopening the popup. **Up / Down** move between the focus's siblings in its column.
- The **camera stays on the focus** and the flowchart slides around it; the popup grows with every level instead of clipping it.
- The active comp keeps the accent colour, the focus is outlined. **Enter** opens the focused comp, **Escape** or **Tab** closes, a click on a comp opens it; a node's small arrow expands one more level.
- Walks are cycle- and depth-bounded (12 levels of 64 comps).

## How

- `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`: Tab dispatches the Mini-Flowchart when the active panel owns the focus (a focused widget inside it gives Tab up), before egui's traversal.
- `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/precomp.rs`: `NestGraph` (one pass over the layers), `MiniLayout` around the focus, `mini_nav` (focus moves, siblings, slide offset) and the popup drawing; `MiniFlowState` in `state.rs`.

title: Templates: extract media only inside the template's media folder (#1227)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1227.

## What was wrong
`essential.importTemplate` stripped `media/` from each archive entry, wrote it at `media_dir.join(rel)` and created its parent folders first. `Path::join` doesn't confine its argument, so:
- a name with `..`, a root or a drive left the `<name> Media` folder;
- a symbolic link in the way (the media folder or a folder in it) redirected the write;
- failed writes were skipped silently.

Under `--automation-read-root`, `essential.importTemplate` counted only as a read of the archive, so the files it extracted ignored the write roots.

## Fix
**Engine (`crates/engine/src/commands/essential.rs`)**
- Every media entry is checked **before anything is written**. Its path after `media/` must be plain folder and file names: no `..`, `.`, empty parts, root, `:` (drive or alternate stream) or NUL, and `\\` is read as a separator. A template with any bad entry is refused with nothing extracted and the project untouched.
- The media folder and every folder between it and the file must not be symbolic links. This is checked before and after creating the folders.
- A failed write now fails the import and removes the files this import created; files that were already there are left alone.
- `essential.templateInfo` also reports `mediaFiles` and `mediaFolder`.

**Automation (`crates/automation/src/confine.rs`, `backend.rs`)**
- `essential.importTemplate` gets a `Lookup::TemplateMedia`: before it runs, the backend asks `essential.templateInfo` where the media would go. A template with media needs that folder inside a write root; one without media still needs only read access. In `engine.batch` it is refused like the other commands that write files they aren't given (the message now says so).

## Tests
- **engine (tests_essential.rs)**
  - `template_media_that_would_land_outside_its_folder_is_refused_before_anything_is_written` covers seven escaping names (`../`, `1/../../`, `..\\`, `//etc/passwd`, `C:/`, `./`, empty). Each is paired with a harmless entry…

title: Atomic writes: a unique, exclusively created temp file per write (#1233)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1233.

## What was wrong
`config::atomic_write` always wrote through `<name>.tmp`, opened with `File::create`. Every native project save (`Services::write_file`), the media cache and the settings store go through it, so:
- **Concurrent writers** of the same file shared that path. They truncated each other's data, and the later `rename` failed with `NotFound` once the first had moved the temp file away. A failure's cleanup could also remove the other writer's temp.
- **Anything already at the predictable name**, a symbolic link included, was followed and overwritten.

## Fix (crates/engine/src/config.rs)
- Each write creates its own temporary file next to the destination, `.<name>.<pid>-<n>.tmp`, with `create_new`. Two writers never share one, and nothing that's already at that name is opened or followed (a name in use is skipped).
- The writer gets the already-open file, so nothing reopens the path. A failed write **or rename** removes only its own temp file.
- The name still ends in `.tmp`, so a file left behind by a hard kill never counts as an auto-save (`autosave::existing` is unchanged).
- API: `temp_path` is gone (only its test used it); `atomic_write_with`'s injectable writer now takes `&mut File` (only the crash test uses it).

## Tests (crates/engine/src/tests_settings.rs)
- `concurrent_atomic_writes_each_publish_a_whole_file`: 8 threads write the same file (256 KB+ each, different sizes) for 10 rounds. Every write succeeds, the file is always exactly one writer's whole data, and no temp file is left. **On main writers fail with `NotFound`.**
- `atomic_write_does_not_follow_a_link_at_the_old_temp_name` (unix): a symlink at `p.ecproj.tmp` pointing at a victim file stays untouched. **On main the victim is overwritten.**
- `atomic_write_survives_a_crash_mid_write` is adapted to the new writer signature and checks that the folder holds no stray temp file.

title: Templates: a confined export packs only footage inside the read roots (#1228)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1228.

## What was wrong
`essential.exportTemplate` packs the raw bytes of every footage file its comp uses (`s.services.read_file` on the paths stored in the project). With `--automation-read-root`, confinement only checked the export's destination `path`. So a permitted project that references a file outside the roots let an agent copy that file into an archive in an allowed folder.

## Fix
**Engine (`crates/engine/src/commands/essential.rs`)**
- `template_source_files` lists exactly the files an export reads (every frame of an image sequence). It shares `footage_files` with `export_template`, so the list and the export can't drift.
- New read-only query `essential.templateSources {comp?} → {comp, files}` returns that list.

**Automation (`confine.rs`, `backend.rs`)**
- `essential.exportTemplate` gets a `Lookup::TemplateSources`. Before it runs, the backend asks `essential.templateSources` for the export's `comp`, and every file must pass the read check. A denied dependency fails with a clear error (`the template's footage can't be packed: cannot read …`) before any archive is written.
- In `engine.batch` it is refused, like the other commands that touch files they aren't given; the message now covers this case.

This is the read-side counterpart of #1343 (#1227, import extracting outside the write roots). The two add parallel `Lookup` variants in the same spots in `confine.rs`/`backend.rs`, so whichever merges second needs a small rebase; I'll handle it. Not changed here: `templates.saveAs` (File ▸ Save as Template, `embedFootage`) and `file.collectFiles` also read the project's footage. They're worth the same treatment in a follow-up. #1243 (relative paths in template commands) is separate.

## Tests

  - the same in a batch: refused;

title: Automation: confine every command that reads or writes a file it is given (#1243)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1243.

## What was wrong
`essential.templateInfo` was missing from `READS` in `crates/automation/src/confine.rs`. A command that isn't listed gets no named-parameter check, and the fallback only scans absolute-looking strings. So a relative `path` (or one through `..`) escaped the read roots, and the command parsed and returned a template manifest from outside them.

## Fix
Following the issue's suggestion to audit coverage, I listed every registered engine command whose parameters (from `commands::accepted_params`) are named like files. That turned up the same gap in more commands, now classified:
- **READS:** `essential.templateInfo`, `file.importProject`, `file.watchFolder.poll`, `footage.relink`, `layer.newModel`, `mediaBrowser.fileInfo` / `list` / `import` / `removeFavorite`, `face.model.install`, `roto.model.install`, and `templates.create` (its `path`).
- **WRITES:** `file.exportTimeline`; `file.createProxy` (`path`/`output` may also be a file-name template, handled like `render.preRender`).
- **New `MIXED_WRITES`:** `templates.create` reads `path` but writes `projectPath` and `footageDir`.

## Fail-closed audit
`every_command_with_file_parameters_is_classified` walks `command_specs()` and fails when a command takes a `path`, `paths`, `folder`, `file`, `output`, `projectPath`… parameter and is not:
- confined (`READS`/`WRITES`), refused, or checked by a lookup;
- a Render Queue output (checked when the queue renders); or
- listed in `NOT_FILES`, the commands where `path` is a property path (`prop.*`, `keys.*`, `essential.addProperty`…), a project folder or a layer.

A new file command can't silently skip confinement any more; the test names what to add. It also checks that every listed id is a real command.

## Tests (crates/automation/src/confine.rs)
- The audit above.

title: Scripts: a script can't confirm executing a file for itself (#1246)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1246.

## What was wrong
With **Warn User When Executing Files** on, `file.executeFile` asks the frontend first (`app.confirmExecute`), and the frontend's form re-runs it with `confirmed: true`. That flag was read from the parameters of whoever called. So a script could pass it itself (`app.run('file.executeFile', {path, confirmed: true})`, also inside `engine.batch`) and the file opened without the question, as long as the user had allowed file and network access.

## Fix (crates/engine/src/commands/app_more.rs)
`confirmed` now only counts when the command isn't running for a script. That uses `Session::running_for_script()`, which #590 already uses for the same reason (scripts can't change the scripting preferences), and it stays set through nested `engine.batch` steps. As a result:
- a script's request always gets the question;
- the user's answer from the frontend's form still opens the file;
- with the warning off, nothing changes;
- the Allow Scripts to Write Files and Access Network gate is unchanged.

## Tests
- **engine** `tests_m145::a_script_cannot_confirm_executing_a_file_for_itself`: without the gate a script can't run files at all; with the gate, a script asserting `confirmed` gets `needsConfirmation` and no `OpenUrl`, both directly and through `engine.batch`. The frontend's confirmation opens the file, and with the warning off a script's request opens it as before.
- **script** `a_script_cannot_confirm_executing_a_file_for_itself` does the same through real JavaScript: `app.run('file.executeFile', {…, confirmed: true})`, `app.run('engine.batch', …)` and `File.execute()`.
- **Both fail on main** (`{"opened": …}`). The existing `execute_file_needs_the_gate_and_asks_first` still passes.

title: fix(effects): bound simulation checkpoint retention (#1238)
author: LabDennis
body:
Long simulation seeks collected every 15-step snapshot before eviction. The final one-time thinning could still leave more than the intended 256 checkpoints, and peak state storage grew with the entire seek distance.

Refs #1238: addresses checkpoint accumulation and the retained-count limit.

One insertion helper now enforces the 256-checkpoint limit both while generating snapshots and while merging them into a cache entry. It drops off-grid targets first, thins aligned snapshots when needed, and keeps the new exact target. The simulator still executes the same steps and returns the same state; repeated requests for the latest target reuse its `Arc` directly.

Validation on Windows / Rust 1.95, upstream `549e9d82`:

- Both new regressions fail with the original production code because the retained checkpoint count exceeds 256.
- All **457 Effects tests** pass, including particle/simulation image hashes. The final cache tests and strict all-target Effects Clippy also pass.
- An instrumented small synthetic state verifies retained counts and a peak bound of 514 live states across sequential warm-cache seeks (up to 256 old snapshots + 256 fresh snapshots + working state/pending clone). No large particle buffers or memory-exhaustion tests are needed.
- Forward/backward seeks, repeated targets and key eviction match a fresh deterministic simulation.
- Formatting, assets, layers and the full WASM gate (32 crates, one existing UI dead-code warning) pass. Full `xtask ci` stops at the unchanged `collapsible_match` finding in `crates/model/src/stl.rs:179`; this PR does not claim a green full workspace CI run.

The limit counts snapshots, not bytes: variable-sized states and concurrent runs still need a broader memory-budget design. Very large advances still execute synchronously and are not cancellable. Those remaining parts of #1238 are deliberately not marked closed by this focused fix.

title: Masks: Mask Expansion past a curve's radius grows a solid mask instead of a ring
author: Ian-Chege
body:
## Problem
Mask Expansion was rendered as the mask fill plus a stroke `2·|expansion|` wide, blended per pixel. Once the expansion was larger than the shape's curvature radius, the stroke's inner edge inverted:

- A 20 px circle expanded by **+60** left a ring from 40–80 px, with the layer showing through at 21–39 px, instead of a solid 80 px mask.
- **+600** cut out only the original 20 px dot.
- **Negative** values left islands instead of shrinking the shape away.

Add and Subtract masks were both affected. For example, a Subtract mask whose Expansion is animated outwards to reveal a layer showed a ring instead of an opening hole.

## Fix
`coverage_at` in `crates/render/src/masks.rs` now offsets the mask outline with `effectcraft_path::offset::offset_path` (the geometry the Offset Paths shape operator uses, which already removes the spurious loops and islands) using round joins, then fills it. Masks with variable-width feather keep their existing signed-distance path.

## Tests
New file `crates/render/src/tests_mask_expansion.rs`:
- `no_expansion_cuts_the_circle` (baseline)
- `expansion_past_the_radius_grows_a_solid_hole`
- `huge_expansion_cuts_the_whole_frame`
- `negative_expansion_shrinks_then_removes_the_hole`
- `expanded_rect_add_mask_has_round_corners` (baseline)

title: CLI: an argument that is not Unicode is a usage error, not a panic
author: iannitram
body:
## What broke

`effectcraft-cli` read its command line with `std::env::args()`, which panics on an argument that
is not valid Unicode, such as a Latin-1 file name on Linux. For example:

    $ effectcraft-cli $'\xff'
    thread 'main' panicked at .../library/std/src/env.rs:864:51:
    called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: "\xFF"
    $ echo $?
    101

`effectcraft-cli render-frame --out $'caf\xe9.png'` panicked the same way.

## The fix

`main` now reads `std::env::args_os()` and turns it into strings with a small `utf8_args`. An
argument that is not Unicode is a usage error (exit 2) that names it, before anything runs, the same
way an unknown option is:

    effectcraft-cli: argument `caf\u{fffd}.png` is not valid Unicode
    usage: effectcraft-cli <...>

It does not use a lossy copy. Every argument is a string here, and `caf\u{fffd}.png` would read or
write a different file from the one named. FilmCraft moved its CLI to `args_os` as well
(storytold/filmcraft#850).

## Tests

- `non_unicode_arguments_are_refused` (unit, unix-only): the conversion refuses a non-Unicode
  argument with that message and passes Unicode arguments through unchanged.
- `non_unicode_arguments_are_usage_errors` in `tests/cli.rs` (process, unix-only): runs the CLI
  with a non-Unicode `--out` path and expects exit 2, the message, no panic and no stdout. On
  upstream main it fails with exit 101.

## What was measured

Machine: ASUS ROG Flow Z13, SteamOS (Linux 6.18). Built in a container, run on the host.

| | `effectcraft-cli $'\xff'` | `render-frame --out $'caf\xe9.png'` | new process test |
|---|---|---|---|
| upstream main 549e9d82 | exit 101 (panic) | exit 101 | fails (101, expected 2) |
| this branch | exit 2 (usage error) | exit 2 | passes |

The `effectcraft-cli` test crate passes on this branch: 3 unit tests, 16 in `cli.rs`, and 8 in

title: Batches: a rollback restores the whole document; refuse what it can't undo (#1232)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1232.

## What was wrong
An atomic `engine.batch` snapshotted only `project`, `history` and `state`. A step that replaced the project (`file.open`, `file.new`, a template…) also changed the session's `path` and saved baseline (`saved_project`), which the rollback after a later failing step left in place. The session then held project A with B's file and save state while reporting "nothing changed", so a plain **Save would write A over B**. Steps that write files or open other applications also ran, and no in-memory rollback can take those back.

## Fix (crates/engine/src/commands/batch.rs)
- **The rollback restores the whole document:** `path` and `saved_project` along with the content, history and state. `bump()` then recomputes the saved state, so A comes back with A's file and A's own modified mark, clean or not. This works whichever command replaced the project, including future ones.
- **`NOT_IN_ATOMIC`:** commands that write files (saves, exports, frames, presets, guides, pre-render, Render Queue render, template export/save/delete, timeline export, proxies), install scripts, or open other applications (`file.executeFile`, Reveal in Finder, Open Source, Reveal Log File). An atomic batch (the default) refuses one **before running any step**, naming the step and pointing to `atomic: false`, which still runs them as before.
  - `file.autoSave` stays allowed: it only writes a recovery copy that the next auto-save replaces, and an existing MCP test batches it with a preference change.
  - The command's parameter docs say all this.
- `commands::batch` is now public so automation can check `NOT_IN_ATOMIC` against confinement's tables. Those tables become `pub(crate)`, with no behaviour change.

## Tests
- `engine` `a_rolled_back_batch_that_opened_another_project_restores_the_whole_document`: with A saved and with A modified, `[file.open B, <failing step>]` is rolled back to A's content (the same `Arc`), A's path, A's dirty state and A's undo history. Saving af…

title: macOS DMG: hdiutil create -srcfolder, so the installed app passes codesign --strict
author: Deeev201
body:
## What

The macOS DMG is built with `hdiutil create -srcfolder` instead of `hdiutil makehybrid -hfs` + `convert`, the way VectorCraft (storytold/vectorcraft#1085) and PdfCraft (storytold/pdfcraft#823) already do, with the same five-try `hdiutil_retry` for CI's "Resource busy". After signing, the image is mounted and the app inside is checked with `codesign --verify --strict --deep`, so this can't regress silently.

## Why

`makehybrid -hfs` stamps a `com.apple.FinderInfo` extended attribute on every file in the image. Gatekeeper still accepts the app (`spctl` says "Notarized Developer ID"), but `codesign --verify --strict --deep` on the app in the mounted DMG, or on a copy installed from it with Finder or `ditto`, fails:

```
EffectCraft.app: resource fork, Finder information, or similar detritus not allowed
```

This shows up in the current releases of PhotoCraft, FilmCraft, EffectCraft and DesignCraft (VectorCraft, LightCraft and PdfCraft, which already switched, pass).

## Checked

- `bash -n packaging/macos/package.sh`
- A small signed test bundle packed both ways: `makehybrid -hfs` left FinderInfo on all 7 files and `--strict` failed; `create -srcfolder -fs HFS+` left none and `--strict` passed.
- I couldn't run the full signed/notarized packaging locally (no Developer ID), so CI's packaging job is the real test.

title: Script sockets: per-socket locks, a write deadline, and close interrupts (#1248)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1248.

## What was wrong
Every socket operation in `crates/script/src/socket.rs` locked one global table and held it through the blocking `write_all`/`flush`. Streams had no write timeout, and accepted ones were explicitly made blocking. A peer that stopped reading therefore kept the script blocked for good, and every other socket call, `close` included, waited behind it.

## Fix (native only; the web build has no sockets)
- **Per-socket locks:** the table maps handles to `Arc<Entry>`, each with its own `Mutex<Sock>`. The table is locked only to look a socket up, add one or remove one, never during network I/O, so one stalled socket doesn't hold up the others.
- **Write deadline:** `write` sets a write timeout from the socket's `timeout` (10 s by default, the same as reads; the JS `Socket` already sends it with every call). It reports `write timed out after N s: the other side isn't reading (some of the data may have been sent)` instead of blocking.
- **Configuration failures are reported:** failing to set the read or write timeout, or to make an accepted stream blocking, now returns an error instead of being ignored.
- **`close` interrupts:** it removes the socket and shuts its stream down through a second handle (`try_clone`), so a call blocked on it fails at once.

## Tests (`socket.rs`, native)
- `a_write_to_a_peer_that_stops_reading_fails_after_the_timeout`: a 64 MB write to a loopback peer that accepts and never reads, with `timeout: 1`, fails with "timed out" well within the bound. **On main it never returns.**
- `a_blocked_socket_doesnt_hold_up_the_others_and_close_interrupts_it`: while socket A is blocked writing (`timeout: 60`), `connected` on socket B answers at once; `close` on A returns at once and A's write ends with an error. **On main B waits on the table lock.**
- Each step runs on its own thread with a bounded wait, so a regression fails instead of hanging. Only loopback is used, no external network.

title: Project: comp_contains walks precomps with a visited set, not recursion (#1237)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1237.

## What was wrong
`Project::comp_contains` recursed through precomp layers with no visited set or depth limit. A damaged project with a precomp cycle that doesn't pass the queried comp (comps A and B nesting each other, C unrelated) recursed until the stack ran out. That **aborts the process** (`fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting`), so it can't be caught as a command error, and unsaved work is lost. Several paths hit this:
- `layer.addItem`, which checks it before adding a precomp;
- the renderer, which calls it for every nested comp (`render/src/lib.rs`, ×4) and for audio (`render/src/audio.rs`).

A long chain used up the stack the same way, and comps shared by many paths were re-walked once per path, which is exponential for stacked "diamonds".

## Fix (crates/project/src/lib.rs)
`comp_contains` is now an explicit stack with a visited set and the same signature. The answers are the same: a comp contains itself, and a target reached through a cycle is still found. Each comp is visited once and nothing recurses, so every caller is safe.

The renderer already skips a precomp that contains the comp being rendered, so a cyclic project now renders (the inner copy is skipped) instead of crashing. Nothing is rewritten on load.

## Tests
- **project** `comp_contains_ends_on_cycles_long_chains_and_shared_precomps` covers the cases the issue lists:
  - an A ⇄ B cycle with an unrelated target (false);
  - a self-nesting comp;
  - a target reached through a cycle (true, and the reverse false);
  - 40 levels of diamonds (2⁴⁰ paths; under 1 s);
  - a 20,000-comp chain.
- **engine** `a_project_with_a_precomp_cycle_opens_adds_and_renders_without_running_out_of_stack`: saves and `file.open`s a project where A ⇄ B and C is unrelated. `layer.addItem` of A into C works, adding C into A is still refused (it would nest C in itself), and rendering C finishes. **On main this test aborts with a stack overflow.**

title: Offloaded analyses: merge the result instead of replacing the group (#1249)
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1249.

## What was wrong
An offloaded analysis (Warp Stabilizer, 3D Camera Tracker, Roto Brush, point tracking, mask tracking) gets a snapshot of the project and returns the whole analysed property group. `Session::poll_offload` found the live group by uid and **replaced it wholesale** (`*g = *group`). Anything changed in that group while the job ran (another setting, the fx switch, a name) was silently put back to what it was when the job started.

## Fix (crates/engine/src/offload.rs)
- The session keeps the group as the job started (`OffloadedJob.base`, captured in `offload_analysis`).
- When the result arrives it is **merged three ways** (`merge_group(base, live, result)`):
  - The group's own fields (name, enabled, label, kind/settings) and each property come from whichever side changed them. Unchanged on one side means the other side wins whole.
  - Sub-groups are merged child by child, matched by uid.
  - Children one side added or removed are added or removed.
- **Conflicts are explicit, not resolved silently.** These cases count as conflicts:
  - both sides changed the same field or property differently;
  - one side removed a child the other changed;
  - both sides restructured the children differently.

  In any of them nothing is applied, and the job's error toast says `“<group>” was changed during the analysis where its result changes it too, so nothing was applied: analyse again`.
- Unchanged: the result is still one undo step, and a target removed during the job is still reported as before.

## Tests
- `offload::tests::analysis_results_merge_with_edits_made_meanwhile` (unit) covers:
  - disjoint edits (user changes `a` and the fx switch; analysis writes `b` and a nested `c`): all kept;
  - an unchanged side: the other wins;
  - the same property changed differently: conflict; changed alike: fine;
  - a child added by the analysis alongside a user edit: both kept;
  - a child dropped by the analysis: dropped, unless the user changed something in…

title: SVG import: bound <use> expansion by an element budget and skip reference cycles
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1236

## Problem
`<use>` expansion was only limited by nesting depth (64). A few kilobytes of branching references (each group using the previous one twice) still expand to 2^N elements, so importing such a file hangs and exhausts memory. Mutually referencing `<use>` elements (A uses B, B uses A) also nested all the way down to the depth limit.

## Fix (`crates/svg/src/lib.rs`)
- The parser counts every element it converts, `<use>` copies included, against a budget of `max(500 000, 2 × the file's own element count)`. Once the budget is spent, conversion stops and `parse` returns `Error::Xml("its <use> references expand to more than N elements")`, so the import fails cleanly instead of hanging. The existing error variant is reused, so there is no API change.
- The `<use>` targets currently being expanded are tracked; a reference back into one of them is a cycle and is skipped, so mutual references stop at the first repeat.

## Tests (`crates/svg/src/tests.rs`)
- `branching_use_references_stop_at_the_expansion_budget`: 30 levels of doubling (2^30 copies) returns the budget error in well under a second; 10 levels (1024 rects) still import in full. On main this test runs until killed.
- `mutually_referencing_uses_are_cut_at_the_first_repeat`: A↔B imports each rectangle once. Fails on main.
- `a_symbol_used_a_thousand_times_still_imports`: normal heavy reuse (3000 shapes) is unaffected.

`cargo test -p effectcraft-svg`, the engine's SVG tests, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-svg --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

title: Tracking: bound feature/search sizes, coordinates and candidate selection inside the tracker
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1239

## Problem
Feature and search sizes from `track.setPoint` or from a loaded project reached the tracker with only a 4 px minimum. The tracker turned them into `i32` radii and multiplied them, so a huge size overflows (a panic in debug builds, a wrap in release). Large but finite sizes also set the size of the crop it allocates and of the exhaustive coarse search, which collected and sorted every candidate. Huge centres or offsets overflowed the crop origin in `Plane::from_image`.

## Fix
All in the tracking API (`crates/track/src/lib.rs`), so every route is covered: commands, loaded properties and offloaded jobs.
- **`PointSpec::bounded()`:** caps feature sizes at `MAX_FEATURE_SIZE` (256 px) and search sizes at `MAX_SEARCH_SIZE` (1024 px), and maps NaN to the 4 px minimum. Sizes below the minimum are left to the tracker's own minimum radii, so ordinary tracks are unchanged. Centres and search offsets are clamped to ±1e9 px. `Tracker::new` tracks the bounded spec, and `step` clamps the predicted and search centres the same way.
- **Scale:** with Track Shape on, a feature's scale stays within 1/4..4, which bounds the crop around it.
- **Candidate selection:** the coarse search keeps only its best 64 candidates (`select_nth_unstable_by`) instead of sorting all of them. The order is now total: scores in 1e-9 steps, then distance to the prediction. The old epsilon comparator wasn't transitive, and Rust's sort may panic on that.
- **`track.setPoint`** (engine) clamps `featureSize`/`searchSize` to the same limits, so the stored properties match what gets tracked.

## Tests
- `huge_and_non_finite_region_sizes_are_bounded`: sizes of 1e12, `f64::MAX`, ±∞ and NaN on a 16×16 image. On main: "attempt to multiply with overflow" at lib.rs:337.
- `huge_and_non_finite_centres_do_not_overflow_the_crop`: centres and offsets of ±1e300, 9.2e18, NaN and ∞. On main: an overflow panic in `plane.rs` `from_image`.
- `a_tiny_feature_in_the_largest_search_region_still_tracks`: a 9 …

title: glTF import: validate accessor spans before allocating, with checked arithmetic
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1235

## Problem
`Doc::floats` and `Doc::ints` (`crates/model/src/gltf.rs`) allocated `count * components` from the accessor's `count` before looking at its buffer view. A few hundred bytes of JSON could therefore ask for a multi-gigabyte buffer, which aborts the whole process: "memory allocation of 48000000000 bytes failed". The view and accessor offsets, `index * stride` and `count * components` used unchecked arithmetic, so overflow was possible too. `idx` converted `u64` with `as usize`, which truncates on wasm32.

## Fix
- **`Doc::layout`** runs before `floats()` or `ints()` allocate anything. It checks `count * components`, adds the view and accessor offsets, rejects a `byteStride` smaller than an element, and checks that the last element ends inside the buffer. All of it uses checked arithmetic. A failure is a normal import error ("accessor reads past its buffer" and similar), and the allocation is then bounded by the buffer's real size.
- **Accessors without a buffer view** (all zeros) have nothing in the file backing their count, so they are capped at 2^24 components.
- **`idx()` and node index lists** (`children`, scene `nodes`, skin `joints`) use `usize::try_from`. An image buffer view's end and a GLB chunk's end use `checked_add`.

## Tests (`crates/model/src/tests.rs`)
- `gltf_accessor_counts_are_checked_against_the_buffer_before_allocating` covers six cases: a huge count over a 36-byte buffer, `count * components` overflow, overflowing offsets, a stride that overflows with the count, a stride smaller than an element, and a huge view-less accessor. Each must fail with the matching error within 10 s. On main the test process aborts with "memory allocation of 48000000000 bytes failed".
- `gltf_integer_accessors_are_checked_too` does the same for index accessors. On main it aborts allocating 16 GB.
- `gltf_strided_and_buffer_less_accessors_still_import`: an interleaved accessor (stride 24) ending exactly at the buffer's end imports, and so does a sm…

title: FBX import: budget the memory an import keeps, and share instanced meshes
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1234

## Problem
The FBX array limit (1 GiB) counted bytes on the wire, but arrays are kept as `Prop::Floats(Vec<f64>)` / `Prop::Ints(Vec<i64>)`. A boolean array therefore keeps 8× its checked size, and a 32-bit array 2×. Nothing bounded the total across arrays either. Separately, every Model linked to a Geometry called `build_mesh` again, so N instances of one large geometry allocated N full copies.

## Fix (`crates/model/src/fbx.rs`)
- **Import budget:** each import gets a 2 GiB `Budget` of memory it may keep.
  - **Binary arrays** are charged 8 bytes per element, i.e. what is actually kept. The charge happens before the array is decompressed or widened.
  - **ASCII files** are charged for their parsed values. They hold each array element as its own `Prop`, so the charge comes after parsing, and the text size bounds them meanwhile.
  - **Each built mesh** is charged for its vertex and index data.
  - Exceeding the budget fails the import with "… would take the import past its 2048 MiB memory limit" instead of aborting on allocation failure. The existing 1 GiB per-array wire check stays.
- **Shared meshes:** Models instancing the same geometry with the same material mapping share one mesh, keyed by geometry id plus model material indices. A different mapping still gets its own mesh, since material slots are per Model.
- **Lower limits for tests:** `parse_within` / `read_within` take a lowered limit. The public `parse` and `read` are unchanged.

## Tests (`crates/model/src/fbx_tests.rs`)
- `fbx_arrays_are_charged_for_the_memory_they_keep`: a 10 000-element boolean array fits a budget of exactly 8 bytes per element and fails one byte below it. 32-bit floats are charged as f64. Three arrays that each fit, but not together, fail. ASCII values are charged too.
- `fbx_models_instancing_one_geometry_share_its_mesh`: two more Models instance the test scene's geometry. One with the same materials shares the mesh, and one with a different mapping gets its own, so 2 me…

title: AEP: clean-room effectcraft-aep crate (.aep container reader/writer and typed view), refs #190
author: vangel76
body:
Refs #190 (does not close it: the importer and exporter follow in separate PRs).

> **Draft, for discussion.** #190 is waiting for a maintainer decision on the clean-room scope for `.aep`. This PR is how I would do it, so there is something concrete to judge. I am happy to split it, shrink the fixtures or rework it. Nothing here depends on py-aep or any other third-party AE parser.

Odd shapes (raw-text LISTs, ids with a trailing space, chunks whose body is itself a chunk) are handled and tested.
- **Typed view:** items and folders, compositions (time base, exact NTSC rates, size, duration, work area, background, pixel aspect, shutter, renderer, display start), layers (switches, label, blend mode, exact start/in/out/stretch as rationals, parent, source), property trees by match name, static values in AE units with the "absent = default" rule, keyframes (time, interpolation in/out, ease, spatial values, roving), expressions, effect instances and parameters, masks and bezier paths, shape groups, text documents, markers, footage items, cameras and lights.

title: AEP: .aep importer (file.importAep), stacked on #1377, refs #190
author: vangel76
body:
Refs #190. **Stacked on #1377 (the `effectcraft-aep` crate PR, draft):** this branch contains its commits, so please review only the **last 7 commits** (importer crate, `file.importAep` command, docs, the merge of the crate branch with its adaptation, and two small docs commits). I will rebase this PR once the crate PR is merged.

> **Draft, for discussion.** Same clean-room basis as the crate PR (observation of own generated files only, see `docs/aep-format.md`, section "Method").

title: Layer cache: hash a selected layer's comp scene into its owner's key
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1252

## Problem
When a layer's effect selects another layer (Displacement Map, Blend, …), `cache/dependencies.rs` hashes that layer's structure, evaluated values, world matrix, time and its own selected layers into the owner's cache key. It did not hash the comp camera and lights that the selected layer's scene-reading effects see (Caustics, CC Particle World, Card Dance, Shatter, Card Wipe). The owner's key includes `comp_scene` only when the owner itself runs one of those effects. A cached owner returns before any effect runs, so the selected layer's own scene-sensitive key is never consulted, and moving the camera or a light reused stale owner pixels.

## Fix (`crates/render/src/cache/dependencies.rs`)
`Dependencies::layer` now hashes `comp_scene(ctx, layer)` for every selected layer that `reads_comp_scene`. That covers layers reached through further selections and layers inside selected precomps (with the nested comp's scene). It's the same policy owner keys already use.

## Test (`crates/render/src/tests.rs`)
`a_selected_layer_reading_the_comp_scene_invalidates_its_owner`: a solid blends with a hidden CC Particle World layer under a camera, and the camera is panned 40 px.
- The owner's key changes.
- A render through a warm layer cache matches an uncached render.
- The blended particles move with the camera.

On main the key assertion fails (same key, `16575944942201124902`, both times).

`cargo test -p effectcraft-render` (217 passed, 1 ignored), `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-render --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.

title: Particles: preserve emitted particles when Birth Rate changes (#1373)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Closes #1373.

CC Particle World simulates from layer time 0 at 60 steps a second, but it used the Birth Rate of the **rendered frame** for every step. With Birth Rate keyed from 3 down to 0, every frame after the drop was simulated with no births at all, so the burst vanished although its particles were well within their Longevity. A ramped rate was simulated as if its current value had always applied. The issue's 0.25 s frame matched a constant rate of 1.5 pixel for pixel.

## The fix
**Each step samples Birth Rate at its own layer time.** The rate only decides that step's births. Particles already alive keep moving and ageing, and the carry and particle ids continue across rate changes. Without a host that can evaluate the effect at other times, the current value applies throughout, as before.

- **`EffectHost::param_at(effect_index, id, layer_time)`** evaluates one parameter of one effect. The renderer walks the effect group by match id and evaluates just that property, keyframes and expressions included.
  - **Exact layer time:** the keyframes are read at the requested layer time exactly (`EvalCtx::value_at_layer_time`). Mapping it to comp time and back truncates a tick early under a fractional stretch, so a Hold cut at 0.5 s read its old value for one step (six extra births at 33.3 % or 133.33 %).
  - **Static rates:** a rate with no keyframes and no expression (`EffectHost::param_is_static`) isn't sampled at all. The effect passes its own `EffectEnv::effect_index`. The existing `params_at` reads the renderer's running-effect index, which GPU-batched effects never update, so a batched effect could read another effect's values.
- **Cache identity:** Birth Rate is no longer part of the simulation key, so an animated rate stops restarting the simulation every frame. Instead each checkpoint is checked against the rate history:
  - **CPU:** the state keeps a hash of the rates it was stepped with (`PState::hist`). `SimCache::run_where` resumes only from a checkpoint…

title: Web: await IndexedDB transaction commits before acknowledging writes (#1242)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Fixes #1242.

## What was wrong
In the web app's IndexedDB storage backend (`apps/effectcraft-web/js/host.js`), `storePut` and `storeDelete` awaited `req()`, which resolves on the request's `onsuccess`, and dropped the transaction. A request's success doesn't mean the write is stored: the readwrite transaction can still abort afterwards (quota at commit, the browser closing) and roll the write back. EffectCraft then treated the write as saved. The Rust flush loop (`src/persist.rs`, the retry from #224) never saw a rejection, didn't keep the key for a retry, and a reload brought back the older data. This affects session snapshots, settings and persisted files whenever IndexedDB is the backend (OPFS unavailable). Remembering and forgetting Media Browser folders had the same request-only pattern.

## Change
- New `write(db, store, op)` helper in `host.js`:
  - opens a readwrite transaction and attaches `oncomplete` / `onabort` before issuing the request (synchronously, while the transaction is active);
  - resolves on `complete`;
  - rejects on `abort` with `tx.error`, so a failed request's own error comes through (for example `ConstraintError`). An explicit `abort()` leaves no error, so that case gets a `DOMException` `AbortError`;
  - when creating the transaction or issuing the request throws, aborts the transaction and rejects with that error.

  It doesn't suppress IndexedDB's automatic abort of a failed request.
- `storePut`, `storeDelete`, and remembering (`openFolder`) / forgetting (`browseForget`) a Media Browser folder use it. The Media Browser callers keep their existing error handling (logged / ignored).
- No Rust change: the flush loop already keeps failed keys, retries them and rejects `effectcraft.flush()` (#224). It now gets the rejection.
- `docs/web.md` lists the new test.

The OPFS backend is unchanged. Its `createWritable().close()` already resolves only once the file is replaced.

title: Expressions: a layer is a callable property group
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Found while working on #1385. (The Windows relink fix that was also here is superseded by #1639 and has been dropped.)

## Expressions: a layer is a callable property group
In After Effects a layer is a property group: `thisLayer("transform")`, `thisComp.layer("Other")("effects")("Blur")`, `thisLayer(1)`. In EffectCraft's expression runtime a `Layer` was a plain object, so these failed with "TypeError: not a callable function". That includes the references the pick whip writes with Compact English off, such as `thisComp.layer("Other")("effects")("ec.noise.fractal")("transform")("scale")`.

**Fix:**
- A `Layer` is now callable, built the way `__mkGroup` builds groups. It looks up its own properties by match name, name or index, and keeps its methods, `name` and `index`.
- The three places that assumed a layer is a plain object accept it:
  - a layer as the result still reads as its index;
  - `thisComp.layer(layer, offset)` works;
  - a Layer Control's value is handed through the property proxy unbound.

## Cost
A callable `Layer` (a function with its own prototype) costs more to make than the plain object it was, so:
- **Each layer is made once per runtime** (`__layer`), not once per evaluation. Its info (`__info`) is read again in each evaluation: it is kept with the evaluation's `__S`, which `__begin` replaces, so nothing is reset or counted per evaluation. `Object.preventExtensions` keeps a field an expression sets on a layer from reaching the next evaluation.
- **The cache is keyed by comp, then layer.** A `c + ':' + l` string key cost about 3.4 µs per lookup in boa, against about 0.55 µs for the two-level lookup (50 000 lookups in one evaluation). That string key was most of what remained of the slowdown.
- **The layer checks read `__isLayer` only on functions**, so numbers and other primitives aren't boxed to look it up.

title: Particles: CC Particle Systems II and CC Mr. Mercury keep emitted particles when Birth Rate changes (#1373)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Refs #1373. **Depends on #1382:** this branch is stacked on it, so the diff here includes #1382's commits until it merges. This PR's own changes are the last 6 commits (from `f4ab728c`).

#1382 fixed CC Particle World, whose simulation used the Birth Rate of the rendered frame for every step since layer time 0. **CC Particle Systems II and CC Mr. Mercury had the same pattern.** A Birth Rate keyed down to 0 emptied them the frame it got there, although their particles (Mercury's blobs) were within their Longevity. - **A constant Birth Rate gives exactly the particles it did**, with or without a host (tested bit for bit).
- The constant-rate step, key and simulation (`Phys::step`, `sim_key`, `simulate`) are now only the tests' reference. Mr. Mercury's physics move into `mercury_phys`.

title: i18n: the CJK fallback sits on the Latin baseline (#1309)
author: zitann2020
body:
Japanese text in the interface sat 3 pt above the Latin baseline at 12 pt: a fallback face is
drawn at `A_face + 0.5·(H_row − H_face)` (epaint's `galley_from_rows`), so its own ascent and row
height decide where its glyphs land, and a CJK face's are nothing like Inter's.

Each registered fallback now carries a `FontTweak` that cancels that offset:

```
y_offset_factor = (A_row − A_face)/px − 0.5·(H_row − H_face)/px
```

The value is derived at runtime from the face's own metrics — `fonts::face(id).metrics(px)`, rounded
the way epaint's `styled_metrics` rounds them — so a face that is already on the baseline gets 0 and
no interface size needs its own number. It also covers the Arabic, Indic, Thai and Hangul fallbacks,
which share the loop.

## Measured

| size | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 12 pt | kana 3.00 pt high | 0.41 pt |
| 15 pt | 4.00 pt high | 0.25 pt |
| 18 pt | 4.00 pt high | 1.13 pt |

The remainder is the two outlines differing — a kana reaches a little below a Latin letter — not a
baseline that is still off.

## Verification

- `cargo +1.95 test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --lib theme::` — 9 passed, 0 failed.
- `fallback_glyphs_sit_on_the_row_baseline` fails without the change: the kana sits 3-5 pt
  at four families and three sizes; it skips when no Japanese face is installed, as the neighbouring
  font tests do.
- `cargo +1.95 check -p effectcraft-ui-egui --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` — no new warnings.
- `cargo +1.95 xtask layers` — ok.
- `cargo xtask ci` itself could not run here: the toolchain this machine has for 1.95 carries neither
  clippy nor rustfmt. Please treat CI as the authority.

Found while translating the Settings dialog; the measurements are in #1309.

title: Render/Export: CPU exports match main byte for byte on top of #1279, and render frame 0 first
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
**Base:** this PR stacks on #1279 (`b51c91a1`, drop the blanket layer cover). Merge #1279 first; then this diff is only the six commits below.

## Why

#1279 drops the blanket layer cover from blur/glow/displace stacks, so those layers run on a buffer about the size of their content instead of the whole layer rectangle. On the CPU this changes how blurred pixels round. On sample d (blur + glow), #1279 alone renders different bytes than main (MD5 differs on every machine we tried). The causes, all in the CPU box-blur running sums:

1. **Vertical block restarts.** The vertical pass restarts its per-column running sum every `block` rows, counted from the top of the buffer. A buffer that starts lower than the covered one restarts on different rows, so the float sums round differently.
2. **Repeat Edge Pixels.** #1279 covers the layer for Repeat Edge, but a stack that was padded first (e.g. Turbulent Displace room) or aligned no longer has the same edge as the covered buffer. So it repeats different pixels.
3. **Read-ahead into residue.** After the content passes, a running sum is not exactly zero (add/subtract rounding). That residue carries on to the buffer's right and bottom edge, and each pass reads `r + 1` pixels ahead into it. A smaller buffer reads zeros there instead. This is normally invisible, but it flipped one 8-bit level in a 4K Fast Box test.

Separately, CPU exports suffer a cold-cache herd: the first batch renders all its frames side by side while the layer cache is empty, so every frame renders the same static layers at once.

## What

1. **Export: CPU exports render frame 0 alone before the first batch.** This applies when there is no GPU accelerator or the project is Software Only. The layer cache is warm before frames run side by side.
2. **CPU blurs use the covered buffer's row phase.** `Buf::align` records how many rows the cover would have added on top (`effectcraft_effects::stack`, per-thread and scoped to one effect stack). The vertical box pass …

`matchnames::node` numbers an effect's parameters in display order unless the effect is listed in `PARAM_NUMBERS`, which so far only had Fill (M13.15). Stroke and Hue/Saturation number theirs out of display order in After Effects, so `ADBE Stroke-0002` found All Masks and `ADBE HUE SATURATION-0004` found Master Lightness, and a script wrote into the wrong control without an error. This adds both effects to the table with the numbers from the issue's listing. Hue/Saturation also has per-channel controls that After Effects doesn't expose (it edits the selected channel through the Master ones), so params of a listed effect that the table doesn't cover are now numbered after the table's last number, in order (`Red Hue` is `-0011`). Without that they kept their display position and collided: `-0007` would have found Red Lightness instead of Colorize. Happy to switch to a different scheme for those, for example keeping their own ids.

The issue lists Hue/Saturation up to Colorize (`-0007`). Colorize Hue, Saturation and Lightness are `-0008`…`-0010` here, following the same order as After Effects' parameter list (Skottie's Hue/Saturation adapter reads them in that order, right after Colorize). `-0001` (a hidden parameter in AE) and `-0003` (Channel Range, which EffectCraft doesn't have) resolve to nothing. Fill already matched, and I didn't touch other effects since I have no AE numbering to check them against.

The other two gaps in the issue (shape operator children of Zig Zag, Offset Paths and Gradient Stroke, and the layer style command ids and match names) are separate features; happy to follow up on them in their own PRs. This builds on the same table #1172 used for the Dashes names.

title: fix(render): preserve preceding effects in GPU Echo
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
## Why

Applying Echo after CC Star Burst on a white solid rendered an entirely white frame on the GPU. Batched effects shared a host whose stack index stayed at zero or the last CPU effect, so Echo sampled the original solid instead of the preceding effects.

## Scope

Give each GPU step an immutable host with its actual stack index, and use a scoped host for CPU effects. Add a regression for all seven Echo operators, 8/32 bpc, full/half resolution, and Echo followed by Posterize Time.

## Blast radius

Temporal GPU effects now read the same preceding effects and animated parameters as the CPU path. Existing batching and recursion limits remain in place.

## Verification

- The new GPU regression fails against the original renderer and passes with the fix on Apple M5 Metal.
- The original 200×100 CLI reproduction changes from 20,000 white GPU pixels to a star field that matches the CPU output exactly.
- `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false cargo xtask ci` passes: 3,399 tests, formatting, Clippy, layers, assets, and WebAssembly checks. Test LTO was disabled to avoid lengthy integration-test linking.
- `cargo build --release -p effectcraft-cli` passes with the normal release settings; the frame comparison above uses this binary.

Closes #1120.

title: GPU: stop 4K effect frames from running out of video memory (and log GPU declines in the CLI)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## Problem

With GPU acceleration on, the 4K benchmark samples c (effects stack) and d (blur/glow) rendered at
CPU speed, byte-identical to a CPU render, and printed nothing.

Frame 0 ran out of video memory part-way through the layer stack (on an RTX 3090, 24 GB). The
"Out of Memory" error retires the GPU context, so every later frame and every effect falls back to
the CPU for the rest of the export.

Why memory runs out: all layers in these samples are static, so each layer's effect run uses its
own `Enc` (upload → kernels → readback), while the frame's own encoder stays open for the whole
frame. A texture released while any encoder is open is parked until that encoder is submitted
(it may still be read by recorded commands). The frame's encoder only submits every 256
dispatches, and a frame of placements doesn't reach that, so every effect run's 4K f32
intermediates stay parked. After about 20 blurred/glowing 4K layers, the device is out of memory.

The CLI installed no logger, so the "GPU declined the frame" warning was never shown.

## Fix

1. `gpu: submit once parked and new textures pass 1 GiB` (`crates/gpu/src/context.rs`)
   - The pool tracks the bytes of parked textures.
   - Each `Enc` tracks the bytes of textures it newly allocated since its last submit.
   - Before recording more work, an encoder submits when either 256 dispatches are pending (as
     before) or its new bytes plus the parked bytes reach 1 GiB, so parked textures go back to the pool.
   - Parked bytes count only for the oldest open encoder (usually the frame's). A parked texture is
     freed only when every encoder open at its release has been submitted, so submitting a newer one
     (an effect chain or Advanced 3D pass inside the frame) frees nothing. Newer encoders count only
     their own allocations and don't submit on every step.
   - The parked bytes and the oldest open encoder are published as atomics under the pool lock, so a
     dispatch reads them without taking the lock.

title: render: opt-in reuse-only input cache (`--exp-input-cache`)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## What

An opt-in mode for the layer cache (`--exp-input-cache`, or `EFFECTCRAFT_EXP_INPUT_CACHE=1`), off by default:

- **Store at once while under budget.** While the cache has room, a mode-on run stores results
  exactly like the default cache, so projects that fit their budget behave as they do on `main`.
- **Reuse-only admission under pressure.** Once a new result would go over the budget, it's stored
  only when it's rendered a second time, so one-off results never push reused ones out.
- **Cropped storage, full-extent hits.** Under pressure, a stored layer is cropped to its non-zero
  pixels (plus a 2 px margin), but only when the crop is at most a quarter of the frame. Marginal
  crops cost a scan plus a full-extent copy on each hit for little memory. Hits are served at the
  full extent and origin, with the original buffer's offset restored bit for bit (not recomputed
  from the crop's), so output is byte-identical to an uncached render.
- **One full-extent copy for hot entries.** A hot cropped entry keeps one full-extent copy (one
  copy and one GPU upload, not one per frame), but only within the budget: other entries' copies
  are dropped, least recently used first, until the new copy fits; if it still doesn't, the hit
  goes without one.
- **Cycle-aware eviction.** Entries reused every frame are kept over a cycle bigger than the
  budget, instead of being LRU-evicted just before they're needed.

Based directly on `main`. It doesn't depend on #898 or any other open PR. The switch is a small
static in `render::cache` that the CLI sets (the CLI also reads `EFFECTCRAFT_EXP_INPUT_CACHE`; the
render crate reads no environment), so there's no new settings plumbing. `EFFECTCRAFT_CACHE_STATS=1`
also reports how many inserts were stored cropped.

## Results

GPU render (`--gpu`), RTX 3090, 30 frames, H.264, benchmark resolution (4K samples at half), layer
cache budget 1024 MB (the default), 3 runs each, interleaved:

| Sample | main | `--exp-input-cache` |

title: Keyframes: a path pasted onto Position becomes a motion path
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1425.

Key paste only accepted a property of the same type, so a Mask Path (or shape Path) key could never land on Position, and a copied unanimated path only pasted back onto the same path. Now a single copied path, its value or a key, pasted onto a selected spatial property (Position, or the `prop`/`path` given to `keys.paste`) becomes a motion path the way After Effects builds one: one key per vertex carrying the path's tangents, spread over 2 seconds from the current time (the duration the [Animate along a path](https://www.adobe.com/learn/after-effects/web/animate-along-path) tutorial shows: "the animation is going to take place over 2 seconds"), the keys between the first and last roving so the layer moves at one speed (`retime_roving` does the timing by arc length), and a closed path gets a last key back on its first vertex. Everything else about paste is unchanged.

The vertices are pasted as they are, in the source layer's space, like After Effects does: that's why the path often lands offset there and has to be moved afterwards (the same tutorial, and [this Community thread](https://community.adobe.com/t5/after-effects-discussions/why-does-my-mask-path-change-position-when-pasting-it-on-a-position-parameter/m-p/10779178)). Converting the path through the source layer into the target's parent space, so the motion follows the path where you see it, would be a small addition; happy to add it as an option if you'd like it.

Not covered: with several path keys copied, the first one is used.

Validation:

title: CLI: a failed render under run/exec exits 1, like render --queue
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1426.

`renderQueue.render` reports a failed item inside its result (`status: {"Failed": …}`) rather than as an error, and `run`/`exec` only treat engine errors as failures, so a script that checks `$?` saw success. `render --queue` already checks the item statuses and exits 1. The other half of the issue (the 52-byte stub replacing a good file) is #1230, which #1320 by @DWAA1660 already fixes by writing to a temporary sibling and renaming on success, so I left it out here.

title: Render Queue: resolve a bare project filename against the working directory
author: Hamza0101
body:
Closes #1427

### The problem

`RenderQueue::resolve_output` takes the project's folder from the project path's parent:

```rust
base.or_else(|| self.path.as_deref()
    .and_then(|s| Path::new(s).parent().map(|d| d.to_path_buf()))
    .filter(|d| !d.as_os_str().is_empty()));
```

For a project saved under a bare filename, `Path::new("proj.ecproj").parent()` is `Some("")`, and the `filter` discards it. Execution then falls through to the unsaved-project default, so a **saved** project's relative outputs went to `~/Movies` (the user profile folder on Windows) instead of beside the project.

That contradicts the doc comment three lines above, which says relative paths resolve "against the project's folder (an unsaved project's against ~/Movies or home)".

Reproduced on `549e9d8` through `renderQueue.list`, which reports the path without rendering:

| `--project` | `outputPath` before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `proj.ecproj` | `~/Movies/clip.mp4` | `./clip.mp4` |
| `./proj.ecproj` | `./clip.mp4` | `./clip.mp4` |
| `sub/proj.ecproj` | `sub/clip.mp4` | `sub/clip.mp4` |
| `/abs/work/proj.ecproj` | `/abs/work/clip.mp4` | `/abs/work/clip.mp4` |

Both of the first two spellings name a project in the working directory, and only the second got it.

### The change

Treat an empty parent as the working directory, which is what a bare filename means. Rows two to four are untouched, and the unsaved-project default still applies when there is no project path at all.

@Tokarzewski diagnosed this precisely in the issue, including the `filter` on line 366 and the suggested fix; this is that fix.

### Tests

`render_queue_resolves_a_bare_project_filename_against_the_working_directory` in `tests_m145.rs` asserts the two spellings agree, and pins the result to `./clip.mp4` so the assertion cannot pass by both being wrong together. Reverting the change fails it with `a bare filename resolved to /Users/macbook/Movies/clip.mp4 instead of ./clip.mp4`.

title: Import: item.metadata counts a WebM's last frame when its duration is not a whole millisecond
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1429.

`footage_metadata` turned the footage duration into a frame count with `frame_at`, which floors. Matroska stores the duration in whole milliseconds, so a one-frame 30 fps WebM lasts 33 ms, just short of one 33.33 ms frame, and reported 0 frames (4 frames came back as 3, and so on). The count now goes through `snap_nearest` first, i.e. it rounds to the nearest frame like the media pool's own `frame_count`, which is why playback and layer length were already right. This also covers millisecond-granular WebM files written by other tools. Thanks @Tokarzewski for the detailed table and for pinning down both the writer and the reader side.

I left the WebM writer's millisecond `Duration` as it is, since the container's timecode scale is in milliseconds anyway; happy to switch to also writing a finer duration there if you prefer.

Validation:
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-host --test webm_metadata`: renders 1- and 4-frame WebMs at 30 fps, imports them and reads `item.metadata`. Fails on main (`frames` is 0 for the one-frame file), passes here

title: Linux: build an Arch package (.pkg.tar.zst)
author: ujo4eva
body:
Adds an Arch Linux package to the Linux release, next to the `.deb` and `.rpm`. Arch users (Manjaro, EndeavourOS, Omarchy, ...) can then `sudo pacman -U` it, and ArtCraft Launcher can install and update it through pacman (storytold/craft-launcher#389).

## What changes

- `packaging/linux/package.sh`:
  - adds an `arch` format, on by default;
  - builds `effectcraft-<ver>-linux-<arch>.pkg.tar.zst` with nfpm's `archlinux` packager from the same `nfpm.yaml`.

  nfpm can't rename a package per format and doesn't env-expand `archlinux.packager`, so the script writes a copy of the config with both set.
- `packaging/linux/nfpm.yaml`:
  - an `overrides.archlinux` block with Arch dependencies: `glibc gcc-libs hicolor-icon-theme libxkbcommon alsa-lib vulkan-icd-loader`;
  - `provides: effectcraft`;
  - `conflicts: effectcraft, effectcraft-bin, effectcraft-git`.
- **Named `ai.storyteller.effectcraft`, not `effectcraft`.** The AUR already has `effectcraft`, `effectcraft-bin` and `effectcraft-git`. An AUR helper treats an installed package with an AUR name as its own and would rebuild it on the next update. The bundle id is also how the launcher tells this package (which it updates) from an AUR build (which it leaves to the AUR helper).
- The README's Linux download table gains an Arch row.

**No workflow change is needed.** `craft-common-actions` uploads and checksums everything `package.sh` writes to `dist/release`, and the riscv64 job passes `--formats "deb rpm tar"`.

## Notes

- nfpm has no `optdepends` for Arch, so the Debian `recommends` have no Arch equivalent.
- Pre-releases sort correctly: `0.7.0-rc.1` becomes pkgver `0.7.0rc.1`, which pacman places before `0.7.0`. Arm64 maps to `aarch64`.

## Testing
