title: GPU: keep an effect chain's result on the device for the compositor instead of uploading it again
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
**Base:** `main`. Three commits: the hand-off itself, a fix so a handed-off result waits for open encoders before it is reused, and the chain hold returned from `Accelerator::effects_held` instead of a thread-local. It no longer stacks on #1415 (closed in favour of #1523). It works on `main` alone, but its 4K gain shows only on top of #1523 (see Results and "Relationship to #1523").

## Problem

With GPU acceleration, a layer whose effects run on the GPU (`Gpu::effects` → `run_chain`) makes three trips:

1. Its CPU buffer is uploaded (RGBA f32).
2. The chain runs, and the result is read back to the CPU (it becomes the layer's buffer and goes into the layer cache).
3. The GPU compositor uploads that same buffer again to composite it.

Blur and glow make the buffer bigger by their reach, so the result is larger than the input. Step 3 uploads that largest buffer again, though the GPU already had it.

## Change

- **Chain hold.** `run_chain_held` returns the chain's result and, when the hand-off is on, the device image that was read back. `run_chain` is now a wrapper that drops the image. The new `Accelerator::effects_held` (default: `effects` with no hold) wraps that image in an opaque `ChainHold` that records the address and length of the pixels it was read back into. The caller owns the hold, and nothing is kept in the accelerator or in a thread-local. Results served through deferred readback (the browser worker path) carry no hold.
- **Renderer.** The CPU effect target (`CpuFx`) calls `effects_held` and keeps the hold only while its buffer is still that chain's result: any CPU effect after the chain drops it. `content_buf` wraps the stack's result in the layer `Arc` and, only if `ChainHold::is_for` confirms the `Arc` holds those very pixels, passes it to the new `Accelerator::adopt` (default: nothing). Other callers of the effect stack (`layer_input`, `apply_effects_timed`) drop the hold.
- **Upload cache.** `Gpu::adopt` files the image in the existing upload cache …

title: Shapes: a stroke's buffer is padded by the miter limit only where it has miter joins
author: wixar172
body:
A shape layer's buffer was padded by `stroke width × Miter Limit / 2` on every side, for every stroke, whether or not the path has a miter join. A straight 1080 px wide stroke used as a wipe track matte became a **4326×6366** layer buffer (~440 MB as RGBA f32). A new one was made every frame while its Trim Paths animated, then cached on the CPU and uploaded to the GPU. Exporting 12 frames in parallel used up the memory of a 16 GB Mac and froze it.

## Cause

`draw_bounds` in `crates/render/src/shapes.rs`:

```rust
let grow = stroke.map_or(1.0, |style| style.width * style.miter.max(1.0) * 0.5 * d.xf.mean_scale().max(1.0) + 1.0);
```

The miter limit only matters where a miter join exists. A straight open segment has no join, so the stroke reaches half its width past the path, or √2 half widths at square-cap corners.

## Fix

A new `stroke_reach(style, paths)` returns how far the stroke can reach past the path, in half widths:

- **Miter Limit:** a miter-joined stroke on a path that has a join (two or more segments, or a closed path).
- **√2:** square caps.
- **1:** any other stroke.
- **Widest padding, as before:** Taper and Wave, which can widen the stroke.

Rendered pixels are unchanged; only the empty margin around them goes away. On the ad where we hit this, a full-resolution frame's peak memory went from 1.7 GB to 0.7 GB.

## Tests

In `crates/render/src/shapes/tests.rs`:

- `straight_stroke_buffer_is_not_padded_by_the_miter_limit`: the 1080 px wipe case. Its buffer is now about 1080×3120 instead of 4326×6366.
- `miter_corner_still_fits_its_buffer`: a sharp V with a miter join still has room for its miter tip, and the tip's pixels are drawn, not clipped.

## Validation

- `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false cargo xtask ci` steps on macOS (Apple silicon): fmt, strict Clippy, layers, assets and wasm pass. `cargo test --workspace --release`: 3,398 passed, 26 ignored, 2 failed. The 2 failures (`av1_webm_with_opus`, `webm_low_bitrate_opus_modes` in `effectcraft-export`)…

title: packaging: RPM requires library sonames, so openSUSE can install it
author: tydude001
body:
## What and why

EffectCraft's RPM requires Fedora package names: `libxkbcommon`, `(vulkan-loader or libglvnd-egl)`, `alsa-lib`.
openSUSE has no `libxkbcommon`, `vulkan-loader` or `libglvnd-egl` package, so zypper refuses it with
`nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` (exit 4, which the ArtCraft Launcher shows as "error 4";
storytold/craft-launcher#341).

This requires the libraries' sonames instead, as PhotoCraft and VectorCraft already do, so the same RPM
resolves on Fedora/RHEL and openSUSE. It also declares the binaries' glibc floor, matching the deb's
`libc6 (>= 2.35)`. The floor names libm, not libc: the
binaries' only GLIBC_2.35 symbols are `hypot` and `hypotf` from libm, and RHEL 9's current glibc
(`2.34-283.el9_8`) provides `libc.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)` through backports but not libm's.

## How it was tested

EffectCraft 0.9.2's released x86_64 binaries, repackaged with nfpm 2.47.0 and this branch's `nfpm.yaml`, then
installed with the distro's own package manager in a fresh x86_64 container and run with `effectcraft-cli --version`.
The released RPM is the same test on the release's own package.

| | released 0.9.2 RPM | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Fedora 44 | installs, runs | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Tumbleweed | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| openSUSE Leap 15.6 | `nothing provides 'libxkbcommon'` | installs, runs |
| Rocky Linux 9 (glibc 2.34) | installs; `effectcraft-cli`: ``libm.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.35' not found`` | refused: `nothing provides libm.so.6(GLIBC_2.35)(64bit)` |

The aarch64 RPMs get the same requires. I checked that side on FilmCraft only: its 0.7.2 arm64 binaries need
GLIBC_2.35 for the same two libm symbols, and its branch RPM installs and runs on arm64 Fedora 44,
Tumbleweed and Leap 15.6 (qemu-user).

`cargo xtask ci` passes. This tests installation and the CLI, not the GUI. The same results for every
Crafting App: https://github.com/storytold/craft-launcher/issues/341#issuecomment-6171570045

title: Fix launch guard ownership during concurrent startup
author: FredApps
body:
Refs #477.

Fixes a reproduced concurrent-launch guard ownership bug discovered during the startup-adapter follow-up. A second launch must not remove or overwrite a live owner's pending marker or reset its graphics preference. This is a narrower verified defect than the original, already-closed NVIDIA/surface report; it does not claim that exact hardware failure was reproduced.

Changes:
- Keep a stable launch.lock file and acquire it before recovery-state changes.
- Read preferences again under the guard, respect older versions holding the pending-marker lock, and leave state untouched when ownership is unavailable.
- Remove the pending marker before releasing ownership; guard failed-OpenGL cleanup too.
- Preserve explicit WGPU_BACKEND overrides and add ownership/recovery regressions.

Tests actually run with Rust 1.99.0 on Linux:
- Native workspace: 3,412 passed, 0 failed, 26 ignored (both recorded aggregate runs).
- Release startup follow-up: 40 unit and 3 argument tests passed.
- Formatting, strict release Clippy, layers and assets passed.
- cargo xtask wasm: 32 crates checked successfully on the offline retry. Earlier aggregates failed only at a missing offline js-sys dependency; checksum-verified reuse of existing cached archives resolved it. One warning remains in unchanged pointer_wrap.rs.
- Actual patched-release initialization recovery and explicit-backend assertions passed.

Not tested: physical NVIDIA hardware or native macOS startup. The original hardware report stays separately scoped. No dependencies or system tools were installed for this validation.

title: perf(expr): reuse validated results within bounded working sets
author: eliasx45
body:
Expressions that repeatedly read other properties rerun scripts and rebuild host data unnecessarily. This PR extracts the expression-performance work from #856 into an independent change against current main, then extends its bounded result memo to retain graph-sized working sets. This PR has no media/audio, GPU residency, UI, dependency or manifest changes.

### What changes

- Collect multiple unresolved host reads per pass, prefetch previously observed reads, and load keyframe arrays only when the keyframe API asks for them.
- Reuse successful expression results only after validating their recorded host answers. Native impurity tracking bypasses memoization for `Math.random` and `Date`, including computed access, aliases and prototype access; existing cycle/time limits remain.
- Allow up to 65,536 small results within a 32 MiB estimated retained-storage budget per thread, account for payload and table capacity, and reuse bounded table storage on clears. Validated hits skip unused metadata preparation.
- Compute shape `sourceRectAtTime` bounds without rasterizing, using the same buffer-extent calculation as rendering.
- Include synthetic regression coverage and a standalone profiling probe; no third-party assets or new dependencies.

### Measurements and limits

The cache-capacity follow-up was measured on a local development integration, **not rerun on this upstream adaptation**. For repeated sweeps of 20 expression properties (28,800 evaluations), the standalone probe improved from **300.97 → 21.02 ms p50** and **321.80 → 26.66 ms p95**. Numeric checksums matched at 1/4/8/20/50 properties. Peak diagnostic-process RSS rose from **27.36 → 57.58 MiB**. The 50-property working set still exceeds the cache and still executes every script.

These are CPU evaluator measurements, not input-to-visible-frame latency or a whole-PR speedup claim. The budget estimates retained memo storage, not allocator RSS or total app RAM, and is per thread. Methodology and the full table:…

title: pdf: bound CFF endchar seac recursion so a cyclic font can't overflow the stack
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Importing a PDF or AI file that embeds a name-keyed CFF font whose accented glyph is an `endchar` seac pointing back at itself (directly or through a short cycle) recurses in `Cff::outline` until the stack overflows and the process aborts — a stack overflow is not catchable by the app's `catch_unwind` guard, so the whole app dies. The seac components are resolved with `find(code).and_then(|g| self.outline(g))` and there is no depth limit, while the Type 1 interpreter one file over already bounds the same nesting with `depth < 2`.

This mirrors that guard: `outline` stays the entry point and routes the components through a private `outline_depth(gid, depth)`, so a cyclic font is cut off instead of crashing. The regression test builds a `w adx ady 65 65 endchar` glyph that seacs onto itself using the existing `write_test_cff` fixture and asserts the outline comes back empty; before the fix the test process overflowed the stack (SIGABRT), after it passes.

Partially addresses #1446 (finding 1, CFF seac recursion). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: pdf: endchar takes its width by operand parity like the stems and rmoveto
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
A CFF glyph whose charstring is a bare four-operand `endchar` seac (`adx ady bchar achar`) imports empty: `endchar` called `take_width(false)`, so it ate `adx` as the glyph width, left only three operands, and dropped the seac entirely; a five-operand `endchar` never took its leading width and silently fell back to the Private DICT default.

`take_width`'s flag means "the no-width argument count is even" (stems and `rmoveto` pass `true`, `hmoveto`/`vmoveto` pass `false`), and endchar's no-width counts, 0 and 4, are both even — so it must pass `true`. The fix is that one-line change plus a comment; the regression test draws a base square, checks that a four-operand seac keeps its base outline, and checks that a five-operand seac reports its stated 600-unit width — both assertions fail before the fix.

Partially addresses #1446 (finding 3, endchar width polarity). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: pdf: checked_add for CFF Private DICT and Type 1 RD offsets from the file
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
Three file-supplied `offset + length` additions in the font readers were still unchecked: the CFF Private DICT slice (`d.get(off..off + size)`), the Private DICT local-Subrs lookup (`index(d, off + s)`), and the Type 1 binary-item reader (`priv_.get(q..q + n)`) add numbers taken straight from the font file, where a huge real saturates to `usize::MAX` on cast. On debug/test builds (overflow checks on) a crafted font — a CFF top DICT with Private `[1E300 1E300]`, or a Type 1 `/Subrs` entry with `RD` length `18446744073709551615` — makes the add overflow and panic the importer, violating the checked-arithmetic rule in AGENTS.md.

All three sites now use `checked_add` and fall back to the existing "empty Private DICT" / "skip the damaged item" behaviour. Regression tests build both fixtures and assert the font still parses (`.notdef` present); both failed with "attempt to add with overflow" before the fix.

Partially addresses #1446 (finding 4, DICT offset overflow). Targeted tests green locally; `cargo xtask ci` left to the project runners.

title: Typed values: with several layers selected, set only the edited component on each
author: DWAA1660
body:
Fixes #1434

## Problem
With several layers selected, typing a value into one field (for example a 3D layer's Z Position) in the Properties panel, the Timeline or Effect Controls sent the edited layer's whole value. Combined with `selected: true`, `prop.set` gave every selected layer that same value. The other layers all took the first layer's X and Y and stacked on top of it, so they seemed to disappear. Scrubbing worked because it sends an offset.

## Fix
- **`prop.set` takes `dims`** (`crates/engine/src/commands/prop.rs`). With `selected` and a typed (non-offset) value, the other selected layers get only those components and keep the rest of their own value. Position with Separate Dimensions is included. The edit stays one undo step, and `dims` is declared in the command's parameter schema.
- **The three panels send `dims`** (`properties.rs`, `timeline.rs`, `effect_controls.rs`). It lists the components the edit changed: the typed one, or both for linked Scale.
- **Agents are unaffected:** without `dims`, `prop.set` still sets the whole value on every selected layer.

## Tests
- **UI test** (`crates/ui-egui/tests/ui_inline_edit.rs`): `typing_one_component_with_several_layers_selected_keeps_their_other_components` selects two 3D solids and types −300 into A's Z Position in the Timeline. title: Fix GPU/CPU parity in numerical effects
author: skylartaylor
body:
GPU renders diverge from the CPU oracle at quantization, arbitrary-map wraps, rotated tile boundaries and particle/VR directions on the tested Vulkan drivers. Use stable angular math and bounded division/rounding in shaders; build arbitrary-map boundaries and shared Grid Wipe/Hex Tile geometry in the CPU's precision before uploading masks or coordinates. Source images remain on the GPU and geometry rows use Rayon.

Add regressions for angular directions, alpha/quantization boundaries, signed and fractional map phases, and GPU residency. Retain existing CPU thresholds. Preserve egui symbol fallbacks in the theme and keep plug-in fixture builds in the assigned target so the complete validation gates run. The branch uses current main dependencies, with only Rayon added to the GPU crate; there are no Wayland/toolkit overrides.

Validation: current-main full CI passes (3,408 tests passed, 26 ignored; 32 WASM crate checks). The same 217-test GPU binary passes on Intel P630 and llvmpipe Vulkan with no adapter skips. Native edit/save/reopen passes on Sway, KDE, Hyprland and a GPU-backed GNOME virtual fixture with an explicit redraw clock. Existing CPU oracle thresholds remain unchanged.

Other GPU vendors/platforms and controlled performance comparisons remain unqualified. Geometry uploads add CPU work and temporary buffers; physical input and physical GNOME presentation are outside this PR's qualification.

title: GPU: match the CPU's rounding in box blur rows and affine warp sampling
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
**Depends on #1415 to show.** Without #1415, 4K effect frames run out of GPU memory and fall back to the CPU, so the GPU kernels this PR changes never run in those tests. The diff itself doesn't depend on #1415.

## Why

GPU and CPU renders of the same comp differ by one 8-bit level in a few pixels around blurred edges. Two sources of this are in the GPU kernels:

1. **Box blur rows.** The GPU's horizontal box pass restarts its running sum every 256 pixels. The CPU keeps one running sum per row, and restarting rounds differently. Vertical passes already restart in blocks on both sides, at the same block size.
2. **Affine warp sampling.** The CPU maps output pixels to source positions in f64. The GPU does it in f32, so a pixel can land on a slightly different source position and get slightly different bilinear weights.

## What

GPU output changes on purpose in this PR, to match the CPU's. CPU output does not change (verified pixel for pixel).

- **Box blur:** the horizontal pass runs one running sum per row (block = row width), as the CPU does. Vertical passes are unchanged.
- **Warp:** the host passes what the f32 inverse matrix rounded off (`f64 - f32`) as a second set of coefficients. For affine warps with nearest or bilinear sampling, `warp_blend` rebuilds the f64 mapping as double-f32 (hi + lo) arithmetic, so a pixel maps to the CPU's source position and weights. A host-set factor of 1.0 keeps the GPU compiler from simplifying away the rounding-error terms. Perspective warps and other sampling modes keep the f32 path.

## Results

GPU = RTX 3090, CPU = Ryzen 7 5800X. 4K, frame 0. Both builds are `main` + #1415, without and with this commit. The table counts pixels that differ between CPU and GPU renders.

| Project | Without | With |
|---|---|---|
| Minimal blur project 1 | 11 | 3 |
| Minimal blur project 2 | 24 | 9 |
| Minimal blur project 3 (Gaussian) | 24 | 11 |
| Minimal blur project 4 | 8 | 2 |
| Transformed layer, no blur | 1 | 0 |

title: ui-egui: a click that opens the colour picker no longer closes it in the same frame (#1476)
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The colour picker could close in the same frame it opened, so it flashed and vanished instead of staying up — most visible when the swatch sat anywhere but the top-left of the window. The cause is that the picker's egui Area only reports its real position from its second pass: on the pass it first draws, its rect is still at the origin, so the click that opened it landed outside that stale rect and was taken for a press outside the popup. The picker now ignores an outside press on the pass that first draws it, tracked per popup id; from the next pass on, clicking outside, Escape and Cancel close it exactly as before. A kittest regression places a swatch away from the origin, clicks it, and asserts the picker is still open, and the picker's own suite plus the gradient-editor suites that close it by clicking outside stay green.

Fixes #1476

title: UI fix: double-clicking an effect controls property should reveal it in the timeline
author: caldiag
body:
Issue https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/issues/1456 mentions that double-clicking a property in the properties panel should reveal it in the timeline.
In After Effects, the same behaviour is observed when double-clicking a property in the effect controls panel: double-click a property and it is revealed in the timeline for quick access.

This pull request implements this expected behavior for the effect controls panel, while not touching the properties panel because that has already been implemented by another pull request from another collaborator. (see https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/pull/1472)

## What changed
- The effect control panel's property click handler discarded the information about whether a click was a single or a double-click. This change actually uses that value, and if it was a double-click, the property is revealed in the timeline. if it was a single click, it proceeds as normal.
- A small function, `reveal_effect_property`, was added to `timeline.rs`. It reveals a given effect property in the timeline. It returns false for a missing layer, a layer without effects, or a property outside the "Effects" group. That prevents a double-click on a non-effect property from changing the Timeline’s reveal state.
- A test was added to prevent regression, which passes normally. I also compiled and tested myself and everything works as expected, matching After Effect's behavior.

The changes are very minimal and don't affect surrounding behavior.

title: bench: a malformed results line is an error naming the file and line, not silently dropped
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The benchmark comparison silently discarded any results line it could not parse, so a truncated or corrupt results file could still produce an apparently valid comparison — and a passing `--fail-over` gate — from the lines that happened to parse. `read_jsonl` now fails with the file and line number of a malformed nonempty line (and of a line that is valid JSON but not a result object); blank lines remain allowed. A regression test writes a file with one valid line and one truncated line, asserts the error names the file and the line, and that blank lines stay acceptable. The whole xtask suite (15 tests) is green. Fixes #1303
Atomic writes used one fixed `.tmp` sibling created with `File::create`, so two writers saving the same destination shared a temporary: each could truncate the other mid-write and the published file could be a mixture, and a pre-existing file or symlink at the predictable name was opened and written through. Two regression tests pin the mixture case (barrier-coordinated writers; the old code published 32×`B` + 32×`A`) and the planted-symlink case, and the existing crash-mid-write test still passes. title: Render speed: blur, shadow and composite only the pixels that draw; coarse grid for wide blurs
author: alexoms
body:
## Summary

Text and shape layers that have a drop shadow, a glow or a blur are the staple of title templates. Rendering one spent most of the frame on empty pixels: the effect stack grew the layer's buffer to the whole comp (#659), and then every pass ran over all of it. This PR makes those effects and the composite work only on the pixels that draw, and blurs wide Gaussians on a coarser grid.

**Changes**

- **Effect stack.** A stack made only of Drop Shadow, Glow and Gaussian Blur (with Repeat Edge Pixels off) no longer grows an authored layer's buffer to the layer rectangle. Each of these effects already pads the buffer by its own reach. Any other effect still triggers the #659 growth.
- **Gaussian blur** (`effectcraft_raster::gaussian_blur`, so also Glow, Drop Shadow, mask feather and character blur): runs over the content's bounds grown by the blur's reach, not over the whole buffer. An empty buffer stays empty.
- **Wide Gaussians** (sigma ≥ 16 px on both axes) are blurred on a grid 2–16× coarser and interpolated back. A test holds this within 1.5/255 of the full-resolution result. It applies only when the content's reach stays inside the buffer, or when edges repeat; otherwise the per-pass truncation at the buffer edge is kept exactly.
- **Drop Shadow:**
  - With no visible strength (Opacity 0 or a transparent colour), it leaves the layer alone.
  - Otherwise it samples only where the shifted content lands.
- **Composites:**
  - A composite reads only the source's drawn area, plus 3 px for the widest filter.
  - Stencil modes keep the full rectangle.
  - Motion-blurred layers trim the buffer once for all their sub-samples. The crop is aligned to 64 px, so minification halvings line up as before.
- **8/16 bpc quantising** skips zero pixels.
- **New helpers:** `Image::content_bounds`, `Image::crop_rect` and `Image::paste`.

## Measurements

The test set was 60 motion-graphics templates: titles, lower thirds, callouts, transitions, overlays, social, logo reveals…

title: Export: render in parallel once the GPU stops for good
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## Problem
A GPU export renders at most `EFFECTCRAFT_GPU_INFLIGHT` frames at once (1 by default, #879), so frames in flight don't exhaust VRAM. The cap stays on after the GPU has stopped for good: its device was lost, or it ran out of memory and its context was retired. From then on every frame is declined and rendered on the CPU, but still one at a time. A heavy 4K comp that runs out of GPU memory on its first frame then exports more slowly than with GPU acceleration off.

## Change
- `Accelerator::available()` (default `true`). The GPU accelerator returns `false` once its context is unhealthy (`check_health`), which is the same condition that makes it decline every frame.
- The export checks it before each chunk of capped frames. Once the accelerator is unavailable, the rest of the job renders like the CPU path: frames in parallel, with no cap.
- The cap and its windows are unchanged while the GPU is healthy, and so is the uncapped CPU path.
- 3 files, +69/-5. New unit test: frames after the GPU stops render more than one at a time, in order.

## Results
RTX 3090 (24 GB), Vulkan, 16 threads. Two 4K bench comps (generated by the bench scripts), 6 frames each, H.264. Both run out of GPU memory on frame 0 on current main.

| Comp | CPU only | GPU before | GPU after |
|---|---|---|---|
| Effects stack (4K) | 76.5 s | 113.1 s | 100.7 s |
| Blur/glow (4K) | 47.9 s | 75.2 s | 61.8 s |

- After the change, frames 1-5 render together, where before they rendered one after another.
- The remaining gap to CPU only is frame 0: the GPU spends 5-20 s on it before running out of memory, and the CPU then renders it alone. Starting the CPU sooner, or not trying the GPU on a frame it can't fit, is a separate change.
- Output is identical to the CPU-only render (decoded frame MD5s match), both before and after.
- A healthy GPU export is unaffected, since `available()` stays `true` and the cap applies as before.

## Tests
- `cargo fmt --check`, plus `cargo clippy --no-deps -D warnings…

body:
## What this is

**Craft AI** — one assistant across the ArtCraft family, as a dock panel in EffectCraft. It talks to a local model runtime on this machine and never to a cloud service:

title: GPU: stop drawing a frame once the device has failed
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## Problem
On heavy 4K comps the GPU runs out of memory partway through frame 0. The compositor keeps drawing the rest of that frame's layers on a device that has already failed. Each later layer fails as well, and frame 0 only goes back to the CPU after the full comp has been walked. In the trace, frame 0 of `c_effects` is declined 20.4 s into the export, 10 s after the GPU retired.

## Change
`walk::draw_comp` now checks `check_health()` before each layer (`draw_precomp` already does this). Once the device has failed, the frame returns `None` right away and goes to the CPU renderer as before. That is 3 lines in `crates/gpu/src/walk.rs`. There is no behaviour change while the GPU is healthy.

Independent of #1511 (the fallback-parallel PR); the two stack cleanly. No overlap with #1415, #1441 or #898.

## Results

title: GPU: free effect working textures after each call instead of at frame end
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## Summary
Effect working textures are now freed after each `Gpu::effects` call instead of being kept until the frame ends, and idle pool owners no longer keep their own sets: unused textures go to one shared free list capped at 256 MiB (`POOL_BUDGET`).

**Scope of the budget:** 256 MiB caps the shared free list of unused textures only. It does not cap total live GPU memory or driver/allocator-reserved memory; textures held by live `Enc`s and textures waiting on open encoders are outside it.

**Current results** ([comment 6223542652](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/pull/1523#issuecomment-6223542652), 4K, old = 13a49c94 (this PR's first commit) vs new = f0297669, the same patches as the current head 73312c25) are mixed on peak memory, not a universal memory reduction:
- RTX 3090 24 GB / Ryzen 7 5800X: d_blurglow wall 277.8–280.7 s → 245.1 s (about 12% faster), peak reserved 9204 → 8948–9204 MB. c_effects wall 46.6–52.4 s → 47.1 s, peak reserved 6080 → 6336–6592 MB (256–512 MB higher).
- GTX 1070 8 GB / i7-7700HQ: neutral. c_effects 84.7 → 84.8 s, peak reserved 6016 → 6272–6448 MB; d_blurglow 557.1 → 558.9 s, peak reserved 8149 MB on both (the card is full).
- Output md5 is identical between old and new in every run.

## Problem
On heavy 4K comps the GPU runs out of memory on frame 0 (RTX 3090, 24 GB), and every frame then renders on the CPU. A per-layer probe of the texture pool on `c_effects` shows where the memory goes:

- Live images: 1 texture (126 MB) after every layer. The layers themselves don't keep their textures.
- The shared pool's `released` list: grows by about 16 textures (about 1.1 GB) per layer, reaching 252 textures (17.7 GB) by layer 17.
- Reserved device memory: 23.1 GB by layer 17, where the device runs out.

Those textures come from the effects path, `Gpu::effects` → `run_chain`. The CPU renderer calls it for each layer with GPU effects, and each call uses a fresh `Enc`. When that `Enc` drops, its textures go back to the shared pool. The…

author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## Problem

When `Gpu::headless()` fails, the effectcraft-gpu test helpers print "no GPU adapter, skipping" and every GPU comparison test passes without running. The real reason is dropped (it only goes to `log::info!`). On DirectX 12, the GPU is present but initialization fails (FXC can't compile `classic3d`, #613). title: EPS and PDF: huge arcs, long paths and loop passes count against the import's limits
author: dotCooCoo
body:
The EPS interpreter in `crates/pdf/src/ps.rs` counted one operation against its budget of 8,000,000 for each name it ran, whatever the operator did, and paths had no length limit. On `main` at 05955c0:

- Parsing an EPS file with `newpath 0 0 10 300 exp 0 90 arc` passed 3 GiB of resident memory after 43 seconds. kurbo divides a quarter turn at that radius into about 3.7 × 10^49 curves, more than `usize::MAX`, and `arc` kept appending them.
- `{ newpath 0 0 2200000000000000000 0 1440 arc } loop` was still running after 60 seconds. A loop of `pathbbox` on a path of 100,001 elements and `{ {} loop } loop` did not finish within 20 seconds.
- PDF content had no path limit either: parsing a page that repeats `0 0 1 1 re` 4,000,000 times peaked at 2.3 GiB of resident memory, and the page budget of 20,000,000 operators allows 100,000,000 path elements.

## What changes

- A path holds at most 1,048,576 elements (`MAX_PATH` in `crates/pdf/src/build.rs`, the limit of VectorCraft's EPS interpreter). In `ps.rs`, `moveto`, `lineto`, `curveto` and their relative forms, `closepath`, `arc` and `arcn` (for each curve), `charpath` (for the outlines it adds) and `rectfill`, `rectstroke` and `rectclip` (for their rectangles) check it, and an operator that would take a path past it stops the program with the skip note "PostScript (path limit)". The PostScript Language Reference lists `limitcheck` among the errors of these operators. In `page.rs`, `m`, `l`, `c`, `v`, `y`, `h` and `re` (each adds at most five elements) stop the content stream with "content (path limit)" when the path already holds more than 1,048,571.
- Each path element an operator makes, reads or copies counts against the EPS budget: the curves of `arc` and `arcn`, the rectangles of an array, the outlines of `charpath`, and the current path that `pathbbox` reads and `clip`, `eoclip`, `gsave` and `save` copy. Each pass of `repeat`, `for`, `loop` and `forall` counts too, and so does each procedure item that is not a name.…

title: Effects: Black & White no longer turns faint colour noise in shadows into blocks
author: guillehr2
body:
Fixes #1463.

## Cause

The screenshots in the issue are dark footage, and the artifacts are blocky bright and black specks in the shadows. It isn't a GPU/CPU mismatch or a precision problem: the `fxc_point` op 3 kernel in `fx_color.wgsl` mirrors `color_fx::black_white` operation for operation, so both paths show it at every bit depth. The formula is the problem:

```
gray = luminance + (hue weight − 0.5) × HSL saturation × 0.6
```

HSL saturation is `(max − min) / (max + min)` below mid-gray, so it is near 1 for *any* tinted near-black pixel: (2, 0, 2)/255 has saturation 1. The faint colour noise that compressed video carries in its shadows (a code or two per channel, in 8×8 blocks) therefore moved the gray by up to 0.18 of full scale at the default weights (more with the sliders pushed), up or down depending on the noise's hue. At the defaults a near-black pixel with a 2/255 magenta tint, (2, 0, 2)/255, went from 0.2 % to 18 % gray, and a slightly green one was clipped to black. In 32 bpc an overbright pixel such as (1.5, 0.5, 0.5) also divided by zero (`2 − max − min = 0`) and came out black or infinite.

## Fix

Keep the hue weighting (the six sliders, interpolated around the colour wheel by hue, as before), but apply it to the pixel's chroma instead of offsetting the luminance:

```
gray = min + (max − min) × hue weight
```

- A neutral pixel keeps its value (as before), at any bit depth.
- A pure hue becomes its slider's percentage: at the defaults pure red is 40 % gray, yellow 60 %, blue 20 %, magenta 80 %. That is what the slider values describe. As far as I know it is also how Photoshop's Black & White adjustment behaves (the same six sliders and defaults), but I couldn't check it against After Effects here. The old formula gave pure red 15 %, pure yellow 99 % and pure blue 0 %.
- The gray never leaves the pixel's own channel range when every weight is between 0 and 100 %, so a code or two of colour noise moves it by at most a code or two.
- Nothing divides…

Fonts configured through `FONTCONFIG_PATH` can be available to Fontconfig but missing from EffectCraft. The current discovery code reads `FONTCONFIG_FILE` and the standard configuration files, but ignores that search path.

title: gpu: upload cache drops textures of freed buffers on every insert
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## Problem
`GpuContext::upload_buf` keys uploaded layer buffers by `Arc::as_ptr` and holds a `Weak<Buf>`.
Entries whose buffer was freed were pruned only once the cache went over its budget
(`UPLOAD_BUDGET`, 1.5 GiB by default). An animated layer makes a new buffer every frame, so each
frame left a dead texture (~127 MiB at 4K RGBA32F) allocated until the cache filled up: up to
1.5 GiB of VRAM that nothing could hit again. Present on main.

## Fix
Drop entries whose buffer has no strong references on every insert, then evict the least
recently used over budget as before. Hits are unchanged.

## Test
`tests::upload_cache_drops_textures_of_freed_buffers` uploads six short-lived 256×256 buffers and
checks the cache keeps at most one more entry than before.
- Without the fix: fails, "the upload cache kept 6 textures of freed buffers (had 0)".
- With the fix: passes.

Run on Apple M4 with `EFFECTCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`: the gpu crate passes 212 of 213 tests. The one
failure is `tests_init::opengl_adapters_get_cpu_compositing_at_once` (no GL adapter on macOS),
which also fails without this change.

## Numbers (AMD Ryzen 7 5800X / NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090, Vulkan, 4K d_blurglow, gpu.mem trace)
- With the fix the cache held 5–6 live entries (0.7–0.84 GB), with at most one dead entry.
- On its own this doesn't fix the out-of-memory error at 3 frames in flight (that's the memory
  back-pressure PR). It stops up to 1.5 GiB being held for nothing.
- The output is unchanged.

title: gpu: memory back-pressure for frames in flight (fixes OOM at 3–4 frames in flight)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Depends on #1523 (fx-owner, 13a49c94).

## Root cause
With several frames in flight, VRAM fills up with resources we already let go of. A
`gpu.mem=detail` trace of 4K d_blurglow at 3 in flight, just before the out-of-memory error:
- The allocator held 45 layer-upload textures (6.7 GB). Only 6 still had a live `GpuImage`
  handle, all in the upload cache. The other 39 (~5.8 GB) were dropped on our side, but wgpu
  hadn't destroyed them yet: it does that only once the submissions that used them complete.
- About 3 GB more was in wgpu's internal staging buffers for queue writes, and 2.6 GB was pool
  textures owned by frames.
- Uploading into pooled textures instead only moved the problem: 14 GB of pool textures sat in
  "pending", and it hit more OOM errors.

So nothing leaks for good: frames in flight record work faster than the GPU retires it.

## Fix
`Enc::mem_gate` runs after each effect call and each layer. Every 8th call it reads the wgpu
allocator report, and if more than the cap is allocated, the frame submits its encoder and waits
for the queue. wgpu then frees what was dropped, and pending pool textures become free.
- Cap: wgpu has no safe query for adapter memory (the workspace forbids unsafe). The default is
  8 GiB on discrete GPUs and 2 GiB on integrated/other adapters. `EFFECTCRAFT_GPU_MEMCAP_MB`
  overrides it; 0 turns it off.
- Backends without an allocator report (Metal, GL, WebGPU) are never gated.
- The first wait logs one info line.

## Results
AMD Ryzen 7 5800X / NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24 GB), Vulkan, 4K, 6 frames, wall-clock seconds,
no environment variables. 3 runs each, interleaved base/memcap; min / median:

| comp | build | in flight | min | median | OOM | output |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| d_blurglow | base 13a49c94 | 2 | 44.75 | 45.77 | 0 | DEA9290B5BAC |
| d_blurglow | base 13a49c94 | 3 | (earlier run) 72.94 | – | yes | 931521E85733 (CPU output: frames that ran out of memory fell back to the CPU path) |

title: fix(script): per-key methods act on keys outside the active comp (#1531)
author: AyberkA0
body:
Fixes #1531.

## Cause

Per-key script methods (`setInterpolationTypeAtKey`, `setTemporalEaseAtKey`, `removeKey`…) go through `exec_on_keys` in `crates/script/src/runtime.rs`. It swaps the named keys into `state.selected_keys` and then calls `exec`, which activates the command's target comp.

Since comps keep their own selections (`activate_comp` → `remember_selection` / `recall_selection`, new in 0.10.0), that activation:

1. stored the freshly injected keys as the selection of the comp that *was* active;
2. brought back the target comp's own key selection, usually empty.

So `keys.interpolation` / `keys.velocity` ran with nothing selected and succeeded doing nothing. That matches the report's table:

| Report's case | Why |
|---|---|
| It works when C is the only comp | No switch happens |
| It works after `C.openInViewer()` | No switch happens |
| It works when the earlier comp is empty | That comp is never activated |
| It fails once another comp with a layer has been active | The switch replaces the injected keys |

## Fix

`exec_on_keys` now activates the keys' comp *before* swapping in the key selection, runs the command (`exec` then has no comp to switch), restores the user's key selection there, and finally makes the previously active comp active again. The return-to-previous-comp logic that `exec` already had moved into a small `leave_comp` helper, so both paths share it.

The user's key selection is kept per comp as before: the target comp gets its own selection back, filtered to keys that still exist.

## Test

`key_interpolation_and_ease_apply_outside_the_active_comp` is the issue's repro: comp A with a layer, then C with a 3D null's Y rotation keyed and eased.

- Without the fix it fails exactly as reported: `[false, false, 33.33, -44.5]` (Linear, default ease, the linear value).
- With the fix: Bezier on both keys, 60 % influence, and an eased value.

`cargo test -p effectcraft-script` (94 passed), `cargo fmt --check`.

title: Scripting: setInterpolationTypeAtKey / setTemporalEaseAtKey act on their key in a comp that isn't active (#1531)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1531

## What was wrong

The per-key methods (`setInterpolationTypeAtKey`, `setTemporalEaseAtKey`, `removeKey`, `setTemporalContinuousAtKey`, …) run through `exec_on_keys` in `crates/script/src/runtime.rs`. It put the target key into the live `selected_keys` while the *current* comp was still active, and only then let `exec` make the property's comp active. Since every comp keeps its own selection while it isn't active (#1037), `activate_comp` stashed the target key under the comp being left and recalled the property comp's remembered selection, so `keys.interpolation` / `keys.velocity` / `keys.delete` ran on that:

- nothing selected there: a silent no-op (the report: keys stay Linear, no ease);
- keys the user had selected there: **those** keys changed, or were deleted by `removeKey`, instead of the one named.

It only worked when the property's comp was already active, hence the `openInViewer()` workaround.

## The fix

`exec_on_keys` activates the property's comp *before* swapping the selection, puts that comp's own selection back afterwards (minus keys the command removed), and then gives back the comp that was active. That last step is the same as `exec`'s, now shared as `restore_active`.

## Tests

New `crates/script/src/tests_key_methods.rs`:
- the script from the report: Bezier on both keys, 60 % ease, `valueAtTime(1.25)` eased instead of the linear -44.5;
- with comp A active and a key selected in A and another in C: `setInterpolationTypeAtKey`, `setTemporalEaseAtKey` and `removeKey` on C's keys change exactly the key named, A stays active with its key selection, and C's remembered selection is still the user's key once C is opened.

Both fail on `main` (the second shows the ease landing on the selected key 3 and `removeKey(1)` deleting key 3) and pass with the fix.

Local (Linux, Gentoo): `cargo fmt --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, `cargo test -p effectcraft-script`, `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask assets`. WIP until the full gate run is reported…

title: fix(viewer): Shift-click with the Pen draws a straight segment (#1544)
author: AyberkA0
body:
Fixes #1544.

## Cause

In `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/viewer.rs`, `pen_press` adds each vertex of the path being drawn at the clicked point, snapped by `vt::snap`, and never reads Shift. So a Shift-click after the first point landed exactly where the pointer was, and a vertical, horizontal or diagonal segment had to be lined up by eye.

## Fix

With Shift held, the new vertex now moves onto the nearest line through the previous vertex at a multiple of 45°: horizontal, vertical or diagonal. It's placed as far along that line as the click lies. The constraint is computed in comp space, after snapping, through a small pure helper, `constrain_45`. It applies to masks and shape paths alike, since both are drawn through this branch. Without Shift nothing changes.

A non-finite or zero offset returns the point unchanged, so there's no NaN direction.

Not included: constraining a Bezier tangent dragged out with Shift. That's a separate gesture (`Gesture::Pen` drag).

## Tests

- `pen_shift_click_keeps_the_segment_at_45_degrees` (unit) covers straight down, left, the up-right diagonal, the vertex itself, and a non-finite point.
- `pen_shift_click_draws_a_straight_segment` (`tests/ui_viewer.rs`) draws a mask on Plate. A Shift-click at (112, 250) after (100, 60) lands on (100, 250); the next plain click lands where it was clicked. Without the fix it fails with the vertex at (112, 250).

`cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --lib panels::viewer::tests`, `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --test ui_viewer pen_` (all passed), `cargo fmt --check`.

title: pdf: a soft mask at an unsupported bit depth is ignored, not fatal
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`mask_image` reads `/BitsPerComponent` straight from the attacker-controlled `/SMask` dictionary with no validation and feeds it into `1u32 << bpc` (`crates/pdf/src/image.rs:184`). The main image path in the same file rejects anything but `1|2|4|8|16` before its own identical shift (`image.rs:234-238`) — the soft-mask path has no such check. Any PDF whose image carries `/SMask << /Width 1 /Height 1 /BitsPerComponent 32 >>` (reachable on file import, drag-and-drop, or control-channel import) makes `1u32 << 32` overflow: a debug/test/fuzz-build panic, and in release a wrapped shift that mistranslates every mask sample into alpha.

**Fix:** mirror `decode()`'s depth check — an unsupported mask depth means "no usable mask", so the image draws with the mask treated as absent (the same degradation a missing `/SMask` gets).

**Regression test:** `smask_with_absurd_bpc_is_ignored_not_fatal` — on main it panics at `crates/pdf/src/image.rs:184`; with the check the image still draws opaque and the full `effectcraft-pdf` lib suite is green (83 passed).

title: pdf: an inline image with absurd dimensions falls back to the EI scan
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`inline_len` computes `(w * n * bpc).div_ceil(8) * h` with `Width`/`Height` taken straight from the inline image's content-stream dictionary and **no size validation** — unlike `decode()` (`image.rs:207`) and `mask_image` (`image.rs:176`), which bound their geometry first. `f64 as usize` saturation turns `/W 5000000000000000000` into a value whose `* bpc` alone exceeds `usize::MAX`: the multiply panics in debug/test/fuzz builds, and in release it wraps to a small length so the caller (`page.rs:518`, `(start + len).min(data.len())`) silently slices the wrong bytes — a misparsed image and a shifted `EI` resync from a ~40-byte content stream.

**Fix:** chain the arithmetic through `checked_mul` and return `None` — a path the caller already handles by scanning for the `EI` token instead.

**Regression test:** `inline_image_with_absurd_dimensions_falls_back_to_ei_scan` — on main it panics at `crates/pdf/src/image.rs:85`; with the chain the stream falls back to the scan and the full `effectcraft-pdf` lib suite is green (83 passed).

title: pdf: a gigantic Type 1 RD length is refused, not overflowed
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`read_binary` parses the `<n> RD <n bytes>` length prefix of every `Subrs`/`CharStrings` entry in an embedded Type 1's decrypted `Private` dict — fully attacker-controlled bytes (`Type1::parse` runs on embedded font programs during PDF import). A length like `18446744073709551615` parses to `usize::MAX`, and `q + n` is evaluated *before* the (otherwise correct) bounds-checked `.get()`: a debug/test/fuzz-build panic at `crates/pdf/src/type1.rs:146`. Release builds already degrade cleanly (wrapped add → `.get()` returns `None` → clean break), which is why this survived so far; the neighbouring PFB framing code clamps with `.min(data.len())` — only this closure adds raw.

**Fix:** one line — `let end = q.checked_add(n)?;`, using `end` for both the slice and the resume position.

**Regression test:** `absurd_rd_length_does_not_panic` — on main it panics at `crates/pdf/src/type1.rs:146`; with the checked add the font parses as `None` ("unreadable CharStrings are refused") and the full `effectcraft-pdf` lib suite is green (83 passed).

title: project: output_size never asks for sides past the comp limit
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
`RenderSettings::output_size` multiplies the comp size by the resolution without a ceiling: comps are repaired to `MAX_SIZE = 30 000` on load (`crates/project/src/limits.rs:92`) and a numeric `resolution` up to `4.0` is a sanctioned control-channel value (`crates/engine/src/commands/render_queue.rs:98`, `.clamp(0.01, 4.0)`, persisted in the project). So `30 000 × 4.0 = 120 000` px sides flow into the exporters' `w * h * 4` (`crates/export/src/lib.rs:238`): the 120 000² multiply overflows `u32` — debug panic, release wrap into a tiny `Vec` that the very next lines index with 64-bit offsets (slice panic) — after already asking the renderer for a ~57 GB frame.

Peer code bounds the same work: the resize path in this file clamps to 30 000 (`render_queue.rs:1107`) and `uncompressed.rs:83` uses `checked_mul` for the frame size.

**Fix:** clamp both sides of `output_size` to the 30 000 comp limit.

**Regression test:** `output_size_never_exceeds_the_comp_limit` — on main a 30 000 px comp at `resolution: 4.0` returns `(120000, 120000)`; with the clamp `(30000, 30000)`, through both `RenderSettings::output_size` and the `OutputModule` wrapper. Full `effectcraft-project` lib suite green (34 passed).

title: project: a hostile ROI cannot overflow the crop math
author: midasmatterhorn
body:
The `roi: [x, y, w, h]` quad is stored **raw**: `crop: {useRoi, roi}` passes `serde_json::from_value::<[f64; 4]>` straight through (`crates/engine/src/commands/render_queue.rs:271`) while every sibling in the same function is clamped (edge pixels ±20 000, resize 1..=30 000, quality/bitrate likewise), and `crates/project/src/limits.rs` repairs comps and solids but has no ROI handling — so a hostile control-channel call or a hand-edited `.ecproj` persists the quad.

`Crop::edges` then converts with `(v * scale).round() as i32` and subtracts raw (`crates/project/src/render_queue.rs:765-779`): `x = -1e12` saturates to `i32::MIN`, and `w as i32 - l` — and later `w as i32 - l - r` in `frame_size` (`:1097`) — overflows `i32`: a debug/test-build panic, and in release a wrap that lands a wrong but bounded crop into every export size computation.

**Fix:** clamp each converted edge to the same ±20 000 the sibling edge fields use, and subtract with `saturating_sub` in both `edges()` and `frame_size()`. Sane ROIs are untouched: the in-tree `roi: [100, 50, 800, 400]` at half resolution still yields `(400, 200)`.

**Regression test:** `hostile_roi_cannot_overflow_crop_math` — on main it panics at `crates/project/src/render_queue.rs:774`; with the fix the hostile quad degrades to a valid 1×1 frame and the full `effectcraft-project` lib suite is green (34 passed).

title: GPU: effect kernels build and match the CPU on DirectX 12 (#613)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## Problem

On DirectX 12 the GPU path was broken in three ways:

1. **FXC rejected kernels.** `classic3d` failed to build (X3550/X3511), so the GPU compositor did not start at all. `fxw_warp` failed too (X3507). Other effect kernels fell back to the CPU per effect.
2. **DXC compiled with fast math.** wgpu-hal passes DXC `-Ges` but not `-Gis`, so DXC marks every float op `fast` and reassociates. Our fma-corrected divisions (`fxs_qdiv`, `fx_noise`, `fx_key`) folded back into plain approximate ones, and those kernels stopped matching the CPU.
3. **Missing UAV barriers.** wgpu-hal's DX12 backend only issues a same-state UAV barrier after `STORAGE_READ_WRITE`. Two dispatches writing one write-only storage texture in a row could overlap, and the earlier write could land last. In the tests, the NaN fill of a pooled scratch texture raced the kernel writing it: for example, a VR blur on a stereo frame returned NaN for one eye. WARP was wrong too, so the bug is in wgpu, not the driver.

## Changes

- **`classic3d.wgsl`:** `occlusion` computes its three channels as one `vec3` instead of writing `o[k]` through a loop index, so FXC builds `classic3d`. Same operations, same output.
- **`context.rs`:** `classic3d` builds like the effect kernels. If a compiler rejects it, 3D runs render on the CPU instead of the whole compositor failing to start.
- **`fx_warp.wgsl`:** `fxw_style` no longer returns inside every `switch` case. The default (Twist) runs after the switch, so FXC accepts it. Same result on every backend.
- **Vendored `third_party/wgpu-hal` (30.0.1)**, via `[patch.crates-io]`. Both patches are small; drop the vendored copy once upstream has them:
  - DXC gets `DXC_ARG_IEEE_STRICTNESS` (`-Gis`). Upstream: gfx-rs/wgpu#10633
  - `transition_textures` also emits the UAV barrier after `STORAGE_WRITE_ONLY` and `STORAGE_ATOMIC`. Upstream: gfx-rs/wgpu#10632
- **Tests:**
  - New `classic_3d_runs_render_on_the_cpu_without_the_kernel`.
  - The 3D GPU-draw assertions skip when the k…

title: Text: a variable font's named instances are styles of its family (#1563)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1563

### Cause

The font scan only read whether a face has an `fvar` table, not its named instances. A variable family therefore showed up with one style (its default instance: `Light` for Figtree), `fonts::resolve("Figtree", "Black")` picked that face by nearest weight and switched on synthetic bold, and `resolve_by_name("Figtree-Black")` found no face with that PostScript name.

### Change

- `sfnt`: the scan reads the named instances from `fvar` (subfamily name, coordinates, PostScript name id; when a font names none, the PostScript name Adobe Technical Note #5902 derives: family prefix, `-`, style without spaces). Offsets use checked arithmetic and the instance count is bounded.
- `fonts`: `families()` lists the instances as styles of the family (so `text.fonts` and the font menu show `Light` … `Black`). A face's own style (its default instance) resolves as before, without axis values. `resolve` selects an instance by style name, by its PostScript name (`font = "Figtree-Black"`) or full name, and the nearest-weight fallback considers instances too, so `Bold` on a variable family takes the nearest instance instead of synthetic bold. `Resolved` carries the instance index.
- `layout`: the instance's axis values are the run's base variations; axes set on the text (`variations`) still win.
- `docs/agents.md`: how a named instance is selected.
- Character panel: the Variable Font Axes fields show the instance's values for axes the text doesn't set.
- `variable::find_variable_face` (test/demo helper) skips faces without Latin glyphs, so the name-and-`fvar`-only fonts the tests add aren't picked as "an installed variable font".

The public scripting API for axis values (third point in the triage note) is not part of this PR.

### Tests

- `sfnt::reads_named_instances_from_fvar`, `named_instances_survive_truncated_and_hostile_fvar`
- `fonts::variable_named_instances_resolve_and_list`, `explicit_variations_override_the_instance`
- `layout::named_instance_sets_the_…

author: eliasx45

title: i18n: the panel tabs, and the labels the call-shape scan cannot see
author: FeiLiuEM
body:

title: Copy only the selected keyframes across Position, Rotation and Scale (#1552)
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
Fixes #1552.

## Problem

Select keyframes on several properties at once (Position, Rotation and Scale), then Copy and Paste. Two things can go wrong:

- **Keys you deselected come back.** Clicking a keyframe also highlights its property. `copy_properties` copied *every* key of any highlighted property that had no selected key. Shift-click the Scale keys off, and Copy still took all of Scale's animation, so Paste wrote keyframes you never chose.
- **An old value copy hijacks the paste.** The selected-keys branch of `edit.copy` cleared only some clipboards and left `value_clipboard` in place. `edit.paste` checks `value_clipboard` before the key clipboard, so a property-value copy from earlier was pasted in place of the keyframes.

Either way, the reliable workaround was to copy and paste one property at a time, which is what the issue describes.

## Fix

In `crates/engine/src/commands/edit.rs`:

- `copy_properties` adds a property's whole animation only when no keyframe is selected, or when the Transform group itself is selected. With an explicit key selection, only those keys are copied. Unanimated highlighted properties still copy their value (#493).
- The keyframe branch of `copy` calls the existing `clear_clipboards`, the same as every other copy branch, so no stale clipboard outranks the new keys.

Key paste already maps a multi-property clip onto the matching properties at the CTI as one undo step. Nothing there changed.

## Tests

- `tests_timeline::copy_selected_keys_excludes_deselected_properties_and_stale_values` uses keys on Position, Rotation and Scale, with Scale toggled off and a stale value copy present. It checks paste timing, values, easing, the untouched Scale, and undo/redo. This test **fails on `main`** and passes with the fix.
- `tests_timeline::copy_mixed_animated_and_static_properties_keeps_the_static_value` keeps the #493 behaviour: animated keys plus a static value paste as one undo step.
- `ui_keyframes::copy_and_paste_key_subsets_across_pos…

title: M7: discover deep font libraries without recursive calls
author: IanHollow
body:
## Summary

An installed font sixteen directories below a configured library is silently missed because the directory walk stops after eight levels. Increasing that number would retain the same cutoff.

```text
walk a directory branch iteratively

```

title: fix(web): scripts can open files in browser storage; stored footage isn't reported missing (#1593)
author: rahal
body:
Fixes #1593

## Bugs (browser editor)
1. **A `.jsx` script can't open any file in browser storage**, even one next to the saved project. `File.open("r")` returns `false` with `File not found`, and `File.exists` is `false`.
2. **The footage check after File ▸ Open marks imported media as missing**, although it is in browser storage.

Desktop and CLI are not affected.

## Why the file is readable but scripts can't read it
- The page reads a stored file fine (`effectcraft.readFile("/data.txt")`).
- A `.jsx` runs inside the script engine and has only the After Effects scripting API. To read a file it must call `new File(path)`, then `open("r")`, then `read()`; `open` is required, as in After Effects.
- `read` goes through the editor's file layer (`Session.services`) and would find the file. But `open` first checks that the file exists, and that check asked the local disk (`std::fs`), skipping the file layer. A browser has no disk, so the check always failed and the read was never reached.
- The footage check asks the same question: `WebServices` kept the trait's default `exists`, which also asks `std::fs`.

This matters for template scripts, which read their data the After Effects way (`new File("props.json")`, `open`, `read`), so the same `.jsx` runs unchanged in After Effects, the desktop app, the CLI and the browser.

## Reproduce (web editor built from `main`, browser console)
`effectcraft.addFile` does what dropping a file on the page does: it stores the file in browser storage and imports it.

```js

  `var f = new File("${p}"); writeLn(f.open("r") ? f.read() : f.error); writeLn(f.exists);`})).output
// main: "File not found\nfalse"     this PR: "hello\ntrue"

await effectcraft.addFile("icon-256.png", "icon.png");

title: Glow: the A & B gradient rings the glow instead of the source (#941)
author: edgarciavfx
body:
Fixes #941.

## The defect

`Glow` with **Glow Colors: A & B Colors** took its gradient position from each **source** pixel's
brightness, in the bright pass, *before* the blur. On a subject of uniform brightness — text, a
logo, a solid, the usual Glow subject — every glowing pixel shares one brightness, so the gradient
collapsed to a single colour and **Color Looping, Color Loops, Color Phase and A & B Midpoint could
not change the result at all**.

Sweeping A & B Midpoint across its whole range left the glow bit-identical. On a white square with
Color A red, Color B blue, `Sawtooth A>B`, `Composite Original: None`:

```
abMidpoint=10  ->  [0.0, 0.0, 0.20668592, 0.20668592]
abMidpoint=50  ->  [0.0, 0.0, 0.20668592, 0.20668592]
abMidpoint=90  ->  [0.0, 0.0, 0.20668592, 0.20668592]
```

With `Triangle A>B>A` the same subject pinned to pure Color A for every midpoint. The slider only
appeared to work on footage that happens to carry a luminance ramp.

## The change

The bright pass keeps the glow's **strength** alone, and the gradient is applied to the **blurred**
glow, so it walks the glow's own falloff. Adobe's Stylize documentation describes Color Loops as
creating "multicolor ringing in the glow", and ringing across the glow is only possible if the
gradient follows the blurred falloff rather than the source pixel.

- `crates/effects/src/misc.rs` — `glow()`: the bright pass writes `k * a` for the gradient modes,
  and a pass after the blur walks `glow_ab_t` over the blurred strength. `glow_ab_t`'s doc comment
  now says what its input is.
- `crates/gpu/src/shaders/kernels.wgsl` — `glow_bright` writes the strength for gradient modes; new
  `glow_colorize` applies the A & B gradient to the blurred glow.
- `crates/gpu/src/shaders/fx_stylize.wgsl` — `fxs_glow_map` becomes the Arbitrary Map's colourise
  pass over the blurred strength, mirroring `glow_colorize`.
- `crates/gpu/src/effects.rs`, `crates/gpu/src/fx_stylize.rs`, `crates/gpu/src/context.rs` — both
  GPU call s…

title: Expressions: a long expression scrolls inside its Timeline field instead of running under the rows below
author: guillehr2
body:
Fixes #1396.

## Cause

The inline expression field grows with its text up to 8 Timeline rows (`EXPR_AUTO_LINES`), or to the height its bottom edge is dragged to. `expr_editor::editor` put the `TextEdit` straight into a child `Ui` with that rect as `max_rect`, but a multiline `TextEdit` takes the height of its whole galley, and the child's clip rect was the whole time-graph area. So a longer expression (the 21-line bounce expression in the issue) drew past the bottom of its field and on under the rows below: the rows painted over it, the line at the field's bottom edge was cut through by the next layer's bar, and the rest could not be read or reached, though the expression still evaluated. With Word Wrap off (the default), a line wider than the field also ran on past its right edge. The line numbers were painted the same way.

## Fix

- The `TextEdit` sits in an `egui::ScrollArea` that fills the field (without egui's 64-point minimum viewport). It scrolls up and down when the rendered text, with the `TextEdit`'s margins, is taller than the field's Timeline rows (wrapped lines and large editor fonts count), and sideways when Word Wrap is off and a line is wider than the field. Nothing draws outside the field's rows. The editor fills the field, so a click anywhere in it still edits, and the cursor is kept in view while typing.
- The comparison is with the rows rather than the inner field: a default-font line with its margins exactly fills one row but is a few points taller than a one-row field, so comparing with the field would make every one-line field scroll by a few points and take the wheel from the Timeline.
- The scroll bars float over the text (`ScrollStyle::floating()` with a visible dormant handle), so they don't eat a one-line field's only line, and a thin handle shows that there is more to see.
- The line numbers are clipped to the field and follow the scrolled text.
- The wheel over a field that scrolls that way scrolls its text, not the Timeline (`timelin…

title: Bump FilmCraft to 4e2d0bc2 (part of #804)
author: vangel76
body:
Part of #804.

## Why

#819 (hardware video decoding) needs a newer FilmCraft than the pinned `2c5ba7a`. The pin bump is the only part of that PR that touches existing code, so it is split out here to be reviewed on its own. #819 builds on this PR. This PR adds no `filmcraft-platform` dependency, no hardware setting and no `register()` call.

## What changed

All `filmcraft-*` git deps move from `2c5ba7a` (2026-10-03) to FilmCraft `main` `4e2d0bc2` (2026-10-10).

- **API:** `MediaInfo.audio` became `audio_streams` (`audio()` / `has_audio()`), and `VideoStreamInfo` gained `hdr`. Mechanical fixes in `interchange`, `media` and two tests.
- **Behaviour 1, frame requests:** FilmCraft now rounds a frame request to the track's nearest timestamp unit, halves up. The media pool asked for the middle of frame *i*; when the timescale equals the frame rate (our own 10 fps MP4 / MOV exports) that rounds onto frame *i+1*. The pool now asks a quarter of the way into the frame, which still tolerates timestamps rounded either way (one line in `pool.rs`). This fixed the export round-trips for H.264 / HEVC / AV1 / ProRes and the automation `qa::kinetic` test.
- **Behaviour 2, VP9 tests:** `filmcraft_vp9::Decoder::new()` now uses frame threads, so a picture can come out of a later call. The VP9 encoder tests expect one picture per call, so they use `Decoder::with_threads(1)`. Only test code uses the VP9 decoder.
- **Rotation and AAC downmix:** adapted to the new FilmCraft behaviour (`media/src/probe.rs`, `downmix.rs`, `pool.rs`).
- **Lockfile:** new FilmCraft crates pulled in by `filmcraft-export` (`render`, `text`, `captions`, `audio-dsp`). No `filmcraft-platform`.

## What maintainers must decide

Only the pin: whether to move to FilmCraft `4e2d0bc2`.

## Gates

`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, full `cargo test` of effectcraft-media, -export, -interchange, -render, -engine, -host and -vp9enc (all green), `cargo xtask layers`, `cargo xtask w…

title: Cryptomatte: skip the ID colours unless Colors shows them, key the layer in place, and cache each rank's last ID colour
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Follow-up to #1183, part of #473 (the speed of the Cryptomatte effect). Picking, the Layer popup and selection parsing are not touched. Two commits on current `main`.

## Change

1. **The GPU path skips the ID colours unless the Colors display reads them; the CPU path keys the layer in place.** `fx_depth::cryptomatte` asked the shared reduction for the ID colour on every aux pixel, but only the Colors display reads it. Matte, Preview and Matte Only now skip it. The CPU effect no longer copies the layer before keying it; it writes the matte into the layer's own buffer.
2. **Colors remembers each rank's last ID colour.** Neighbouring pixels mostly carry the same ID, so each rank keeps its last (ID, colour) pair and hashes only when the ID changes. Same hash and same colour, so the output does not change.

The arithmetic and its order are unchanged: the output is bit-identical in every display, on the CPU and on the GPU.

## Measured

CPU: AMD Ryzen 7 5800X (8 cores / 16 threads). GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (Vulkan), on Windows, idle machine. Test project: the issue's `blender_style_cryptomatte.exr` (2560×1440, 3 ranks), Selection `sphere`, `render` of 30 frames to H.264, wall time for the whole process, median of 3 with builds alternating.

| Display | 0.10.0 CPU | this PR CPU | 0.10.0 `--gpu` | this PR `--gpu` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Colors | 7.69 s | **6.92 s** | 8.52 s | **7.71 s** |
| Matte | 6.82 s | **6.60 s** | 8.44 s | **7.40 s** |
| Preview | 7.08 s | **6.97 s** | 8.76 s | **7.67 s** |
| Matte Only | 6.73 s | **6.61 s** | 8.52 s | **7.15 s** |

That is roughly 35–45 ms less per frame with `--gpu`, and 25 ms less on the CPU for Colors. In isolation (2560×1440, 3 ranks, 2000 IDs, 8 cores) the CPU effect drops from ~87–135 ms to ~44–54 ms, and the GPU path's aux reduction from ~38 ms to ~8 ms (Matte, Preview, Matte Only) and from ~35 ms to ~14 ms (Colors).

title: fix(effects): let CC Particle World's Textured Square use a Texture Layer
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1465.

CC Particle World had no Texture Layer control, and Textured Square fell through to the same plain coloured square as Cube in `type_sprite`, so there was nothing to pick. This adds Particle ▸ Texture ▸ Texture Layer (a regular layer parameter, with the usual Source / Masks / Effects & Masks companion) and, for Textured Square, draws that layer at the current comp time stretched over each square, turned with it, at the particle's opacity. The layer is read through the host, so a layer pointing at itself or a reference cycle gets nothing back and the squares keep the particle colour instead of recursing. With no layer chosen they also keep the particle colour, as before. Happy to switch that to an empty particle if you'd rather match After Effects exactly there.

The sprite plan the GPU compositor uses doesn't carry another layer's pixels, so I added the Texture Layer to `CPU_ONLY_CONTROLS`: with a texture chosen the effect renders on the CPU, like Camera Lens Blur's Blur Map Layer. title: Expressions: propertyGroup() and a group's propertyIndex (#1619)
author: switch87
body:
Fixes #1619

## What

The shape-group stagger expression After Effects users copy from the Adobe Community ("Expression to offset shape group scale animation"):

```js
offset = .1;
id = thisProperty.propertyGroup(2).propertyIndex;
content("circle").transform.scale.valueAtTime(time-id*offset)
```

failed with `TypeError: not a callable function`: the expression object model had no `propertyGroup()` and property groups had no `propertyIndex`. The scripting (ExtendScript) side already had both.

## How

- `Property.propertyGroup(countUp = 1)` and `PropertyGroup.propertyGroup(countUp = 1)` return the group `countUp` levels up, as the Expression Language Reference describes; going up from a top-level group (Transform, Effects, Contents, Masks…) reaches the layer.
- `PropertyGroup.propertyIndex`: the 1-based index among its siblings. A shape group holds Blend Mode, Contents and Transform in After Effects' order, so `propertyGroup(2).propertyIndex` on a group's Transform ▸ Scale is the group's index in Contents, and `propertyGroup(1).propertyIndex` is 3.
- One new host request, `Req::Ancestor`, walks up from the node's full `@uid/…` path (`PropGroup::path_of`), so it works for the property being evaluated as well as for properties and groups reached through `thisComp.layer(…)`, `effect(…)`, `content(…)`. `Req::Child` answers carry the index too.
- Never crash: a count below 1, `NaN`, a string or one above the layer is an expression error naming `propertyGroup`; a fractional count rounds down.

`crates/expr/src/tests/property_group.rs` (6 tests, red before the change): the stagger expression (Rectangle 2 at t = 0.5 s reads Rectangle 1's scale at 0.3 s → 30 %), walking up from the evaluated property, reaching the layer, an effect parameter's group is its effect (and `effect(thisProperty.propertyGroup(1).name)` works), other layers' properties and groups, and out-of-range counts. title: fix(viewer): drag a 3D layer along a gizmo axis (#1618)
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
Fixes #1618.

## Why
With a 3D layer selected, the viewer draws the X (red), Y (green) and Z (blue) gizmo arrows, but they were decoration only. A drag anywhere on the layer moves it in the view plane, so the only way to push a layer in depth was to type Z Position in the timeline. Worse, in the default front view the Z arrow points straight at the camera and projects to a dot, so it isn't visible at all.

## What
In `crates/ui-egui/src/panels/viewer.rs`:
- Each gizmo arrow is now a hit target (outer part of the arrow, so a drag on the anchor point still moves the layer freely). Hovering shows the move cursor. The arrows are painted over the box handles, so they are also hit-tested first (press and hover). Elsewhere the box handles behave as before.
- Dragging an arrow with the Selection tool moves the layer along that axis only. It reuses the existing `Gesture::Move`: `axis_drag` turns the axis's parent-space direction and its on-screen vector into the per-comp-pixel `(ax, ay)` the gesture already uses. So the drag goes through `prop.set` with a merge id (one undo step), skips snapping, and needs no new gesture or command.
- An axis shorter than 12 screen px on screen is drawn as a short up-right stub so it can be grabbed. Dragging along the stub pushes the layer away from the camera, and dragging back pulls it closer.
- The arrows register `viewer.gizmo.<layer>.<x|y|z>` automation ids. Locked layers get no hit targets.
- `parent_world_inverse` is pulled out of `drag_axes`, which now shares it with the gizmo.

Out of scope: the gizmo drags only the grabbed layer (not the rest of the selection), and there are no rotation or scale gizmo handles.

title: Export: convert H.264 frames to YUV 4:2:0 on the GPU
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
YUV part of #898, split out.

With the GPU on, H.264 export reads every frame back as RGBA f32 and converts to 4:2:0 on the CPU. At 4K that's ~133 MB per frame back for ~12 MB of planes. This does the conversion in a small compute kernel and reads back only the planes.

- New `Accelerator::comp_frame_yuv420`, defaults to `None`. The GPU compositor implements it.
- Export asks for planes only when nothing happens after the render (progressive, project bit depth, no crop/resize, output size). Otherwise, or on `None`, it's the old RGBA path. Deferred readbacks (browser worker) keep their path. Sizes the kernel can't do (width not a multiple of 8, odd height) are rejected before rendering.
- `rgba_to_yuv420` moved from export to `effectcraft_raster::yuv` so export and the GPU tests share it.

GPU output is within one level of the CPU conversion. llvmpipe matches exactly; on an RTX 3090 (Vulkan) ~0.25% of bytes come out one level off, probably FMA contraction / divide precision in the driver. Tests require exact on software adapters and allow ±1 on a small fraction elsewhere.

Tests:
- `yuv420_matches_cpu` (noise, NaN/inf, out-of-range, a few sizes)
- `rounding_ties_match_cpu` (every Y tie, plus U/V ties)
- `comp_frame_yuv420_is_the_cpu_conversion_of_comp_frame`, `odd_sized_comps_fall_back_to_the_cpu`, `unsupported_sizes_are_not_converted`
- `export/tests/h264_gpu_yuv.rs` (fake accelerator, checks the wiring, fallback and deferred path)

GPU tests follow the crate's usual `tests::gpu()` pattern and skip without an adapter.

Tested on llvmpipe and an RTX 3090 (Vulkan). DX12 on that card fails to create the context on main already (`classic3d: Validation Error`), separate issue. fmt/clippy clean; only the two known main failures (`tests_fx_pixel2::stylize`, `tests_fx_stylize::posterize_thresholds_strobe_vignette`).

Async version is #1632, on top of this.

title: GPU: read export YUV frames back asynchronously
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Stacked on #1631, so the diff includes it until that lands.

On top of #1631, also from #898.

Adds `Accelerator::comp_frame_yuv420_async`: render, submit, return. Planes come later in a per-frame callback from `poll_readbacks`, so the next frame can record while the previous copy runs. Nothing calls it yet; export still uses the sync path. Switching needs a small reorder buffer, I'd do that separately once the API looks right.

- `done` runs exactly once: planes, or `None` on failure/device loss (uses the context's existing bounded readbacks).
- Declined or can't start → `Err(done)`, callback untouched, caller can go CPU. (`GpuContext::try_map_readback`; `map_readback` wraps it.)
- Staging ring of 4; buffers go back only after unmap.
- Max 4 frames in flight, slot reserved before rendering; the 5th call polls (and sleeps briefly if the other frames are still rendering) until one frees.
- `done` runs on whichever thread polls, outside locks. Don't block in it or call back into the accelerator.
- `poll_readbacks` uses a new opt-in `poll_readbacks_busy_ok`, where a wait timeout means "busy". Everything else, `wait()` included, still retires on timeout. (Adds a crate-private `Gpu::wait_for(Duration)` for that test.)

Tests:
- `frames_in_flight_each_get_their_own_planes`
- `in_flight_cap_holds_across_threads` (8 threads × 6 frames, never >4 pending)
- `a_device_failure_fails_every_pending_readback_once`
- `cancelled_readbacks_return_their_buffers_only_once_unmapped`
- `wait_past_its_deadline_retires_but_the_yuv_poll_does_not`
- `declined_async_frames_hand_the_callback_back_unused`
- `async_yuv_defaults_to_the_synchronous_conversion` (render crate)

Same test setup as #1631.

title: Window menu: choosing a checked panel closes it, as in After Effects
author: marcoarnulfo
body:

title: Preview: an edit keeps the cached frames outside the layers it changes (#1641)
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
Fixes #1641. Also addresses #1492.

## Why

Making a cut in a long edit throws away the whole RAM preview. The viewer then shows "Caching frames…" and the user waits minutes before playback is smooth again. #1492 is the same bug: nudging an unrelated layer kills cache that had nothing to do with it.

The cause is in `Frames::content_of` / `Frames::identity` (`crates/ui-egui/src/frames.rs`). Every cached frame is keyed by one identity of the whole comp. Any edit to the comp gives it a new identity, so every frame misses. The only exception was #103, where the edit changes no pixels at all (Audio, Lock and Shy switches, markers).

## What

- `Comp::changed_span(old)` (`crates/project`) returns the comp-time span where two versions of a comp can differ. That is the union of the old and new In-Out spans of every layer that was changed, added or removed. It returns `None` when the edit can reach any frame:
  - a comp setting changed,
  - common layers were reordered,
  - the comp has an expression,
  - a changed layer is a parent, a track matte, or an effect layer pick of another layer.
- `Frames::identity` runs this when the only comp that changed is the one being viewed (nested comps and footage are the same). Frames of the old identity outside that span, plus one frame either side for motion blur, move to the new identity. They are rekeyed in place, so eviction order and memory accounting don't change. Undo moves them back the same way.
- `Comp::same_pixels` is split into `same_settings` plus the layer comparison, so both checks share one exhaustive field list.

Time effects (Echo, Timewarp) read only their own layer's source at other times (`Renderer::layer_input`). So they can't reach past the changed layer's span.

For the reporter's timeline, cutting clip 2 now recaches clip 2's span only. The other clips stay green.

## Testing

- New `frames::tests::an_edit_keeps_the_frames_outside_the_layers_it_changed` runs real commands. It trims two solids into a sequence, c…

title: Scripts: the project-folder check compares Windows paths in one form
author: bflatastic
body:
## Why

On Windows, a script's file-access check could refuse a file inside the project folder. `normalize` canonicalizes whatever part of a path exists, and canonical Windows paths carry the `\?\` verbatim prefix. So the project folder (on disk) came out prefixed, while a file under a folder that doesn't exist yet stayed lexical, and `starts_with` failed. For example, `new File(projectDir + "/renders/out.mov").exists` threw an access error instead of returning `false`. Found while testing #1594, whose test hit it.

## What changed

- `normalize` drops the verbatim prefix from canonical drive paths, so both sides compare in one form. UNC (`\?\UNC\…`) and Unix paths are untouched.
- The check still fails closed: nothing outside the project folder becomes readable.
- Unit test for the helper.

## Tests

Windows 11: `effectcraft-script` 99 passed, clippy `-D warnings` and fmt clean.

title: #1582, #1585: guard web serviceWorker against SecurityError in opaque contexts
author: krinry
body:
## Summary

Closes #1582.
Closes #1585.

In sandboxed iframes without `allow-same-origin` (or other opaque origin contexts), accessing `navigator.serviceWorker` throws a synchronous `SecurityError: Failed to read the 'serviceWorker' property from 'Navigator'`.
