title: CLI: log warnings to stderr by default
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
The CLI never installed a logger, so `log::warn!` from the GPU path (a frame the GPU declines, device out of memory, falling back to the CPU) went nowhere and an export could quietly render on the CPU with no hint why.

This installs the engine logger in the CLI with a `warn` default; `RUST_LOG` still overrides it. The app keeps its current default (`warn,effectcraft=info`) through `logging::install()`, which now just calls the new `install_with(DEFAULT_FILTER)`.

Split out of #1415 as suggested; no other changes from that PR.

Tested: fmt, clippy `-D warnings` (cli + engine), `cargo test -p effectcraft-cli`, engine logging tests, on Linux, llvmpipe.

Note: a failed render now shows the error twice on stderr, the engine's `WARN` line from the render queue (with the item id) plus the CLI's own error.

Possible follow-up: also print the chosen adapter/backend at warn (or behind `-v`) so CLI users see which GPU, if any, they got.

title: Convert a shape layer's parametric path to a bezier path
author: Hamza0101
body:
Closes #932.

## The bug

`path.convertToBezier` only ever touched masks:

```rust
fn convert_to_bezier(s: &mut Session, p: &Value) -> Result<Value> {
    edit_mask_groups(s, p, "Convert To Bezier Path", |g| {
        if let GroupKind::Mask { roto_bezier, .. } = &mut g.kind {
            *roto_bezier = false;   // the whole command
        }
        Ok(())
    })
}
```

So on a shape layer it did nothing at all: a Rectangle, Ellipse or Polystar path stayed parametric and its vertices could not be edited or animated. That is what the reporter asked for — "so we can custom and animate the path for default shape layers".

In After Effects, Convert To Bezier Path on a parametric shape path replaces it with an editable **Path 1** of the same geometry. That is what this does.

## How

The geometry is not re-derived. `parametric_path` calls the same `effectcraft_path::{rect, ellipse, polystar}` functions the renderer calls in `render::shapes::collect`, with the same property defaults, so the path that comes out is the shape that was on screen rather than an approximation of it. `effectcraft_path::from_kurbo` then turns it into a `ShapePath`, and `build::shape_path` makes the group — the same builder `layer.newShape` uses, so the result is an ordinary Path 1 with nothing special about it.

Details worth stating:

- **Masks still behave as before.** Shape items take precedence when they are selected; with no parametric shape selected the command falls through to the old mask path, and the existing `roto_bezier_and_convert_to_bezier` test passes unchanged.
- **Path Direction is carried over**, not reset to the default — reversing a path is a separate command and this should not quietly do it.
- **The new path is selected afterwards**, so its vertices can be edited straight away, which is the point of converting.
- **The result is static, by nature.** The parametric properties are read at the current time; a Size or Roundness animation cannot survive becoming a vertex list. Af…

title: fix(engine): report the keys keys.delete removed, not the keys selected
author: detth
body:
## What

`keys.delete` returned the number of *selected* keys, even when some of them no longer existed. A delete that removed nothing still reported success. It now returns the number of keys actually removed; a selected key that is gone, or listed twice, is not counted. The return type is still a number, and the UI callers ignore it or pass it through.

## Why

While scripting against 0.10.0 I saw `removeKey` once do nothing (`numKeys` unchanged) with no error, in a long session that had run heavy Roto Brush / Object Matte work. It worked again after an engine restart. I could not reproduce it, so I am not claiming this explains that case. What I found by reading the code is that `delete_keys` skips keys it can't find without saying so, and reports the selection size either way, so an agent or script can't tell a no-op from a real delete. `key_at` also relies on the key list being sorted by time (binary search), which I couldn't prove always holds.

This PR only makes the result truthful. It does not make `removeKey` throw; I'd like your view on whether it should.

## Tests

`tests_delete_keys.rs`: two real keys (one listed twice) plus a key of a nonexistent property returns 2 and leaves the third key; a selection that matches nothing returns 0 and removes nothing.

`cargo fmt`, `clippy -D warnings`, `layers`, `assets`, `wasm` and the workspace tests pass, except `effectcraft-gpu`: two comparison tests (`tests_fx_pixel2::stylize` CC HexTile, `tests_fx_stylize::posterize_thresholds_strobe_vignette` CC Threshold RGB) fail on my machine, which only has Mesa llvmpipe over Vulkan. They fail without this change too, and the GPU crate is untouched.

## Disclosure

Prepared with Claude (Anthropic) working on my behalf, per AGENTS.md; I reviewed and ran the checks.

title: Auto-orient: keep the last heading when an expression-driven Position stops
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1650.

Thanks for the project file, it made this easy to pin down. The Car's Position has no keyframes: it comes from an expression (`pointOnPath()` driven by the Progress slider). `path_tangent` treats an expression-driven Position as moving on purpose, so Orient Along Path follows expressions. But once the slider reaches 100 the central difference is zero, and the fallback added in #1090 for #1081 only looks back at Position keyframe times. With an expression there are none, so the heading dropped to 0 degrees one frame after the motion ended (about a 177 degree flip in the attached comp).

This keeps the #1090 key-based fallback as it is, and adds a sampled one for when it finds nothing and Position (or a separated dimension) has an expression. It steps back 1, 2, 4, ... frames, never earlier than the layer's in point and capped at 12 samples, until the position differs from the current one. Then it bisects down to 5 ms to find when the motion stopped and takes the direction of travel there. The bisection keeps the heading the same on every frame after the stop. Without it, a curved path would drift as the search lands on different earlier points. If there's no motion before the current time, it searches forward the same way, which mirrors how #1090 handles the time before the first key. 2D and 3D share `path_tangent`, so both are covered.

Cost: this only runs when the layer isn't moving at the current time. On the attached comp, the Car's Position is evaluated 2 times per frame while moving (as before), 9 on the first frame after the stop and at most 17 per frame afterwards. In the worst case (an expression that never moves) it's bounded at about 40 per frame. The cap and the 5 ms resolution are a judgement call, happy to tune them.

On behaviour: AE derives auto-orient from the keyframed motion path, so it doesn't really have this case. EffectCraft already orients from expressions (`path_tangent` treats an expression-driven Position as moving via `has_e…

title: Lumetri: hue/saturation curves stay inside their box beside a close point
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Fixes #1656.

The overshoot isn't only in the drawing: the panel already samples the effect's own `OffsetCurve` LUT, so what you see is what gets applied. The spline's tangents were the plain mean of the neighbouring slopes, which keeps local extrema flat but not a segment next to a very short, steep one. With a point dragged to the bottom right beside another, the long segment next to it swung far outside 0..1 (an offset of +1.5 in the test, i.e. roughly 4x saturation on the hues around it, while the hue shift wraps and the luma offset just keeps adding). This limits each tangent to three times the smaller neighbouring slope (Fritsch-Carlson), which is enough for the curve to stay between its points, so it stays inside the box in both the picture and the render, like Lumetri's curves do. Curves that didn't overshoot render as before except where a tangent hits the limit.

I went for fixing the spline rather than clipping the line to the box, because clipping alone would hide an adjustment the effect still applies. Happy to switch if you'd rather keep the curve shape and only clamp the values.

Validation:
- `color3::tests::hue_saturation_curve_stays_between_its_points`: fails on main (`0.3,0.4 0.31,0 0.7,0.6 at 0: 1.5125015`), passes here; the existing Lumetri tests still pass
- checked the Hue vs Sat graph with the points from the issue in a headless render, before and after
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-effects --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`

title: Add in-app updates with verified downloads and coordinated restart
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
## Summary

EffectCraft currently requires users to find and install each GitHub release themselves. This adds **Help > Check for Updates** using the existing release assets and the verified-download/native-installer/helper pattern from craft-launcher.

```text
check release -> download and verify while editing -> Install and restart
             -> save/cancel in every window -> wait for exit -> install -> reopen saved projects
```

Downloading never installs or closes a project. All participating windows approve before any closes. Cancel, canceled Save As, failed saves, active jobs, and other open copies prevent replacement. Windows portable updates preserve `EffectCraftData` and roll back failed file swaps.

The implementation stays in the desktop app. The shared UI gains a small prepare/commit interface around its existing save prompt. There is no new service, update feed, or engine networking. [Supported formats and recovery behavior](https://github.com/arnav-hiwarkar/effectcraft/blob/t3/in-app-app-upgrade/docs/updating.md) cover MSI, portable ZIP, macOS bundles, AppImage, and Debian/RPM packages. Externally managed installs keep their package-manager workflow.

## Evidence

- `cargo test --locked -p effectcraft --bin effectcraft update::`: **12 passed**. Covers release selection, checksum failures, partial/canceled downloads, multi-instance approval and locks, repeated commit polling, separate UI actions, and a helper that waits, replaces, and reopens a saved project.
- `cargo test --locked -p effectcraft-ui-egui --lib panels::unsaved::tests`: **9 passed**, including asynchronous Save As success, cancellation, failure, and the existing quit guard.
- Focused desktop/UI Clippy with `-D warnings`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, and `git diff --check`: passed on Linux.
- Added native Windows portable replacement/rollback and macOS signed-DMG tests to the focused three-platform workflow. **Windows/macOS execution and real MSI/deb/RPM installation are not verified local…

title: Text: drag a Range Selector's Start and End in the Composition viewer (#1011)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Text: a Range Selector's Start and End show as bars on the text in the Composition viewer, and you can drag them

In After Effects, selecting a text Range Selector shows its Start and End as two bars on the text in the Composition panel, on the boundaries between characters (or words / lines, by Based On). Dragging one sets Start or End, and keys it at the current time when it's animated. This PR does the same. The bars show while the Range Selector, its animator or a property inside the animator is selected (the issue mentions both "Range Selector 1" and "Animator 1"), and they follow View ▸ Show Layer Controls. Only the Selection tool drags them. A drag is one `prop.set` merge, the way the gradient points from #612 work: one undo step, and Undo restores the previous value. In Index units the value snaps to whole units. The bars are drawn at Start + Offset and End + Offset, which is where the renderer applies the range, and a drag writes Start/End minus the Offset and leaves Offset alone. I couldn't check that detail against After Effects, so happy to switch. They follow right-to-left runs and ligatures, and with multi-line text a drag goes to the line nearest the pointer. The bars sit on the static layout on purpose, so an animator that moves the characters away doesn't carry them out of reach. The grab zone is the small triangle standing on the baseline, and where it still meets one of the layer's bounding-box handles (small text), the handle keeps the press. With a negative Offset a bar pins to the text's start and a drag writes Start for where it's dropped.

Left out: dragging Offset itself, and bars on vertical text and on text on a path (there the static layout isn't where the characters are drawn).

Closes #1011

title: gpu: honour wgpu env overrides in headless/CLI (with_env, WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME, WGPU_POWER_PREF)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## What
The desktop app honours wgpu's environment variables through egui-wgpu (`WGPU_BACKEND`, `WGPU_DX12_COMPILER`, `WGPU_VALIDATION`, `WGPU_DEBUG`, `WGPU_POWER_PREF`, ...). The CLI and headless path (`GpuContext::request()`) only read `WGPU_BACKEND`. This PR makes the CLI/headless path read the same variables, and adds `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` for the CLI/headless path only:

- `InstanceDescriptor::with_env()` replaces `Backends::from_env()`.
- Without `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME`: `request_adapter` with `PowerPreference::from_env()` (`low` / `high` / `none`), defaulting to `HighPerformance` as before. An unknown value (e.g. `WGPU_POWER_PREF=bogus`) is ignored like in wgpu, but logs a `log::warn!` (visible where a logger is installed; the CLI installs none today).
- `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME` picks the adapter: the first adapter whose name contains the value, compared case-insensitively. The value is trimmed, and an empty or blank value counts as unset (otherwise `""` would match the first adapter and silently skip the power preference). This uses a small private matcher, not `wgpu::util::initialize_adapter_from_env`, because that panics (`expect`) when nothing matches.
- Only the adapter **name** is matched (as in wgpu); the backend is chosen with `WGPU_BACKEND`, so `WGPU_ADAPTER_NAME=dx12` matches nothing.
- If nothing matches, `--gpu` fails with a clean error that says the match is against the name only and lists each distinct adapter once as `name (backend)` (identical name+backend entries, e.g. the same DX12 adapter enumerated twice, are shown once), e.g.

title: xtask bench --repeat N: median/p90 summary, compare by median
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
## What
Whole-process numbers from `cargo xtask bench` (peak memory, max RSS, wall time) are noisy run to run. `--repeat N` (default 1, so behaviour is unchanged) runs every scenario N times:
- Every run is appended to `target/bench/results.jsonl` as before.
- With N > 1, one **summary row per key** (scenario, run, resolution, frames, format) is appended after the runs, marked `"kind": "summary"`. Its `metrics` are the **medians** of the successful runs (including `user_s`/`sys_s`; byte and instruction counts rounded to integers). `summary` holds `runs`, `failed` and `stats.{metric}.{median,p90,min,max}`. Its other fields (`date`, `load`, `frames_rendered`, ...) are copied from the key's last run. Scripts that count or average rows should skip `kind: summary` lines (documented in docs/testing.md).
- p90 is the nearest rank, so **for N < 10 it equals the max**. With an even N the median is the mean of the two middle values (for N = 2, just the mean). Documented in HELP and docs.
- A summary table (median/p90/min/max rows per key) is printed after the per-run table.
- `--compare` / `--fail-over` use the **latest row per key**. A key is compared by its median only when its summary is the latest row. A later `--repeat 1` run of that key, or a batch that aborted before writing its summaries, leaves a raw run as the latest row. The compare table therefore labels each side `median of N` or `1 run` and prints a warning when they differ, and `--fail-over` refuses those keys as insufficient evidence. Older files without summaries behave as before.
- If any run of a key failed, the summary is `ok: false` (“k of N runs failed”), so the regression gate refuses the whole key. `metrics` still holds the median of the successful runs, for information.
- `--repeat` together with `--compare A --with B` is rejected (nothing is rendered there).

## Tests
- Unit tests, one per behaviour: `stats_median_p90`, `stats_small_n_p90_is_max` (N=2, N=3), `summary_row_is_valid_and_median` (outlier…

title: test(script): per-key methods in another comp leave both key selections alone (#1531)
author: AyberkA0
body:
Follow-up to #1558 (fixes #1531), adding the regression test @switch87 suggested in https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/pull/1558#issuecomment-6191264919 (the test is theirs; thanks!).

## What it covers

#1558's test covered the silent no-op. This one covers the worse half of the bug: the property's comp *remembers* a key the user selected while another comp is active. In that case the code before #1558 applied the change to the user's selected key instead of the one named, and `removeKey(1)` deleted the selected key.

The test checks:
- only the named keys change: key 1 holds, key 2 is eased, key 3 is untouched;
- `removeKey(1)` removes key 1;
- the active comp stays active with its own key selection;
- once the other comp is opened again, its remembered selection comes back unchanged, now as key 2.

## How it was tested

- `cargo test -p effectcraft-script`: 100 passed. `cargo fmt --check` is clean.

title: fix(effects): starred effects survive a restart (#1692)
author: AyberkA0
body:
Fixes #1692.

## Cause

Effects & Presets toggles its stars in `UiState::effects_favorites` (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/effects_presets.rs`). Nothing writes that field out: the only UI state saved across sessions is the workspace layout (`workspace_state.rs`, `Snapshot`). So every star was lost when the app closed, as the ticket's source inspection suspected.

## Fix

The favourites now live in the settings, beside the other lists the user builds up: the recent projects, footage, presets and fonts.

- `Prefs::effects_favorites` (`effectsFavorites` in the settings file) holds the starred ids, in the order they were starred. `is_effect_favorite` and `toggle_effect_favorite` read and change it.
- Clicking a star changes the list and saves the settings right away, as the Character panel does for a recent font. The Favorites folder reads the list from the settings.
- Reset All keeps the list, as it keeps the recent lists.
- On load, `normalize` drops empty and repeated ids and caps the list at 1,000.
- The field is removed from `UiState`.

"Recently Used" stays per session as before. Making it persistent too would be a separate choice.

## How it was tested

`effects_favorites_persist_across_sessions` (`crates/engine/src/tests_settings.rs`) checks that:

- two stars come back in a new session that loads the same settings store;
- un-starring one sticks across sessions too;
- Reset All keeps the stars;
- a hand-edited list with an empty and a repeated id is cleaned on load.

Commands run:

- `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine --lib -- tests_settings prefs`: 37 passed.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --lib effects`: 17 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-engine -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

I didn't run the full workspace gate (`cargo xtask ci`) here.

title: Resolve Microsoft font names to installed metric-compatible fonts
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1677

## Cause
`resolve()` in crates/text/src/fonts.rs only checked for an exact family match and then a PostScript or full-name match. If neither matched, it fell back to the bundled Inter. Because there was no alias lookup, an installed metric-compatible substitute (Carlito, Caladea, Liberation, Arimo, Tinos, Cousine) was never used for Calibri, Cambria, Arial, Helvetica, Times New Roman or Courier New.

## Fix
Added a built-in table of metric-compatible aliases, using the same pairs as fontconfig's 30-metric-aliases.conf. `resolve()` now checks it before the Inter fallback. The face it finds stays flagged `missing`, so Find Missing Fonts still lists the requested name. The test helper in crates/script/src/tests_services.rs now handles mutex poisoning instead of calling `unwrap()`. Clippy does not treat its `cfg(all(test, not(windows)))` module as test code, so the `unwrap()` calls failed the workspace lint.

## Verified
- Regression test `microsoft_families_resolve_to_metric_compatible_substitutes`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-text --lib microsoft_families_resolve_to_metric_compatible_substitutes`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
No fontconfig query was added. Substitution uses only the fixed alias table, so it works the same on every platform.

Also adds my entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

title: Preview: replaced browser media gets a new disk-cache key (#1253)
author: vbasky
body:
Replacing browser media at the same path used to keep the old persistent preview key, because virtual files have no native metadata. The page then served that hit and never reached the worker transfer.

A virtual-file write now bumps a generation counter. Preview lookups key on that counter and do not stat footage or hash bytes. A miss rebuilds the content key through a callback, which hashes the stored file once and keeps the hash on the entry. The worker uses the same callback for its layer salt. There is no process-global stamp hook.

Fixes #1253.

title: Advanced 3D: Accepts Shadows Only draws just the shadow (#1691)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #1691.

## What and why

In an Advanced 3D comp, a layer whose Material Options › Accepts Shadows is **Only** still drew as an ordinary lit surface, so a shadow catcher stayed opaque. Importing a model switches the comp to Advanced 3D, which is how the issue's "Track Solid 1" hit it. The camera tracker's Create Shadow Catcher sets `acceptsShadows` to Only too (`camera_cmds.rs`), so it was affected in the same way.

The Advanced 3D scene folded the three-state enum into a bool: `receives_shadows: accepts_shadows != 0` for cards (`card_material`) and for models and primitives (`model_options`). Only and On therefore rendered the same. Classic 3D already handles Only (`compose::shade_texel`, `classic3d.wgsl`): black at alpha × the shadow amount, and nothing where the layer takes no lights.

- `adv::Material` gets `shadows_only`, set when the enum is 2, in both places.
- `shade::shade` returns `shadow_only(...)` for such a material: `[0, 0, 0, alpha × amount]`, where `amount` is the strongest `1 − light_shadow` over the lights that reach the fragment (same attenuation and back-face rules as the lit path). It returns transparent when the material is unlit or doesn't accept lights. This mirrors the classic renderer.
- `Material::transparent()` is true for it, so it draws in the blended pass and doesn't write depth. What is behind the catcher shows through, as in the classic renderer, instead of being cut out.
- The GPU gets the same thing: flag bit 4 (`shadows_only`) in `adv3d.rs`, and `shadow_only_amount` in `advanced3d.wgsl`. I moved the light-direction code the two loops share into `to_light` on both sides.

## Before / after

A 2D blue backdrop, a grey 3D solid behind a sphere with Accepts Shadows set to **Only**, and a shadow-casting point light. Rendered with `effectcraft-cli render-frame` (release build):

| `main` | this PR |

title: GPU: build effect kernels on first use, each family from a module of its own (fixes #1590)
author: 00xJS
body:
## Problem

`GpuContext::new` compiled one ~460K-character WGSL module and built every compute pipeline from it up front: ~20 compositor kernels and ~208 effect kernels. On the web, the page and its frame workers each create a device and do this. Dawn compiles the module again for each pipeline, so Chrome's GPU process stays busy past its watchdog and the device is lost about 60 s after every load (#1590). On desktop DX12 with FXC, the same up-front build keeps the window from appearing for about a minute (#613).

## Change (`crates/gpu/src/context.rs`)

1. **Effect kernels are built on first use.** The compositor's own kernels (`ENTRIES`, sky, `EXT_ENTRIES`) are still built with the context and still required. Effect kernels sit in `effect_pipelines` (`OnceLock<Result<ComputePipeline, String>>`) and are built the first time `Enc::dispatch_ext` asks for one, inside the same `init_resource` error scopes, so a kernel a compiler rejects still renders its effects on the CPU (`Enc::take_missing`). `unavailable_kernels()` lists the failures so far, and `build_all_kernels()` builds the rest.
2. **Each kernel family is a module of its own.** Each `FAMILIES` entry is `common.wgsl` + `kernels.wgsl` + its own file, plus the files it borrows functions from (fx_color→fx_lut, fx_key→fx_distort, fx_extra→fx_generate, fx_pixel2→fx_stylize, fx_particles→fx_stylize+fx_sim). That's at most ~120K characters, built with the family's first kernel. The compositor's kernels, sky and classic3d each get a small module (52–67K).

New test `effect_kernels_build_on_first_use`: no effect kernel is built with the context, and once asked for, every one builds on the device, so a kernel no test dispatches still can't break without anyone noticing. `effects_whose_kernels_failed_render_on_the_cpu` now expects a sorted list.

## Results (Windows 11, AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT, Adrenalin 32.0.21045.5002)

**Chrome 155.0.8059.80**, release web build (`cargo xtask web`), served on 127.0.0.1 with COOP/COEP, fr…

title: #1487: size the GPU memory cap from the card's video memory where Linux reports it (depends on #1550)
author: 00xJS
body:
**Depends on #1550**: this branch is #1550 (`23da45dd`) plus one commit (`d02f000a`). Review only the last commit; the rest is #1550's. Refs #1487.

## Problem

#1487 is a 2–4 GB **RX 550 on Fedora** that took the whole system down during export (`amdgpu_vm_validate() failed`, `Not enough memory for command submission!`). #1550's default cap is 8 GiB for every discrete card, which is more memory than that card has, so the gate would never trigger there.

## Change (`crates/gpu/src/memcap.rs`)

wgpu has no safe memory query, but on Linux the amdgpu driver publishes the card's memory in sysfs, and reading it needs no `unsafe`: `/sys/class/drm/cardN/device/mem_info_vram_total`. `MemCap::new` matches the DRM card by PCI `vendor` / `device` against `AdapterInfo` and caps discrete cards at **min(8 GiB, ¾ × VRAM)**:

| card | cap |
|---|---|
| 2 GB (RX 550) | 1.5 GiB |
| 4 GB (RX 550 / 6500 XT) | 3 GiB |
| 8 GB (RX 7600) | 6 GiB |
| 16 GB and up | 8 GiB (unchanged) |

Integrated GPUs keep 2 GiB (an APU's carve-out isn't its limit). `EFFECTCRAFT_GPU_MEMCAP_MB` still overrides it. Where the size isn't known (Windows, NVIDIA on Linux), the 8 GiB default applies as in #1550. Windows' WDDM pages video memory to system memory instead of hard-crashing like #1487, which is why this targets Linux.

## Tests

- `known_video_memory_lowers_the_discrete_cap`: the arithmetic above.
- `video_memory_is_read_from_the_matching_drm_card`: a fake sysfs tree with an Intel card that has no `mem_info_vram_total`, the RX 550 (`0x1002:0x699f`, 4 GiB) and a `card1-DP-1` connector entry; plus a non-matching id and a missing directory.

Run on Windows 11 / RX 6900 XT, Vulkan: `cargo test -p effectcraft-gpu --lib --release` gives 212 passed. The only 3 failures also fail on `main` (#1605). `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-gpu --all-targets --release -- -D warnings` is clean. **Not tested on Linux**: the fixture covers the parsing, but the real sysfs read still needs a Linux/amdgpu machine.

title: Replace non-ASCII characters in EXR layer names so ProEXR export no longer panics (#1702)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1702.

`comp.saveFrameAsExr` names each layer's channels after the layer (`Hello.R`, ...). `exr_name` already replaced dots and control characters, but passed any other character through. The `exr` crate panics (`exr::Text contains unsupported characters`) when a channel name has a character it cannot store, so a text layer named `你好` stopped the export and no file was written.

`exr_name` now keeps only printable ASCII (letters, digits, punctuation, space) and replaces every other character with `_`, the same way it already handles dots and control characters. The existing fallback to `Layer` for an empty name and the ` 2`, ` 3` suffixes for duplicate names are unchanged, so two non-ASCII layers of the same length still get distinct channel names.

Only the EXR channel naming changes; `exr_name` is used only by `layered_exr`, and the PSD export does not go through it.

Test: `proexr_names_a_non_ascii_layer_with_underscores_instead_of_panicking` saves a comp with a solid named `你好` and checks that the EXR is written with channels `__.R` ... `__.A`. Without the fix the command fails with the panic from the issue.

title: Keep Essential Graphics instance keyframes in the comp so valueAtTime and numKeys see them (#1682)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1682.

When an instance renders its nested comp, `essential::with_overrides` set each overridden source property to the instance's value at the current frame and cleared its keyframes. So expressions in the comp that read the property got the right `value`, but `valueAtTime(t)` gave the current value back and `numKeys` was 0.

Changes:

- `essential::Override` now also has `keys`: the instance property's keyframes.
- `with_overrides` copies those keys into the comp property instead of clearing them. The value is still set too, so nothing changes for properties that have no keys.
- `effectcraft_render::essential_overrides` passes the instance keys along. Keyframes are in layer time, and the instance's layer time is the nested comp's time (stretch included), so the keys need no shifting. Two cases still get only the value, as before: Time Remap and Responsive Design - Time (a stretched precomp with protected regions), where layer time and nested time differ. Same for an instance property with an expression, which replaces its keys.

With the keys in place, `valueAtTime`, `numKeys` and `key(n)` inside the comp read the instance's keys, the same as keys set on the control in the comp.

Tests (`crates/engine/src/tests_essential_more.rs`):

- `instance_keyframes_reach_the_comp_so_expressions_can_look_ahead`: `with_overrides` keeps the override's keys on the comp property.
- `keys_set_on_an_instance_are_passed_to_the_nested_comp_render`: follows the issue's repro. It keys an instance's exposed Opacity at 0 s / 1 s, evaluates at 0.25 s through `essential_overrides` + `with_overrides`, and checks that the nested property has both keys and gives the instance's value at 0.75 s. With Time Remap turned on, no keys are passed.

Both tests fail on main, where the keys get cleared.

title: Duplicate the selected text animator or selector instead of the whole text layer (#1665)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1665.

With a Range Selector (or a whole text animator) selected in the timeline, Edit ▸ Duplicate (Ctrl+D) duplicated the entire text layer. `edit.duplicate` already handles selected effects and selected shape items before it falls back to duplicating layers, but it did not check for selected text animators or selectors.

`edit.duplicate` now does the same for text layers as it does for shape layers. A new `prop_groups::selected_animator_items` lists the animators and selectors selected under `text/animators` on the active comp's text layers, built like `selected_contents` (the shape-item version) and using the same `collect_selected` walk. A selector inside a selected animator is not listed again, because it is copied with the animator. The items then go through the existing `duplicate_contents`. Each copy is put in place above the original, gets a unique name the After Effects way ("Range Selector 1" → "Range Selector 2"), and is selected. All of it is one undo step. The error message in `duplicate_contents` now says "the group is gone" instead of "the shape item is gone", because it covers both cases now.

Test: `tests_text::duplicate_copies_selected_text_selector_not_the_layer` selects the Range Selector of a new animator and runs `edit.duplicate`. It checks that the comp still has one layer and the animator now has two selectors, and that undo removes the copy. Then it selects the animator and checks that the animator is copied. On `main` the test fails, because a second text layer is created.

title: Fall back to the page's thread when new Worker throws in a sandboxed iframe (#1586)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1586.

In a sandboxed iframe (`sandbox="allow-scripts"`) the document's origin is opaque, so `new Worker(...)` throws a `SecurityError` at once. Before this fix, `js/host.js` handled only workers that fail *asynchronously* (`onerror`). The exception from the constructor escaped from `frameWorkerStart` during startup (`WebFrames::start`), and the app stayed on "Loading…".

Both `new Worker` call sites in `js/host.js` now catch the throw and handle it the same way as the existing asynchronous failure:

- **Frame workers** (`frameWorkerStart`): the index is still returned and its slot is kept (as `null`, which `frameWorkerPost` already ignores). The failure goes to `onMessage(index, …, error)` on a `setTimeout`, so `src/frames.rs` gets the same "worker died" path that a failed start already uses (`on_message` sets `alive = false`). When no worker is left, frames render on the page's thread, as with `?noworkers`. The call is deferred for two reasons: the Rust caller must record the index first, and the call must not happen while `STATE` is still borrowed in `WebFrames::start`.
- **Job workers** (`workerRun` → `spawn`): the job fails with the error message, also deferred. This is the same `"error"` reply that a worker which failed to start already sends (#216). `src/worker.rs` then marks the job Failed + Done, after it has registered the job's handler.

Nothing changes when workers can be created.

Tests: `apps/effectcraft-web/tests/workers.mjs` (Node, fake `Worker`, run with `node apps/effectcraft-web/tests/workers.mjs`) now replaces `Worker` with a constructor that throws. It checks that the job fails with the `SecurityError` and that the worker is not counted as running. It also checks that the frame worker keeps its index, is reported dead with the error, and that a later post to it is ignored. On `main` the test fails with the uncaught `SecurityError`; with this change it passes. `docs/web.md` describes the new case in the frame-worker fallback paragraph and …

title: #1714: reopen each comp at its saved current time
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
Fixes #1714.

## Why
After reopening a project, the Composition viewer was black and the layers seemed to have moved. The issue blames tick deserialization, but that part checks out. Ticks are serialized as plain integers (`#[serde(transparent)]`), and saving refuses to write a file that doesn't read back. At 59.94 fps (4 237 833 600 ticks per frame), the values in the issue decode to sane times:

| field | ticks | frames | seconds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start_time` | 144086342400 | 34 | 0.57 |
| `in_point` | 1334917584000 | 315 | 5.26 |
| `out_point` | 12853349308800 | 3033 | 50.6 |

So that layer only starts at 5.26 s. The actual bug is that the current time wasn't saved. A reopened comp always started at 0:00:00:00, before its layers, so the viewer showed black. After Effects saves each comp's current time with the project.

## What
- `SavedView` is the editor state already saved next to `savedBy` (#748). It now also records each comp's current time as `compTimes`.
- `Session::restore_view` restores those times, snapped to a frame within the comp's duration. A hand-edited time that's out of range lands on the last frame. `set_time` and restore share one helper, `comp_frame_at`.

title: Paste path operators below the shapes they act on (#1681)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1681. Fixes #1629.

Copying Trim Paths (or Wiggle Paths, a fill, a stroke…) from one shape layer's Contents and pasting it into another shape layer with nothing selected in its Contents put the copy on top of Contents. Paints and path operations act on the items above them, so on top it acted on nothing and the paste looked like it did nothing. #1629 noticed exactly this ("it inserts itself to the top of Content. When I add Trim Path myself, it appends").

Now, when the clipboard holds only paints and path operations (nothing that draws a path: no group, rectangle, ellipse, polystar or path), and nothing is selected in the target layer's Contents, the copies go to the bottom of Contents. That is where Add puts them (`layer.addShapeItem` appends), so they act on the layer's shapes like a hand-added one does.

Unchanged:
- Pasting shapes, groups or a mix still goes on top, as before.
- With an item selected in the target layer, the paste still goes above that item, as before.

Test: `pasted_path_operator_goes_below_the_shapes_it_acts_on` copies Trim Paths from one shape layer and pastes it into another; Contents must be `["Polystar 1", "Trim Paths 1"]`. Without the fix it is `["Trim Paths 1", "Polystar 1"]`. The existing copy/paste test (`shape_contents_copy_cut_and_paste_between_shape_layers`) is not affected: it pastes shapes. The doc comment on `paste_contents` is updated to match.

  - Pasted shapes and shape operators are now placed according to the clipboard item type when no destination item is selected. Merge Paths is positioned with path and paint items so it can operate as expected.

title: Keep CC Simple Wire Removal between points A and B (#1724)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1724.

CC Simple Wire Removal treated the wire as an endless line through points A and B: it tested only the distance across the wire, so every pixel along that line was repainted, also before A and after B. That is the overshoot in the issue's screenshot.

The fix projects each pixel onto the A-to-B direction and skips it when the projection is outside `0..len`, so only the segment between the two points is changed. Both render paths have it:

- CPU, `wire_removal` in `crates/effects/src/keying2.rs`.
- GPU, the `fp2_wire` shader in `crates/gpu/src/shaders/fx_pixel2.wgsl`. `wire_removal` in `crates/gpu/src/fx_pixel2.rs` now passes the segment length in the unused `f[1].w` slot. The shader gets the tangent back from the normal it already receives, so no other parameter changes. The existing CPU/GPU parity cases (`keys_and_3d` in `tests_fx_pixel2.rs`, including the one with Point B inside the frame) cover the new check.

The ends are a hard cut, with no taper. The Slope softness across the wire is unchanged.

Test: `wire_removal_stays_between_a_and_b` (`keying2.rs`) puts a vertical black wire through a grey image and sets A and B at y = 5 and y = 15. It checks that the wire is removed between them and that pixels on the wire above A and below B are not changed. Without the fix it fails because those pixels are repainted.

title: Timeline: trimming the Out point to the playhead keeps its frame visible
author: elZanco
body:
Alt+] (Trim Layer Out Point to Current Time) set the Out edge exactly at the playhead time. Layer intervals are half-open [in, out), so the playhead frame was already gone after the trim — the current frame showed nothing.

This restores After Effects' original behaviour: the Out edge lands one frame after the playhead (`t.max(in) + frameDuration`), so the playhead frame is the layer's last visible frame — exactly what Alt+] does in After Effects. A layer still keeps at least one frame when trimmed past its In point. Alt+[ (trim In point) already matched AE's behaviour and is unchanged.

Verified interactively (Alt+] leaves the current frame visible, Alt+[ and the one-frame minimum behave as before, undo restores the span). Regression test in `tests_shortcut_cmds.rs` covers the new Out edge, the In-point behaviour, the one-frame minimum and undo.

title: Fix #1275: open the commands' file dialogs without blocking the frame on Linux
author: gmrmad1

title: Media: millisecond-rounded MP4 footage imports at its true frame rate (#1442)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Fixes #1442.

## Problem
Phone and screen-recorder MP4s often store frame times in milliseconds, so a 30 fps clip alternates 33 ms and 34 ms frames (60 fps: 16/17 ms). The pinned FilmCraft MP4 reader takes the frame rate from the median sample duration, which gives 30.303 or 58.824 fps. EffectCraft copies that rate into the footage, New Comp from Selection copies it into the comp, and export follows it: a 4 s, 30 fps clip renders as 122 frames at 30.303 fps.

## Fix
The FilmCraft fixes (storytold/filmcraft#1729, #1829) are unmerged, and moving the pin is the large update tracked in #1187. This PR corrects the rate on the EffectCraft side instead, in `crates/media/src/probe.rs`:

- On import, EffectCraft reads the MP4/MOV sample durations from the header it already parses for rotation. It averages the durations close to the median and snaps the result to the nearest standard rate within 0.5%.
- The FilmCraft rate is kept when the median already gives a standard rate, or when the average lands on no standard rate (variable-rate or unusual footage).
- The comparison is done in `u64`, so extreme durations can't overflow.

The pinned FilmCraft reader only uses its rate for the value it reports. It decodes frames by time, and EffectCraft picks the frame times itself from the footage rate (mid-frame). So with the right rate, the right frames get read too.

Existing comps keep the rate they were saved with; nothing is retimed on load. When the FilmCraft pin moves past the upstream fix, this correction will usually do nothing and can be removed or kept as a safety net.

## Tests
- `effectcraft-media` unit tests: millisecond-rounded 30, 60, 23.976, 29.97 and 59.94; exact rates; variable rate; extreme and zero durations.
- `crates/export/tests/ms_rounded_footage.rs` (no ffmpeg needed): writes H.264 MP4s with a 1 ms timebase, each frame showing its own number as bars. It checks:
  - the 30 and 60 fps clips import with 120 and 240 frames, from disk and from memory;
  - a comp ma…

title: Puppet: Shift-select several pins in the Timeline and edit them together
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Fixes #1751.

## Problem
1. **Shift-click didn't add pins to the selection.** Shift-clicking Puppet pins in the Timeline replaced the selection instead of adding to it. Pins are group rows. The group-row click handler sent `prop.select` without `add`, unlike property rows, which pass `"add": shift`.
2. **Editing one pin didn't affect the others.** The issue also asks to change several pins' values at once. Even with several pins selected, editing one pin's Position (or Scale, Rotation, Amount…) changed only that pin. The multi-edit path (`selected_twins`) only reached the same property on *other selected layers*, never sibling pins on the same layer.

## Change
- **Selection** (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`): the group-row click passes `"add": Shift`, the same way property rows do. This covers every group row (Puppet pins, masks, effects, shape groups, text animators); a plain click still selects only the clicked row.
- **Editing** (`crates/engine/src/commands/prop.rs`, `selected_twins`): when the edited property belongs to a selected pin, the twins also include the same parameter (same `match_id`, same value kind) of every other selected pin on an unlocked layer, this layer included. The behaviour builds on how After Effects edits the same property across selected layers; I haven't checked against After Effects whether it does this for several pins within one layer. Because `prop.set`, `prop.toggleAnimation` and `prop.toggleKey` all share `selected_twins`, all of these now apply to every selected pin, in one undo step:

  - a scrub, and each pin moves by the same change from its own value;

title: Resolve effects/<match name> property paths in anim.applyPreset (#1746)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes the first problem in #1746: `anim.applyPreset` skipped every effect property that `anim.savePreset` writes.

**Cause.** `savePreset` stores a property by its match path, e.g. `effects/ec.control.slider/slider` or
`effects/ec.control.slider#2/slider` for the second instance. Path lookup (`parse_path`) splits on `/` and on `.`,
so the effect match name `ec.control.slider` is cut into `ec`, `control`, `slider`, no child matches, and the
property ends up in `skipped`. Transform paths have no dots, so they worked.

**Fix.** A small helper in `commands/mod.rs`, `resolve_effect_path`, next to `match_path_of` (which writes this
format). It turns `effects/<match name>[#n]/<rest>` into `effects/@<uid>/<rest>` for the nth effect with that match
name on the target layer. Any other path, or an effect the layer does not have, is passed on unchanged, so
`effects/#1/...`, `effects/<display name>/...` and `transform/...` behave as before. Old `.ecpreset` files work
without being saved again.

**Same bug, other paths.** Edit > Copy of an unanimated effect property and Edit > Copy Expression Only /
Copy With Property Links store the same match path, and Edit > Paste looked it up the same way, so pasting
an effect value or expression onto another layer's effect also did nothing. `paste_properties` and
`paste_links` in `edit.rs` now use the same helper.

**Not in this PR.** The second point of the issue (Essential Properties saved as `essential/eg<control id>`,
which changes with every template import) is a change to what `savePreset` writes. It needs a decision on the
saved format, so it is left for a separate change.

author: skylartaylor
body:

title: Timeline: a shape group's inner Contents draws no row, as After Effects elides it
author: elZanco
body:
## What

A shape group's inner Contents (After Effects' `ADBE Vectors Group`, which AE flags *elided*) no longer draws a row in the Timeline. The group's items - path, fill/stroke and Transform - now list directly under the shape group. The layer-level Contents (`ADBE Root Vectors Group`) is unchanged.

So a rectangle shape now reads:

    Contents
      Rectangle 1
        Rectangle Path 1
        Fill 1
        Transform

instead of an extra `Contents` row between `Rectangle 1` and `Rectangle Path 1`.

## Why

AE elides the per-group Vectors group in the Timeline: *elided* is a static property-group attribute whose purpose is to make the UI lighter, while the group stays reachable from scripts (confirmed in the Adobe scripting community). EffectCraft drew that row, so shape groups had one nesting level too many.

This is a **display-only** change. The data model, the scripting API and the match paths (`contents/#1/contents/fill/color`) are untouched, and expressions already skip the step via the prelude's transparent `content()`.

title: Fix #341: on macOS, a quit from a visible window goes through `terminate:`
author: dotCooCoo
body:
Fixes #341

## Cause

Quit EffectCraft and Finder's Quit send `ViewportCommand::Close`, and the close button sends the window's close request. In each case eframe drops the window while AppKit's run loop is still running. On a Mac with a Touch Bar, AppKit's Touch Bar code then raises an uncaught Objective-C exception (`-[_NSTouchBarFinderObservation invalidate]`) and the app crashes. The crash report attached to #341 shows this stack. This is storytold/craft-libs#3, the crash that `craft-quit` was added for.

## Change

- `panels::unsaved::close_or_quit` runs the existing unsaved-changes check and then `craft_quit::on_close_request`. When nothing holds the window open, it cancels the close and quits through `-[NSApplication terminate:]`. When the Unsaved Changes prompt holds the close, it does nothing. On other platforms it does nothing. `frame` calls it where it called `on_close_requested`.
- The window close after a lost graphics device goes the same way.
- A quit while the window is minimized or hidden still closes the window as before: eframe does not run `ui` then, and the unsaved-changes check and the new call both run from `ui`.
- `on_exit` still runs: `terminate:` reaches winit's `applicationWillTerminate:`, which runs eframe's exit handling (`on_exit`: launch guard, window position, workspace, crash-recovery cleanup) before AppKit ends the process.
- On macOS, a quit through `terminate:` ends the process before `eframe::run_native` returns, so the code after it in `apps/effectcraft/src/main.rs` does not run. The only line on the success path was the log line for the closed window; it moves into `Desktop::on_exit` on every platform. A quit does not return an error, so the error branch stays.
- `craft-quit` is a workspace dependency pinned to the craft-libs rev that `craft-docpath` already uses (`82a24b0`), with the `egui` feature in `effectcraft-ui-egui`. `Cargo.lock` gains only `craft-quit`; its other dependencies were already locked. pdfcraft adds `craft-q…

title: Export: cap CPU frames in flight with EFFECTCRAFT_CPU_INFLIGHT (#1615)
author: Higgs32584
body:
Part of storytold/EffectCraft#1615 (the memory-sized default and the partial `.mp4` stay open as follow-ups)

CPU exports kept one frame per thread in flight (`batch_size()` = threads, clamp 2..16), and `Cx::frames` rendered the whole batch at once. Only GPU renders had a cap (#879, `EFFECTCRAFT_GPU_INFLIGHT`). A heavy comp needs gigabytes per frame, so a 16-thread machine got OOM-killed. The headless CLI doesn't read `prefs.json`, so `memory.*` budgets gave no way to lower this.

### Change (`crates/export/src/pipeline.rs`)
- New `EFFECTCRAFT_CPU_INFLIGHT=N` caps how many frames render at once. It reuses the existing capped path `map_frames_while`: renders go in chunks of N, encodes stay parallel, and there's no lock, so a failing frame can't deadlock or leak.
- `cpu_inflight()` parses the value. Unset or blank means no cap, which is today's behaviour. An invalid value logs a warning and leaves frames uncapped.
- `Inflight { gpu, cpu }` combines the caps. While the GPU renders, the smaller cap applies. Once the GPU stops for good (#1511), the GPU cap lapses and the CPU cap alone applies (uncapped when there is none), so `EFFECTCRAFT_CPU_INFLIGHT=4` on a GPU project falls back to 4 renders at once, not 1.
- A CPU cap also bounds the window of finished images waiting to encode: windows are `cpu` frames instead of one per thread, so a cap of 2 on 16 threads never holds more than 2 rendered images. Each window still encodes in parallel. A GPU cap alone keeps its window of `max(cap, threads)` as before.
- Unit tests cover the parsing, the combination rules, a cap of 2 on an 8-thread pool keeping at most 2 renders in flight and at most 2 images waiting to encode, and the CPU cap taking over after the GPU stops.

### Not in this PR (follow-up design)
- An automatic default sized from available memory, e.g. `min(threads, (available - memory.ramReservedGb) / frame_bytes)`. This needs a per-frame cost estimate. The issue measures 1.8 to 5.5 GB per 1080p frame, about 50 to 15…

title: Fix HexTile centerline cell selection
author: sanyamsingh001
body:
HexTile now computes its third cube coordinate symmetrically in both the CPU implementation and the WGSL shader. This avoids deriving it by subtracting separately computed coordinates with floating-point rounding, which can select a different cell at a centerline tie.

The existing stylize regression uses a 70×44 layer with center (35,22), radius 9.3, scale 0.5, and zero rotation and smear. Its effective 35×22 buffer has center (17.5,11) and radius 4.65. The retained shader-only comparison failed at the original tolerance before the correction and passed afterward; the recorded worst pixel was (17,2). Cell-index calculations explain that recorded color, but were not GPU tracing.

This f3f24ef-based successor changes only the CPU and shader expressions. It preserves upstream WireRemoval changes and test-service poison recovery; the historical Mem fixture lint allowance is no longer included. Inputs and tolerance remain unchanged, with no parameter sweep.

Original full repository CI passed on this exact two-file source: formatting, strict release Clippy, 3,671 native tests and 2 doctests passed, with 31 native tests ignored and no failures. The native total includes the 222-test GPU harness and the existing stylize regression. PDF backend policy, layering, 39 attributed assets, and compilation of 32 Wasm crates passed. The Wasm check retained the non-fatal pointer_wrap::State.disabled warning; Mesa diagnostics are preserved.

Validation ran on Linux with Mesa software-rendering settings and EFFECTCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1. Passing harness counts do not prove every optional GPU, FFmpeg or parser branch executed. These results qualify the f3f24ef-based successor, not later main revisions, other hardware/backends/platforms, or browser/Wasm runtime behavior.

title: feat(cli): render --progress reports frames on stderr when it is not a terminal
author: ArchersIntel
body:
## What

`effectcraft-cli render --progress` prints progress on stderr when stderr is not a terminal:

```
progress <frames done> <frames total> <seconds elapsed> <seconds left, or - when unknown>
```

At most four lines a second, one per change. On a terminal nothing changes (it keeps its live `[1/1] frame 16/180 … ~14s left` line), and without the flag nothing changes anywhere.

## Why

A program that starts the CLI reads stderr through a pipe and sees nothing until the render ends. FilmCraft's new Replace With EffectCraft Composition ([storytold/filmcraft PR](https://github.com/storytold/filmcraft/pulls?q=is%3Apr+author%3AArchersIntel)) renders a composition in the background and shows a real percentage and time left from these lines, on the clip and in the monitor. FilmCraft still works with a CLI that lacks the flag (it retries without it and shows no percentage), so the two PRs can land in either order.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-cli`: 14 of 15 pass. `render_out_is_relative_to_the_working_directory` fails on Windows with or without this change: the test compares a `canonicalize()`d path (`\\?\C:\…`) with the path the CLI prints (`C:\…`).
- Output checked by hand on a 6 s 1080p render (`render --demo --end 6 --progress`): 11 lines, e.g. `progress 16 180 1.4 14.2` … `progress 160 180 9.6 1.2`.
- Documented in the usage text, the module header and `docs/agents.md`.
- Not tested on macOS or Linux (the change doesn't touch platform code).

title: Format negative Audio Samples time as a signed timecode
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/lib.rs:383-387` (no existing issue): format_time in Audio Samples mode prints a negative time as garbage like `00:00:-1:24000` instead of a signed timecode.

## Cause
The Audio Samples branch of `format_time` split the signed tick count with `div_euclid`/`rem_euclid` and fed the resulting negative seconds into the hours, minutes and seconds fields. A negative time therefore printed output like `00:00:-1:24000`, with the minus sign inside a field and a positive sample remainder.

## Fix
The branch now takes the absolute tick count (saturating, so `i64::MIN` can't overflow) and computes the hours, minutes, seconds and sample remainder from it. It puts a single leading `-` in front when the time is negative, as the Timecode and Feet modes do. -0.5 s now prints `-00:00:00:24000` and -3700 s prints `-01:01:40:00000`.

## Verified
- Regression test `neg_samples`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-time --lib neg_samples`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The Timecode, Frames, Feet and Seconds modes and the positive Audio Samples output are unchanged.

title: Effects: colour-only effects skip the layer cover, Glow at intensity 0 skips its blur, Glow blurs in place (#1205)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
**Base:** stacks on #1400, which stacks on #1279. Please merge those first (both are based on 0.9.2 `549e9d82`). This branch is one commit on top of #1400's head `6ca27d49`.

## Problem

#1205: a zoomed shape layer with Glow uses a lot of memory, and the amount isn't monotonic in zoom. @muazio's analysis in #1205 found three causes. #1279/#1400 fix the main one for Glow-only stacks: they skip the full-layer cover for a list of effects that grow their own margins. Measured in https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/issues/1205#issuecomment-6250003821, these were still open:

1. Any stack with an effect outside that list still gets the comp-sized cover at the raster scale. Glow + Fill at 585 % on a 1080×1920 comp needs 6.63 GiB on #1400, the same as on main. That's because `raster_scale`'s ~16 MP cap looks at the content bounds, and the cover's only limit is the 16384 px side check.
2. Glow has no early-out at intensity 0.
3. Glow keeps four image-sized buffers alive at once: the padded original, the bright pass, and two blur pass buffers.

## Change

- **Colour effects no longer force the cover.** Tint, Tritone, Brightness & Contrast, Hue/Saturation and Exposure recolour pixels with alpha > 0 only (`Image::map_straight`). Fill without Invert or masks scales its colour by the pixel's alpha. So these effects leave transparent pixels exactly as they are, and the area the cover adds stays transparent through them. New `KEEPS_CLEAR` list and `EffectSpec::skips_cover_with(params)`. A stack made of these plus the `SKIPS_COVER` effects now gets `align` instead of `cover` (CPU and GPU target alike). Fill with Invert or masks keeps the cover: Invert paints transparent pixels, and mask coverage depends on the buffer. Levels, Curves, Invert, generators and distortions are unchanged.
- **Glow at intensity 0** keeps its pad and runs the composite with a zero glow, but skips the bright pass and the blur. It doesn't just return the input: "None" and several Glow Operations change p…

title: Roto Brush: apply correction strokes in drawing order (#1646)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Refs #1646.

## Problem
Paint foreground (green), subtract part of it with Alt (red), then paint green over that part again: the area stays background. Strokes are stored in drawing order, but segmentation rasterized all green strokes into one mask and all red strokes into another, and background won wherever both covered a pixel. So an earlier red stroke beat every later green stroke. Refine Edge had the same problem: an erase stroke beat every later refine stroke.

Reproduced through the segmenter and through `roto.stroke` + render, the same command the Layer panel sends (Alt maps to `kind: "bg"`).

## Fix
Strokes now apply in drawing order: where they overlap, the one painted last wins. Unpainted pixels are still left to the segmentation.

- `resolve` (in `crates/track/src/roto/mod.rs`) paints a pair of opposing stroke kinds in order. Foreground and background use it for the graph-cut constraints, the colour samples and the cleanup seeds. Refine and erase use it for the Refine Edge band. The band carried from the previous frame stays under this frame's strokes.
- Trained-model prompts follow the same rule. Points along a stroke are kept only where a later stroke of the other kind hasn't painted over them, so a spot is never sent as both foreground and background. If a stroke loses every sampled point but still owns some pixels (for example, a small Alt tap in the middle of a large foreground dot), it gets one point at the pixel deepest inside what is left. Without that, the model would be skipped for the classical cut. A stroke painted over completely still sends no point. The propagated matte's points, box and mask take this frame's strokes over it, so generated foreground points can't land in a background correction.
- Stroke history is unchanged. All strokes are kept for Undo, serialization and propagation; overlaps are resolved when segmenting.
- The disk cache's `segmentation-v1` key and `RENDER_VERSION` are bumped, so segmentations and frames cached before …

title: Shift Channels: After Effects' Take … From menu order, so 10 is Full Off (#1797)
author: Anubhav-Rai
body:
Fixes #1797.

## The problem

Shift Channels' four `Take … From` menus had eleven options to After Effects' ten: an extra **Half On** sat at position 10, where After Effects has **Full Off**.

```
After Effects:   … 9 Full On   10 Full Off
EffectCraft:     … 9 Full On   10 Half On   11 Full Off
```

Menu choices are stored as numbers, so a project or script written against After Effects set the channel to 50 % grey instead of turning it off — silently, no error. The classic RGB-split recipe (three copies of a layer, each keeping one channel and setting the other two to Full Off, blended with Add) rendered pink, light green and light blue instead of pure red, green and blue.

## The change

After Effects' ten options now come first, in its order, and `Half On` moves to the end as an EffectCraft extra:

```
Alpha, Red, Green, Blue, Luminance, Hue, Lightness, Saturation, Full On, Full Off, Half On
```

Values 1 to 10 now mean what they mean in After Effects, and nobody loses `Half On`. This is the second option the reporter suggested; removing `Half On` outright would have changed renders for anyone already using it.

**Saved projects keep the option they picked.** The issue flagged migration as the catch, but `migrate::upgrade_instance` already remaps popup values **by label** when an option list is reordered, so no new migration code is needed — there's a test for it below.

Both the CPU path (`crates/effects/src/channel.rs`) and the GPU path (`crates/gpu/src/fx_key.rs`) clamped the index with a hardcoded `.min(10)`; both now use `SHIFT_ORDER.len() - 1`, so the clamp can't go stale if the list changes again. The GPU path shares `SHIFT_ORDER`, so it picks up the reorder itself.

`docs/effects.md` lists the parameter count (4), which is unchanged.

## Tests

- `channel::tests::shift_channels_menu_follows_after_effects_order` — option 10 (`Enum(9)`) renders the channel at 0, option 11 (`Enum(10)`) at 0.5, and a value past the end stays on the last option instead of pani…

title: fix(engine): preserve alpha channel when saving still PNG frames
author: kk376
body:
### Summary
Fixes #1815.

When saving a still frame via `comp.saveFrameAs` or "Composition ▸ Save Frame As ▸ File...", the exported PNG previously composited the image over `comp.background` via `to_rgba8_over(bg)`, setting alpha to 255 across the entire canvas and destroying transparent areas. Additionally, `TemplateSlot::Still` defaulted to `"PNG Sequence"` (`Channels::Rgb`) rather than `"PNG Sequence with Alpha"`.

1. **`comp.saveFrameAs`**: Default to preserving straight alpha with `img.to_rgba8()`, while respecting `transparent: false` if explicit background flattening is requested.
2. **`TemplateDefaults`**: Set `TemplateSlot::Still` default output module to `"PNG Sequence with Alpha"`.
3. **Tests**: Added regression tests in `crates/engine/src/tests_frame_export.rs` verifying that transparent regions preserve alpha (`alpha == 0`), that `transparent: false` composites over the background, and that still frames default to the RGBA template.

title: Tests: serialise disk-cache-opening tests with the roto tests
author: iannitram
body:
`object_matte_mattes_persist_in_the_disk_cache` can fail when the whole engine suite runs in parallel.

The Roto/Object Matte segment store is one per process (`roto::set_seg_store`), and every `Session::configure_disk_cache` that opens a cache takes it over. The roto and disk-cache tests already serialise on `hold_roto_cache_test_lock()`, but many other engine tests build a `Session` with a settings store, which opens the disk cache in the platform folder and takes the store. Once that session drops, the weak store is dead and the Object Matte test sees no disk writes.

`configure_disk_cache` now takes that lock under `cfg(test)` before opening a cache, so every such test runs apart from the roto tests (re-entry on the same thread is a no-op). Product code is unchanged: only the app's one session ever opens a disk cache.

Tested:
- On another of our machines (reported when the fix was written), the test failed 3 of 3 runs of the full parallel engine suite before this change.
- On Linux (Legion Go, SteamOS), with this branch on `main` ef74d829: `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine` passed 3 of 3 runs (661 passed, 0 failed); `cargo fmt --check` is clean. Without the change it also passed 6 of 6 there, so the race shows up on some machines only.

AI-assisted: yes (Claude), tested on a Legion Go.

title: GPU: Posterize and CC Grid Wipe match the CPU on AMD and Intel (#1605)
author: 00xJS
body:
Fixes the two remaining GPU-vs-CPU mismatches in #1605 that show on AMD and Intel but not NVIDIA: **Posterize** and **CC Grid Wipe**. (The third, CC Hex Tile, is fixed by #1776.) Shader-only plus one test.

## Posterize: a fused multiply–subtract in `round_away`

`round_away` decided the half-way case with `abs(x - trunc(x)) >= 0.5`. Posterize calls it on `c = v * lv`, and a driver may fuse that product with the following subtraction into one fma (AMD's compiler does; the same card fuses a plain `a * b + c`). That skips the product's rounding.

For straight value `v = 5/6` at level 4: in f32, `x / a` is `0x1.aaaaaap-1` and `v * 3` rounds to exactly **2.5**, so the CPU rounds up. Fused, it's `fma(v, 3, -2) = 0.49999994`, so the GPU rounded a whole level down. Every failing pair in the test is such a tie (15/18, 30/36, 55/66, … all 5/6).

**Fix:** `round_away` compares `x` with `t ± 0.5` instead (exact for integer `t`). A product can't be fused into a comparison. The level divide also uses a new `div_rn` (one fma-corrected step, the pattern `fxs_qdiv` already uses), so the output is the CPU's to the bit.

## CC Grid Wipe: inexact division in the cell lookup

`floor(q / cs)` picks the cell. WGSL's `/` may be off by 2.5 ULP. In the failing case `cs = 70 × 0.5 / 10 = 3.5` and pixel (23, 17) is at `q = (7, 7)`: AMD and Intel return just under 2, so `floor` picks the neighbouring cell and the pixel flips (alpha 0.991 vs 0). NVIDIA returns exactly 2. **Fix:** `floor(div_rn2(q, cs))`.

## Test

`posterize_matches_the_cpu_on_every_8bpc_pair` runs Posterize at levels 4, 7 and 9 over every 8 bpc premultiplied colour and alpha (65 280 pairs) and requires bit-identical output. Without the shader change it fails on the RX 6900 XT (59 715 pairs differ at level 4: the 8 ties, plus 1-ULP differences from the plain division).

## Results (Windows 11, AMD Radeon RX 6900 XT, Adrenalin 32.0.21045.5002, `EFFECTCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1`)

| Vulkan, `effectcr…

title: Text: draw Faux Bold and synthetic bold (#1676)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #1676.

## What and why

Faux Bold was saved and carried all the way to the glyphs, then dropped. `resolve_in()` sets `synth_bold` when a bold style is asked of a family without that face, and the layout ORs in `faux_bold` (`layout.rs`), so `CharGlyph::synth_bold` is right. But nothing in `crates/render/src/text.rs` read it: `PlacedGlyph` had no such field, and `raster_pass` only filled the outline. Faux Bold and synthetic bold (Inter's missing Bold Italic, the issue's Arial row) therefore drew as regular.

- `PlacedGlyph` gets `bold`, how far the outline grows on every side in character space: `FAUX_BOLD_RADIUS × glyph size` for a `synth_bold` glyph, otherwise 0.
- A bold fill is `grown_coverage`: the outline's fill coverage merged (`max`) with a round-join stroke `2 × radius` wide. That is a dilation by the radius, and the edges stay anti-aliased.
- A bold glyph's stroke is the band between the outline grown by `radius + width/2` and by `radius − width/2`, so the stroke sits on the bolder shape and keeps its width instead of being buried by the fill. Glyphs that aren't bold keep the existing `stroke_coverage` path, so their pixels don't change.
- Runs of opaque same-colour fills (#415) only merge glyphs with the same bold radius in layer space. A run is drawn in layer space, so its radius is scaled by the glyph's transform.
- The patch padding in `draw_glyphs`, the buffer bounds in `render()` and `per_char_planes` grow by the radius.

The radius is 0.03 em. I measured it rather than copying photocraft's 0.036 (tuned in storytold/photocraft#4360 to match its earlier look, which storytold/photocraft#3705 found heavier than Photoshop). At 200 px, Inter Regular's `l` stem is 17.5 px and Inter Bold's 29.25 px. 0.036 em gives 32 px and 0.03 em gives 29.5 px, so synthetic bold now stands in for a missing bold face at about the real face's weight. It's one constant if you'd rather match photocraft or After Effects.

Not in this PR: Create Shapes from Text and Create…

title: Cryptomatte: pick the ID under a point into the Selection (`effect.pickCryptomatte`)
author: MatejKozlovsky
body:
Part 1 of 3 of Cryptomatte viewer picking for #473. This is the engine part. The viewer eyedropper (PR 2) and a Layer popup from the file's metadata (PR 3) build on it.

## What it does

- **`effect.pickCryptomatte {layer?, effect?, x, y, mode?: replace|add|remove, scale?, time?}`.** Takes a point in effect space (layer pixels on footage and precomp layers).
  - It finds the ID with the most coverage there in the effect's Cryptomatte layer. Coverage is summed per ID over ranks; ties go to the lower rank. On files whose ranks are sorted, as the spec asks, this is rank 0.
  - It then replaces the Selection with that ID, adds it, or removes it, in one `prop.set`, which is one undo step. The edit is written at the time the Selection was read (`time`, default the current time), so a keyframed Selection is edited at that key.
  - Nothing is set, and no undo step is made, when the edit wouldn't change what the Selection selects.
  - Reply: `{name, hash, layer, selection, changed, selected}`.
  - Errors: not a Cryptomatte effect, no Cryptomatte channels on the layer, a layer with no pixels at that time, nothing at the point, an invalid `scale`, or a Selection driven by an expression.
- **`effect.cryptomatteAt`.** The same lookup as a read-only query (`{name, hash, layer, selected}` or `null`). It is the plumbing for PR 2's hover hint.
- **Snaps the point to the pixel the effect samples.** `scale` is the viewer's resolution factor (default 1). The point moves to the centre of the pixel of the buffer the Cryptomatte effect receives in a render at that scale, which is not always the preview grid: from 3/4 scale up footage keeps its native pixels, a proxy has its own size at any scale, a Preserve Resolution precomp is drawn at full size, and earlier effects can pad or offset the buffer.
  - That pixel centre goes to an aux point through `effects::aux_point`, which the effects' `index_map_at` now uses too, so both round identically.

title: Snap layer bar drags to targets while Shift is held
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1828

## Cause
The layer bar drag handler in the Timeline never read Shift or called any snap function. It only turned the pointer delta into whole frames and sent `layer.timing`. Snapping existed only for work-area and current-time dragging.

## Fix
While Shift is held, a bar move or trim now computes the moved In/Out times and snaps them within 8 px to the existing snap targets. Those targets are markers, keys, other layers' In/Out points, the work area and the current time. The correction is rounded to whole frames and added to the drag delta. The dragged and selected layers' own In/Out points are not snap targets.

## Verified
- Regression test `shift_dragging_a_bar_end_snaps_to_other_layers`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --test ui_timeline_trim shift_dragging_a_bar_end_snaps_to_other_layers`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not change slip dragging or Quick Offset. Snapping runs only when a drag step moves at least one whole frame. I only tested snapping to another layer's Out point, not the composition marker or the current time, although those targets are in the candidate list.

title: Make Fractal Noise evolution progress linearly
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1816

## Cause
Fractal Noise blended the two neighbouring evolution (z) lattice slices with the quintic `fade` curve. Each revolution of evolution therefore started slow, peaked at 180° and slowed again towards 360°.

## Fix
The evolution axis now interpolates linearly (`z - z0`) in `typed_noise` on the CPU. The same change is applied to the GPU Fractal Noise paths (`fxn_typed_noise` in `fx_noise.wgsl` and `soft_linear_noise` in `kernels.wgsl`), so CPU and GPU output stay identical. A regression test checks that the noise is linear in z for all four noise types.

## Verified
- Regression test `noise3::tests::evolution_is_linear`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-effects evolution_is_linear`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests_roto::object_matte_mattes_persist_in_the_disk_cache`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The x/y interpolation is unchanged. The separate `value_noise` function, in `generate.rs` and its GPU copy in `kernels.wgsl`, still uses `fade` on z, because Fractal Noise doesn't evolve through it. I only ran the effects crate tests, clippy and fmt. The GPU crate tests couldn't run in this environment (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR errors).

title: Hold position between identical auto-Bézier spatial keys
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1675

## Cause
`auto_spatial` always set a key's auto-Bézier spatial tangents to (next − previous) / 6 (Catmull-Rom), even when a neighbouring key had the same value. So the segment between two identical position keys got control points away from that position. In the issue's example, the layer drifted to about 450 px halfway through a hold at 400 px.

## Fix
In `auto_spatial`, a key now gets a zero tangent on any side that faces a real neighbour with the same value. This makes the segment between two identical keys zero-length, as in After Effects. The other side keeps its normal Catmull-Rom tangent, and end keys behave as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::auto_spatial_holds_between_identical_keys`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-keyframe --lib auto_spatial_holds_between_identical_keys`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Stored (non-auto) spatial tangents, temporal ease computation and `spatial_handles` are unchanged.

title: Keep exact sub-frame key times for script setValueAtTime/addKey
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1799

## Cause
Script `setValueAtTime` and `addKey` send `prop.addKey`, which always snapped the key time to the nearest frame. At an exact half frame the tie goes to the earlier frame, so a key at 1.5 s in a 25 fps comp landed at 1.48 s. Other sub-frame times, such as 1.51 s, were moved to a frame as well.

## Fix
`prop.addKey` now takes an optional `snap` parameter. It defaults to true, so the old behaviour is kept, and `snap: false` keeps the exact time. The script prelude's `setValueAtTime` and `addKey` pass `snap: false`, so keys stay at the time the script gives, as in After Effects.

Verified: regression test `tests::script_set_value_at_time_keeps_subframe_key_time` (`cargo test -p effectcraft-script --lib script_set_value_at_time_keeps_subframe_key_time`).

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests_roto::object_matte_mattes_persist_in_the_disk_cache`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed

title: Timeline: layer switches, labels and modes act on the whole selection (#1849)
author: ki2pixel
body:
Closes #1849.

With several layers selected in the Timeline, a click on one selected layer's row changed only that
layer: each switch (Lock, 3D, Video, Solo, Shy, …), the label swatch and the Modes column had to be
set one layer at a time. After Effects applies the change to every selected layer. The engine
commands already took a `layers` list — the Timeline's row controls passed the clicked layer alone.

## What changed

- **One rule for these controls.** On a selected layer's row, the A/V Features and Switches columns,

  apply to that layer alone. The targets are computed when the press happens, not while the row is
  drawn, so a big comp's Timeline costs nothing more than before.

  doesn't apply to are left out — 3D on a camera or light, Audio on a layer without audio, Effect on

  decides which cells a row shows now also picks the targets (`switch_applies`), so the two can't

author: Silvertree2010

The viewer's `pick()` chooses a selected layer under the pointer before any layer in front of it. That rule exists so a covered selected layer can still be dragged (#230). title: Use frozen Object Matte in sessions without the freezing model
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1457

## Cause
The Object Matte frozen key includes the segmentation model's id, and `frozen_alpha` only compared it against the key for the session's current model. A fresh headless render that hasn't loaded MobileSAM therefore rejected a MobileSAM-frozen matte, while `is_frozen` still reported it as frozen. The effect then fell back silently to Classical segmentation.

## Fix
The frozen key is now computed from a model id (`frozen_key_of` / `seed_of`; the public `frozen_key` and `seed` delegate to them). When the key for the current model doesn't match, `frozen_alpha` also accepts the key for Classical or any known model. Frozen mattes are therefore used as stored, with no segmentation, whatever model the rendering session has loaded. As a consequence, switching the segmentation model in a session no longer invalidates frozen mattes.

## Verified
- Regression test `object_matte::tests::frozen_mattes_survive_a_session_without_their_model`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -q -p effectcraft-effects frozen_mattes_survive_a_session_without_their_model`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The CLI still does not restore or select the segmentation model when it opens a project, so `roto.models` and the model-keyed computed list in `objectMatte.status` still reflect the session's own model. Changing the prompt, the span, the Input Key or the matte settings still invalidates frozen mattes as before.
