title: Fit layer transform bounds to the area its masks reveal
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1257

## Cause
`content_bounds` (used for the viewer's transform box, handles and hit testing) returned only the source, text or shape bounds and never looked at the layer's masks. A masked layer therefore kept a box the size of the whole layer.

## Fix
A new `masks::visible_bounds` combines the bounding boxes of the enabled, closed masks the way `masks::apply` combines them (Add/Lighten/Difference union, Intersect/Darken intersect, Subtract ignored, the first Intersect/Darken treated as Add), padding each box by its expansion and feather. `content_bounds` intersects the layer bounds with that result. It keeps the full bounds when the masks can't be bounded (an inverted mask, a variable-width feather, or a leading Subtract, unless a later Intersect/Darken narrows them) or when nothing would be visible.

## Verified
- Regression tests `tests_mask_expansion::content_bounds_follow_an_add_mask`, `tests_mask_expansion::content_bounds_ignore_a_subtract_mask`, `tests_mask_expansion::content_bounds_include_mask_expansion_clamped_to_the_layer`: fail on `main` without the fix and pass with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-render --lib content_bounds_`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes except `tests_roto::object_matte_mattes_persist_in_the_disk_cache`, which also fails on `main` without this change.

## Not changed
The callers of `content_bounds` (viewer handles, hit testing, align and layer menu commands) are unchanged, so they all pick up the mask-aware bounds. Feather padding is a conservative estimate rather than the exact blurred extent.

author: CharlesBaumer
body:
Two small test-only fixes I hit running `cargo xtask ci` on Windows. No change to non-test code.

### 1. Engine tests: `Stills` is Unix-only

`cargo xtask ci` stops at clippy on Windows:

    error: struct `Stills` is never constructed
      --> crates\engine\src\doc_path\tests.rs:38:8
       = note: `-D dead-code` implied by `-D warnings`

`Stills` is only used inside the `#[cfg(unix)]` block of
`footage_on_other_computers_is_never_looked_at`, so on Windows it is dead code. It now
carries the same `#[cfg(unix)]`.

### 2. Media tests: ffmpeg fixtures survive concurrent first runs

On a first run (no `target/fixtures/media` yet) tests that share a fixture, e.g.
`cache_budget_evicts` and `a_called_off_read_does_not_decode`, each generate it and rename
their temp file into place. On Windows the losing rename fails while the winner has the
file open:

    panicked at crates\media\tests\footage.rs:43:33:

`ffmpeg_fixture` now treats a failed rename as "another test made it first" when the
fixture exists, removes its temp file and goes on, like `png_sequence` already does.
A rename that fails with no fixture in place still fails the test.

title: gpu: run Content-Aware Fill's PatchMatch and flow on the GPU
author: gmrmad1
body:
## What and why

Content-Aware Fill's two expensive per-frame stages now run on the GPU (Metal / Vulkan / Direct3D 12 /
WebGPU through wgpu compute shaders): **PatchMatch synthesis** — the stage that makes the tool slow — and
the **flow's block matching**, which the sequence's flow-guided propagation starts from. The architecture
is staged so the rest can follow as each one pays.

`Refs #1839.`

## How

* **`effectcraft_raster::inpaint::FillBackend`** — a trait whose stages (`membrane`, `membrane_known`,
  `flow`, `patch`) *default to the CPU reference*, so a backend implements only what it can and every
  other stage keeps the CPU's exact behaviour. `fill_sequence` became a wrapper over
  `fill_sequence_with(input, opts, backend, progress)`. The sequence's orchestration stays on the CPU:
  it is sequential frame-to-frame, and the flow-guided propagation needs every frame of the range
  resident at once. The trait documents that stages may be entered concurrently (the per-frame and
  per-pair work runs under `rayon`).
* **`effectcraft_render::Accelerator::inpaint()`** — the compositor-side hook (next to `particles()`),
  returning `Option<&dyn FillBackend>`.
* **`effectcraft_gpu::inpaint`** — `impl FillBackend for Gpu`, kernels in `shaders/inpaint.wgsl`:
  PatchMatch's pyramid downsample, coarse-to-fine upsample, NNF upsample, field init, a two-pass
  checkerboard propagation (replacing the CPU's scan order), the halving random search, the SSD with the
  CPU's early-out, a shared-memory 1024-bin histogram of the targets' distances for the vote's σ², the
  distance-weighted vote and the membrane solve used as PatchMatch's coarsest level; and the flow's luma
  pyramid halves, coarse-to-fine search, sub-pixel parabola fit and 3×3 vector median.
* **`Enc::read_rect`** — a sub-rectangle readback. A fill only changes its hole, so only the hole's
  bounds (and the flow's small `cols × rows` field) cross back to the CPU: that alone took the 1920×1080
  patch from 662 ms to …

title: Text: language-aware All Caps (Turkish İ) and multi-character capitals
author: eylmz1986
body:
## Problem
All Caps used Unicode's default, language-less casing and kept only single-character mappings:

- Turkish/Azerbaijani "istanbul ılık" was drawn as "ISTANBUL ILIK" instead of "İSTANBUL ILIK"
  (the dotted i lost its dot — a spelling error, not a style choice).
- Multi-character capitals were dropped: "straße" stayed "STRAßE" instead of "STRASSE", and the
  glyph's reported character (`ch`, used by Character Offset/Value) disagreed with what was drawn.

## Change
- **New character attribute `language`** (BCP 47 tag, e.g. `"tr"`, `"az-Latn"`; default none = Unicode
  default rules) on the Source Text base style and on style runs (`CharStyle` / `TextDoc`).
  - `layer.setText {language}` / `layer.newText {language}`; `null` or `""` clears it; malformed tags
    are rejected with an error (`_` is normalised to `-`).
  - Serde: `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` on `#[serde(default)]` structs, so
    existing projects load unchanged and untouched documents serialize exactly as before.
  - Reported by `char_style_json` (Character panel / scripting round trip).
  - Scripting: `TextDocument.language` (EffectCraft extension; `""`/null clears).
- **Casing** (`effectcraft_text::Casing`, `layout::Upper`): for `tr`, `az`, `crh`, `gag`, `kk`, `tt`

title: Agents over the bridge: `file.import {alpha}` and modal dialogs that report themselves
author: eylmz1986
body:
Two commits, one per part. Part 2's test relies on Part 1's `alpha` param, so they are kept in one PR.

Found while driving the desktop app over `effectcraft-cli mcp --bridge`: importing a ProRes 4444 movie
opened Interpret Footage, after which `ui_click` / `ui_drag` / `ui_type` replied `ok` and did nothing.

## Part 1 — `file.import`: `alpha` param so agents can interpret unlabeled alpha without the Ask User form

### Problem
TGA, TIFF and movies with alpha (ProRes 4444, QuickTime Animation…) don't say whether their alpha is
straight or premultiplied. With Settings ▸ Import ▸ Interpret Unlabeled Alpha As on its default,
Ask User, `file.import` pushes `Event::Frontend {command: "file.interpretFootage", reason:
"unlabeledAlpha"}` and the desktop app opens Interpret Footage, a modal form. An agent driving the
app over the MCP bridge has no way to decide per import; the only workaround is changing the
user's global preference (`import.unlabeledAlpha`).

### Change
- `file.import` takes `alpha?: straight|premultiplied|ignore|guess` (the values of
  `file.interpretFootage`'s `alpha`). It replaces the preference for this import and never asks.
  `guess` runs Interpret Footage ▸ Guess on the first frame (with its matte colour), inside the
  same "Import" undo step; when the frame has no partly transparent pixels it falls back to the
  preference's Guess (premultiplied movies, straight stills). Background imports apply it too.
- Files that state their alpha (PNG, OpenEXR, PSD…) are unchanged.
- Reply: `unlabeledAlpha` now lists **every** imported item whose alpha is unlabeled (it used to
  list only the items Ask User asked about; under Ask User both are the same), plus
  `askedAlpha` (the items Interpret Footage was opened for) and
  `alphaInterpretation: [{item, alpha, matteColor, from: "alpha"|"settings"|"ask"}]`.
- An invalid `alpha` is rejected before anything is imported.
- Docs: agents.md cookbook, footage.md, preferences.md.

title: Report the build's git commit in `app.capabilities` and `effectcraft-cli info`
author: eylmz1986
body:
## Problem
A release and a local build of `main` report the same version: today the v0.11.1 MSI says `0.11.1`,
and a build of `main` 128 commits later says `0.12.0` like every other build of `main`. Agents and
bug reports can't tell which code they are talking to, and a tool that pins EffectCraft to a commit
has no way to check that the binary it runs is that commit.

## Change
- `crates/engine/build.rs` records the commit as the compile-time env `EFFECTCRAFT_BUILD_COMMIT`:
  - an `EFFECTCRAFT_BUILD_COMMIT` value in the build environment wins (release CI, source tarballs,
    Nix and other builds without `.git`);
  - otherwise `git rev-parse HEAD` in the crate's directory;
  - `unknown` when neither is available. It never fails a build, and only hex digits (or
    `unknown`) reach the binary.
  - Re-runs when HEAD moves (HEAD, the branch ref it points at, `packed-refs`, found with
    `git rev-parse --git-path`, so git worktrees work too).
- `effectcraft_engine::BUILD_COMMIT` exposes it.
- `app.capabilities` (and so MCP `get_state`'s `app`) and `effectcraft-cli info` report `commit`.
  The human-readable `info` line shows the first 12 characters:
  `EffectCraft 0.12.0 (f3f24ef18909, headless), 731 commands, 307 effects`.
- Docs: agents.md (`get_state`, `info`) and control-protocol.md (`app.capabilities`).

No dependency added; the wasm build is unaffected (the build script runs on the host).

## Tests
- `crates/engine/tests/build_commit.rs`: `app.capabilities.commit` equals `BUILD_COMMIT` and is a
  commit id (or `unknown`).
- `apps/effectcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs` `info_and_commands`: `info --json` reports the same commit.

## Testing notes
Rebased onto `upstream/main` ef74d829 and re-run on Windows 11 (Rust 1.99.1, MSVC 2022): `cargo fmt --check` clean; `effectcraft-engine --test build_commit` and `effectcraft-cli --test cli` (21 passed) pass. title: Make `cargo xtask ci` pass on Windows
author: eylmz1986
body:
On Windows 11 (`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`, Turkish locale) `cargo xtask ci` failed on `main` (f3f24ef; still on ef74d829) in
four places that pass on Linux/macOS. One commit per fix:

1. **engine — clippy `-D warnings`:** the `Stills` test importer in `doc_path/tests.rs` is only used by the
   `#[cfg(unix)]` part of `footage_on_other_computers_is_never_looked_at`, so it was dead code on Windows.
   It is now gated the same way.
2. **media — `tests/footage.rs` fixture race:** `perf_sequential_1080p_h264` and

title: Text Range Selector: Start, End and Offset show as counts with Units = Index (#1814)
author: SBaksa
body:
Part of #1814 (the display; whether switching Units should also convert the values is left open, below).

With a Range Selector's **Units** set to **Index**, the selector already counts characters (or words, lines): the engine stores the value and the renderer selects by count (`render/src/text/tests.rs` covers it). The timeline, though, kept showing **Start**, **End** and **Offset** as percentages, so End = 3 read "3.0%" and switching Units looked like it did nothing.

They're now shown without the % sign while Units is Index. `render::text::in_index_units(layer, uid)` tells the timeline whether a property is a Range Selector's Start, End or Offset in Index units; Amount and other properties are unaffected.

**Tests:** `index_units_mark_start_end_and_offset` (Percentage by default; Index marks Start/End/Offset only, not Amount, the animator's properties or the layer transform). Checked in a headless snapshot: with Units = Index and End = 3 the timeline shows `0.0 / 3.0 / 0.0` and the first three characters take the animator's Opacity 0.

**Left open:** whether switching Units should also convert the existing values (End 100% to the character count). Today they keep their numbers (End 100 is capped at the count, so the selection doesn't change on its own); happy to add a conversion if that's wanted.

title: AEP: open and save After Effects projects (.aep / .aepx import and export), refs #190
author: vangel76
body:
**EffectCraft can now open After Effects projects, and save its own projects as After Effects projects.**

Until now, anyone coming from After Effects had to rebuild their work by hand. With this PR, File ▸ Import ▸ After Effects Project… opens an `.aep` (or `.aepx`) file and brings in the compositions, layers, animation, text, shapes, masks, effects and layer styles. File ▸ Export ▸ After Effects Project… writes an EffectCraft project back as an `.aep` that After Effects opens. Whatever cannot be converted is listed in a report, never dropped silently.

Tested on about 80 real production projects: every one imports without a crash, more than 98 % of layers, keyframes, masks and shapes come across exactly, and what is still missing is mostly third-party plug-ins. A project taken from After Effects through EffectCraft and back renders in After Effects almost identically to the original.

It is built clean-room: everything comes from small test projects we made ourselves in After Effects, one change at a time, and from checking the results in After Effects. No third-party `.aep` parser or format description was used.

This replaces the drafts #1377, #1378 and #1422 (refs #190). The details for reviewers follow.

---

title: Reject non-finite numbers in CSS colour parsing
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/svg/src/color.rs:182-185` (no existing issue): CSS colour parser returns NaN components for rgb(nan,...) and similar input.

## Cause
`parse_color` read rgb()/rgba()/hsl()/hsla() components and alpha with `f64::parse`, which accepts `nan` and `inf`. `clamp` leaves NaN unchanged, so NaN reached the returned colour. Infinite values were clamped in rgb but were still accepted as valid input.

## Fix
Each numeric parse in the rgb, hsl and alpha paths now goes through `.filter(|v| v.is_finite())`. `parse_color` therefore returns `None` for `nan` and `inf` instead of a colour with NaN components. A regression test covers the rgb, alpha and hsl cases.

## Verified
- Regression test `color::tests::non_finite_rejected`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-svg non_finite_rejected`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Hex and named colour parsing, and the clamping of finite out-of-range values, are unchanged.

title: Expressions: cubic-Bezier easing helper (bezier(...)) (#1884)
author: ki2pixel
body:
Closes #1884.

After Effects' expression language only has `linear`, `ease`, `easeIn` and `easeOut`. The Adobe
community request for a CSS-style cubic-Bézier helper has been open since 2022
(https://community.adobe.com/feature-requests-530/add-a-new-cubic-bezier-interpolation-type-for-expressions-1214070).
`bezier()` adds it as an EffectCraft extension; existing expressions are unchanged.

## What changed

- **`bezier(t, tMin, tMax, value1, value2, [x1, y1, x2, y2])`**, plus the short
  `bezier(t, value1, value2, [x1, y1, x2, y2])` form. The curve is the last argument; everything
  before it follows `linear` / `ease`.
- **CSS `cubic-bezier()` semantics.** `x1` / `x2` clamp to 0..1, `y1` / `y2` are free (overshoot
  allowed), `t` clamps to `tMin..tMax`, and `tMin == tMax` behaves like the other helpers.
- **Scalars and arrays** work like `linear` / `ease`; `ease(t, …)` is exactly
  `bezier(t, …, [1/3, 0, 2/3, 1])`.
- **Invalid or missing curves fall back to linear** (a curve that is not four finite numbers),
  reading the curve by argument position so a bad value cannot swallow the last value or break a
  render.
- **Solver:** Newton–Raphson on `x(u)`, with a bisection fallback when Newton leaves 0..1 or the
  derivative vanishes. `y(u)` is then read directly (overshoot included).
- **Discoverability:** the helper is in the Expression Language menu's Interpolation group and in
  the expression editor's auto-complete and syntax highlighting; accepting it inserts the call
  parentheses like `linear` / `ease`.

title: fix(script): interrupt blocked socket writes on close
author: TimotheusG
body:
<!-- effectcraft-batch-dependencies:start -->
## Dependencies and merge order

Independent; proposed landing position 5. The socket cancellation fix is not a runtime dependency of audio/export. Its Cargo.lock changes merge cleanly with #1922.

[Full nine-PR index, merge instructions, audited heads and validation evidence](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/pull/1827#issuecomment-6320269490). The first five positions are independent, not a serial dependency chain. Combined CI evidence is not a claim of nine standalone full-suite passes.
<!-- effectcraft-batch-dependencies:end -->

Closing a socket on Windows did not reliably interrupt a blocked `write_all`: `close` returned, but the writer remained blocked. The existing regression fixture hid this because Windows could accept its entire 64 MiB write before any backpressure occurred.

Use a nonblocking write loop with one operation deadline and an explicit close flag, yielding for at most 5 ms while the send buffer is full. Restore blocking mode before returning so subsequent reads retain their behavior. The global table remains unlocked during I/O, and only the socket being written is locked.

The test peer now has bounded receive/send buffers and is filled until it actually reports backpressure. `socket2` is a native-only dev dependency for configuring that fixture; the write payload shrinks to 64 KiB. The close test verifies the writer is still pending before closing. A further scenario checks complete 256 KiB transfers and delayed reads on both outgoing and accepted sockets. Related: #1248.

The corrected fixture reproduced the close failure before the production fix. All three socket tests then passed in 10 consecutive runs (30 checks). Companion fixes: Unix-only test-helper guard (#1889) and host-independent font tests (#1890).

title: Windows: document and verify the GNU toolchain's import-library requirements (#1886)
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Fixes #1886. Refs #1882.

`webbrowser` 1.2.4 (through `egui-winit`, for opening links) asks the linker for `shlwapi`. A mingw-w64 install has `libshlwapi.a`; Rust's bundled LLD with self-contained libraries doesn't, so that setup stops with `unable to find library -lshlwapi`. This is a missing build-time import library, not a missing DLL at runtime.

Instead of a project-wide linker change, or copying the host's `shlwapi.dll` into the build (as #1861 and the reporter's branch do), this documents the setups that work and checks them in CI.

**CONTRIBUTING.md, new "Windows" section**
- MSVC, the default, is what the releases use.
- GNU needs a current mingw-w64 GCC and binutils first on `PATH`; the MSYS2 commands are given. An older MinGW on `PATH` (CodeBlocks' GCC 8.1, #1882) can break the link.
- Bundled LLD works when mingw-w64's `libshlwapi.a`, copied into a folder of its own, is on the search path in the user's own Cargo config. Adding all of mingw-w64's `lib` folder doesn't work: its C runtime clashes with Rust's bundled one (`undefined symbol: DllEntryPoint` linking `boa_engine`), which CI showed on the first run.

**`.github/workflows/windows-toolchains.yml`**

Builds `effectcraft` and `effectcraft-cli` in one `cargo build` and runs both with `--version`, three ways:
- MSVC
- GNU with MSYS2's mingw-w64
- GNU linked by `rust-lld`, self-contained, with only mingw-w64's `libshlwapi.a` added

It runs nightly, and on PRs that change the workflow or `Cargo.lock`, since a dependency update is what brings in a new system library.

Not covered: cross-compiling, ARM64 GNU, the GUI beyond `--version`, and the workspace tests under GNU. #1882's old-MinGW conflict is only documented here: there's no repo-wide linker change.

**Testing:** the new workflow running on this PR is the test; I haven't built locally.

title: Resolve SVG font-size percentages against the parent font size
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/svg/src/lib.rs:624` (no existing issue): SVG font-size percentage resolves against the viewport instead of the parent font size.

## Cause
`cascade` parsed `font-size` with `length`. For `%` values, `length` uses the viewport diagonal, not the inherited font size. So `font-size: 200%` in a 100x100 SVG gave 200px instead of 32px.

title: Fix hsv_to_rgb returning magenta for tiny negative hues
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lib.rs:143-158` (no existing issue): hsv_to_rgb returns magenta for a tiny negative hue near red.

## Cause
In f32, `h.rem_euclid(1.0)` of a tiny negative hue such as -1e-9 rounds to exactly 1.0. That makes `h6 = 6.0` and `i = 6`, which falls into the `_` arm and returns (v, p, q), which is magenta.

## Fix
After wrapping the hue, `hsv_to_rgb` sets `h6` to 0.0 when it reaches 6.0, so a hue that rounds up to 1.0 is treated as 0.0, which is red. Regression test `tests::hsv_to_rgb_tiny_negative_hue_is_red` asserts that `hsv_to_rgb(-1e-9, 1.0, 1.0)` returns a red colour. Run with `cargo test -p effectcraft-color hsv_to_rgb_tiny_negative_hue_is_red`. Without the fix the same input returns magenta (`1 0 1`).

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::hsv_to_rgb_tiny_negative_hue_is_red`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-color hsv_to_rgb_tiny_negative_hue_is_red`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The other colour conversion functions and the match arms in `hsv_to_rgb` are unchanged.

title: Reject signed fields in multi-field parse_timecode
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/time/src/lib.rs:443` (no existing issue): parse_timecode accepts signed numbers inside timecode fields.

## Cause
The multi-field branch of parse_timecode parsed each field with i64::parse, which accepts a leading '+' or '-'. Input like "00:+5:-30:00" was accepted and the signed fields were combined arithmetically, giving a wrong frame number.

## Fix
Each non-empty field in the multi-field branch must now be all ASCII digits, as in the single-field branch. Otherwise it returns a ParseError ("bad field ..."). A leading sign on the whole value still means 'relative'.

title: effects: speed up Match Grain's CPU analysis (~3x on 1080p/4K)
author: ki2pixel
body:
### What

Make Match Grain's CPU analysis proportional to the sample boxes instead of the whole frame:

- `grain_stats_boxes` measures the per-channel high-pass std and the lag-1 autocorrelation from small crops around each sample box (3 px halo = the support of the three box passes at sigma 1.5), deduplicating overlapping boxes so the sums are the same as the previous full-image masked version;
- `sample_boxes` scans the candidate rows in parallel (the sort is a total order on variance/y/x, so the chosen boxes do not change);
- the "own" boxes and statistics are only computed when **Compensate for Existing Noise** is on, and the frame is cloned for the Preview composition only in Preview mode;
- `Plane::transpose`/`map_rows` now run on the calling thread below 4096 px: with the per-box crops, the rayon dispatch was the dominant cost (240 blurs of ~15x15 per frame).

Release build, AMD Ryzen Threadripper 1920X (24 threads), synthetic noisy source and flat target, default settings (80 boxes of 9 px), best of 4 runs (1 warm-up + 3). Same harness before/after, at 1080p / 4K:

title: xtask bench: run on Windows (scenario commands from an args file, os error 206)
author: ded-achtung
body:
## Summary

`cargo xtask bench` doesn't run on Windows past the `demo` scenario. `build_project` passes a scenario's commands to `effectcraft-cli --empty run <id> <json> …` on one command line. The `layers` scenario (100 layers with effects and keyframes) is longer than Windows' 32 767-character limit, so the CLI never starts:

```
… --save-as …\target\bench\projects\layers.ecproj: The filename or extension is too long. (os error 206)
```

Splitting the batch over several CLI runs doesn't work: commands such as `effect.apply` and `dup` act on the current selection, which a new process doesn't have.

This PR:

- adds `effectcraft-cli run --args-file F`, which takes the same `<id> <json>` arguments one per line of F (blank lines skipped) and appends them to any positional ones. A file that can't be read is a usage error (exit 2);
- makes `xtask bench` write each scenario's commands to `<project>.args` next to the project, run them with `--args-file`, and remove the file afterwards.

The usage text and the CLI's module docs mention the new option.

## Tests

- New: `run_reads_arguments_from_a_file` (`apps/effectcraft-cli/tests/cli.rs`). A batch longer than 32 767 characters (401 commands) runs, and a missing file exits with 2 and names the file.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-cli --test cli` (22 passed) and the xtask bench tests pass. `fmt` and `clippy -D warnings` are clean for both crates.
- `cargo xtask bench --repeat 3` now runs all four scenarios on Windows 11 (16 threads). Before, it stopped at `layers`.

A note on `xtask bench` on Windows: it records wall time only, because there's no `/usr/bin/time`.

title: EPS: Illustrator EPS files draw their artwork (#955)
author: JWesCampbell
body:
Fixes #955. Also reported in the SonduckFilm review: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RJ7KzcPfQ0Q at about 7:30.

## Problem
An EPS saved from Illustrator 2026 parsed without error but came out empty (`root.children` = 0), so the imported footage showed nothing.

## Cause
Three gaps in the PostScript interpreter (`crates/pdf/src/ps.rs`), each checked against the PostScript Language Reference, 3rd ed.:

1. **Operators stored under another name didn't run.** `/mo /moveto load def` stores the operator, and executing `mo` should run it. We pushed the operator's *name* instead. Illustrator's prolog aliases every path and paint operator this way (`mo`, `li`, `cv`, `cp`, `f`, `@`, …), so nothing was ever drawn.
2. **Device queries didn't return values.** `currentpagedevice`, `currentscreen`, `currentflat`, `currenthalftone`, `currentblackgeneration`, `currentundercolorremoval`, `currentcolortransfer`, `currentsystemparams`, `status`, `dictstack`, `maxlength` and `internaldict` pushed nothing. That shifted the stack under the prolog's guards. They now push a plain device's defaults, and `setscreen` now pops all three of its operands.
3. **Embedded data ran as PostScript.** `currentfile 0 (eod) /SubFileDecode filter` now skips to the end-of-data string, so an embedded XMP packet (with its stray `(` and `{`) is no longer interpreted.

## Tests
- New `tests_import::eps_with_aliased_operators_device_queries_and_embedded_data_draws` covers all three cases with **synthetic PostScript only**: no Adobe procset or fixture is committed. It fails on `main` and passes with this change.

title: Keep the 3D gizmo a constant screen size whatever the layer's Scale (#1910)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1910.

The 3D axis gizmo was drawn as `60 / zoom` units in the layer's own space, then projected through the layer's world matrix. So its on-screen size followed the layer's net Scale (its own and its parents'). A layer at 10 % got arrows 10x shorter, and at 1-5 % (common with Blender `.jsx` imports) the gizmo became a dot.

The new `gizmo_axis_lengths` helper divides each arrow's length by the length of that axis in the world matrix (`w.apply_vec(unit)`). Each arrow is now 60 screen px in world space at any Scale, and parenting is included because the world matrix already holds the parents. Non-uniform scale is handled per axis. A degenerate (zero or non-finite) axis falls back to the old length.

The drag mapping (`axis_drag`) uses the arrow vector and its screen projection together, so it still follows the cursor. The short stub drawn for an axis pointing at the camera now moves a scaled layer at the same speed as an unscaled one.

Test: `gizmo_arrows_keep_their_length_when_the_layer_is_scaled` checks a 10 % layer, the zoom factor, and the zero-scale fallback.

title: #1812: stills at reduced resolution are resampled once, and their layers cached
author: ded-achtung
body:
Part of #1812 (slow playback of the 3D parallax project). This PR fixes the CPU side. #1918 and #1928 fix the GPU side (#1326 keeps a GPU failure from turning the compositor off).

## What was slow

The #1812 project has five still plates about 21 120 px wide (≈1.85 GB as f32). At Quarter resolution:

1. `MediaPool::frame_at_size` honoured the requested size only for movies. Stills came back at full size, so `footage_buf` resampled every plate from 21 120 px on every frame. The plates also don't fit the default 1 GiB media pool, so they were decoded from PNG again and again.
2. Footage layers have no layer-cache key. Each preview worker built a new layer buffer for every still on every frame. The GPU compositor's upload cache is keyed by buffer, so it uploaded every plate again each frame.

## Change

- **Media pool:** a still asked for at a reduced size is resampled once with `effectcraft_raster::resample`, the same call the renderer made, so pixels are unchanged. The pool keeps the reduced copy under the sized key.
- **Layer cache:** stills without a proxy are keyed like text and shape layers, without the source time. Movies and sequences keep their current behaviour.

## Numbers

Windows 11, RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB), 16 threads. #1812 project with footage relinked locally. Desktop runs use default prefs with the disk cache off, so every frame is really rendered.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `effectcraft-cli bench --scale 0.25 --play 30` | 413 ms/frame | 33 ms/frame |
| desktop playback from 30 s, first pass | 1–5 % of real time | 32–42 % |

Five frames at Quarter are bit-identical to `main`.

## Tests

- `stills_at_reduced_sizes_are_resampled_once` (media) checks that the result equals `resample` and that later frames hit the pool.
- `still_layers_are_cached_across_times_and_movies_are_not` (render) checks the new cache keys. It fails on `main`.

title: #1812: keep Classic 3D atlases for the same layer buffers
author: ded-achtung
body:
Part of #1812. Independent of #1917, but it pays off fully with it: there, still layers keep the same buffers from frame to frame.

## Problem

`classic3d::draw_run` packs every plane texture into a new atlas on every frame. For the #1812 plates at Quarter that is a 5280 × 4056 texture, about 343 MB, plus the copies into it. Up to 16 preview workers render frames in parallel, each with its own atlas. On an 8 GB laptop GPU that runs the device out of memory.

## Change

When no plane has depth of field, the atlas depends only on the layer buffers. It is now:

- built once, in its own encoder that is submitted right away, so a frame that later finds it reads it filled;
- kept in the `GpuContext` and reused while the same buffers are alive. Matching uses `Weak`s and `Arc::ptr_eq`, as in the upload cache.

Limits: at most 2 atlases, each within half the upload budget. Least recently used atlases and atlases of freed buffers go first. `clear_uploads` drops them. Runs with depth of field and atlases over the limit keep the current per-frame pooled atlas.

## Numbers

Windows 11, RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB), 16 threads, #1812 project, default prefs with the disk cache off.

| desktop playback from 30 s, first pass | without | with |
|---|---|---|
| speed (#1917 applied) | 32 % of real time | 72–84 % |
| peak VRAM | 5.1 GB | 3.6 GB |

## Test

`classic_3d_atlases_are_kept_for_the_same_layer_buffers` checks that:

- a second draw, in another encoder, reuses the same atlas texture and draws the same pixels;
- new buffers miss the cache and build their own atlas.

title: GPU: a failed allocation fails the frame, not the context (#1812)
author: ded-achtung
body:
Found while testing #1812. One allocation failure retired the GPU for the rest of the session, and every later frame rendered on the CPU.

## Problem

`Gpu::within_memory` catches `OutOfMemory` and `Internal` errors, and the preview then retries the frame on the CPU with fewer GPU frames kept. That is the intended path from #106 and #591.

A texture whose allocation failed is invalid, though. Its next use, a `create_view` or a copy in the same render, is a **validation** error. Nothing caught that error, so it reached the uncaptured-error handler and retired the context:

```
ERROR [ec-frame-7] effectcraft: uncaptured GPU error: Validation Error
  In Texture::create_view
    Texture with '' label is invalid
WARN  [ec-frame-14] effectcraft_ui_egui::frames: the GPU context is retired (...); the frame renders on the CPU
```

On the #1812 project this happened in most cold-start playbacks: 16 workers allocate at once while the caches are empty.

## Change

`within_memory` also pushes a `Validation` error scope. Scopes are thread-local in wgpu 30, so this only catches errors from the guarded work. Out-of-memory is still reported first. The frame then fails the way an out-of-memory frame already does: the CPU renders it, uploads are cleared, and the GPU keeps working.

## Result

Desktop playback of the #1812 project, 10 runs, together with #1917 and #1918:

- the GPU context was never retired;
- a few cold-start frames (0–6 per run) fell back to the CPU, as designed;
- the first pass ran at 68–84 % of real time.

## Test

`within_memory_catches_the_use_of_a_failed_texture` creates a texture over the size limit and makes a view of it inside the guard. It checks that the work returns an error, that `check_health` is still `Ok`, and that the next guarded work succeeds. On `main` the test fails, because the uncaptured error retires the context.

title: Preview: keep rendering past the cached frames after a loop or restart
author: ded-achtung
body:
## What you see

Play a comp that is only partly cached, stop, and play it again from the start (or let it loop). Rendering stops: the CPU sits idle and the green cache bar doesn't grow. It resumes only when the playhead is about 1.6 s before the end of the cached run. If rendering can't catch up from there, playback stalls.

## Cause

While a preview plays, `update_playback` looks for uncached frames only within `ahead * 3` frames of the playhead. `ahead` is twice the number of frame workers, so the window is 96 frames with 16 workers: 1.6 s at 60 fps. After a loop or a restart all of those are cached, so nothing gets queued.

## Change

A playing preview now looks for the next uncached frames as far ahead as the RAM preview holds, capped at the length of the range. It still queues at most `ahead` frames at a time.

The far-ahead frames don't push out the near ones. When the cache is full, eviction removes the frames the playhead reaches last (#595, #793). While paused, the window is unchanged.

## Measured

Windows 11, 16 threads, #1812 project at Quarter. The test: play from 0 for 12 s, stop, play from 0 again.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| CPU during the second play, 1–12 s | 0.6 cores (idle) | rendering continues |
| cached when stopped at ~13 s | up to ~15 s | up to ~105 s (the 3 GB RAM preview) |

## Test

`playback_prefetches_past_the_cached_frames_ahead`: frames 0–119 are cached (more than the widest old window), playback starts at 0, and a frame past 119 must render within the first second. On `main` the test fails.

## Related

#1121 (open) fixes a different stall: the order in which prefetch frames *finish*. It touches `cache_when_idle` in the same file, so whichever lands second may need a small rebase.

title: Clipboard: export keyframes as After Effects-compatible text
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Refs #1908. Related: #1667, which asks for the same readable text along with an internal paste bug. This PR doesn't import text into EffectCraft.

## Problem
Copying keyframes filled EffectCraft's internal clipboard, but the system clipboard only got a line like `EffectCraft: 3 keyframes`. Other applications received no animation data, so tools such as AE2Blend, which read After Effects keyframe text from the clipboard, had nothing to work with.

## Change
`crates/engine/src/keyframe_text.rs` turns copied keys and unanimated properties of one layer into After Effects keyframe text. `keys.copy` and Edit > Copy with properties selected store it in `State::keyframe_text`, every other copy clears it, and the UI's Copy handler puts it on the system clipboard instead of the note. EffectCraft's own paste still uses the internal clipboard, so easing, tangents and roving keys survive.

The format follows real After Effects output. I captured After Effects 2019's clipboard text for the same layers and values on this machine (ExtendScript selects the properties and runs Edit > Copy), and the tests assert the same blocks.

- **Layout:** the `Adobe After Effects 9.0 Keyframe Data` header, the layer's source size and pixel aspect, a `Layer` line, one block per property, a tab after every column, and `End of Keyframe Data`. Current After Effects writes the 9.0 header with the `Layer` line; 2019 still wrote 8.0 without it. `ae-keyframes` needs the `Layer` line, and AE2Blend skips it.
- **Rows:** a keyed property has one row per copied key, at its comp frame (the layer's start offset and stretch applied). An unanimated one has a single row with an empty frame cell. After Effects 2019 wrote a Time Remap key at layer frame 6 of a layer starting at frame 10 as frame 16, which confirms comp-frame numbering.

title: #1812: workers that render a layer at once share the cached buffer
author: ded-achtung
body:
Part of #1812; the follow-up promised in [the #1918 review](https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/pull/1918#discussion_r4322710767).

## Problem

Preview workers that start together miss the layer cache together. Each renders every layer and keeps its own buffer. On the GPU each of those buffers is then uploaded, and each Classic 3D run is packed into an atlas of its own. On the #1812 project that means up to 16 copies of the plates and of a 343 MB atlas at once. That is what still ran the GPU out of memory on a cold start after #1917, #1918 and the validation-scope fix (#1326; my duplicate #1919 is closed).

## Change

- `LayerCache::insert` keeps the **first** buffer for a key and returns the buffer it holds.
- The renderer continues with the returned buffer at the content, input, blending-space, styled and footprint insert sites.
- Workers that rendered a layer at the same time therefore end up with one shared `Arc`. The GPU upload cache and #1918's atlas cache are keyed by buffer, so they upload and pack it once.

Renders don't wait for each other. I tried a single-flight first: the first miss renders, the others block until it is done. It stalled playback. Frames and pixel loops share one rayon pool, so a blocked frame job can be sitting on a stack beneath the very pixel work it waits for, a cycle only a timeout breaks. I logged waits of 5 002–5 028 ms in 4 of 8 runs. Sharing the result instead costs some duplicate CPU work on a cold start and cannot block.

## Numbers

Windows 11, RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB), 16 threads, #1812 project from 0 s, 8 cold starts of the desktop app. The second column has #1917, #1918 (including its atlas single-flight) and the validation-scope fix of #1326 (as my closed duplicate #1919) applied, plus the #1920 fix to the prefetch window.

title: Layer: replace a layer's source with Alt-drag and Ctrl+Alt+/ (#991)
author: ki2pixel
body:
## Summary

Alt/Option-drag a Project item onto a Timeline layer, or press Ctrl+Alt+/ (Cmd+Opt+/) with the layers and Project item selected, to replace the layer's source. This is After Effects' Replace Source workflow and closes #991 (#1924 and #1707 are duplicates). It also implements the remaining `AVLayer.replaceSource` item of #813.

## What it does

- New `layer.replaceSource` engine command: swaps `source` for a composition, footage item or solid, and leaves every layer property alone — name, timing, transforms, keyframes/eases, expressions, effects, masks, switches, blending, parenting, track matte and markers.
- Precompositions bring their Essential Properties group (through `sync_project`); a source with audio adds an Audio group when the layer has none.
- Folders, data files and 3D models are refused. A composition that contains the target comp is refused (no nesting cycles). Locked layers are skipped; an all-locked selection is an error. One undo step; no layer is added.
- Timeline: Alt/Option-drag targets the layer under the pointer (one layer, as in After Effects). The shortcut replaces every selected layer.
- Scripting: `AVLayer.replaceSource(newSource, fixExpressions)` calls the command; `layer.source` returns the new item. `fixExpressions` is accepted for compatibility and is a no-op because only AV sources are replaced, so the property tree and layer name stay.
- Docs: `docs/footage.md`.

## Tests

- `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine --lib` — 666 passed
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-script --lib` — 114 passed

title: #1926: an edit no longer stamps every image-sequence frame for the disk cache
author: ded-achtung
body:
Fixes #1926 (text fields lag in compositions with large image sequences).

## Cause

`Session::bump` runs at every edit, on the UI thread. With the disk cache on, which is the default, it took `disk_cache::footage_salt(&project)` each time. That reads the size and modification time of **every footage file, each frame of every image sequence included**.

A text edit is an edit: every typed character, and every caret move through `text.edit`, bumps the revision. So in a mapping project with a few long sequences, each keystroke paid tens of thousands of `fs::metadata` calls.

## Reproduction

Windows 11, desktop app, three generated image sequences of 5 000 frames each in a 1920×1080 comp, plus a text layer. Times are per control-channel command and include the UI-thread work.

| | `main`, disk cache on | `main`, disk cache off | this PR, disk cache on |
|---|---|---|---|
| caret move (`text.edit`) | 588 ms | 9 ms | **16 ms** |
| typed character (`layer.setText`) | 601 ms | 21 ms | **28 ms** |

## Change

`Session::refresh_disk_salt` keeps the salt together with a fingerprint of the footage items: their ids and settings, hashed in memory with no file access. `bump` takes the salt again only when that fingerprint changed: an import, a relink, a reload that changed an item. It is also taken with `force` in three cases:

- a project is opened (`replace_project`): its files may have changed since they were last stamped;
- footage is reloaded (`footage_reload::forget`, both File ▸ Reload Footage and the automatic reload);
- the disk cache is attached (`configure_disk_cache`).

A file rewritten in place, with no reload, now keeps the old salt until the next reload or reopen. The media pool and the in-memory layer cache already keep its old pixels until then, so the disk cache now behaves the same way. The automatic reload (#625) still forces a new salt for the files it watches. Image sequences are watched only with Automatically Reload Footage set to All Footage; the default…

title: Return identity from Mat3::square_to_quad for a degenerate quad
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/geom/src/lib.rs:252-264` (no existing issue): Mat3::square_to_quad returns a NaN/inf matrix for a degenerate quad.

## Cause
Mat3::square_to_quad divides by `den = dx1*dy2 - dx2*dy1` to compute `g` and `h`. When three consecutive corners are collinear and the quad isn't a parallelogram, `den` is 0, so the matrix holds NaN and inf values that callers never check.

## Fix
square_to_quad now returns the identity matrix when `den` is zero or non-finite, so no NaN or inf matrix is produced. The regression test is in `crates/geom/tests/square_to_quad.rs`. It covers a collinear quad and a non-degenerate control quad.

## Verified
- Regression test `square_to_quad_degenerate_is_finite`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-geom --test square_to_quad`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The signature is unchanged (it still returns Mat3, not Option), so callers such as crates/gpu/src/fx_stylize.rs are not modified.

title: CLI: preserve template composition names when rendering
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Fixes #1937.

`render --template` builds its render composition by duplicating the template's composition, emptying the copy, and adding the original to it as a layer. That keeps the template's exact frame rate, duration, work area, renderer and motion blur settings, and lets values override the instance. But `project.duplicate` gives the copy a numbered name, and that name ends up in the output. `[compName]` outputs came out as `Title Card 2.mp4` (and `Title Card 3_00012.png` for a composition already named `Title Card 2`), and the CLI reported that name.

## Change

title: Negate temporal ease speeds in time_reverse
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/keyframe/src/lib.rs:492-503` (no existing issue): time_reverse keeps temporal ease speeds unnegated, so reversed keyframes overshoot.

## Cause
time_reverse swaps each key's in/out ease lists but keeps the speeds unchanged. Ease speed is signed units per second along the time axis, so mirroring time flips its sign. A reversed key with non-zero speed therefore had a tangent pointing the wrong way, and the curve overshot.

## Fix
After swapping the in and out ease lists, time_reverse now negates the speed of every ease entry. The reversed track now equals the original curve mirrored in time. The regression test `tests::time_reverse_negates_ease_speed` checks both the negated speeds and the mirrored curve values. Run it with `cargo test -p effectcraft-keyframe time_reverse_negates_ease_speed`. CI is run by the pipeline.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::time_reverse_negates_ease_speed`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-keyframe time_reverse_negates_ease_speed`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Influence values, interpolation types and spatial tangent handling are unchanged. Easy Ease keys have speed 0, so they behave as before.

title: #1388: 3D text and shapes rasterise only the part the frame shows
author: ded-achtung
body:
Fixes #1388 (text close to the camera freezes or crashes EffectCraft).

## Cause

A 3D text or shape layer is continuously rasterised at its on-screen scale. Close to the camera that scale is large, so the whole layer was rasterised up to the ~16 million pixel cap: about a quarter gigabyte as f32. That happened even though the frame shows only a small part of it.

The layer cache doesn't keep such buffers, so each preview worker rendered its own. Behind the camera the layer was still rasterised at the cap and then not drawn (as @marcoarnulfo noted).

With 16 workers, a single static 200 pt title close to the camera took the desktop app to 8.6–12 GB on `main`. In one of three runs the GPU compositor also retired and playback stalled. On a machine with less memory that is the reported freeze and close.

## Change

`Renderer::raster_clip` finds the part of the layer the output shows. It projects the output frame (padded by two pixels) back onto the layer's plane, with the same camera, scale and region-of-interest offset that the Classic 3D compositor draws with (`compose::visible_clip`). `text::render_in` and `shapes::render_in` then rasterise only that part:

- The window is cut from the **whole raster's pixel grid** (`raster_window`), so the buffer offset shifts by whole pixels. It is padded by 24 pixels; see the note on anti-aliasing below.
- **Nothing** is rasterised when the content is behind the camera.
- The part is snapped to **cells of a power-of-two grid** about a quarter of its size. A moving camera keeps one raster, and its cache entry, while the visible part stays within the same cells. A dolly changes the grid only at each doubling. The cells cover at most about 2.25 times what shows. The clip is used only when it leaves out at least half of the content.
- The ~16 Mpx cap in `raster_scale` now applies to the clipped area, so close text stays sharp instead of being held at the cap.
- The clip is part of the content cache keys (`clipped_key`).

title: script: comp.width and comp.height resize the frame without moving the layers (#1942)
author: Anubhav-Rai

title: Fix feather points when deleting first vertex of a closed mask path
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/keyframe/src/value.rs:79-95 (ShapePath::feather_after_remove, called from crates/engine/src/commands/mask.rs:330)` (no existing issue): Deleting the first vertex of a closed mask path misplaces its feather points.

## Cause
`ShapePath::feather_after_remove` had no branch for removing vertex 0 of a closed path. Feather points on segment 0 stayed there with their old `t`. Points on the old closing segment were moved down a segment but kept their `t`.

## Fix
Added a closed-path, `i == 0` branch. The old closing segment and segment 0 now both map to the new closing segment `segs-1`. Points from the old closing segment get `t*0.5`, and points from segment 0 get `0.5+t*0.5`. Other segments shift down by one. A regression test covers this.

## Verified

- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
Open-path behaviour, where segment-0 feather points are dropped, and removal of any vertex other than 0 are unchanged.

title: Grow the buffer to the pinned quad so Corner Pin draws outside the layer rectangle (#1938)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1938.

Corner Pin drew into an image the size of its input buffer, so any part of the destination quad outside the layer rectangle was clipped, and a quad fully outside it drew nothing.

Before warping, both paths now grow the buffer to the union of its own rectangle and the bounding box of the four pinned corners, then build the warp matrix with the new offset:

- CPU (`distort.rs`): new `Buf::grow_to`, an asymmetric version of `Buf::cover` (they share the pixel copy). Its plan, `grow_plan`, is capped at 16384 px a side like `cover_plan`.
- GPU (`fx_stylize.rs`): the same `grow_plan` result, done with `e.image` + `copy_into` the way `cover` does it on the GPU. If the device can't allocate the texture, it returns `None` and falls back to the CPU path, like the other GPU effects that grow.

The two paths use the same plan, so `gpu_effects_match_cpu` (which already has a Corner Pin case with corners outside the layer) keeps comparing equal outputs.

Test: `corner_pin_draws_outside_the_layer_rectangle` pins a 20×10 red layer to a quad at x 40-60, y 30-40, fully outside it. It checks that the output covers the quad and that the quad's centre is red. Without the fix the output stays 20×10.

title: Make Gaussian Blur and Fast Box Blur continuous at small values (#1939)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1939.

**Gaussian Blur.** Three integer-radius box passes cannot get close to a small Gaussian. Below sigma ~0.6 px (Blurriness ~1.15) every radius is 0, so nothing happens, and from there up to Blurriness 2.0 the result is one 3-tap box. When the per-axis sigma is under 3 px (Blurriness under 6), the effect now uses a sampled separable Gaussian kernel (radius 3 sigma, normalised): `raster::gaussian_blur_exact`, chosen by `raster::gaussian_is_exact`. Larger sigmas keep the three box passes, as before. Gaussian Blur (Legacy) has the same code and the same bug, so it gets the same change.

**Fast Box Blur.** The radius was rounded, so 0.5 to 1.2 gave identical output. A fractional radius now blends the two nearest integer radii (`floor` and `floor + 1`) by the fractional part. Integer radii give the same output and padding as before.

**GPU.** The GPU kernels only do integer box passes. For these cases (sigma under 3 px, fractional radius) `apply` returns `None` and the CPU kernel renders them, the same fallback path `gpu/src/lib.rs` describes for other settings a kernel cannot match. The GPU and CPU still give the same output. Glow, Drop Shadow and the other users of `box_radii` are not changed.

The Blurriness-to-sigma mapping (`sigma = blurriness / 2`) is not changed. The issue mentions calibrating it against AE, but that is a separate decision.

**Tests**
- `effects::misc::small_gaussian_blurriness_is_continuous`: Blurriness 0 / 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.6 / 2.0 / 2.4 across a hard edge all give different rows. On main, 0 = 0.9 and 1.2 = 1.6 = 2.0.
- `effects::misc::fractional_box_blur_radius_is_continuous`: radius 0 / 0.5 / 0.9 / 1.2 / 1.6 / 2.4. On main, 0.5 = 0.9 and 1.6 = 2.4.
- `effects::obsolete::gaussian_legacy_small_blurriness_blurs`: Blurriness 0.9 now softens a single pixel. On main it does nothing.
- `gpu::small_blurs_fall_back_to_the_cpu`: a full GPU frame with Gaussian 0.9 and Fast Box 1.5 matches the CPU frame.

title: Start a movie at its first frame's time, not at 0 (#1940)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1940.

An MP4 written by ffmpeg with B-frames and no edit list puts its first video frame at 0.08 s (25 fps). The pool asked the file for footage frame `i` at `native.tick_of(i)` + half a frame, counted from 0, so frames 0-2 all clamped to the file's first frame and everything after was 2 frames late. After Effects treats the first frame as footage time 0.

- `Footage` gets `first_frame_time` (serde default 0, not written when 0, so existing projects load unchanged).
- `probe_bytes` sets it for movies: the video track's smallest pts plus its edit-list offset (the same presentation time `filmcraft_isobmff::Track::sample_at_presentation_time` uses when the decoder looks up a frame), never negative. Files with an edit list that already starts at the first frame, and non-MP4/MOV containers, stay at 0.
- `Inner::locate` adds it to the media time it asks the file for.
- Reload Footage refreshes it together with the duration and native rate, so a reloaded file picks up its new first-frame time.

Only the video frame lookup changes. Audio keeps its own timing, as before.

Tests:
- `probe::tests::first_frame_time_is_where_the_first_frame_sits`: 1024 units at timescale 12800 is 0.08 s; an edit list that cancels it gives 0; a negative result is clamped to 0.
- `pool::tests::a_movie_is_read_from_its_first_frame_time`: with `first_frame_time` = 0.08 s, footage frame 0 is read at 0.08 s + half a frame, and later frames are shifted by 0.08 s.

title: Reveal in Explorer selects the file in the file manager instead of opening the browser (#1961)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1961.

`file.revealInFinder` and `layer.revealInFinder` pushed `Event::OpenUrl(file:///folder/)`. egui hands URLs to the `webbrowser` crate, which on Windows always opens a browser tab, even for `file://` URLs.

Reveal is now its own event, `Event::RevealFile(path)`, and the desktop UI shows the file in the system file manager:

- Windows: `explorer.exe /select,"<file>"`, so Explorer opens the folder with the file selected, as After Effects does;
- macOS: `open -R <file>` (Finder, file selected; before, Finder opened the folder without selecting the file);
- Linux and other systems: `xdg-open <folder>`, which opens the folder in the default file manager. The FileManager1 D-Bus `ShowItems` call suggested in the issue would also select the file, but it needs a D-Bus dependency, so I left it out of this fix.

A program that cannot start puts its error in the status bar. The child process is waited on in a background thread, so no zombie process is left behind. Explorer's exit status is not checked because Explorer exits with 1 even when it succeeds.

The folder checks stay the same: a path that is not followed, or a folder that opens as an app or bundle, is still refused. `reveal_url` is now `reveal_path` and returns the footage file itself. For an image sequence that file is the first frame, which `Footage::path` already stores. The commands now return `{"path"}` instead of `{"url"}`.

Help ▸ Reveal Logging File (`help.revealLogFile`) had the same bug: it opened the log folder's `file://` URL. It now uses `RevealFile` too, which makes `folder_url` unused, so I removed it.

Tests:
- `layer_menu::tests::layer_reveal_shows_the_source_file` (new): Layer ▸ Reveal in Finder emits `RevealFile` with the source file and no `OpenUrl`.
- `doc_path::tests::footage_on_other_computers_is_never_looked_at`: Project ▸ Reveal in Finder emits one `RevealFile` for the followed file, and Edit Original still emits its `OpenUrl`.

title: Evaluate mask feather beyond source bounds before cropping
author: yuraizmailov
body:
A mask extending beyond the layer can fade along the layer boundary because the blur convolves an
already cropped coverage buffer. Evaluate padded mask coverage, convolve, then crop to the source
canvas. Preserve the existing mask algebra and do not extend source pixels.

Temporary work buffers are bounded; large frames size tiles from the remaining work-buffer room
after feather padding, and exceptionally broad feather uses
reduced-resolution coverage. Regressions compare against an extended reference canvas and cover
Smooth/Linear profiles, inversion/expansion/modes, variable feather, preview scale and tile seams.
This renderer change is independent of the editor transform features.

Dependency: includes the small system-font coverage prerequisite (https://github.com/storytold/effectcraft/pull/1973) so the full

title: Clamp polystar point count to avoid overflow panic on huge Points
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/path/src/lib.rs:145-150` (no existing issue): polystar panics on a huge Points value (multiply overflow / capacity overflow).

## Cause
`polystar` cast `points.max(3.0).round()` to `usize` with no upper bound. A huge Points value saturated to `usize::MAX`, so `n * 2` overflowed in debug builds, and `Vec::with_capacity` could fail in release builds.

The Points value is now clamped to 3..=100000 before the cast, and NaN is treated as 3. The vertex count stays bounded and `polystar` always returns a path. title: Ease a roving span as one curve between its fixed keys
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Fixes #1935

## Cause
`retime_roving` spaced roving keys by path length alone, so they moved at constant speed. `segment_value` eased each segment using only its own two keys. The first key's out ease and the last key's in ease therefore shaped only the end segments, which left a flat speed plateau between them.

## Fix
A run of roving keys is now evaluated as one temporal ease, from the fixed start key's out side to the fixed end key's in side, over the run's total path length. Roving keys are retimed to the points where that ease reaches each key's share of the length, so speed stays continuous through them and forms a single hill. When both fixed sides are linear, the result is the same constant speed as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::roving_span_eases_as_one_speed_hill`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-keyframe --lib roving_span_eases_as_one_speed_hill`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The Graph Editor and Keyframe Velocity dialog still report roving keys' sides as linear. A run whose start key holds keeps the old per-segment behaviour. The engine test `interpolation_dialog_temporal_spatial_and_roving` has eased end keys, so its expected roving key times now follow the eased span (about 1.424 s and 2.847 s instead of 1.5 s and 3.0 s).

title: Fix panic in path::rect when both size components are NaN
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/path/src/lib.rs:136` (no existing issue): path::rect panics when both size components are NaN.

## Cause
`rect` clamps the roundness with an upper bound of `size[0].abs().min(size[1].abs()) / 2.0`. When both size components are NaN, `f64::min` returns NaN, and `f64::clamp` panics on a NaN bound.

## Fix
`rect` now checks whether the upper bound is NaN. If it is, the roundness falls back to 0 and the clamp is skipped. Any other size behaves as before.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::rect_with_nan_size_does_not_panic`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-path rect_with_nan`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
The callers in `render/src/shapes.rs` and the path commands are unchanged. NaN sizes are not rejected earlier, and `rect` still returns a path for them.

title: Fix integer overflow in sampleImage for huge sample points
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/expr/src/sample.rs:102` (no existing issue): sampleImage panics with integer overflow for a huge sample point.

`sample_image` converts pixel coordinates with `floor() as i64`, which saturates to `i64::MAX` for huge inputs like 1e300. The loop bounds `y0 + 4096` and `x0 + 4096` then overflow. That panics in dev and test builds and wraps in release.

title: Never crash: scripts that nest without brackets, or through eval, return an error
author: simeulinuxkaliaiwr
body:
## Problem

#27 made scripts that nest brackets too deeply return an error, so they no longer overflow the stack. The check only counts brackets, though. Many constructs make boa's parser recurse without any bracket, and two ways of compiling code at run time skip the check altogether. In both cases the script thread overflows its stack, and the whole process aborts: `catch_unwind` can't catch a stack overflow, so unsaved work is lost.

Each of these aborts `effectcraft-cli --empty script x.jsx` on `main`, and the app does the same from File ▸ Scripts or the Script Console:

| Script | Result on `main` |
|---|---|
| `x => ` × 20 000, then `1` | `thread 'script-1' has overflowed its stack`, SIGABRT |
| `if (1) ` × 100 000, then `1` | same |
| `1 ? ` × 100 000 … ` : 1` × 100 000 | same |
| `2 ** `, `1 \|\| `, `x = ` × 100 000 | same |
| `!` × 200 000, `typeof ` / `void ` × 100 000 | same |
| 100 000 labels, `while (0) ` × 100 000 | same |
| `eval(Array(100001).join('(') + '1' + …)` | same: `eval` never runs the check |
| `new Function(Array(100001).join('['))` | same |

Expressions are not affected. `effectcraft_expr::rewrite::check_nesting` already estimates the parser's stack use for every one of these constructs, and the same patterns in a layer expression return an error.

## Fix

- `effectcraft-expr`: the stack estimate (`too_nested_from`) now takes `Weights`: its budget and what binary operators, member accesses or calls, and comma operators cost. With `lists`, the commas of object literals and of argument and parameter lists cost nothing, because the parser reads those in a loop. Expressions keep their weights. The new `pub fn nests_deeper_than(code, weights)` runs the estimate on plain JavaScript, without the expression rewrite.
- `effectcraft-script`: `check_nesting` keeps its bracket count, with the same message, and then runs `nests_deeper_than` with weights calibrated against a release build (see the review thread for the measurements). Each construct gets…

title: Plug-in effects re-render at every frame time
author: storybored379
body:
A plug-in effect gets the layer time in `render` (`docs/plugins.md`: "Time is layer time in seconds"), but the layer cache only folds the time into its key for effects listed in `TIME_DEPENDENT` or named `ec.sim.*`. Plug-in ids can't be either, so a plug-in that animates from `time` alone, with static parameters, was rendered once and that frame was reused at every other time.

title: Keep rgb_to_hsv and rgb_to_hsl hue within 0..1
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/color/src/lib.rs:133 (rgb_to_hsv) and :96 (rgb_to_hsl)` (no existing issue): rgb_to_hsv and rgb_to_hsl return hue 1.0 for a red with a tiny blue component.

## Cause
For a red-dominant colour with a tiny blue component, `(g-b)/d` is slightly negative. Adding 6.0 (or `rem_euclid(6.0)`) rounds to exactly 6.0 in f32, so the hue came out as 6.0/6.0 = 1.0, outside the half-open range 0..1.

## Fix
The red-dominant branch of both `rgb_to_hsv` and `rgb_to_hsl` now wraps the computed hue with `rem_euclid(1.0)`. A hue that rounds to 1.0 becomes 0.0, which is the same point on the hue wheel. Regression test `tests::hue_stays_below_one_for_tiny_blue` covers both functions.

## Verified

title: Motion Tile's Output size works on adjustment layers (#1727)
author: ded-achtung
body:
Fixes #1727. Probably also covers #1991 and the adjustment-layer report in #1409 / #369.

### What was wrong
On an **adjustment layer**, Motion Tile ignored Output Width / Height. The effect kept the comp-sized buffer, and the adjustment draw (on CPU and GPU) dropped any stack result whose size was not the canvas size. So the usual "Motion Tile 200–300 % + Transform scale down" trick gave black edges, not mirrored tiles. On a regular layer this already worked, as explained in #369.

After Effects grows or crops the comp rectangle on an adjustment layer, the same as on any other layer. A Transform after Motion Tile then brings the extra tiles into view. The frames attached to #1727 (TootiFruti) and #1409 (joymantb) show this.

### Change
- `effectcraft_effects::motion_tile_frame`: one output frame, shared by the CPU effect and the GPU kernel.
  - On an adjustment layer the frame grows or crops about the comp rectangle, snapped to whole pixels.
  - At 100 % it keeps the buffer it was given, as before.
  - It also keeps the buffer if the frame would exceed 16 384 px on a side.
- `effectcraft_effects::adjustment_crop` maps the result back onto the canvas when the stack changed the frame, in both `Renderer::draw_adjustment` and the GPU `walk::draw_adjustment`. Before, the result was dropped. The GPU side uses a new `Enc::crop`, which does a texture-to-texture copy.

### Tests
- `render/tests_motion_tile.rs`:
  - The **After Effects frames from #1727**: 1920×1080, Motion Tile 910 × 340 % or 90 × 340 %, then Transform Scale 12 % at (1361, 540). The tiled band lands at x 313–1920, y 320–760, and the 90 % column at x 1257–1465, matching the AE screenshots.
  - Tiles reach past the frame (Output 300 % + Scale 50 %) on an adjustment layer and on a full-frame layer.
  - Output under 100 % crops.
- `gpu/tests_fx_stylize.rs`:
  - GPU vs CPU for adjustment and full-frame layers at 8 and 32 bpc, full and half resolution.
  - A new `effect_case` that crops on an adjustment layer.

title: Offset all selected keyframes when a value is edited on one of them (#1963)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #1963.

When several keyframes of a property are selected and the playhead sits on one of them, editing that property's value now moves every selected keyframe by the same amount. This is what After Effects does. Before, only the key under the playhead changed, so the motion path got bent instead of moved as a whole.

**What changed** (`prop.set` in `crates/engine/src/commands/prop.rs`)
- If the playhead is on a selected key and at least one other key of the same property is selected, the change (new value minus the old value at that key) is added to each of the other selected keys, per component. This happens in the same undo step as the edit.
- If the playhead is between keys, nothing changes: the edit only adds a key at the current time, as the issue asks.
- Keys that are not selected, and keys selected on other properties, are left alone.
- Moved keys stay inside the property's slider range, the same way the edited value already does. For example, Opacity never goes above 100.
- Values that can't be offset are left alone: hold-only types (bool, enum) and paths/gradients, which have no numeric components.

**Entry paths:** dragging in the viewer (position, scale, rotation, anchor) and scrubbing or typing a value in the Timeline or Properties panel all go through `prop.set`, so they all get this behaviour. Separated Position goes through the per-axis X/Y/Z properties. This covers every property the issue lists. Scripting's `setValueAtTime` and `setValueAtKey` use `prop.addKey` and `keys.set`, so they still edit only one key, as in After Effects.

title: A region of interest over an adjustment layer shows the full frame's pixels
author: ded-achtung
body:
Found while working on #2003. It is wrong on `main` too, with no Motion Tile involved.

### What was wrong
With a **Region of Interest** or the **Extended Viewer** on, the CPU canvas holds only the region. An adjustment layer's effect stack therefore saw only that part of the comp below, so the region showed pixels the full frame doesn't:
- A Transform that scales the comp down pulled in transparency where the full frame has content.
- A blur next to the region's edge blurred against transparency.
- Auto Levels measured its statistics on the region instead of the frame.

In the Extended Viewer the stack also took in layers lying past the frame, and a Transform pulled them into the frame. A render never shows them there.

Regions are CPU-only (`walk::render` declines them), so the change is in the CPU compositor only.

### Change
- `Renderer::comp_frame_cpu`: a region that does not already hold the frame, over an adjustment layer with an enabled effect, now renders the frame with the region around it and crops.
  - Inside the frame, this renders the whole frame on any backend, as 3D comps with a region already do.
  - Past the frame, the region grows just enough to hold the frame.
- `Renderer::draw_adjustment`: under a region that holds the whole frame, the stack gets the comp frame below and nothing past it, as in a render. Its result then goes back onto the canvas by offset.
- Comps without such an adjustment layer render as before. Regions keep their speed-up there.

### Tests (`render/tests_roi.rs`)
- `roi_over_an_adjustment_layer_equals_the_full_frame`: Transform (scale 50 %), Gaussian Blur, Auto Levels and Invert adjustments. Regions at the frame's corner, in its middle, and at half resolution all equal the cropped full frame.
- `extended_region_over_an_adjustment_layer`: the frame part of an Extended Viewer region equals the full frame. A solid lying past the frame shows unadjusted and is not pulled in.
- Both fail on `main` (the Transform case first).

Follow-up to storytold/cadcraft#1785: replace this repo's hand-rolled UTC/calendar

title: Fix #1708: calibrate CC Blobbylize from the AE oracle
author: ki2pixel
body:
# Fix #1708: calibrate CC Blobbylize from an AE 26.2 oracle

Replaces the matte-preserving approach of #1965 with behaviour measured from
After Effects 26.2 at 16 bpc. The oracle projects, TIFFs and analysis stay local
under `plan/aftereffects/ref/blobbylize/`; no `.aep` support or Adobe asset is
added to EffectCraft.

## Measured behaviour

- **Softness kernel:** a Cut 25/75 step contour moves by 5.55 px at Softness 20.
  For a Gaussian, `sigma = 5.55 / 0.67449 = 8.23`, i.e. `sigma = 0.42 * Softness`.
- **Cut Away:** a binary threshold of the blurred height with about 1 px of
  antialiasing, not a broad alpha ramp. Cut Away 100 is fully transparent, including the endpoint guard for opaque edges.
- **Source matte:** AE does not preserve it. A self alpha step moves inward by
  5/9/14/18 px at Softness 5/10/20/40 (`Cut Away = 0`). The patch models this
  with a `z = 1` bevel normal, a depth of `span / 64` and a slope of
  `1.5 * Softness`.
- **RGB refraction:** independent of Softness. A horizontal ramp gives
  `dx ≈ -0.34 / h`, i.e. a `z = height` normal with a `0.34 * span` scale.
- **Defaults:** Softness 20, Cut Away 25, Light Height 65, Light Position
  (0.5, 0.5), Ambient 75, Diffuse 25, Specular 100, Roughness 0.025,
  Metal 100 and Property Red, matching the plug-in manual and the AE project.

## Changes

- CPU implementation in `crates/effects/src/distort3.rs`.
- GPU parameters and `ftr_blob` kernel in `crates/gpu/src/fx_transition.rs`
  and `crates/gpu/src/shaders/fx_transition.wgsl`.
- CPU regression tests:
  - Cut Away thresholds a height ramp with a one-pixel edge;
  - Cut Away 100 leaves no opaque pixel, including an opaque edge with h = 1;
  - Softness 20 moves a self-step matte inward instead of preserving it.
- GPU/CPU parity continues to pass at full and half resolution.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p effectcraft-effects --lib`: 461 passed.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-gpu --lib`: 222 passed (NVIDIA GTX 1650, Vulkan).
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-…

title: Fix #1986 Cmd+A ("select all") doesn't work in "Import multiple files…
author: jerome25000
body:
Fixes #1986

**Cause.** On macOS the open panel has no key equivalents of its own. Cmd+A (and C/V/X/Z) work
because the menu bar sends `selectAll:`, `copy:` and so on down the responder chain to the key
window. EffectCraft's Edit items are custom muda items, so while the sheet was up Cmd+A ran
Edit > Select All on the Project panel behind it.

**Fix.** The native file dialogs on screen are counted (`native_dialogs`). While one is open on
macOS, Undo / Redo / Cut / Copy / Paste / Select All become macOS predefined items, which send
the real actions to the dialog. The other `edit.*` items are disabled. The UI is repainted when
a dialog opens so the menu is rebuilt before the next key.

**Tests.** `edit_menu_is_disabled_while_a_file_dialog_is_open`,
`edit_text_commands_are_predefined_while_a_file_dialog_is_open`. Checked by hand on macOS:
Cmd+A in "Import multiple files" selects the files.

title: Text: Chinese Han text uses the installed Chinese face (#453)
author: midasdf
body:
## What was wrong

Issue #453: Chinese text in a composition draws incorrectly. The screenshot shows a Japanese/Chinese
file name in the Project panel with a Han character as a missing-glyph box, and the report says
"Chinese in the composition displays incorrectly".

Two CJK paths exist:

- the **interface** font stack registers installed CJK fallbacks and already picks a Chinese face
  for a Simplified Chinese interface (`theme::install_script_fallbacks`, the `页` probe, #1141);
- **composition text** goes through `effectcraft_text::fonts::fallback_for`. Han ideographs are
  shared by Japanese, Chinese and Korean, so the locale decides the order (`han_order_for`), and
  the script's usual families are tried before any installed face. The Simplified Chinese list
  named only Windows and Linux families (`Microsoft YaHei`, `SimSun`, `PingFang SC`, Noto/Source
  Han/WenQuanYi).

macOS 27 on an English install does not ship `PingFang SC` (it is an on-demand font) but does ship
`Hiragino Sans GB`, `Heiti SC`, `Songti SC`, `STSong` and `Arial Unicode MS`. None were in the list,
so the fallback walked past the Simplified Chinese families to the exhaustive search, whose first
installed face covering a Han character is **Hiragino Sans** — a Japanese face. Chinese Han text in
comps therefore drew Japanese glyph forms. Chinese-only characters the Japanese face lacks (`页`,
`选`, `删`) still found a Chinese face through the exhaustive search, which is why the symptom
looked selective.

## The fix

Add the macOS Chinese faces to the fallback lists (`crates/text/src/fonts.rs`):

- Simplified Chinese: `Hiragino Sans GB`, `Heiti SC`, `Songti SC`, `STSong`, after `PingFang SC`
  so older macOS keeps PingFang first;
- Traditional Chinese: `Songti TC`, beside the existing `Heiti TC`, `Hiragino Sans CNS` and
  `PingFang TC`.

The language rule is unchanged: the interface language (`general.language`) or
`EFFECTCRAFT_CJK_LOCALE`/`LANG` chooses the script, and an English interface keeps the
…

title: Fractal Noise: resolve the Blending Mode once per layer, not per pixel
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
## Why

On the CPU, Fractal Noise and Turbulent Noise resolved their Blending Mode **for every pixel**: an index lookup, then a string match through `BlendMode::from_name`. The GPU path already resolved it once per layer.

## What

`crates/effects/src/noise3.rs` only:

- a `blend_mode(u32) -> Option<BlendMode>` helper, which the CPU and GPU paths now share;
- the CPU `render` resolves the mode once and passes `Option<BlendMode>` to the per-pixel `composite`.

The semantics are unchanged: None means the noise alone, and an unknown index means Normal.

## How much better

`render-frame` on the CPU, 1080p, one solid with Fractal Noise in Overlay, 3 alternating runs per build:

| machine | main | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|
| Apple Silicon Mac | 1,467.7 ms | 109.3 ms | **−92% (13× faster)** |
| Intel i5-8350U (Linux) | 1,380.0 ms | 382.0 ms | **−72% (3.6× faster)** |

The output MD5 matched main on both machines.

Limits: one scene and one frame. The gain depends on the mode and the scene. Modes that do little per-pixel work gain the most.

## Testing

- New `resolved_blend_matches_per_pixel_lookup`: every Blending Mode, plus out-of-range indices, gives bit-identical results to the old per-pixel lookup.

title: Save: check the file's values without reparsing it in release builds
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
## Why

Every save serialised the project, then **parsed the whole file back** to make sure it would reopen. The check exists to refuse values JSON can't hold: NaN or infinity (written as `null`) and nesting deeper than serde_json's 128-level limit. On a 400-layer project, that reparse is about a third of the save time.

## What

- New `crates/project/src/file_check.rs`: a no-output `Serializer` that walks the value once. It refuses non-finite numbers and nesting past 127 levels, and it allocates only on error.
- `to_file_json_with_view` runs that check, then writes the file. It also refuses a project schema newer than this build, the remaining thing `from_json` would reject in a file we wrote.
- **Debug builds still reparse the text as well**, so a new kind of mismatch still shows up in tests.

The bytes written are unchanged.

## How much better

400-layer project, Mac, 5 alternating rounds:

| | median per save |
|---|---|
| main | 55.5 ms |
| this PR | 36.4 ms (**−34%**) |

The saved files are byte-identical to main's (`cmp`). This also applies to autosave.

Limits: measured on the Mac only.

## Testing

- Infinity is now refused in either profile, newer schemas are refused (`project_files_refuse_newer_schemas`), and saved files reopen in both the pretty and compact forms.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-project`, plus the save/check tests in `--release`. `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-project --all-targets -D warnings`, `rustfmt --check`.
