title: Close, New and Open Project free the closed project's memory
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
## Why

Close Project, New Project and Open kept the closed project's decoded footage, its decoders and the viewers' RAM preview. On a Mac, after playing a 1080p comp and closing the project, the app still held about 3.4–4.0 GB for a project that was no longer open.

## What

`Session::replace_project` (`crates/engine/src/lib.rs`), shared by Close, New, Open and the demo project:

- forgets the decoded frames and decoders of the closed project's footage, as well as the new project's (the existing #1070 behaviour);
- emits `Event::PurgeCaches` after the swap, so the viewers drop the RAM preview of the closed project. Its comp ids can also collide with the new project's.

Cache budgets and LRU order are unchanged; only the release path changes.

## How much better

macOS physical footprint after closing the project, 3 runs per build in each of 2 sessions:

| | after Close |
|---|---|
| main | 3,407–3,957 MB |
| this PR | 1,200–1,527 MB |

That is roughly **60% less memory** held once the project is closed.

Limits: macOS only. The variance between sessions wasn't diagnosed, and per-pool counts weren't captured.

## Testing

- New `replacing_project_releases_old_footage`: Close, Open and New each forget the old project's footage and emit `PurgeCaches`.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine --lib tests_menu_cmds`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-engine --all-targets -D warnings`, `rustfmt --check`.

title: Preview: a zoom or resolution change evicts the other sizes' frames first
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
## Why

Change the viewer's zoom or resolution, then come back to it, and the RAM cache (full by then) evicted by plain least-recently-shown order. That **threw out the frames of the size you're looking at** and kept those of the size you just left, so the preview re-rendered frames it already had.

## What

`crates/ui-egui/src/frames.rs`:

- The cache remembers the scale of the frame on screen (the active viewer's urgent request). Prefetch and passive viewers don't change it, so a second viewer at another zoom can't evict the active viewer's frames.
- RAM and GPU eviction take frames of other scales first, then fall back to the existing playhead-aware order.

## How much better

1 GiB cache on a Mac, filled at Full, then at Half, then back to Full, 3 alternating pairs:

| renders on the first Full pass after the Half fill | |
|---|---|
| main | 256 |
| this PR | 29 (**−89%**) |

Second passes rendered nothing on either build. Peak RSS was the same (1,509 vs 1,513 MiB); this makes the cache keep the right frames, it doesn't use less memory.

Limits: GPU-frame eviction wasn't measured separately. The pass-only-on-urgent refinement came after that measurement; it changes nothing for a single viewer, and the new test covers a passive viewer.

## Testing

- New `a_size_change_evicts_frames_of_other_sizes_first`: frames of the old size go first, a passive viewer's request doesn't change the kept size, then the order is plain LRU again.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --lib frames::`, `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -D warnings`, `rustfmt --check`.

title: Fast Previews: Adaptive Resolution applies while dragging in the Timeline
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
## Why

Fast Previews ▸ Adaptive Resolution lowers the viewer's resolution while you drag in the viewer or scrub a property, but **not while you drag in the Timeline**. Dragging the playhead, a layer bar or keyframes rendered every frame at full resolution, so scrubbing a heavy comp lagged. title: Timeline: the disk-cache bar checks only the visible frames
author: arnav-hiwarkar
body:
## Why

When a disk cache is on, the Timeline's blue disk-cache bar computed a disk key and checked membership for **every frame of the comp** on every repaint, even when only a few hundred frames are on screen. On a long comp, that is the largest share of the app's idle CPU.

## What

- `Frames::disk_frames` takes a frame range instead of a frame count, still clamped to the existing 100,000-frame limit.
- The Timeline passes the visible range (`disk_bar_range`), including frames only partly in view, and clips the blue bar to the work-area row.
- Membership stays live: nothing is cached, so the bar updates as before when frames are written, evicted or promoted to RAM.

## How much better

Apple M5, a 100,000-frame 30 fps comp zoomed to about 241 frames, three alternating 30-second samples:

| | mean process CPU |
|---|---|
| main | 0.99% |
| this PR | 0.45% (**−55%**) |

`disk_frames`' share of the CPU samples fell from 55.1% to 2.2%. The screenshots matched.

Limits: one machine and one zoom. The saving scales with comp length divided by visible frames, and is about zero when fitted to the comp.

## Testing

- New `disk_indicator_range_tracks_live_membership`, `disk_indicator_range_is_bounded` (probe counts, edge clamping) and `disk_bar_range_covers_partial_frames` (NaN, zero zoom, beyond the comp).

title: Light Settings: expose and preserve Environment lights
author: tylerjenningsw
body:
Fixes #1588.

## Problem
Layer ▸ New ▸ Light offered Parallel, Spot, Point and Ambient, but not Environment, although `layer.newLight` and `layer.lightSettings` already accept Environment lights. The dialog's light types were a hard-coded four-entry list, and the dialog stored the chosen type as an index into that list. title: Decode QuickTime Animation MOV frames, including 32-bit alpha
author: Batkixni
body:
## Summary

- QuickTime Animation (`rle `) MOV files now import and play. This is the codec After Effects uses for a transparent layer ("Millions of Colors+"): 32-bit frames keep their alpha.
- 16-bit (RGB555) and 24-bit (opaque RGB) Animation are read too. Paletted 1/2/4/8-bit is refused with an error instead of being guessed.
- A frame may update only some lines. Pixels it does not write stay from the previous frame, which is how this codec stores the parts that did not move.

FilmCraft's MOV reader does not recognise `rle `, so these files were rejected before a frame could be decoded. The reader lives in `effectcraft-media` and is used only when the video sample description is Animation.

The layout follows Apple's QuickTime File Format Specification (sample-description depth 32 means an alpha channel, stored as 8-bit alpha then RGB) and the published Animation chunk layout: a size, a header, then per-line skip and run-length codes.

## Test

`cargo test -p effectcraft-media --lib qt_anim`

A synthetic 32-bit movie checks a transparent pixel, an opaque pixel, and a second frame that repaints one line and leaves the other line alone.

title: security: enforce HTTPS on curl downloads (SonarCloud S6506)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Enforces HTTPS on `curl` downloads flagged by SonarCloud rule **S6506** (`shell:S6506`, `docker:S6506`, `githubactions:S6506`, Security).

These `curl` calls use `-L`/`-fsSL` (follow redirects). A redirect could transparently downgrade to plaintext HTTP, exposing the download to MITM tampering. Adding `--proto '=https'` forces curl to refuse any non-HTTPS protocol, including across redirects, without changing behavior for the legitimate HTTPS endpoints already in use.

## Change
`curl <args>` → `curl --proto '=https' <args>` on each flagged line.

title: security: use crypto.randomUUID for temp file suffix (SonarCloud S2245)
author: dylanmtaylor
body:
## Summary
Resolves SonarCloud **javascript:S2245** in `apps/effectcraft-web/js/host.js`.

The `cacheWrite` helper built a temp filename suffix with `Math.random().toString(36)`. The value is only a uniqueness token for an atomic write-then-move (not a key/token/nonce), so this was not a real vulnerability — but `crypto.randomUUID()` is a trivial, zero-downside replacement that gives a stronger collision-resistance guarantee and clears the finding.

```diff
- const tmp = canMove ? `${name}.tmp.${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)}` : name;
+ const tmp = canMove ? `${name}.tmp.${crypto.randomUUID()}` : name;
```
`crypto.randomUUID()` is available in all modern browsers and Web Workers (secure contexts).

🤖 Generated to address SonarCloud findings.

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

* **Bug Fixes**

Lets a same-origin page embed EffectCraft in an `<iframe>` and own its files, as WordCraft's and GridCraft's bridges do.

title: Text: add stroke Line Join (Miter / Round / Bevel)
author: HarpeLm
body:
Fixes #2077

Related: #2075 (stroke width control), #2076 (stroke order).

## What was wrong

Text strokes were always drawn with round joins: `Join::Round` was hard-coded in the 2D text renderer (`crates/render/src/text.rs`) and in the extruded 3D text path (`crates/render/src/three_d/adv/scene.rs`). Thick outlines therefore always had rounded corners, with no way to get sharp (miter) or cut (bevel) corners. The path renderer already supported all three joins (shape layers use them).

## What changes

- **Model** (`crates/keyframe`): a new `LineJoin { Miter, Round, Bevel }` and a `line_join` field on `TextDoc`, saved with the project.
  - New text defaults to **Miter**, as in the reference app.
  - Documents saved before this change have no `line_join` and load as **Round** (`#[serde(default = "round_join")]`), so existing projects render exactly as before.
- **Commands / scripting**: `layer.setText` and `layer.newText` accept `lineJoin: "miter" | "round" | "bevel"` (case-insensitive, `"bevel join"` etc. also accepted). Any other value returns an error and leaves the join unchanged. Command help strings list the new key.
- **Rendering**: `PlacedGlyph` carries the document's join, and both stroke sites (2D raster pass and 3D extrusion) use it instead of `Join::Round`. Stroke buffers are padded by `PlacedGlyph::stroke_reach()` (2 stroke widths for Miter, whose tips reach `miter / 2` widths with the default limit of 4; 1 width otherwise, as before), so Miter tips are not clipped.
- **Expressions**: when a Source Text expression restyles text, the line join is carried over alongside Stroke Over Fill.
- **UI**: a "Join" row with three toggle buttons (Miter / Round / Bevel) in both the **Character** panel and the **Properties** panel's Text section, with automation ids `character.lineJoin.<join>` and `properties.text.lineJoin.<join>`.
- **Credits**: adds my own entry to `contributors/people.toml`.

The join is a document-level attribute (like Stroke Over Fill), as the is…

**Point editing**
- Clicking a path picks the **nearest** point or tangent handle instead of the last one drawn, so overlapping points and tangents no longer steal each other's clicks. Selected and hovered points are distinctly marked.
- Double-clicking a shape or path enters point editing without a transform box or free-transform box; `Enter`/`Escape` or a click away restores the layer box.
- Parametric shapes (Rectangle, Ellipse, Polystar) convert to a Bezier Path first, at the current time.
- The Pen hides the layer box while a path is being drawn and shows it again when the path closes.

**Pick whips**
- A pick whip pulled on a selected layer applies to the whole selection: parenting whips parent every selected layer, and property whips link the same property on each selected layer in one undo step.

**Selection/transform fixes**
- Dragging a null no longer snaps to its own descendants.
- A selected child of a selected parent is no longer moved twice.

## Rebase note

The branch was 161 commits behind `main`. Conflicts were resolved in favour of upstream where `main` had since implemented the same area more thoroughly:

- `crates/engine/src/commands/paths.rs` — kept `main`'s `convert_to_bezier` (#932), which builds the path from the renderer's own geometry and preserves direction, enabled state and selection. Only the command's parameter documentation from this branch was kept.

title: fix: bound Classic 3D depth-of-field blur and reject non-finite focus distances (#2092)
author: ChristopherLinnett
body:
Fixes #2092. Part of #1988.

## What crashed

**Layer ▸ Camera ▸ Set Focus Distance to Layer** can abort EffectCraft. I reproduced it headless on
`main` (`f37f20ff`) with the issue's own steps: 3D layers, then a camera with depth of field on
(that frame renders fine), then the command. The scene also had one ordinary ingredient, a 3D
layer at 0% scale, as on the first frame of a scale-in. The process dies with a SIGABRT that no
panic guard can catch:

```
memory allocation of 51847406582463232 bytes failed
  effectcraft_raster::Image::new(width=56925076, height=56925052)
  effectcraft_raster::Image::padded(pad=28462502)
  effectcraft_render::three_d::compose::dof_blur
  effectcraft_render::three_d::compose::prepare_with ← prepare ← prepare_all
```

**Cause.** The Classic 3D blur radius is the circle of confusion divided by the on-screen size of
one layer pixel. For a 0%-scaled layer that size is about 0 (the code clamps it to 1e-9). An
ordinary 10–300 px defocus then becomes a radius of about 1e9 buffer pixels, and the padded blur
buffer sized from it is tens to hundreds of petabytes. A huge but finite Focus Distance does the
same to any layer: typed in, set from a far-away target layer, or a large expression result.

Before the command, Focus Distance equals the zoom, so layers at z = 0 are exactly in focus and
nothing blurs. That fits the video, where "enabling depth of field also seems to work". The same
code is in v0.11.1, the build in the video. There is no crash log for the video, so this is a
mechanism that is consistent with it and reproduced on `main`. It is not a confirmed match.

**Separately**, the command could store a Focus Distance that isn't finite. Extreme but finite
positions (camera z = −1e308, target z = 1e308) overflow the depth to +inf, and the old
`d <= 0.0` guard lets NaN and +inf through. JSON has no infinity, so `file.saveAs` then refused the
project: "the project can't be saved: it holds a value a project file can't store".

title: Physical Glow: energy-conserving power-law glow on CPU and GPU (#1845)
author: onlykshitij
body:
Addresses #1845: a native glow effect for professional work, as asked there as an alternative to After Effects plug-in support. This PR does not add plug-in support, so the issue stays open for that half.

## Physical Glow (`ec.stylize.physicalglow`, Stylize)

An energy-conserving glow whose radial falloff follows a power law, inverse square by default. It is a sum of Gaussians whose widths double per octave. With octave weights proportional to σ^(2−α), the sum approximates a point-spread function I(r) ∝ r^−α, and the weights are normalised so the glow carries the bright pass's energy before exposure.

| Control | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Radius | 100 | σ of the widest octave is Radius / 2; up to 12 octaves down to σ = 0.5 px |
| Exposure | 0 | Glow gain in stops |
| Falloff | 2 | Power-law exponent α (2 = inverse square) |
| Threshold, Threshold Softness | 0, 50 % | Brightness (max of premultiplied RGB) below which pixels don't glow, with a smoothstep knee |
| Aspect Ratio | 1 | Stretches the glow horizontally (>1) or vertically (<1), keeping its area |
| Dispersion | 0 | Per-channel α: positive spreads red farther than blue |
| Tint, Tint Amount | white, 0 % | Multiplies the glow by a colour |
| Composite | Add | Add, Screen or Glow Only |
| Fast Mode | off | Computes wide octaves on a downsampled pyramid (below) |
| Render Method | GPU | GPU, or CPU to keep this effect on the CPU in a GPU project |

## Implementation

- **CPU reference** in `crates/effects/src/misc.rs`. `physical_glow_plan` computes the padding, octave sigmas and weights once, and the CPU and GPU paths share it.
- **GPU** in `crates/gpu/src/fx_stylize.rs` with kernels in `shaders/fx_stylize.wgsl`. The kernels use core WGSL only (no `enable` extensions, subgroup operations or f16) at the module's existing 16×16 workgroup size, so nothing is vendor-specific. The full-quality path reuses the existing `gaussian_blur` (3 box passes, identical on CPU and GPU).

title: Return None from Mat4::inverse for non-finite input
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/geom/src/lib.rs:362-390 (pivot check at line 367)` (no existing issue): Mat4::inverse returns Some(NaN matrix) for non-finite input instead of None.

## Cause
Mat4::inverse only rejected pivots with `abs() < 1e-300`. That comparison is false for NaN, so a matrix with NaN went through elimination and came back as `Some` with a NaN-filled matrix.

## Fix
Mat4::inverse now returns None up front if any input entry is not finite (NaN or infinity). A regression test covers NaN at a pivot position, NaN at a non-pivot position, and an infinite entry.

## Verified
- Regression test `tests::mat4_inverse_rejects_non_finite`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-geom mat4_inverse_rejects_non_finite`).
- `cargo xtask ci` passes.

## Not changed
I did not add a finiteness check on the output. A finite matrix whose inversion overflows could still produce non-finite values. I also did not change Mat3::inverse.

title: model: cap glTF buffer-less accessors per file, check element offsets (#2139)
author: Barzabel
body:
## Summary

Closes #2139.

The trigger from the issue (`{"count": 100000000000, "type": "MAT4"}`) is already refused on `main` since #1235: `Doc::layout()` checks every accessor's span against its buffer before allocating. This PR closes the gap that was left and pins the trigger with a test.

- **Buffer-less accessors share one budget per file.** An accessor without a `bufferView` is all zeros, so its count is capped at `MAX_ZERO_COMPONENTS` (16M) instead of being checked against a buffer. That cap applied per read. One capped accessor referenced from N primitives (about 40 bytes of JSON per reference) allocated about 64 MB N times. The cap is now one budget for the whole file. Going over it returns the crate's usual malformed-file error.
- **Checked offsets when reading elements.** `floats()` and `ints()` now read each component through a helper with checked offset math (`i*stride + base + c*csize`), and the element size `csize * n` is checked too. The span was already validated, so this is extra safety rather than a reachable bug.

Real exporters only emit buffer-less accessors as sparse bases, which this importer ignores, so realistic models never come near the shared budget.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p effectcraft-model`: 31 passed.
- New `gltf_buffer_less_accessors_share_one_zero_budget` (four primitives sharing one 15M-component buffer-less accessor must be refused, a single reference still imports) fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- New `gltf_issue_2139_huge_mat4_count_is_an_error` pins the issue's exact trigger, with and without a `bufferView`, read through a skin's `inverseBindMatrices`.
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-model --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `rustfmt --check` are clean.

title: svg: share CSS declaration blocks and cap <style> work (#2140)
author: Barzabel
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2140.

`parse_css` gave every selector of a comma list its own clone of the declaration block, and `declared()` checked every element against every rule. Less than 1 MB of `a,a,…{…}` stored selectors × declarations strings (about 5e9 for the issue's example) and did elements × rules × declarations work.

- **Shared blocks.** A rule now refers to its declaration block by index, so the selectors of a comma list share one stored block.
- **Rule index.** Rules are bucketed by id, else first class, else type, else universal. An element only checks the buckets it can match, and the full selector test still runs on each candidate. Element classes are deduplicated so no rule is checked twice.
- **Caps.** Across all `<style>` sheets: at most 20 000 selectors and 50 000 declarations. Matching work (rules checked plus declarations applied, `<use>` copies included) is capped at 50 000 000 steps and charged before the work is done. Past a cap the import returns an error, like the existing `<use>` expansion budget, instead of a silently partial or unstyled drawing.
- **Cascade unchanged.** Presentation attributes, then matching rules by (specificity, source order), then the `style` attribute. Specificity now uses saturating arithmetic.

Behaviour change: a style sheet past the caps (for example a generated map with tens of thousands of classes) now fails to import instead of importing slowly. Exports from Illustrator, Inkscape and Figma stay far below them.

title: media: cap image decoding with image::Limits (#2130)
author: Barzabel
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2130.

- **Stills (`probe::load_oriented`).** It called `into_decoder()` and then `DynamicImage::from_decoder()`. Unlike `ImageReader::decode()`, that path never reserves the output buffer against `image::Limits`, so a tiny PNG/BMP/TGA/HDR header claiming a huge picture got its whole buffer allocated first. It now sets limits on the reader, reserves `total_bytes()` and hands the decoder the rest, in the same order `decode()` uses. This covers footage stills (`pool.rs`) and PSD smart objects (`layered.rs`).
- **GIF (`gif_anim::Anim::load`).** `GifDecoder::new` ran with `Limits::no_limits()`, and every frame allocated a full canvas before the existing cumulative `MAX_BYTES` check. A canvas whose RGBA size is over the decode budget is now refused before any frame is decoded, as `webp_anim::load` already does, and the decoder gets the limits for its own buffers.

Budgets, with no new byte constants:
- Every picture: no side over 30 000 px, the largest comp side.
- Stills: at most `gif_anim::MAX_BYTES`, the memory one animation may already hold: 1 GiB on desktop, 256 MiB on wasm. Large legitimate stills, such as a 16-bit 100 MP TIFF (about 610 MB), still open.
- GIF canvases: at most `image`'s default 512 MiB.

Behaviour change: stills with a side over 30 000 px, or that decode to more than 1 GiB (for example a 100 MP RGBA32F EXR), are now refused with a limits error instead of being allocated. On wasm the limit is 256 MiB.

Follow-up, not in this PR: `dynamic_to_image` still widens a decoded still to f32 RGBA. A single fallible `Image::try_new` in `crates/raster` would bound that (F-16/F-21).

## Verification

title: expr: bound runtime parser and native recursion depth (#2124, #2125)
author: Barzabel
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2124. Fixes #2125.

Both issues are stack overflows. They abort the process: `catch_unwind` can't catch them, so the app dies when the project renders. On the web, the auto-restored session dies again on every reload.

**#2124: runtime-built source skipped the nesting guard.** `rewrite::check_nesting` only sees the expression text. Source built at run time and passed to `eval`, `Function` or the hidden constructors (`(function(){}).constructor`, generator, async, async generator) was parsed with no limit. The prelude now wraps `eval` and the four constructors. Each wrapper runs a native nesting check (`check_plain_nesting`, the existing token check without the array-maths rewrite) on the parameters and the body first. The wrappers keep `Function.prototype` and `.constructor`, so `instanceof Function` and `(function(){}).constructor === Function` still hold.

**#2125: native recursion on deeply nested values.** Some of boa's built-ins recurse once per level of a nested value with no limit and no script frame in between, so boa's recursion limit doesn't count them:
- `Array.prototype.join`, which `toString`, `String(a)`, `a + ''` and template strings all use;
- `toLocaleString`;
- `JSON.stringify`;
- `flat`;
- lookups through Proxy chains.

The fixes:
- **Stack budget.** A native `__stack()` throws `RangeError: value is nested too deeply` once the current evaluation has used more than 256 KiB of stack, measured from where `run` started. No counter is kept, so nothing can leak past an exception and scripts can't reset it.
- **Guarded built-ins.** `join` and `toLocaleString` call it once per level. `JSON.stringify` calls it once per value, through an internal replacer that still applies a user replacer function or key list. `flat` caps its depth at 64.
- **No Proxy chains.** `Proxy` and `Reflect` are removed from the expression globals. The object model keeps private references and always proxies a fresh target, so no chain can be built.
- **`detach`.…

title: Make the audio preview follow mute changes made during playback (#2104)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2104.

**Cause:** `AudioPlayback` mixes the sound from the `RenderSource` it gets when playback starts, and that source holds an `Arc<Project>` snapshot. Edits made while the preview plays (such as toggling a layer's Audio switch) replace `session.project`, but the feeder kept mixing from the old snapshot, so muting or unmuting had no effect until playback was stopped.

**Fix:**
- The feeder's project, cursor and a generation counter now live in a shared `Feeder` state behind a mutex (used by the feeder thread, and by `pump` on wasm32).
- `AudioPlayback::set_project` swaps in the new project, drops the audio still queued (it was mixed from the old project) and resumes mixing at the first sample the device has not played yet. It also clears the "finished" flag, so an edit near the end of a non-looping span does not end the preview early.
- A block that was being mixed from the old project when the edit came in is dropped (generation check). The mix itself runs without holding the lock, so an edit never waits for a slow mix.
- Every UI frame during playback, `lib.rs` compares the playback's project with `session.project` and calls `set_project` when they differ. Moving the current time does not touch the project (times are in session state), so this runs only on real edits: mute, unmute, solo, Audio Levels and so on.

**Test:** `muting_a_layer_while_playing_silences_the_preview` starts a preview of a comp with one constant-tone audio layer, waits for sound, turns the layer's Audio switch off, calls `set_project`, and checks that everything queued after that is silent. It fails without the fix.

title: Fix u32 overflows in PDF CID width tables and CMap ranges (#2147)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Part of #2147.

The issue lists three problems. This PR fixes the PDF font one and the overflows of the same kind next to it in `crates/pdf/src/font.rs`:

- **`/W` and `/W2` (CID widths and vertical metrics).** A first CID of `u32::MAX` (larger numbers saturate to it) overflowed `first + k` in the list form `c [w1 w2 ...]` and `first + 65535` in the range form `cfirst clast w`. Debug builds panicked. Release builds put the list's later widths on CID 0, 1, ... and dropped the range. The list form now uses `checked_add` and skips entries past `u32::MAX`. The range form uses `saturating_add`.
- **ToUnicode `bfrange` with an array** (`<lo> <hi> [<dst1> <dst2> ...]`) overflowed `lo + k` the same way when `lo` was `0xFFFFFFFF`. It now uses `checked_add`.
- **Encoding CMap `cidrange` lookup.** `c + (code - lo)` overflowed when the range mapped onto CIDs near `u32::MAX`. It now uses `checked_add`. An overflowing code goes to CID 0, which is what an unmapped code already gets.

Not in this PR:

- **`sampleImage` overflow** (`crates/expr/src/sample.rs`): already fixed on main by 28f97be7, which uses `saturating_add(4096)`.
- **FilmCraft `file_url_to_path` char-boundary panic**: this code lives in FilmCraft, not in this repo, so the fix belongs there.

Tests (`crates/pdf/src/tests.rs`):

- `cid_width_entries_at_the_top_of_the_cid_range_do_not_overflow` loads a Type0 font for each of the four `/W` and `/W2` forms starting at CID 4294967295. It checks that the value lands on `u32::MAX` and that nothing wraps round to CID 0.
- `cmap_entries_at_the_top_of_the_code_range_do_not_overflow` covers the `bfrange` array and the `cidrange` lookup.

Without the fix, both tests panic in debug builds. In release builds (`cargo xtask ci` runs tests with `--release`) they fail on the wrapped or missing values.

title: control: require a per-launch token on the control channel (#2122)
author: Barzabel
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2122.

With `--control` or `EFFECTCRAFT_CONTROL_PORT`, the app listens on `127.0.0.1:<port>` and runs whatever any local process sends. That includes `prefs.set` on `scripting.*` followed by `script.run` with File and Socket access, so any local client could run code as the user: other users on a shared machine, containers or WSL sharing the network namespace, sandboxed processes. The channel now requires a per-launch token, mirroring PhotoCraft's handshake.

- **Token.** 32 bytes from the OS RNG (`getrandom`), stored as 64 hex characters in `control-<port>.token` in the settings folder (`effectcraft_host::config_dir()`; `EFFECTCRAFT_CONTROL_TOKEN_FILE` overrides the path). The token is never printed or logged; only the file path is logged.
  - The file is written after the port is bound and before the accept thread starts, so there is no window without a token. A second instance that fails to bind leaves the first instance's file alone.
  - The previous launch's file is replaced with `create_new`, which does not follow a planted symlink. On Unix the file is created `0600`, and clients refuse a file that group or others can read.
  - On Windows the folder's default user-only ACL is relied on, as documented.
- **Fail-closed.** If the token can't be created or written (no config dir, unwritable dir, RNG failure), the control server does not start rather than running unauthenticated.
- **Handshake.** The first request must be `{"id":"auth","method":"auth","params":{"token":"…"}}`.
  - Anything else gets `authentication required` and the connection is closed. Lines pipelined after a refused request are never dispatched.
  - The comparison runs in constant time over the 64 bytes.
  - A repeated `auth` is answered locally and never reaches the app.
  - The existing rejection of non-JSON and HTTP first lines (browser cross-origin `fetch`) still runs first.
- **Pre-auth deadline.** A connection must authenticate within 10 s of being accepted, or it is clo…

title: expr: an expression cannot rebind a prelude name for the next one (#2133)
author: Anubhav-Rai
body:
Fixes #2133.

## The leak

One runtime serves every expression on a thread (`runtime.rs`) and user code runs as a script at
global scope, so a write at the top of one expression rebinds the name for every expression after
it — including those of another project opened later in the same session. Reproduced on the shipped
v0.15.0 macOS build, four layers in one comp:

| layer | expression | expected | v0.15.0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | `linear = function () { return 777 }; 50` | 50 | 50 |
| b | `linear(time, 0, 1, 0, 100)` | 0 | **777** |
| c | `var clamp = 5; 10` | 10 | 10 |
| d | `clamp(50, 0, 100)` | 50 | **100** — the expression failed, so opacity fell back to its static value |

The existing `try{…}` wrapper in `Runtime::script` keeps `let` and `const` to one evaluation, but
`var` and a bare assignment both land on the global object, which a block cannot contain.

## The fix

The prelude now takes its own function bindings non-writable, and freezes the standard namespaces
and prototypes so that `Math.sin = …` cannot persist either. A write is then a silent no-op in
sloppy mode, and `var` leaves an existing global property alone, so an expression that shadows a
built-in name still evaluates — it just no longer changes anyone else's.

Two details that decided the shape:

- A script's own function declarations land on the global **non-configurable but writable**, and
  `writable: false` is the one change the spec still allows on such a property. My first attempt
  skipped non-configurable properties and therefore skipped all 104 prelude names; the new test
  caught it. The configurable built-ins are closed off completely so a redefinition cannot reopen
  them.
- Names the user introduces are untouched, so `functions_and_let_are_reusable_across_evaluations`
  still holds. That test is also why I did not take the "fresh realm per evaluation" option from the
  issue: the engine deliberately lets a re-run see its own declarations.

The `__global` names keep their setters…

title: engine: deleting a layer clears the references to it (#2153)
author: Anubhav-Rai
body:
Fixes #2153.

## The gap

Nothing cleared a `Value::Layer` reference when its layer was deleted, so the property kept the dead
id. `env_pixels` resolves it with `ctx.comp.layer(id)?` and yields no environment at all — not even
the Environment-Layer fallback — while the UI reads "None", which `build.rs` documents as "none =
the comp's Environment Layer". So deleting an HDRI layer gives a light that looks like it fell back
and renders nothing.

## The fix

The delete path already unparents the children of deleted layers and drops a `track_matte` that
pointed at one. A layer reference now goes the same way, inside the same `s.edit("Clear", …)`, so
undo restores the layer and the reference together — the issue asked for one history step, and the
test covers it.

Two things worth noting for review:

- **This is not only the Environment light.** There are 73 `ParamUi::Layer` properties across ten
  files — Clone Source, Set Matte, Gradient Layer, Back Layer, Water Surface, Sky, Ground — and all
  of them kept a dead id. One fix in the delete path covers every one.
- Keyframes carry the same value kind as the property, so they are fixed too, matching the existing
  idiom in `essential.rs`.

The issue notes that After Effects' behaviour on source-layer removal is **unverified**. I have not
observed AE, so I took the option the issue lists first — clear the reference, so that "None"
honestly means the documented fallback — rather than inventing a "missing layer" UI state. If you
would rather the UI told the truth about a dangling id, say so and I will swap the approach.

I have left out the `prop.set` validation that @ChristopherLinnett raises in the comments: accepting
a layer id that names no layer is a separate command's input check, so it wants its own commit. Glad
to file and fix it next.

title: Draw a line to the end point of degenerate SVG arcs
author: Silvertree2010
body:
Found while testing `crates/svg/src/pathdata.rs:228-233` (no existing issue): SVG path arc with a very large radius is dropped, so the path skips the arc's end point.

## Cause
With a huge radius next to the chord, `kurbo::Arc::from_svg_arc` returns `Some` with a zero sweep, so `to_cubic_beziers` emits no segments. The parser only fell back to `line_to` when `from_svg_arc` returned `None`, and it still set the current point to the arc's end. The path never went to the end point.

## Fix
The `A`/`a` branch now records where the last cubic segment ended. If no segment was emitted, or the last one ends away from the arc's end point, it adds `line_to(e)`. A regression test covers the small-arc, large-arc and relative forms.

## Verified
- Regression test `pathdata::tests::huge_radius_arc_still_reaches_end_point`: fails on `main` without the fix and passes with it (`cargo test -p effectcraft-svg --lib huge_radius_arc_still_reaches_end_point`).

title: Reload a numbered still as its own file (#2074)
author: HEOJUNFO
body:
Fixes #2074.

## What and why

Reload Footage probed every item with `Session::probe_footage`, which goes through `sequence::probe_path` with `SequenceOptions::default()` (`sequence: true`). For a still whose name ends in a number, `group()` finds its neighbours as a run, and `sequence::probe` reads the run's first file. So `Photo_2.jpg` imported as a still, with `Photo_1.jpg` beside it, came back from Reload Footage with `Photo_1.jpg`'s width and height. `refreshed()` keeps the item a still but copies the probed size. Automatic reload (`apply_stamps`) goes through the same `reload()` and had the same problem.

- `reload()` now probes a `Sequence` item the way it imports, so the run is found again. Every other item is probed as its one file with `importer.probe(&f.path)`.

This doesn't touch Replace Footage (#2073), which #2107 is fixing in `file_more.rs`.

## How it was tested

- New test `tests_sequence::reloading_a_numbered_still_measures_its_own_file`: import `shot_0002.png` with `sequence: false`, rewrite it at a new size, reload. The `Stills` test importer now reports a width of 64 + the file's byte length, so files can differ in size. Existing tests write empty files and still see 64 × 32. On `main` the test fails with width `64` (the size of `shot_0001.png`) instead of `80`.
- `replace_footage_and_reload_keep_sequences` still passes: a sequence still picks up a new frame on reload.
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine --lib`: 663 passed, 4 ignored.
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`.

title: Project Settings: Frame Count, Start at 0 or Start at 1
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Part of #1807.

`ProjectSettings.frame_start` was already honoured by the Frames and Feet + Frames time display, the Timeline ruler and typed time entry (#530, #710, #731), but nothing could set it, so frames always counted from 0. This adds After Effects' Frame Count setting (Project Settings ▸ Time Display Style ▸ Frames ▸ Frame Count: Start at 0 / Start at 1) in the three places that drive project settings:

- `file.projectSettings` takes `frameStart: 0|1`; anything else is an error. It goes through `Session::edit`, so it's one undo step, and it is saved with the project (the field was already serialized).
- The Project Settings dialog has a "Frame count" row under "Time display style".
- Scripts get `app.project.framesCountType` and `app.project.displayStartFrame` (0 or 1), as in the [Project object reference](https://ae-scripting.docsforadobe.dev/general/project/#projectframescounttype). The `FramesCountType` values are After Effects' own (`FC_START_0` = 2612, `FC_START_1` = 2613, `FC_TIMECODE_CONVERSION` = 2614), taken from [docsforadobe/Types-for-Adobe](https://github.com/docsforadobe/Types-for-Adobe) (MIT, `AfterEffects/*/index.d.ts`), so a script that stored the number keeps working.

Adobe's [Timecode and time display units](https://web.archive.org/web/20260712191125/https://helpx.adobe.com/after-effects/desktop/animate-in-after-effects/add-timecode-and-time-display-units/timecode-time-display-units.html) page (archived copy; helpx refuses non-browser requests) says Frame Count "Determines the starting number for the time display style for Frames", and "Start at 1: The counting for frames begins at one."

Since it's a starting number, it applies to positions, not to lengths. Before this, `display_time` was also used for lengths, which would have shown a 30-frame layer's Duration as 00031 with Start at 1. So there's now `display_duration` (a frame count, with neither Frame Count nor the comp's Start Timecode added), used by the Timeline's Duration column an…

title: CI: shared gate workflow; FreeBSD nightly and on release
author: aiongg
body:
Adds EffectCraft's first CI gate, through the suite's shared gate workflow, and takes the slow platform builds off the pull-request path. **Depends on storytold/craft-common-actions#69**; merge after it. Until then this PR's CI fails, because `gate.yml` doesn't exist yet.

- `ci.yml` is new. It calls `storytold/craft-common-actions/.github/workflows/gate.yml@main`, which runs `cargo xtask ci` with the cached apt install, nextest, rust-cache saved only from main (keyed on the root `Cargo.toml`, so profile changes start a fresh cache), and a check that `Cargo.lock` is unchanged. Every push to main runs to the end, and pushes to a PR branch cancel their older run. Packages: `pkg-config libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxcb1-dev libxcursor-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libfontconfig1-dev libfreetype-dev mesa-vulkan-drivers libgl1-mesa-dev libasound2-dev`. title: effects: CC Radial Fast Blur grows its buffer so streaks pass the layer edge (#2095)
author: mercuryVM
body:
## Problem

CC Radial Fast Blur smears pixels along rays from Center, but it rewrote the buffer it was handed in place, so its output could never extend past the layer's rectangle. A radial "long shadow" stopped dead at the layer edge (#2095), while the other blurs (Gaussian, Fast Box, Directional, Channel, Compound, Camera Lens, Glow) grow their buffer first.

## Fix

- `radial_fast_pad` (`crates/effects/src/blur2.rs`): an output pixel `R` from Center averages the source between `R·(1−s)` and `R`, so content `r` from Center reaches `r / (1−s)`. The buffer is padded on every side by the farthest corner's reach, `d·s / (1−s)` (+1), capped at 4096 like the other growing effects.
- `radial_fast_blur` pads before sampling and takes Center after the pad, so it keeps its place. Adjustment layers are comp-sized already and are not padded (as Gaussian / Directional Blur).
- The GPU path (`crates/gpu/src/fx_generate.rs`) pads the same way through the shared helper, so CPU and GPU still agree.

## Tests

- `blur2::tests::radial_fast_blur_streaks_past_the_layer_edge`: an opaque 20×20 square with Center outside it on the left and Amount 80. The buffer grows, a pixel 10 px past the right edge is lit, the square stays opaque, and an adjustment layer's buffer is not grown. It fails on `main` (the buffer stays 20 px wide) and passes with the fix.
- `tests_fx_generate::cc_radial_fast_blur`: a new GPU-vs-CPU case with Center outside the layer.

## Gates

Every stage of `cargo xtask ci`, run on Windows 11 (dev profile, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4`), rebased on `c2df1c1a`. The stages were run as their individual commands, because on Windows `xtask ci` cannot rebuild its own running `xtask.exe` in the test stage.

- fmt, clippy (`--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`), doc tests, translations report, pdf-deps, layers, assets, wasm: all ok.
- tests: `effectcraft-effects` and `effectcraft-gpu` (the crates this PR touches) pass in full. 40 tests fail on this machine, and the **same 40** fail on #…

title: #2094 (adv): crisp cast shadows so diffusion only softens
author: ChristopherLinnett
body:
Fixes #2094

## Problem

Advanced 3D cast shadows were visibly pixelated — hard stair-steps along the shadow edge (reporter's video, ~6:28–7:13) — and raising **Shadow Diffusion made them worse instead of softer**: on the issue's own repro the shadow decayed into blotches and, at high diffusion, lit surfaces speckled themselves.

## Root causes

1. **Shadow maps were too small and mis-sized.** Maps were a power-of-two of the *raster* side; point-light cube faces were additionally halved and capped at 1024, so one map texel covered many output pixels — the stair-steps were the map texels themselves.
2. **The PCF kernel was fixed (5×5) and texel-scaled**, so at 1080p its reach was far smaller than the requested penumbra; diffusion was partly faked by widening the *bias*, which is what made the filter lift shadows off their casters and produce acne/streaking instead of softening.
3. **Bias was entangled with radius** (`bias ×(1+radius)`): it had to be big to hide the texel steps of the binary depth compare, and that same big bias let a lit caster win its own depth test wherever it also cast.
4. **The WGSL mirror was invalid WGSL**: `u32(x) * C ^ u32(y) * C` — Tint (Chrome's compiler) rejects mixing `*` with `^` without parentheses; naga accepted it, so native tests passed while the web build's shader module would fail to compile.

## Fix (CPU reference + WGSL mirror, step-for-step)

- **Map sizing:** full scene-derived power-of-two (512–4096); point-light faces use the full size capped at 2048 (the issue's own suggestion); scene-wide 26 M-texel budget, halved largest-map-first (deterministic, O(n log n)); adapters whose storage-binding limit can't hold the budget fall back to the CPU raster, as before.
- **Penumbra measured in output pixels:** reach = wanted penumbra ÷ the receiver's texel footprint (min 2 texels, max 256), so diffusion width is identical at any map resolution and hard edges ramp over two texels instead of showing one-texel sawtooth.
- **Receiver-plane…

title: End an open text edit when Deselect All runs (#2096)
author: ChristopherLinnett
body:
## Problem
While a text layer was being edited in the canvas, **Deselect All** (Edit menu, Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A, or the F2 binding) selected every character instead — the layer stayed selected, and the issue's `forwardable_during_text_edit` guard (Cmd/Ctrl/Alt chords and F1–F35 only) means a rebindable shortcut kept working as a shortcut while a bare letter binding stayed typing.

## Fix — one final state on every route
- **Engine** (`deselect_all`): commits the open edit first through the same code path as `text.endEdit` — a created-but-empty type-tool layer is discarded (its own undo step, as with Escape), typed text is kept with no extra undo step, and the command still deselects.
- **Editor forward**: while the in-canvas editor holds the keyboard it forwards the command's *currently assigned* shortcut (default Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+A, F2, or a rebind) plus function-key chords. Bare-letter bindings keep typing; Cmd/Ctrl+A still selects characters.
- **Project-panel focus**: the Project redirects in `menus::invoke` and `entry_enabled` stand down while a text edit is open, so Layer ▸ New ▸ Text (which keeps Project focus) reaches the command from menu, shortcut, script and MCP routes — and the menu item is enabled/disabled by what the routed command can actually do.

## Tests
3 engine tests + 6 kittest UI tests (chords, F2, rebinding incl. bare-letter and function-key rebinds, menu enabled-ness both ways, Project-focused entry). All are RED at base and GREEN here; mutation-tested — each gate (invoke redirect, enabled-ness, forward arm, empty-layer discard) is individually killed by a named test. `cargo xtask ci` green on this tree.

## Follow-ups (pre-existing, split out, out of scope here)
- #2226 — Duplicate during a text edit leaves the edit on the original layer while selecting the copy
- #2227 — Edit ▸ Clear deletes the composition being typed into when the Project panel is focused, with no confirmation

Closes #2096

title: Add RGB Split, Halftone, Pixel Sort and Dither (Stylize)
author: kuyamcliff
body:
Four looks motion designers usually buy third-party plug-ins for, which After Effects doesn't ship. They are EffectCraft's own effects: the parameters are ours, the maths standard image processing.

- RGB Split: red and blue move apart along a direction (Linear) or away from a centre, growing with the distance (Radial, like lateral chromatic aberration). Per-channel shift weights; the layer grows by the shift. Premultiplied channels keep their own alpha.
- Halftone: an amplitude-modulated dot screen at any angle, circles, lines or squares whose area carries the ink, as ink on paper (custom colours) or as colour channels (red, green and blue light screens at the angle, +30° and +60°). Neighbouring cells are checked, so big dots spill over as on a real screen.
- Pixel Sort: along rows or columns, runs of pixels whose brightness, hue or saturation lies between two thresholds are sorted by it, with a maximum span length and reverse order: the streaky glitch look.
- Dither: Bayer 2×2 / 4×4 / 8×8 ordered or Floyd–Steinberg dithering to 2–256 levels, colour or monochrome, on cells of a chosen pixel size.

All four keep alpha, take Blend With Original where it applies, are deterministic, don't read the clock and run on the CPU (not marked GPU). Each has behaviour tests (tones, shifts, sorted spans, average kept by dithering), a determinism test and a hostile-parameter test (NaN, ±1e9, out-of-range popups). On a real 640×360 Big Buck Bunny frame each renders in 2–55 ms.

Also: Simplified Chinese names for the four, `docs/effects.md` regenerated (311 effects), and `app` info counts the registered effects instead of a hard-coded "307 registered".

title: MCP: get_property and get_layer list an enum property's options (#2085)
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
`get_property` and `get_layer` now list the allowed values of enum properties, so a client can set the Range Selector's Shape (or any popup) without guessing the mapping.

In After Effects these properties are popups in the Timeline and Effect Controls: the user picks a label and never sees the number behind it. Over MCP the number is all a client gets, so `prop.get` and `layer.tree` (and with them `get_property` and `get_layer`, flat mode included) now add `options: [{value, label}]` to any property whose UI is a popup, the same shape `effect.list` already uses. The values are zero-based, as `set_property` takes them. Text Path Options ▸ Path is the one popup whose list depends on the layer (None, then its masks); the Timeline already built that list inline, so it moves to `Layer::popup_options` and the Timeline, `prop.get` and `layer.tree` share it. `effect.list` goes through the same JSON helper. Enum properties with no popup UI (hidden ones such as a shape's Blend Mode) still have no list. Flat mode carries `options` too, which makes it a bit less compact; happy to keep it out of flat mode if you'd rather.

Closes #2085

title: EPS: bound operand-stack copies and runtime allocations (#2138)
author: donovan-yohan
body:
## Summary

Fixes #2138.

Numeric PostScript `copy` extended the operand stack without the existing 100,000-value cap. Repeated `count copy` could therefore grow the stack exponentially. `aload` used capped pushes, but could silently discard part of its result.

Check the complete result before either bulk operation. A resource-limit diagnostic stops execution, including inside `stopped`, while keeping artwork already drawn. `astore` consumes operands before returning its array and does not require an extra stack slot.

Runtime array/procedure payloads and string bytes now share a cumulative 256 MiB allocation budget. Constructors and payload-copy paths charge it before allocating; discarded objects do not replenish it. Executable strings and lossy UTF-8 comparison copies use conservative preflight bounds. Existing individual constructor limits remain unchanged. Array length, indexed reads and matrix reads no longer clone an entire array unnecessarily.

This is a runtime payload budget, not a process-wide memory bound. Source tokens, dictionaries/names, font internals, graphics/output and allocator/container overhead are excluded and documented in the crate README.

## Regression coverage

- A bounded synthetic EPS exceeds the operand-stack limit through 18 `count copy` rounds. It fails against the original interpreter and passes with the repair, without attempting an out-of-memory allocation.
- Public import tests cover `aload` rejection, propagation through `stopped`, preserved earlier artwork and normal copy/render ordering.
- Reduced private budgets exercise cumulative allocation, intervals, conversions, comparison copies and other payload snapshots without allocating hundreds of megabytes. Repeated short array/procedure intervals charge only returned slots, not a full-source snapshot; the regression failed on the preceding PR head and passes with the follow-up.
- Compatibility controls cover shallow compound identity, exact stack boundaries, no-refund behavior,…

title: Scale Composition: comp.scale resizes a comp and scales its layers, keys, cameras and guides by one factor
author: marcoarnulfo
body:
Scale Composition over the CLI/MCP: `comp.scale {factor | width | height}` resizes a comp and everything in it by one factor, so a template can be rendered at 4K, 1080p and smaller sizes without rebuilding it.

In After Effects this is the bundled File > Scripts > Scale Composition.jsx: you give a new scale factor, width or height, and the comp's contents are scaled and repositioned proportionally, keyframes included ([ProVideo Coalition's walkthrough](https://www.provideocoalition.com/introducing_after_effects_script_of_the_week/); I couldn't find an Adobe help page that documents the dialog, so the exact field names and defaults are unverified). This PR follows that: one undo step; the comp's width and height; Position (or X/Y/Z Position), Point of Interest and Scale of every layer that isn't carried by a scaled parent, with every key, spatial tangent and speed; camera Zoom, Focus Distance and Aperture, so 3D layers land in the same place in the frame. A 2D parent's Scale carries no depth, so its 3D children scale their own Z (Position, Point of Interest and Scale), unless a 3D ancestor further up already carries it. Their speeds follow: a Position key's speed grows by how much the path stretches in that key's direction, and Scale's Z speed by the factor (a key storing one ease for all dimensions gets its own for Z first), so the ease keeps its shape. The parent chain is walked through cameras and lights, as the renderer applies every ancestor: a layer is carried by any ancestor with a Scale, and children of a camera or light with no Scale above it scale like unparented layers. Pixel guides move; percentage guides are left alone, so they keep their percent exactly. The viewer's region of interest is scaled too when the scaled comp is the active one, so it covers the same part of the frame. Anchor points, masks, shapes and layer effects live in layer space, so the layer's Scale carries them and they aren't touched. `factor` is a multiplier (2 = twice the size); hap…

title: ui: each drop-down pick and checkbox click is its own undo step (#2152)
author: mercuryVM
body:
## Problem

Every write from the Timeline's and Effect Controls' value editors carried the scrub merge key (`scrub-{uid}` / `ec-{uid}`), and `Session::edit` folds consecutive edits with the same key into one history step. That is right for a scrub (one drag, one step), but drop-down picks and checkbox clicks used the same key and nothing ended the merge when the popup closed. Two deliberate picks in a row became one undo step, so a single undo jumped back past the first pick (#2152). In After Effects each choice is its own undo step.

## Fix

In `value_editor` (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/timeline.rs`) and Effect Controls' property row (`crates/ui-egui/src/panels/effect_controls.rs`), a `pick` closure sends the same `prop.set` as `set` but without the merge key. It is used for:

- Timeline: enum drop-downs and checkboxes;
- Effect Controls: enum drop-downs, checkboxes and the mask ("Path") popup;
- the shared layer drop-down (`widgets::layer_picker`, from #2155) in both panels: a Layer Control's layer, an Environment light's Source, and so on.

Scrubs, typed numbers, colours and the other continuous editors keep their merge key. A pick also ends any merge in progress, so a scrub followed by a pick is two steps.

`it::ui_effect_controls::each_drop_down_pick_and_checkbox_click_is_its_own_undo_step` (egui_kittest, a Gaussian Blur on a solid):

title: Viewer: motion path follows X/Y Position when dimensions are separated (#2242)
author: MarekSpodBiedry
body:
Fixes #2242.

With Separate Dimensions on, the layer is driven by X Position and Y Position, but the viewer's motion path was still drawn from the combined Position property, which the layer no longer uses. Editing X/Y keys moved the layer while the path stayed put, and it only lined up again after turning Separate Dimensions off.

`motion_path` (crates/ui-egui/src/panels/viewer_overlays.rs) now checks for `positionX` / `positionY` on the transform, the same test the engine commands use (`prop.rs`, `layer.rs`, `align.rs`), and when they are there:

- the path and its frame dots are sampled from X and Y Position, and the keyframe squares sit at the union of their key times;
- dragging a key square edits both X and Y at that time; if only one of them has a key there, the other gets one first, so `keys.set` never falls back to a neighbouring key;
- selecting a square (drag, Pen Delete) selects the X and Y keys at its time, and a square shows as selected when either of them is selected;
- Pen / Add Vertex on the path adds the key to X and Y Position instead of the unused combined Position;
- Pen Convert does nothing on these squares, since separated X/Y have no spatial interpolation (no tangent handles are drawn for them).

The combined-Position path is unchanged.

Tests: `separated_motion_path_uses_x_and_y_keys` checks the key times and the sampled X/Y values; `separated_key_dot_refers_to_its_axis_keys` checks that a separated key square refers to the X/Y keys at its own time.

title: Export: animated WebP output (lossless, with alpha)
author: waj334
body:
Adds **Animated WebP** as a Render Queue output format. EffectCraft already imports animated WebP (#762); this adds writing it.

## What it does

- New `OutputFormat::WebP` ("Animated WebP", `.webp`), available in the Render Queue, the CLI (`--format webp`), `renderQueue.*` commands, scripting output-module templates and the web app's downloads (`image/webp`). Two new output-module templates: **Animated WebP** and **Animated WebP with Alpha**.
- RGB, RGB + Alpha (straight or premultiplied) and Alpha channels, as the other still/animation formats.
- **Loop Forever** (`gif_loop`, the `loop` parameter) now applies to WebP too; off writes a loop count of 1 (play once).

## How it's written (`crates/export/src/webp.rs`)

- Container written from **RFC 9649**: RIFF `WEBP` with `VP8X` (animation flag, alpha flag with RGB + Alpha), `ANIM` (background colour, loop count) and one `ANMF` per frame. The RIFF size is filled in at the end (output files are seekable).
- Frame images are lossless `VP8L` bitstreams from the `image` crate's pure-Rust encoder (MIT OR Apache-2.0, already in the tree through `effectcraft-media`'s `webp` feature), lifted out of the still file it writes. Only its public API is used.
- A frame stores only the **area that changed** since the previous frame (corner snapped to the even offsets `ANMF` stores, drawn with *do not blend* so alpha is replaced, not composited). A **run of identical frames is one frame** held for the run's length, so a hold costs a few bytes. Holds longer than a frame can store (24-bit ms) continue in a 1×1 frame that changes nothing.
- Durations are whole milliseconds with the rounding error carried (60 fps → 17, 17, 16…), like GIF's centiseconds; never 0 ms.
- Fully transparent pixels drop their colour before diffing and encoding.
- Never-crash: every buffer access is checked; frame sizes over 16384 px (VP8L's 14-bit limit), frame rates that can't be timed and files over the 4 GB RIFF limit are `Unsupported` errors. The encoder's …

title: Transform: Fit to Comp sizes shape and text layers by their painted bounds (#2198)
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Fixes #2198

## What was wrong
Fit to Comp (Layer ▸ Transform ▸ Fit to Comp, `Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+F`, and `layer.transform` with `op: fit` / `fitWidth` / `fitHeight`) took the layer's size from `effectcraft_render::source_size`. That returns `(0, 0)` for layers without a source item, i.e. shape and text layers. The fit arm requires `w > 0 && h > 0`, so for those layers the command returned `Ok` and changed nothing.

## What changed
In `transform_op` (`crates/engine/src/commands/layer.rs`), when a fit op runs and the source size is empty:
- **Size:** it falls back to the layer's painted `content_bounds` at the current time, using an `EvalCtx` built the same way `parent_fixes` builds one.
- **Anchor:** it goes to the bounds' centre instead of `(w/2, h/2)`. Content bounds live in layer space, where a shape is centred on the origin and text sits above its baseline, so `(w/2, h/2)` would fill the frame but land the content off-centre.
- **Everything else is unchanged:**
  - Source-backed layers keep their current behaviour, because `(w/2, h/2)` is already their bounds centre.
  - `reset` and the other ops still use the source size.
  - Empty bounds still do nothing.

## Tests
- `tests_menu_cmds::fit_to_comp_fills_the_comp_with_shape_and_text_bounds`: it maps the painted bounds to comp space and checks them for a 180×80 rect shape and an 80 px text layer:
  - after `fit` they span `[0, 0, 640, 360]`;
  - after `fitWidth` they span the full width, centred vertically.
- It fails on main (scale stays 100). It also fails with the size fix alone, because the old anchor lands the content off-centre.

Run: `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine --lib fit_to_comp_fills_the_comp`

## Counts
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-engine --lib` (rebased on current main): 686 passed, 0 failed, 4 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

title: Edit: an open text edit stands down the Project-panel Clear redirect (#2227)
author: SusieeTheLinuxUser
body:
Fixes #2227

## What was wrong
Edit ▸ Clear follows panel focus. With the Project panel focused, it redirects to `project.delete`, which removes the Project selection straight away when nothing uses it (the `delete_items::guard` prompt only opens for items compositions use). If a text edit was open in the canvas while the Project panel kept focus, Clear deleted the composition being typed into, without asking. Undo brought the item back but not the active composition.

## What changed
In `crates/ui-egui/src/menus.rs`:
- `invoke`: while `app.session.state.text_edit` is open, the Project-panel `edit.clear` redirect stands down. It returns `Ok` and deletes nothing.
- `entry_enabled`: with the Project panel focused, the Clear entry is disabled during a text edit. This mirrors how Deselect All stands down in the #2096 work.

The Render Queue redirect and every other `edit.clear` path are unchanged.

## Tests
- `ui_project_delete::clear_with_the_project_focused_stands_down_during_a_text_edit`. Setup: the active composition is selected in the Project panel, a text edit is open, and the Project panel has focus. It sends Clear through `menus::invoke`, the path the menu, the shortcut and the control channel share. It then checks that the composition survives, the project is unchanged and the text edit stays open.
- It fails on main and passes with the fix.

Run: `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui --test it clear_with_the_project_focused_stands_down`

## Counts
- `cargo test -p effectcraft-ui-egui` (rebased on current main): lib 267 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored. Integration: 550 passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p effectcraft-ui-egui --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
